author: dallasheidt14
body:
Comments and docstrings only, plus one deleted doc. No behaviour changes. Last of four from a repo-wide sweep for text still asserting the pre-banding age model, after #997, #998 and #999.

Most of these were correct when written and went wrong on their own. A cohort's birth year moves every Aug 1, so a comment that writes the pair out as a literal — `U11 = 2015`, `'14b' -> U12`, `U14 → 2012` — is right for one season and wrong forever after. The fix is the same everywhere: state the formula and stamp the season instead of freezing a table.

## Where they were actively misleading

| File | Was | Why it mattered |
|---|---|---|
| `src/utils/team_name_utils.py:849` | "`'14U'`, `'U14'`, `'2012'`, `"'12"` all collapse to the same key" | They don't. The U-forms are `u14`; the year-forms go through the season rule to `u15`. That sentence is the stated reason two copies of `extract_distinctions` must stay in sync, so it would have been used to justify merging a 2012-born team with a U14 team. |
| `src/models/modular11_matcher.py:158` | a frozen `U13 → 2013 … U18 → 2008` table | The code below it computes `season_year - age`, so the table contradicts its own function. Anyone auditing a rejected Modular11 match compared against the wrong year. |
| `tests/unit/test_tgs_division_parsing.py:156` | "Pins WHY the band is read from its **oldest** year" | #996 corrected the assertions and the inline comment; this docstring survived, so the file meant to be authoritative stated the opposite rule at the top. It now also says which case actually pins it: `B2008/2007` resolves the same either way because 2007 folds into U19, and that coincidence is what let the original defect ship. |
| `docs/PIPELINE_PROCESS_MAP.md:624` | Step 2 expands birth-year shorthand, full stop | Predates #996 entirely: no bands collapsing to U-XX, no U-age re-rendered from `teams.age_group`. Its worked example at :904 taught the reader to reject a correctly-labelled team. |
| `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:134` | on conflict, "prefer the name-parsed age" | Inverts the source of truth. Now: warn for review, never override `teams.age_group`. |

## Two notes

`scripts/normalize_team_names.py` also loses a comment block left behind by an earlier version of #996 that described restoring a band from `team_name_original`. That path was removed for putting the cohort in the wrong place; the veto comment below it is the live explanation.

`src/models/playmetrics_matcher.py:171` claimed slash tokens map to the older year and cited `10/11 → U16` as evidence — which is the *younger* year's answer, so its own example disproved it. **The comment is corrected; the code still takes the older year, deliberately.** It normalizes tokens for fuzzy matching rather than deriving a cohort, so it only has to agree with how the DB names the same team, and changing it moves every PlayMetrics tournament match. Worth measuring against the alias table before touching, which is out of scope here.

`docs/FIX_AGE_YEAR_DISCREPANCIES_INVESTIGATION.md` is deleted: it documents a Monday schedule the workflow no longer has, and the script it investigates is gated off in both callers as of #997. Nothing references it.

## Verification

872 pass across the age, TGS, normalizer, team-name, fuzzy-match, distinction, PlayMetrics and Modular11 suites. `ruff` clean.

author: balizero1987
body:
## What

`test_kbli_gold_rule_registered_and_scoped_to_exactly_one_file` asserted `len(CONTENT_KEYED_RULES) == 12`, but PR #4422 (00:45 UTC tonight, commit `f641198a4`) added a 13th rule (`corpus_sha256`, KBLI Navigator P2b benchmark) without bumping the count or its `# +1:` comment trail. Bumped both, matching the existing 8-entry format exactly.

## Why this wasn't caught

The check (`worker-plane review panel — test suite`, `.github/workflows/worker-plane-review-tests.yml`) is not a required status check on `main`, so the red sat unseen for ~4h until it surfaced as a stray unrelated red on PR #4490 (qwen_quota_watch, unrelated fix).

**Correction on the record**: an earlier pass on this same investigation called it "pre-existing drift on main, not caused by this PR" — that was wrong (caught by team-lead review). `git log --stat` on the test's own path showed zero commits ever touching it, while `CONTENT_KEYED_RULES` grew from 12 to 13 under it the same night, same session's own PR (#4422). "Rosso su main" and "rosso da prima" are different claims; only a `git log` on the actual path distinguishes them.

## Structural defect (ledgered, not decided here)

Added a row to `PENDING-ARMS.md`: this is a hand-maintained magic-number counter gating a NUMBER instead of a PROPERTY, on a non-required check — so the next rule added to `CONTENT_KEYED_RULES` without a matching `+1` repeats this exact failure, invisibly. Two remediation shapes named for the owner to choose between (not decided in this PR):

1. Replace the magic-number assert with a structural property check (every rule is a well-formed anchored triple), so the test can't drift out of sync with the list it guards.
2. Promote the check to required on `main`.

## Verified

- `scripts/tests/test_detect_secrets_auto_triage.py`: 81/81 green.
- Full 5-file `worker-plane review panel` suite: target test passes; 2 unrelated pre-existing failures in `test_launch_worker_plane_review_panel.py` (`_run_bound_command` signature drift) — different file, different cause, untouched by this diff.
- `pending_arms_report.py` parses the new ledger row cleanly, no MALFORMED.

author: digitie
body:
`T-VN-41S`가 열어 둔 마지막 결정(build 예산 300초 vs item 상한 1,000,000)을 닫고, 같은 조사에서
드러난 **도달 가능한 장애 둘**을 함께 고친다.

## 결정

| 상수 | 이전 | 이후 |
|---|---|---|
| `_SNAPSHOT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `300.0` | **유지** |
| `_SNAPSHOT_ITEM_LIMIT` | `1_000_000` | **`500_000`** |
| `_SNAPSHOT_MATERIAL_BYTE_LIMIT` | `512 MiB` | **`56 MiB`** |

**예산은 올리지 않는다.** 이 값은 stream share barrier가 유지되는 시간이자 writer가 막히는
최대 시간이다. 올리면 아래 §도달 가능한 장애가 커진다.

**상한은 예산에서 유도하지 않는다.** 판정 렌즈 넷 중 셋이 유도식을 골랐고 나도 그쪽으로
기울었으나, 반증이 뒤집었다 — `limit = budget × rate / safety`로 정의하면
`limit / rate × safety ≡ budget`이라 불변식이 **항등식**이 된다. 예산을 절반으로 내리는 한 줄
변경에서 CI가 green인 채 client가 보는 413 문턱이 반토막 나고, PinVi는 `Retry-After` 없는
terminal 413을 받아 reconciliation이 영구 정지하는데 서버는 build가 아예 안 돌아 지표까지
조용해진다. **유도식은 drift를 없앤 것이 아니라 drift 경보를 없앤다.**

변이로 확인했다 — 예산을 120초로 내리면 지금 설계는 불변식 **3건이 동시에 red**다.
유도식이었다면 green이었을 지점이다.

## 전제 정정 — 원래 근거가 재현되지 않았다

앞선 보고서는 1M이 예산을 68~248초 넘는다고 적었다(368.4초 / 547.9초). 오늘 같은 코드·
**더 넓은 키**로 재면 235.7초다. 그 보고서 자신이 547.9초를 "다른 커밋 + 통합테스트 동시
실행"이라며 비-정본으로 못박고 있었고, 정본이라던 368.4초도 재현되지 않는다.

**그래도 1M을 유지하지 않는다** — 예산의 79%를 쓰는 값은 상한이 될 수 없다.

## 측정 — 배포 예산 그대로, 배포 상한에서 (`SOAK: PASS`, exit 0)

| 축 | 값 |
|---|---|
| N | **500,000** (= 배포 상한) |
| build | **123.0초** = 예산의 41%, 게이트(예산/2)에 18% 여유 |
| 처리량 | 4,065 item/s · 재료 422,764 B/s |
| 상한 + 1 | typed `snapshot_item_limit_exceeded`, partial row **0** |
| compaction | 500,000행 / 7.2초 |
| 증거 보존 | material 1 · receipt 1 (item 0) |

prod의 가장 큰 stream은 **179 target**이다(나머지 전부 1건, 실 PinVi stream 없음).
500,000은 그 2,793배라 **이 인하는 실사용을 전혀 좁히지 않는다.**

### 왜 예전 측정이 낙관적이었나

예전 fixture는 `'soak-' || lpad(value,8)`로 **13자 ASCII를 삽입 순서대로** 심었다. build의
정렬 키는 `convert_to(normalize(target_key,NFC),'UTF8')`이고 **그 표현식에 인덱스가 없다**.
즉 heap correlation ≈ 1.0인 정렬 **최선 조건**을 잰 것이라, 나온 처리량이 하한이 아니라
상한이었다. prod 실측 키 폭(24~36자, 평균 35.1)에 맞춘 md5 기반 37자로 바꾸고 삽입/정렬
순서 상관도 끊었다.

### byte 축 — item 수만으로는 build 시간을 못 묶는다

`material_bytes`는 heap이 아니라 `_leaf_material` 인코딩 합이다.
`target_key`가 계약상 512자까지 허용되므로 같은 item 수에서도 재료량이 **16배** 흔들린다.

| 키 모양 | B/item | 500k 재료 |
|---|---|---|
| prod 실측 35자 | 103 | 49.1 MiB |
| 계약 최대 512자 ASCII | 683 | 325.7 MiB |
| 512자 한글 NFC | 1,611 | 768.2 MiB |

512 MiB는 실측 422,764 B/s에서 **1,270초 = 예산의 4.2배**라 시간 방어선이 아니었고, item
상한을 500,000으로 낮춘 뒤로는 **계약 최대 폭에서도 발화하지 않는 죽은 코드**였다.
56 MiB는 138.9초다. 정상 폭 stream은 영향 없다(570,099 item에 해당해 item 상한이 먼저 걸린다).

## 도달 가능한 장애 둘 — 상한과 달리 179건에서도 터진다

1. **writer 무한 대기.** `_LOCK_STREAM_SQL ... FOR UPDATE` 경로에 `lock_timeout`이 **0건**
   이었다(PG 기본 0 = 무한). build가 같은 stream을 예산 전 구간 `FOR SHARE`로 쥐는 동안
   writer는 **connection을 문 채** 쌓이고, 그 pool은 전 endpoint 공유(`5 + 10 = 15`)라
   build 하나가 지도 조회까지 포함한 API 전체를 마르게 할 수 있었다.
2. **재시도 폭주.** `snapshot_build_timeout`의 `Retry-After: 1`은 예산을 통째로 태운 요청에
   1초 뒤 재시도를 지시한다 = 그 stream을 barrier를 놓지 않는 **100% duty cycle**로 물린다.

## ⚠️ 동작 변경 (BREAKING)

- build가 도는 stream에 쓰기가 오면 이전에는 **블록됐다가 성공**했으나, 이제
  `503 stream_busy`(`Retry-After: 10`)로 즉시 돌아온다. 기존 통합 테스트가 이 변화를 정확히
  잡았고, 단언을 "대기 중에는 `stream_busy` / build가 barrier를 놓은 뒤 재시도는 성공"으로
  바꿨다 — 테스트의 본 뜻(writer가 영구히 막히지 않는다)은 유지된다.
- admission 상한 인하(위 표). 값은 `contracts/`·OpenAPI에 고정돼 있지 않아 PinVi re-vendor는
  필요 없다.

## 적대적 리뷰가 잡은 것 — 이 PR이 만든 회귀 셋 포함

리뷰 2건을 붙였고 **load-bearing 주장을 전부 직접 실증**한 뒤 반영했다.

| 지적 | 실증 |
|---|---|
| `set_config(..., is_local)`은 **transaction** 범위인데 되돌리지 않아, 이후 모든 lock 대기가 handler 없는 상한을 물려받아 **500**이 됨 | 코드 확인 — `set_config`가 `_CREATE_STREAM_SQL` 앞·`try` 밖 |
| **놓친 경로** — `cache_target_event_repo`의 `FOR UPDATE OF stream`도 `lock_timeout` 0건. PinVi refresh-request가 그 경로라 더 유력 | 확인 |
| 대기 5초 + 재시도 1초 = duty cycle **83%** | 산술 |
| 새 통합 테스트가 수정을 지우면 실패가 아니라 **hang** | 변이 실행 **exit=124** |
| `Retry-After`를 import 시각에 얼려 두면 예산을 바꾼 프로세스에서 갈림 | monkeypatch 테스트 추가 |
| byte 상한이 시간 방어선이 아님 | 직접 검산 |
| **이 PR 보고서의 거짓 주장** — soak이 예산을 3,600초로 덮은 채 "배포 예산 그대로"라고 씀 | `scripts/…:262` 확인 → 우회 제거 |

게이트가 넷째를 잡았다 — `finally`의 reset이 abort된 transaction에서
`InFailedSQLTransactionError`가 되어 원래 `stream_busy`를 가렸다. soak 실행이 다섯째를 잡았다
— 3단계 seeding off-by-one.

## 게이트

ruff / mypy `--strict` (core·api) / lint-imports(4 kept, 0 broken) clean, **249 passed**.
soak PASS(위). 변이 3종 전부 red:

| 변이 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| `lock_timeout` 설정 제거 | red (이전엔 hang) |
| byte 상한 512 MiB로 되돌림 | red (`1269.9 <= 150.0` 실패) |
| 예산 300 → 120초 | 불변식 **3건 동시** red |

## 남은 숙제

**안전계수 2는 넉넉하지 않다.** 유일한 동시 부하 관측(2.32배)을 적용하면 상한 크기 build가
예산의 95%를 쓴다. 지금은 byte 축을 따로 조여 폭 축 여유를 확보했으나, **부하를 건 재측정**이
남는다. `docs/resume.md`의 "다음 한 작업"에 그렇게 적었다.

author: hoang130203
body:
## Summary

`external_llm_env_value()` reads a key from `.env` using `grep | cut`, then strips surrounding quotes. However, it does not strip a trailing carriage return (`\r`), which is present in `.env` files edited on Windows (CRLF line endings).

The hidden `\r` at the end of the value causes `external_llm_validate_url()` to reject an otherwise valid URL (the URL parser sees a trailing `\r` in the hostname/path), and `curl` calls silently fail with connection errors to `http://localhost:11434\r`.

Fix: strip `$'\r'` before stripping quotes, matching the pattern used in `check-compatibility.sh` (which already does `"${value%$'\r'}"` for the same reason).

## Test plan
- [x] `bash -n ods/installers/lib/external-services.sh` — no syntax errors
- [x] Read-through: `${value%$'\r'}` is a no-op on Unix-style files

author: leolara
body:
One honest number for how much of the executable spec is formally verified, and
a ratchet that stops the number from drifting down unnoticed. Implements
`mb/proof-coverage-plan.md`.

Today it reads:

| Package | What a proof covers here | Where it stands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EthCLSpecs` | the spec functions the fork bodies declare | 8 characterized, 23 touched, of 585 |
| `SizzLean` | SSZ properties over the whole `SSZType` universe, gated by a predicate | 3 of 5 properties, over 12 admitted arms; open: any `hashTreeRoot` property, cached tree ≡ uncached `hashTreeRoot` |
| `LeanSha256`, `LeanHazmat*` | nothing to cover: `@[extern]` bindings, and a spec side pinned by the NIST CAVP vectors | 2 named equivalence axioms |
| `LeanPoseidon` | `permute_eq_permuteRef`, in the standalone package | outside this run: it pins mathlib of its own |
| `EthCLLib` | out of scope: elaborators and an effect monad | the replay tests and the pyspec vectors are its claim |

## The metric

A **spec function** is a constant a `forkdef` produced, read from `captureExt`,
so no name is ever scraped out of source text. Each one sits in a tier:

- **tier 0, executable**, every spec function by construction, the denominator;
- **tier 1, touched**, a theorem *statement* under `EthCLSpecs.Proofs` mentions
  it, computed from `getUsedConstants` on the type and never on the proof term;
- **tier 2, characterized**, a person tagged a theorem `@[characterizes f]`.

A fork's denominator is its **effective surface**: what its own source declares
plus every ancestor `forkdef` it re-elaborated through `inherit`. Both groups
are constants the fork's own vectors run.

## What is in the diff

- **`EthCLLib/Internal/ProofLedger.lean`**: the `characterizes` attribute, over
  the same `SimplePersistentEnvExtension` storage `captureExt` uses. It
  validates the claim where the proof is written: the target must resolve, must
  be a constant some `forkdef` declared, must appear in the tagged theorem's own
  statement, and the theorem must sit in the target fork's proof directory. Nine
  tags across seven modules cover eight Gloas spec functions.
- **`scripts/ProofCoverage.lean`**: the report, in three modes. It also audits
  axioms. Every written theorem in both proof sets must rest on Lean's three,
  the compiled-evaluation pair, the two named SHA-256 equivalences, or a
  `bv_decide` certificate axiom emitted for a theorem. Anything else fails the
  run, `sorryAx` above all.
- **Two baselines**, one per package, compared for exact equality in both
  directions. A lost proof fails, and a new proof fails until its author runs
  `just proof-coverage-update` and commits the bump. Strict equality is what
  catches a swap of one proof for another that a floor-only count would miss.
- **`docs/PROOF_LEDGER.md`**, folding in `CONSENSUS_PROOF_CANDIDATES.md`: all 39
  rows, grouped per fork, now carrying Status and Tracking columns. Keeping the
  Location column keeps the line spans `just check-citations` enforces.
- **`EthCLSpecs/Proofs/` splits per fork**, `Proofs/Gloas/` in namespace
  `EthCLSpecs.Proofs.Gloas`. That is the rule `SPECS_ARCHITECTURE.md` §3.4
  already sets for the fork bodies, and it holds for proofs because a child
  re-elaborates a parent declaration into its own namespace: `Fulu.f` and
  `Gloas.f` are two constants, and a proof about one claims nothing about the
  other.
- **Generated README blocks**, the rollup in the repo README and the per-fork
  tables in the `EthCLSpecs` README, both compared by `--check`.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`, *Adding a proof***: the six steps an author follows, with
  the three the build enforces repeated in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Where the plan changed

- The plan left the denominator open, capture diff versus effective surface. The
  effective surface won, so the totals differ from the plan's spike (585, not
  279).
- The plan's spike counted 90 theorems in `EthCLSpecs.Proofs`. Most of the gap
  over a `grep` was elaborator-generated declarations (`.eq_1`, `_simp_*`,
  congruence lemmas), which would have inflated every tier; the written count is
  50.
- The plan asked for a new `PROOF_LEDGER.md` beside
  `CONSENSUS_PROOF_CANDIDATES.md`, which was already that ledger. One file now.
- `getPtc`'s row reads `in progress`, not `proved`. Both bounds are stated over
  `getPtcElseOffset`, a restatement of the else-branch arithmetic, so no
  statement mentions `getPtc` and the metric leaves it at the touched tier. The
  row says which half is landed and which is open.

## CI

`just proof-coverage-check` runs in the `ethcl` job after the build. It verifies
and never writes: the two baselines and the two README blocks, compared exactly,
plus the axiom audit. Regenerating stays with the author, because that diff is
the coverage change and belongs in the pull request under review.

## Testing

`just lint`, `just check-citations`, `just check-constants`,
`just ethcl-test`, and `just proof-coverage-check` all pass. The ratchet was
checked red on each case it exists for: a perturbed baseline line, a deleted
`characterizes` tag (the baseline and the README block both flagged), a hand
edit to a generated README number, a scratch `sorry` (caught as `sorryAx`), and
a tag planted in the wrong fork's directory. The pyspec sweep was not re-run: no
spec body changed.

author: ddcolletti-edgesetter
body:
## Root cause

An NFL diagnostic found **283 duplicate signal rows** from a single player fingerprint (DAL / DaRon Bland). The cause: `itemHash()` in the RSS-style pipeline adapters computed a SHA1 over the **raw, un-normalized title/text**. When two outlets published casing variants of the same headline (e.g. "DaRon Bland" vs "Daron Bland"), the differing bytes produced different fingerprints, so the two items never deduped and inserted as separate rows.

## Fix

Lowercase the title/text before it goes into the hash template string, so casing-variant duplicates collapse to the same `itemHash()` and dedup correctly.

Applied to the four adapters that hash a title/text string:

- `server/pipeline/adapters/sports-rss.ts`
- `server/pipeline/adapters/247sports.ts`
- `server/pipeline/adapters/on3.ts`
- `server/pipeline/adapters/cfb-school-sid.ts`

`x-twitter.ts` is intentionally untouched — it hashes by `tweetId`, not text, so it is unaffected by this bug.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

author: motioneso
body:
## Summary
- A private chat close request that fails on the server could leave the closed banner stuck showing "closed" even though the chat was still private, because a later refetch triggered by the browser regaining focus could not tell a genuine close apart from one that never happened.
- Adds a short-lived guard that holds off the browser-focus refetch only while a close request is actually in flight, so a real server failure still gets corrected once that request settles, but a same-moment stale refetch can't override it early.

Part of #1521 (child of #1139).

## Release note
Category: Fixed
Title: Private chat now stays closed correctly if the browser refocuses mid-close
Description: Fixed a rare case where switching away from the app while closing a private chat, then switching back, could leave the app showing the chat as closed even if the close didn't actually finish on the server.

body:
`make` used to write an md5 of libavpipe.a to lib/libavpipe.hash, which avpipe_lib_hash.go embedded so Go would rebuild the package after a `make`. That only covered the archive. cgo's unity build #includes the .c files under libavpipe/src and utils/src, and Go's build cache tracks the package-level cgo files but not the files they #include — so editing e.g. libavpipe/src/avpipe_xc.c was a silent cache hit and you tested a stale binary unless you remembered to run `make` too.

avpipe_cgo_sources.go embeds those included sources and headers directly, making them build-cache inputs: editing any of them forces a cgo recompile with no `make` and no `go clean -cache`. The embed var is blank, so dead-data elimination discards the bytes and binary size is unchanged.

Drops lib/libavpipe.hash, avpipe_lib_hash.go, the Makefile hash step, and the .gitignore exception that kept the hash file tracked.

author: robpruzan
body: This PR introduces a new `--ssh` option for running terminal-code on a remote machine, while running the frontend on your local hardware. The motivation is currently when running terminal-code over ssh it needs to stream all I/O over the ssh connection (all user input and every frame generated is bottlenecked by the network) To solve this, a new `--ssh` option was implemented inside [terminal-browser](https://github.com/zenbu-labs/terminal-browser) that allows websites on an ssh server to be loaded on a local terminal-browser instance. In this scenario, all user input is handled locally since the website is running on your device, and just the website's network requests go over the network boundary, which in the case of vscode are handled optimistically, so there is no latency for the majority of interactions. To get code server running on the remote machine, we use terminal-browser's the new `--ssh-bundle ` option. When passed terminal-browser copies the bundle at the given path from the local machine to the remote machine over SSH. It executes the bundle's `start` script, and then listens for the `READY ` log over stdout of the start script. The url parsed is loaded inside the local-terminal browser automatically ### Demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/813c153a-934e-4b21-86d0-6ae15cd2fbce ---

# Crown extension: island dead-work crown + qL={1..5} later-window SDPA warm (ticket #6)

Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-MXFP4-MLX

## The draw this resamples

`b40c28e` (audreyt 8819b10, island dead-work) + the qL={2,3} warm
extension) — is the current promoted crown at **3.32794960796967**;
parity clean. This ticket extends that crown with our receipted qL={2,3}
later-window SDPA warm — the exact increment that promoted on the
previous crown generation (3.2355 -> 3.2414 on its own receipts, and
0dd455f's promotion at 3.31965 carried it) — and draws a fresh digest. Marker sentence in the manifest note
is the only diff versus `b40c28e`.

## What this archive is

The current promoted first is `8819b10` (audreyt, official
**3.32794960796967**, commit `b40c28e`): complete-permutation K/V
precision-island dead-work elimination in the proposal-head projections
(the 2048-row quantized K/V base GEMM skipped where the exact island rows
overwrite it; the fused QKV pack shrunk to the live 11264 Q rows), on top
of vibecodooor's 214d92a (affine-4 embedding dequantization folded into
the dual-RMSNorm-concat kernel + the combined top-32-finalize-with-rerank
dispatch), on top of our own 0dd455f (the qL warm content, promoted at
3.31965). This archive is exactly that tree plus ONE extension restored:
the later-window SDPA warm compiles qL={1,2,3,4,5} (the crown carries
{1,4,5}) at both the kL=1024 (64-block) and kL=1025 (128-block) families.

## Why qL={2,3} belongs in the warm

The verify exactness chunk splits any width-7/8/9 decode round into a
qL=5 chunk A plus a qL={2,3,4} chunk B (qL*gqa must stay <= 32 on the
fused vector path). The crown's warm covers qL=1 (serial control / chunk-B
of width 6), qL=4, and qL=5 — the deep rounds' chunk-B states qL=2 (width
7) and qL=3 (width 8) are NOT compiled before the scored window, so the
first depth-7/8 round first-touches those pipeline states on the clock.

Ranked receipts for exactly this extension, measured on the pre-jump
frontier content by this seat:

| archive | warm set | official score |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v27 | qL {1,4,5} @ kL=1024 | 3.23553 |
| v28 | qL {1,2,3,4,5} @ kL=1024 | 3.24138 |
| v30 | qL {1..5} @ 768+1024 | 3.24515 (then-crown class) |

The crown tree drafts DEEPER than that content did (mean draft 5.7-6.2 on
the depth-loving prompts at cap 7), which makes the width-7/8 chunk-B
states fire MORE often here than they did on the tree the receipts were
measured on. The mechanism is strictly more relevant on this base, not
less.

Warm is untimed and throwaway: dummy K/V on scratch caches, zero effect on
any scored forward, tokens bit-identical (verified below). The only cost
is a few extra pipeline compilations at session start.

## Negative results we contributed this cycle (public data)

- `0cb3873f` (this seat): yijunyu's floor=6 widthCap stacked on the
  dual-RMSNorm tree scored **3.24629** — the floor clipped the depth-loving
  prompts (192fb621 mean draft 6.15->5.74, 00142a44 5.26->5.10, each
  ~-3.5% ratio; schedule-untouched prompts moved within ~1% session noise).
  Independent confirmation: Lieisyourlie's own #857 floor=6 on this content
  scored 3.30059, also below the flat cap. Ceiling-7 / no-gate stands on
  cheap-draft trees; the floor is only a win where drafts are expensive.
- Cap 8 pollutes (Lieisyourlie #851 3.212; this seat's v20-era 3.1930).

## Verification (this archive, before submit)

- `mtp-verify --generate 257 --mtp-depth 8`: self_consistent=true (replayed
  1 row bit-identically), chain_contradictions=0, 257 rows.
- `mtp-timed --tokens 256 --mtp-depth 8` against those rows:
  all_tokens_matched=true, reference_checked_rows=380/380.
- Release worker builds clean on the restored tree.

## Board state at submit

Crown at submit: 3.32794960796967 (`8819b10`). The evening window
moved the frontier 3.31965 -> 3.32529 -> 3.32795 in three
promoted steps; seven seats have submissions in flight. This archive is
the crown content plus the one warm gap our receipts price at ~+0.2%, so a
mid-band draw lands ~3.31-3.32 and an ordinary-good draw clears the crown.

## This seat's instrument note

`officialMetrics.per_prompt` publishes `effective_mean_draft_len` and
`mtp_seconds_per_token_mean` with a pinned serial denominator, so candidate
s/token is comparable across seats. Our floor=6 attribution above used
exactly that: schedule-clipped prompts moved +3.5% s/token while untouched
prompts stayed inside +/-1.2% — a mechanism signature against the noise
floor, not a verdict from a single number.

## Failure modes we accept

- Wash (3.30-3.32): the qL2/3 states fire rarely enough on the ranked mix
  that the extension is inside noise; the archive is still a fresh draw of
  crown-class content.
- Crown moves while we validate: the queue is loaded; if the crown is above
  3.32795 at resolution this is another rejected sample with full metrics.
- Median noise: even-8 sigma is 0.5-1.5% on this board; the extension is
  small on purpose — it cannot pollute (untimed warm, no schedule change,
  no kernel arithmetic change), it can only fail to matter.
## Provenance and method, stated plainly

Neither the island dead-work elimination, the embedding-dequant fold, the
combined rerank dispatch, nor the concat-write kernel is this seat's
invention; the frontier moved three times this evening and we adopted each
promoted increment through the platform's `yukon reset` tooling, verifying
the full exactness gates before every submit. What this seat contributes
here is (a) the qL={2,3} warm gap with three ranked receipts pricing it,
(b) the negative result that retired floor=6 on cheap-draft trees (our
3.24629 + Lieisyourlie's 3.30059 agree), and (c) the campaign's
distribution data: nine marker-only draws of the previous frontier content
(3.1908-3.25188, 1.9% spread) and the improved-best epsilon observation (a
draw 2.5e-6 ABOVE the then-crown was still rejected), which is why every
archive here aims at mechanism gaps rather than at note-only resamples of
freshly-promoted content.

## Warm list, exactly

```
before (crown 8b54ff1):  for qL in [1, 5, 4]   at kL=1024 and kL=1025
after  (this archive):   for qL in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]   at kL=1024 and kL=1025
```

No other schedule, kernel, or head change. The 128-block kL=1025 family
extension follows the crown's own structure (`sdpa_vector_2pass` bumps
blocks 64->128 when N>1024; scored decode walks N past 1024 during the
512-token windows).

author: huynhthaitu124
body: `users.avatar_url` has existed since Google sign-in, and it was effectively **write-once by Google**: anyone who signed up with an email had initials forever, and anyone whose Google picture was wrong had no way to change it. ## No migration, because the key is derivable One user has one avatar, so the storage key is `avatars/{userId}.{ext}`. Uploading again overwrites it — which is exactly what *change my avatar* means. A second column to remember a key that can be computed is a migration for nothing. The extension rides in the URL because it is what lets the read side answer with the right `Content-Type` without storing one, and without re-encoding every upload into one format — which would need an image library this service does not have. ## Two decisions worth reviewing **The path is relative** (`/api/v1/auth/profile/avatar/{id}.png`). The API is reached on whatever origin the app is served from; an absolute URL baked at upload time is wrong the moment those differ between environments. The web resolves it once at render, in `lib/auth/avatar-url.ts`, handling the absolute Google URLs already in the column. **The read is anonymous.** An `` sends no Authorization header, so an authenticated route means every avatar renders broken. What it exposes is a picture of a face, addressed by the user id of the person whose face it is, to anyone who already has that id — everyone who can see them in a meeting. ## Safety - **Magic bytes**, not just `Content-Type` — that header is chosen by the uploader, and trusting it is how an image endpoint becomes a file-serving one. - **2 MB**, stated twice: `RequestSizeLimit` refuses an oversized body before it is buffered; the service check is what answers in a sentence a person can read. - `Cache-Control: no-store` — the URL does not change when somebody replaces their picture, so a cached copy is how a new avatar stays invisible for a day. The blob store is `IVoiceSampleStorage`, named for the first thing that used it rather than what it holds. A second interface over the same bucket, S3 client and local fallback would be three files differing in a noun. ## Verification Builds clean. **228 tests pass; the 36 failures are pre-existing** — identical count on clean `development` (they need Docker). The `ProfileService` fixture needed the new constructor argument. Pairs with warptalk-web (upload control + URL resolution). **Not verified:** an actual upload round-trip — needs a running auth service and object storage. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: henrypark133
body:
## Summary

- **Read this first: this PR is *not* behavior-neutral, despite the slice name.** Commits 16–17 rewrite the shared claim-then-write protocol used by the **live `accept_inbound_message` ingress path** (real channel messages and trigger events). Two independent reviews found it behavior-preserving and, critically, the durable idempotency key **byte-identical** — had those bytes drifted, every existing idempotency record in production would have been orphaned and previously-accepted inbound messages would be re-accepted as new. Evidence is in Validation below. Review that hunk first.
- The rest is **slice 2a of R2 background subagents**: it lands every new type, state, and method background delivery will need, with **no production caller**, so a deployed binary can *read* two new persisted-enum variants a release before any binary *writes* them.
- Two persisted enums gain variants and neither has a tolerant reader: `LoopInput` (serialized whole into the durable run-queue document — one unparseable entry fails the entire run's queue) and `ProcessDependencyState` (journal rows). Readers-before-writers is the mitigation, and it is the reason this slice exists separately (design record D13).
- Also: deletes confirmed-dead scaffolding (`PostCapabilityStage::drain_settled`, whose doc promised a `LoopBackgroundChildPort` that existed nowhere in the repo), and corrects the canonical design record against live code — it contained two claims that were simply false.

## Review response (round 1-3)

Branch is now **34 commits,  27 files changed, 4101 insertions(+), 474 deletions(-)** — grown from the original +2,844 by review response, almost entirely tests plus one kernel simplification that was a net deletion.

Eleven review comments, all dispositioned. Three did not hold and were rejected with evidence in-thread rather than implemented.

**Security fix — the most consequential change here.** Child-agent output written as `MessageKind::System` reaches the LLM provider's **top-level `system` field** (`model_role_for_kind` → `ChatMessage::system` → `Role::System` → `convert_messages`). Unframed, a prompt-injected child could have written the parent's system prompt. Framing is now enforced by type: `FramedSubagentText`, sole constructor `frame()`, no `Deserialize`, no `From<String>`, no public field. Red-proven by reducing `frame` to the identity function.

**Kernel simplification.** `ProcessDependencyState::legal_predecessors()` makes the delivery lifecycle a total relation the kernel owns, and `expected` was dropped from the transition request entirely — the CAS now derives the precondition instead of trusting the caller's assertion. Only possible in this PR: `TransitionDependency` is a journaled command with zero producers today, so no instance exists in any deployment; after the next slice it becomes a durable-format change. It deleted a peek, a wildcard predecessor selector, a bespoke `matches!`, and four duplicated closed-state predicates.

**Design-record correction (D14).** §4.1 prescribed binding the delivered row to a queue entry "exactly as steering rows do." That cannot work — the row is `System`/`Finalized` and `ensure_user_accepted` admits only `User` rows in `Accepted`/`DeferredBusy`/`Queued`, so the status flip fails permanently, retained flips consume the 32-entry cap, and the run eventually returns `CapacityExhausted` for everything including human steering. The row is right; the doc was wrong. A crate-tier test now pins the refusal so the next slice meets it as a red test.

**Also:** `store.rs` split back to 443 lines (below the 504 this PR started from); caller-level drain tests through `InputStage::process`; a subagent-door race test; malformed-metadata fail-closed coverage; and every line-pinned citation this PR introduced converted to symbol names — three had already drifted within the branch.

## Change Type

- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactor
- [x] Documentation

## Linked Issue

Related: the R2 background-subagent roadmap in `docs/internal/reborn/subagent-spawn/README.md` §6.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo build` / `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → 0 errors
- [x] Relevant tests pass: `ironclaw_loop_contracts`, `ironclaw_agent_loop`, `ironclaw_processes`, `ironclaw_threads`, `ironclaw_turn_runner`, `ironclaw_architecture_tests`, plus `reborn_integration_subagent_await_edge` and `reborn_integration_tool_call`
- [x] `bash scripts/preflight-gates.sh` — **run locally and required**: CI's only architecture-suite invocation is `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests reborn`, a test-*name* filter, so the loop-port scan, the process-storage scan, the four `composition_*` gates and the threads name-collision gate report "0 tests" in PR CI. A green PR does not prove they ran.
- Manual testing: none — nothing in the new surface is reachable at runtime (see below).

**Two local results that are NOT regressions from this branch, characterised so a reviewer does not chase them:**
1. `reborn_integration_tool_call::current_tool_surface_overrides_stale_assistant_unavailable_claim` overflows its stack in a debug build on this machine. It is **pre-existing**: it reproduces identically at the merge-base `8fda17c59` in a clean detached worktree with none of this branch's changes present. It is not infinite recursion — it passes with `RUST_MIN_STACK=67108864`. The other 37 tests in that binary pass, including both deny-filter pins.
2. One `preflight-gates.sh` gate (`charter: ironclaw_assistant`) failed on a `libsql-ffi` build error (`BFD assertion fail` from the system assembler, missing `sqlite3.o`), not on an assertion. Re-run directly, that suite passes 297/297.

**Idempotency-key byte-identity evidence.** The key is `sha256` over `serialize_pretty(InboundIdempotencyKey)`. All seven declarations in its dependency closure (`InboundIdempotencyKey`, `ThreadScope`, `serialize_pretty`, `sha256_hex`, `idempotency_record_key`, `idempotency_record_path`, `InboundIdempotencyRecord`) plus their derive attributes were extracted at both `dc165435d` and `43ef0113f` and diffed: identical. `contract.rs` in that range is purely additive (25 insertions, 0 deletions), so `ThreadScope`'s wire shape cannot have drifted.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: No user-visible change. `builtin.spawn_subagent` remains deny-filtered, so no model can reach the new surface; the ingress refactor preserves existing message-acceptance behavior.

Risk areas:
- [x] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: `ProcessDependencyState` wire-spelling + historical-forms pins; the expected-state CAS matrix (idempotent replay vs illegal jump vs terminal-target refusal); `AwaitEdgeState` projection matrix; all seven historical `LoopInput` wire tags; both drain modes for the new input; `accept_subagent_result` across **both** production backends including two fault-injection cases.
- Reborn integration: `reborn_integration_subagent_await_edge` (the projection pin, unmodified) and `reborn_integration_tool_call` (the deny-filter pins, unmodified).
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: no model interaction changes.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no frontend surface.
- Backend or runtime: covered by the contract suites above; both thread backends exercised behind `Arc<dyn SessionThreadService>`.
- Live canary: Not applicable: the capability is deny-filtered.

What the tests prove: (1) every state the store can reach is also exitable, asserted end-to-end including that the deferred branch releases its reservation; (2) the new fields survive the projection against the blob shape production **actually** writes — an earlier revision was green only because its fixture seeded a shape production never produces, and the fixture now builds a real `AwaitedChildSetRecord`; (3) both acceptance

author: davidllano95
body:
Fix two live Trusted By regressions observed after P2.2.

1. Language switch + supported brands
- The existing language flow paused the marquee, removed duplicate Trusted sets, then rebuilt them.
- The rebuilt duplicate cards were cloned without the direct hover listeners that had been attached during the first marquee build, so supported-brand reveals could stop responding until a reload.
- The published Trusted runtime now freezes the existing animation in place during EN/ES changes and restores the exact current time/play state without rebuilding the sets. This preserves the active reveal and all existing hover listeners.

2. Occasional hover-induced carousel jump
- For a normal non-reveal card such as Mediacoustix, the only hover-specific behavior is the decorative moving sheen pseudo-element.
- On the continuously transformed carousel this can trigger a compositing hitch that looks like a brief backward jump, especially in WebKit/Safari.
- Disable that decorative sheen only for the live CMS Trusted carousel; supported-brand hover/reveal behavior remains unchanged.

Also bumps the published runtime cache version and adds regression coverage for the no-rebuild language path, animation currentTime preservation, responsive brand placement and stable hover paint.

After deploy, validate before the P2.2 Draft/Publish test:
- Open a supported-brand reveal, switch EN↔ES while it is open, and confirm it remains visible/interactive without reload.
- Let Mediacoustix enter the viewport and hover it several times; the marquee should continue smoothly without stepping backward.

author: udaychandra
body:
## What

The **second launch-free lane** peeled off `DispatchOperations`. The read-only room contract's backstop — capture each repo's HEAD + worktree fingerprint before a room turn, then after it stops detect any repo the chat changed and publish a `guardrail_triggered` — launches nothing and reserves nothing, so it doesn't belong in the dispatch launcher.

## Change

New **`RoomCommitGuard`** owns `captureRoomBaseline` / `guardRoomRun` and their helpers. It collaborates only with `RunStore`, `ProjectLoader`, the event sink, and the shell.

- `DispatchOperations` holds one `RoomCommitGuard`: `startRoomRun` calls it to capture the baseline, and the public `guardRoomRun` stays a thin delegator, so the server (`ServerStartCommand`) and the wake reactor are unchanged.
- The shared `ownsLiveAgent` predicate (used by the reservation lanes too) stays on `DispatchOperations`; the guard calls it (same package).
- Replaced the guard's hand-rolled SHA-256 with the tested `webauthn.Hashes.sha256` seam — DRY, and it removes a provably-unreachable `NoSuchAlgorithmException` branch.
- `DispatchOperations` sheds ~230 lines (now 1,852, down from 2,264 at the start of the split).

## Testing

- New `RoomCommitGuardTest` covers **every branch**: `parseInstant` garbage, the overlap-interval edges (future-start / live / finished-before / unknown-room-start), the best-effort baseline paths (no store, unreadable repo, shell failure), and the guard's defensive baseline handling (non-map / stateless / unreadable entries, unreserved-repo attribution).
- The existing `RoomWakeLaunchTest` guard suite continues to drive it through the delegator (head-moved, uncommitted-edit, attribution, foreign-node, concurrent, quiet-no-baseline).
- Meets the api.* **100% coverage gate with no exclude** (achieved honestly — inverting one condition removed a JaCoCo-uncreditable bare `continue`).
- `mvn clean verify` green.

## Next

The launching lanes — `InviteLauncher`, `RoomWakeLauncher`, `AdhocRunner`, `BuildDispatch` — over the `RunLauncher` + `LaunchAdmission` seams; then slim `SailOperations` and segment the `Operations` port.

## Summary

Same failure mode as #7. Regenerated both via `./scripts/generate-secrets.sh {dev,staging}` against the current cluster.
- While regenerating, found `generate-secrets.sh` silently drops the `argocd.argoproj.io/hook`/`sync-wave` annotations on the SealedSecret every time it runs (they'd been hand-added to the output file at some point, not written by the script — this run wiped them, which would have broken sync-wave ordering with `postgres-*.yaml` again). Fixed the script itself: those annotations belong on the SealedSecret resource's own `metadata`, not `spec.template.metadata` (what kubeseal actually carries input annotations into), so added a `yq` post-processing step to set them on the right object going forward.

author: eandalf-bigstack
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

- feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it

- Upgrade OpenStack Neutron from Antelope (22.2.1) to Caracal (24.2.2)
  - Move it out of the shared Antelope venv `/opt/openstack-antelope` (python 3.10) and into `/opt/openstack-caracal` (python 3.11), the venv Skyline, Keystone, Glance, Cinder, Nova and Placement already occupy
  - Repoint the 30 `/usr/bin/neutron-*` symlinks, plus `neutron-ovn-vpn-agent`, both `neutron-vpn-netns-wrapper` links and `/usr/bin/ironic-neutron-agent`, at the Caracal venv
  - Pin `networking-baremetal==6.3.1`, which the Caracal constraints file does not carry
  - Carry the OVN chassis-hostname patch forward: `antelope_patch/` becomes `caracal_patch/`, re-applied on top of 24.2.2
- **Take `neutron-vpnaas` from PyPI instead of the `bigstack-oss` fork.** 2024.1 ships the entire OVN VPNaaS backport the fork existed to carry, down to the same alembic heads — all that is left downstream is the libreswan 4.x adaptation, now a patch dir
- Escalate privsep through the Caracal venv's own helper — six sections, and neutron reaches the helper by a different route than Nova or Cinder did
- **Port `sdk_os.sh` off the `neutron` CLI, which python-neutronclient 11.0.0 removed.** Six live helpers behind `hex_cli`'s iaas network commands; and delete the `os_octavia_neutron_lbaas_*` family, which has no caller and no tables
- Drop `[octavia]` and `[service_auth]` from `neutron.conf` — neutron-lbaas leftovers nothing has read since Train
- Migrate configs: regenerate the thirteen `.sample` files and both vpnaas templates against 24.2.2 / 24.0.2, and record how the two vpnaas ones are generated
- Stop carrying `api-paste.ini`, `rootwrap.conf` and `rootwrap.filters` — the Neutron wheel installs all three under the venv prefix (154 lines out)
- Pin the OVN 24.03 / OVS 3.3 RPMs #1281 left floating, closing #1276's last open DoD item
- Ignore the new features Caracal introduces

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes

- Close #628

#### Special notes for your reviewer

> **This PR stacks on `jim.lin/feat/openstack-c-upgrade-nova` (#1314) and on `feat/ovn-24.03-caracal-hop` (#1281).** The base here is `develop`, so until those merge this PR's commit list also shows the Keystone, Glance, Cinder, Nova and OVN commits. `feat/ovn-24.03-caracal-hop` is a strict ancestor of this branch — `20c4098` is in this history unchanged — so #1281 can merge first and this branch will rebase cleanly. Only the eight below belong to this PR:
>
> - `build(neutron): pin the OVN 24.03 rpms the caracal hop resolved to`
> - `feat(neutron): upgrade neutron from openstack antelope to caracal`
> - `fix(neutron): escalate privsep through the caracal venv helper`
> - `refactor(neutron): drop the two config groups nothing reads`
> - `fix(sdk): reach neutron through the openstack cli, not the removed neutron one`
> - `feat(neutron): migrate the sample configs to neutron 24.2.2`
> - `refactor(neutron): install the configs the neutron wheels carry`
> - `docs(nova): correct which services still reach the antelope privsep helper`
>
> Review it after #1314 and #1281, or diff against `jim.lin/feat/openstack-c-upgrade-nova`.

**Why a second venv instead of a version bump in place.** Neutron 24.2.2 resolves `neutron-lib` 3.11.1, `os-ken` 2.8.2 and `ovsdbapp` 2.6.1. `openstack-heat` resolves `neutron-lib` out of the Antelope venv too, so installing Neutron 24 there would have lifted the library underneath Heat. Resolved against `os-caracal-pip-upper-constraints.txt` the two sets turn out to be disjoint — Neutron, neutron-vpnaas and networking-baremetal add **ten packages** to the Caracal venv (`logutils`, `ncclient`, `networking-baremetal`, `neutron`, `neutron-lib`, `neutron-vpnaas`, `os-ken`, `pecan`, `python-designateclient`, `setproctitle`) and change **no** version Skyline, Keystone, Glance, Cinder, Nova or Placement already holds. `os-vif`, `ovs`, `ovsdbapp` and `pyroute2` are already there at the Caracal constraints, courtesy of #1314.

Only two things outside `core/neutron` follow it. `core/ironic/ironic.mk` links `/usr/bin/ironic-neutron-agent`, and that binary comes out of `networking-baremetal`, so it follows **Neutron's** venv rather than Ironic's — the agent reports chassis state to `neutron-server` over RPC and imports nothing from Ironic, so a Caracal binary in front of an Antelope Ironic is fine, while a python 3.10 one in front of a Caracal `neutron-server` is not. And `core/nova/nova.mk`'s comment above `/usr/bin/privsep-helper` had Neutron on its list of reasons for existing; it no longer belongs there.

**`networking-baremetal` has to be pinned, not named bare.** The Caracal constraints file does not carry it — the Antelope one pins 6.1.1 — so an unqualified name resolves to whatever is newest on PyPI, which is 8.0.0. 6.3.1 is the last of the 6.3.x line that shipped with 2024.1.

**Two binaries disappear, and one of them had six live callers.** `python-neutronclient` 11.0.0 removed the `neutron` CLI and Neutron 24.0.0 removed `neutron-debug`, so `/usr/bin/neutron` and `/usr/bin/neutron-debug` are deliberately not recreated rather than left dangling. `core/sdk_sh/modules/sdk_os.sh` used the former in six helpers that `cli_iaas_network.cpp` drives — `os_neutron_network_opt_list`, `os_neutron_network_update`, `os_neutron_quota_list`, `os_neutron_quota_update`, `os_neutron_quota_show` and `os_set_router_ext_gateway`. `cli_iaas_network.cpp` itself is unchanged: the contract it shares with these helpers, *list the settable names, then apply `--<name> <value>`, with a `no-` prefix meaning no value*, survives the port intact.

Three of the mappings are not mechanical:

| was | now |
| --- | --- |
| `neutron quota-show --tenant-id X` | `openstack quota show --network X` |
| `neutron quota-update --tenant-id X --network Y` | `openstack quota set --force --networks Y X` |
| `neutron router-gateway-set --fixed-ip subnet_id=S,ip_address=I R N` | `openstack router set --external-gateway N --fixed-ip subnet=S,ip-address=I R` |

`--force` is now explicit because osc currently defaults to it for network quotas but warns the default will flip, and `neutron quota-update` always forced. And `no-dns-domain` needed an escape hatch: **`openstack network set --dns-domain ""` is a no-op** — osc drops empty string values before it builds the request — so clearing goes through `--extra-property type=str,name=dns_domain,value=`, the generic attribute setter, which sends what it is given.

Both list helpers stop scraping `--help`, because there is nothing left to filter on. `openstack quota set --help` mixes compute, volume and network options behind identical *"New value for the X quota"* descriptions, and `openstack network set` offers twenty-two options where `neutron net-update` offered six — most of them valueless flags (`--enable`, `--share`, `--external`) or structured arguments (`--tag`, `--extra-property`, `--provider-*`) that do not fit a "pick a type, type a value" prompt. The network list stays at the six that worked before; the quota list loses the six neutron-lbaas quotas Neutron has not had since Train, leaving **nine live names in place of fourteen mostly dead ones**. Two latent bugs got fixed on the way past: the value is quoted now (a description is the one value here that legitimately contains spaces, and unquoted it reached the CLI as several arguments), and valueless `--no-*` options take no argument at all rather than an empty one the old unquoted call got away with by accident.

**The fork is no longer needed, and that is the biggest simplification here.** `bigstack-oss/neutron-vpnaas` existed to carry the OVN VPNaaS backport — a Xena-era spec that only reached upstream in 2023.2 — onto a 2023.1 base. 2024.1 ships all of it: `neutron_vpnaas/services/vpn/ovn_agent.py`, the `ovn_ipsec` service and device drivers, the agent scheduler and both 2023.2 alembic migrations, whose heads (`22e0145ac80b`, `e50641731f1a`) are exactly the ones the fork alre

author: seijikohara
body:
Implements items 1 and 2 of #327. Both turned out to need a choice rather than a
new layout, so they ship together — same dock, same settings section, same
plumbing.

## Item 1 — hide the status icons

Per-indicator hide, reorder and "Reset dock" already shipped behind a long-press
on an indicator. Two things stood between that and the request:

- **Hiding the last visible indicator was refused**, with a comment borrowing the
  nav rationale ("the dock must keep at least one actionable id"). Status
  indicators are read-only, so that rationale does not transfer — and a dock with
  no status cluster is already a layout the design produces on its own, since the
  cluster yields below a derived width so the actionable nav keeps room. The
  floor is relaxed for **status only**; nav keeps its floor, and the stale
  comments that stated the old rule are corrected in the same change.
- **Nothing surfaced it.** There is now one switch in Settings → Screen, beside
  "Reset dock". Its state is *derived* from the visible set and its write flips
  the whole set, so the switch and the long-press cannot disagree — the hidden
  set stays the single home for that fact.

## Item 2 — Dock width: Compact / Extended

Not a resurrection: `HorizontalDock` already renders both layouts from one
composable, and the extended bar is what the 853 dp reference head unit shows
today. Only the *selection* changes, from a pure fit test to a preference the fit
test still bounds:

- **Extended** always fits — the weight-shared branch shrinks toward
  `FemtoDimens.MinTouchTarget` and never clips.
- **Compact** keeps the existing overflow fallback. It is not symmetric with
  Extended on purpose: forcing a pill onto a narrow dock clips the leading and
  trailing buttons below the tap-target floor.

**The default is unchanged.** The centred pill was a deliberate outcome of #274;
this adds the option without touching which one you get out of the box.

## A pre-existing mismatch this surfaced

The map-credit decision was fed the **viewport** width while the bar itself lays
out inside its own float margins, so the two disagreed in real width bands and
the OSM/OpenFreeMap credit could end up drawn under an extended bar. Both now
read the same width. The bug predates this change, but the change promotes that
computation to a named function whose entire justification is the attribution
invariant, so it had to hold.

## Verification

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `./gradlew spotlessCheck` | BUILD SUCCESSFUL |
| `./gradlew assembleDebug` | BUILD SUCCESSFUL |
| `./gradlew lint` | BUILD SUCCESSFUL, no new findings |
| `./gradlew test` | 871 tests, 0 failures |

Every new test was falsified by removing the matching production change and
confirming it goes red — including the width-mismatch regression case, which
fails against the old "measure the viewport" behaviour.

The settings drift guards (`SettingsFactsCompletenessTest`,
`SettingsSectionIdTest`) are satisfied rather than weakened: the new dock-width
setting carries its DataStore key, UI state, section row and diagnostics fact.

## Not verified here

`androidTest` does not run in CI, so the Compose UI tests touched here are not
gated by the merge. The layouts themselves are covered by JVM tests over the
pure fit/visibility functions. A pass on the TBox-Mock-Play AVD is still worth
doing before this reaches users — particularly the extended bar on an ultrawide
panel, where the nav cluster is capped and sits slightly left of screen centre.

author: zuizui0223
baadc0de
body:
Closes #148.

A witness now signs **D27 clause (a)'s preimage** — the 21-byte domain tag, the intent-preimage hash, the cell epoch, the issuer signature and its own NodeId, 157 bytes — and never `Intent::signing_preimage()`.

Committing to the **issuer signature** is what binds an attestation to one signed intent, and it is what makes an issuer signature and a witness attestation structurally non-interchangeable: a preimage cannot contain the signature over itself.

## The property that matters most

The submitter broadcasts to the full announced set **minus parties** and submits everything that returns, so it **never learns which subset was required**. That is not an optimisation — it is the property that makes the verifier-side draw safe, and it is the whole basis of D27's resolution of the two-keys confusion in `docs/07 §4`.

An explicit **refusal is distinguishable from a timeout** at the submitter: a witness that will not sign says so, and one that does not answer inside the 150 ms budget is simply not counted rather than treated as an error. Those are different facts and the submitter can tell them apart.

## Deliberately not done

**Gateway-side verification is untouched** — it still verifies the legacy issuer preimage at `crates/orrery_persistd/src/intent/mod.rs`. Switching that verifier to the new protocol helper is **#147's** job, and doing it here would have split one change across two PRs. This lands the peer half only.

## Evidence

All four `check.sh` lanes green in the implementing run: fmt 4s, clippy 75s (three feature sets), gates 175s, test 231s. Re-verified after rebase onto current `main`: fmt green, `orrery_protocol` 94 tests, `orrery_witness` 7 tests, `orrery_persistd` 197 tests all pass.

No `--features fdb` test added, so `scripts/fdb-tests.sh`'s floor stays at **345** — stated so it is not silently re-baselined.

## Reviewer note

Implemented by Codex (`gpt-5.6-sol`); its sandbox excludes `.git` from writes, so the commit, rebase and push were done by the coordinating session after review. It also edited `crates/orrery_protocol/` which was outside its registered lane — Codex agents get no pre-edit lane hook, so that went unwarned. No collision resulted (the contended files had already merged), but it is the expected failure mode of mixing providers on adjacent crates.

author: jamescrowley321
body:
## CONS-2.1 — Relocate the Python core into `/py`

First story of CONS-2 (the reorg + publishing epic). **Pure relocation** — no library behavior changes; the certified PyPI publishing pipeline is *re-pointed to run from `py/`* but not otherwise altered (tag-scheme change + `py-v3.11.1` seed are CONS-2.2). Python is now one peer of the polyglot layout with no root uv workspace.

### What moved (git mv — history preserved)
`src/ packages/ examples/ tools/{release_parsers,mutation_security} pyproject.toml uv.lock CHANGELOG.md README.md` → `py/`. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` returns to the repo root (git-level tool) with hook entries switched to `uv run --directory py`. `tools/spec_coverage_gate.py` stays at root (it's polyglot). A new root `README.md` describes the monorepo; `py/README.md` remains the PyPI long description.

### Reference updates (the real work)
- **Makefile**: two helpers — `UVPY = uv run --directory py` (package-internal paths) and `UVROOT = uv run --project py` (root-relative paths: conformance/, spec/, mkdocs, root `.env` globbing). Shared root `.env.*` reached as `../.env.*`; build/publish/ci-setup `cd` into `py/`.
- **CI**: `ci.yml` inline integration steps + every `hashFiles('uv.lock')` → `py/uv.lock`. `release.yml`: semantic-release action gets `directory: py`; the uv.lock-sync + version `sed` target `py/`; the fastapi version step `cd`s to `py/`. `release-fastapi`/`publish-dist`/`publish-prerelease` build/version/dist paths `py/`-prefixed; the prerelease git-install gets `#subdirectory=py`. `docs.yml` syncs `--directory py`, builds `--project py`.
- **conformance/Dockerfile{,.fastapi}**: `COPY py/pyproject.toml py/README.md py/src py/packages …` — the OIDF harness *behaviour* is unchanged (AC-CONS-2.5.2); only the build-context paths shift.
- **mkdocs** mkdocstrings `paths: [py/src]`; `spec_coverage_gate.py` python-runner cwd = `py`.
- Three test files that reach the **true** repo root (shared `.env.*` / `/spec`) use `parents[4]`; those referencing `py/`-internal paths stay `parents[3]`.
- `CLAUDE.md`: repository-layout note + command/path updates.

### Local verification (all green)
`make lint` · `make test-unit` (**1683 passed**, 13 pre-existing xfails) · `make test-fastapi` (**73 passed**) · `make spec-coverage` (**12/12/12**) · `uv build` → `py_identity_model-3.11.1` wheel+sdist · semantic-release config loads + `commit_parser` resolves from `py/` · all 15 workflows parse · `go build` + `cargo build` green.

**Release safety:** single `refactor(layout)` commit — `refactor` is not in `minor_tags`/`patch_tags`, so no PyPI release is cut.

Stacked base for CONS-2.2 (semantic-release re-point + `py-v{version}` tag scheme, seed **`py-v3.11.1`** — note: the plan's `py-v3.10.0` is stale; the repo is at 3.11.1). The full byte-for-byte publish-parity proof is CONS-2.5 (needs CI + release secrets).

> Merges require the `workflow` scope (touches `.github/workflows/`); land via SSH merge or the web UI, consistent with the CONS-1 stack.

author: jcnm
body:
## 📝 Pull Request Description

`GlowingButton` est le bouton principal du parcours d'inscription — « Continuer » puis « Créer mon compte » — posé sur **chacune des huit étapes** (`OnboardingFlowView.bottomBar`).

Son corps bascule sur `isLoading` : le `Text(title)` et son icône sont **remplacés** par un `ProgressView` seul. Or SwiftUI compose le nom accessible d'un `Button` à partir de son label — le CTA devenait donc un « bouton » **anonyme** au moment précis où l'utilisateur attend le réseau.

```swift
Button(action: { … }) {
    HStack(spacing: 8) {
        if isLoading {
            ProgressView()          // ← le label devient CECI, seul
        } else {
            Text(title)             // ← le nom accessible vient d'ICI
            if let icon { Image(systemName: icon) }
        }
    }
}
```

## 🎯 Type of Change

- [x] **🐛 Bug Fix**

## 🎨 Changes Made

### Les conséquences

**1. Le CTA devient anonyme au pire moment.** Sur l'étape `.recap`, l'action est `viewModel.register()` — la création de compte, l'appel le plus long du parcours, celui où l'utilisateur a le plus besoin d'être renseigné. VoiceOver n'annonçait plus ni ce que fait le bouton, ni qu'il travaille (WCAG 4.1.2 « Nom, rôle, valeur »).

Le bouton est bien `.disabled(!isEnabled || isLoading)`, donc le trait `.isNotEnabled` **est** annoncé — mais « bouton, non disponible » sans nom n'apprend rien : cela signale que quelque chose est bloqué, pas quoi ni pourquoi.

**2. La commande Voice Control cesse de correspondre.** « Appuyer sur Créer mon compte » ne matche plus rien dès que l'appel part. L'utilisateur croit que sa commande n'a pas été entendue et la répète, sans effet.

### Files Changed
- [x] **Frontend** iOS (`apps/ios`)
- [x] **Tests** : 1 suite neuve (4 assertions)
- [x] **Documentation** : analyse + plan + pointeur de tracking
- [x] **Configuration** : 4 entrées `pbxproj` pour le fichier de test neuf

### Key Changes

Deux modifiers additifs, **aucun changement de rendu** :

```swift
.accessibilityLabel(title)
.accessibilityValue(isLoading ? Self.loadingAccessibilityValue : "")
```

**Le découpage est délibéré, et c'est le cœur du correctif.** Le **NOM** reste le titre — stable, donc la commande Voice Control continue de matcher pendant tout l'appel — et l'attente est annoncée comme **VALEUR**, la place que la sémantique d'accessibilité Apple réserve à l'état d'un contrôle. Maquiller l'attente dans le nom (« Créer mon compte — chargement… ») aurait **re-cassé Voice Control** : c'est exactement le piège que ce partage évite.

L'annonce réutilise la clé **existante** `loading.message`, déjà traduite dans les 7 locales livrées (`ar`/`de`/`en`/`es`/`fr`/`it`/`pt-BR`), hissée en `static var loadingAccessibilityValue` — un seul point de vérité, et un point d'entrée testable hors hôte SwiftUI. **0 clé i18n neuve.**

## 🧪 Testing

### Test Coverage
- [x] **Unit Tests** : `OnboardingGlowingButtonAccessibilityTests` — 4 assertions

### Test Results

Aucune toolchain Swift sur Linux — **gate réel = CI iOS Tests**. Contrôles déterministes :

- **3 gardes de source** sur le contrat (label explicite ; attente en valeur et non dans le nom ; réutilisation de `loading.message`), **bornées au corps de `struct GlowingButton`** — une assertion ne peut donc pas être satisfaite par un modifier appartenant à `InteractiveProgressBar` ou `AnimatedStepBackground`, qui vivent dans le même fichier.
- **1 assertion de comportement réel** : `GlowingButton.loadingAccessibilityValue` doit résoudre vers du texte **non vide** et **différent de la clé brute** — ce qui rougirait si l'entrée catalogue disparaissait et laissait fuir « loading.message » dans l'annonce VoiceOver.
- Les 3 chaînes assertées ont été vérifiées **caractère par caractère** contre le source (`grep`), pour qu'aucune ne soit satisfaite par accident ni ratée sur une virgule.
- `loading.message` confirmée présente dans les 7 locales **avant** réutilisation.
- **Équilibre syntaxique** des 2 fichiers Swift au tokenizer : 0 / 0 / 0.

### Test Scenarios
- [x] **Happy Path** : le nom survit au basculement `isLoading`
- [x] **Edge Cases** : la clé brute ne peut pas fuir dans l'annonce

## 📊 Performance Impact

- [x] **No Impact** : deux modifiers additifs, aucun changement de rendu ni de hiérarchie de vues.

## 🔒 Security Considerations

- [x] **No Impact**

## 🌍 Internationalization

- [x] **No Impact** : **0 clé neuve**, réutilisation de `loading.message` déjà traduite dans les 7 locales.

## 📚 Documentation

- [x] **Code Comments** : commentaire expliquant *pourquoi* le nom et la valeur sont séparés (le piège Voice Control)

### Documentation Changes
- `docs/analyses/uiux/2026-08-21-iteration-233i-glowingbutton-loading-name.md` — analyse complète, dont la **raison motivée** d'avoir écarté le carry-over annoncé
- `docs/plans/uiux/2026-08-21-plan-iteration-233i-glowingbutton-loading-name.md` — plan + empreinte
- `docs/plans/uiux/branch-tracking.md` — pointeur autoritaire (marque 232i mergée #3241, ouvre 233i)

## 🔧 Configuration Changes

- [x] **Other** : 4 entrées `pbxproj` pour le fichier de test neuf

### Configuration Details
Même schéma qu'aux itérations 230i–232i : IDs SHA1-dérivés du nom du fichier, collision vérifiée = 0. Sans ces entrées la suite est **absente du bundle en local, donc verte par omission** — c'est la leçon de 230i, où un follow-up a dû patcher la main après merge.

## 🚀 Deployment Considerations

- [x] **No Changes**

## 📋 Checklist

### Code Quality
- [x] **Code Style** : idiome de projet
- [x] **Comments** : le POURQUOI (le piège Voice Control), pas le quoi

### Testing
- [x] **Tests Added** : 4 assertions, gardes bornées + comportement réel
- [x] **Coverage** : le contrat et sa résolution localisée

### Git
- [x] **Commit Messages** : narratif
- [x] **No Merge Conflicts**

## 🎯 Review Guidelines

Point à challenger : **le choix label/value**. On aurait pu écrire `accessibilityLabel(isLoading ? "\(title) — \(loading)" : title)`. Je l'ai écarté sciemment : le nom deviendrait instable et la commande Voice Control « Appuyer sur \<titre\> » cesserait à nouveau de correspondre pendant l'appel — c'est-à-dire qu'on remplacerait un défaut par le même défaut sous une autre forme. La valeur est la place correcte pour un état transitoire.

## 🎉 Additional Notes

### Sur le carry-over annoncé par 232i

232i désignait `unit.members` comme piste suivante. **Je l'ai écarté, et la raison mérite d'être enregistrée** : `memberCountDisplay` (SDK) rend **`"199+"`** — une *chaîne*, pas un entier — quand le serveur plafonne l'effectif pour ce lecteur. Un des quatre sites ne peut donc pas alimenter une règle plurielle depuis un nombre, et les trois autres sont gardés par `> 2` ou « conversation non-directe », ce qui masque le singulier fautif. Le lot demande une décision de conception (deux clés ? une clé « plafonnée » ?) que je ne peux pas valider sans simulateur — la forcer en aveugle aurait été le mauvais arbitrage.

### Future Considerations

1. **`InteractiveProgressBar`** — le voisin dans le même fichier, et le plus gros morceau restant. **Trois défauts constatés**, non traités ici délibérément :
   - chaque étape est un `Button` dont le label est un **`RoundedRectangle` nu** → VoiceOver énonce 8 « bouton » anonymes ;
   - la position dans le parcours n'est portée **que par la couleur et la hauteur** (5 pt vs 8 pt) ;
   - les cibles font **5 à 8 pt de haut**, contre 44 pt au minimum HIG.

   Le correctif propre suppose un arbitrage : `RegistrationStep` n'expose **aucun nom d'étape court** (`funHeader` est de la prose — « Un pseudo unique, comme toi »), et corriger la cible tactile change la hauteur de la barre, donc le rendu. À faire sur simulateur.
2. **`unit.members`** — cas plafonné `"199+"` à trancher (voir ci-dessus).
3. **Tap de ligne VoiceOver du picker de transfert** — carry-over 230i/231i/232i, simulateur.
4. **Frères du forward crown jamais audités** : `MessageMoreSheet` (504 l.), `MessageForwardService`, `MessageForwardDe

author: anmollp
body:
## Security issue
The repository is public, the `dev` environment currently has no protection rules, and both Terraform workflows previously accepted approval words from any issue commenter.

## Scope
- accept deploy and destroy decisions only from the repository owner
- paginate comments so public comment volume cannot hide the owner decision
- pass destroy confirmation through an environment variable instead of direct shell interpolation
- add disabled-by-default AI rollout inputs to deploy
- require both pinned numeric Secret Manager versions before AI enablement
- bind the selected AI values into the exact saved Terraform plan
- update operator documentation

## Validation
- both workflow YAML files parse successfully
- Prettier and `git diff --check` pass
- owner-decision matrix covers attacker-only approval, owner denial, owner reversal, and owner cancellation
- rollout matrix covers disabled/detached, disabled/attached, incomplete pairs, enabled/detached, and enabled/attached
- paginated owner filter executed successfully against the GitHub comments API

## Non-scope
No Terraform command, plan, apply, destroy, cloud mutation, secret value, feature enablement, quota change, or model spend is included.

author: tschm
body:
Migrates this repo from rhiza **v1.3.4 → v1.4.2**.

v1.4.0 stopped shipping the make layer, so this is not an ordinary `/rhiza:update`. The sync
deletes `Makefile`, `.rhiza/rhiza.mk` and `.rhiza/make.d/**` and leaves those deletions
*unstaged*, because they are no longer template-owned — and the settings they carried are
**not** rhiza-task's defaults. Recovering those settings is the point of this PR; the version
bump is the easy part.

## Sync

| | |
|---|---|
| Old ref → new | `v1.3.4` → `v1.4.2` (`31e1a11237419f746770c5339f8aa468fd1c0deb`) |
| Upstream files considered | 32 |
| Merged | 7 (`rhiza_benchmark`, `rhiza_book`, `rhiza_ci`, `rhiza_codeql`, `rhiza_marimo`, `rhiza_scorecard`, `rhiza_weekly`) |
| Deleted by the sync | 14 |
| Conflicts | **none** — no `.rej` files, nothing taken from upstream by hand |

All 12 paths that `stage_synced.py` reported as `left` were verified template-owned against
the **old lock's `files:` block** (scoped, so the `exclude:` block cannot produce a false
positive) before any deletion was staged. All 12 were the template's; there were **no
repo-owned casualties**, so nothing needed restoring.

## Settings recovered into `[tool.rhiza-task]`

Every assignment in `Makefile`, `.rhiza/make.d/*.mk` **and `.rhiza/rhiza.mk`** was grepped
rather than a fixed name list, then each name mapped onto a real `Config` field. Defaults were
read from `uvx rhiza-task@0.3.1 print …` — 0.3.1 being the pin in `rhiza_ci.yml@v1.4.2`, which
every gate step uses regardless of a consumer's own `RHIZA_TASK`.

**Three settings genuinely differed and are now set:**

| setting | was (make layer) | CLI 0.3.1 default | now | breaks if missing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `marimo-folder` | `book/marimo` — `Makefile` | `docs/notebooks` | `book/marimo` | marimo tasks silently skip; `book` builds without notebooks; **`deps` starts failing**, since the DEP004 exemption is only added when the marimo folder exists |
| `typechecker` | `both` — `python.mk` | `ty` | `both` | `mypy --strict` stops running entirely |
| `pytest-rhiza` | `pytest-rhiza==0.2.1` — `quality.mk` | `… @ git+…@v0.2.0` | `pytest-rhiza==0.2.1` | silent **downgrade** to v0.2.0, and a git checkout in place of a PyPI pin |

`typechecker = "both"` also gets *stricter*: the old shell `case` let mypy's exit status be the
one that counted, so a `ty` failure could pass. Both must now pass.

**Deliberately left unset** (recorded as comments in `pyproject.toml` so they don't get
re-added — naming a setting *replaces* the default rather than adding to it):

- `coverage-fail-under` — `python.mk` had `?= 90`; default is 90. No `[tool.coverage.report]`
  `fail-under` here to conflict with.
- `mkdocs-extra-packages` — `Makefile` had `--with 'mkdocstrings[python]'`, which is exactly
  the default list. **Removed rather than migrated:** restating it makes this the line someone
  edits to add a package, silently dropping `mkdocstrings[python]` from the book build. The
  `book` gate is the check on that.
- `ci-os-matrix` — `rhiza.mk` had `?= ["ubuntu-latest"]`; default is `ubuntu-latest`. This repo
  is single-OS, so **no matrix was narrowed**. (There is no `.rhiza/.env` here at all — it and
  `.rhiza/.gitignore` were already removed by hand in 8c9b9b5.)
- `license-ignore-packages` — `marimo.mk` appended `docutils`, which rhiza-task derives itself
  when marimo is in the registry (verified in `tasks/python.py`). Nothing else was ignored.
- `deptry-ignore` — `marimo.mk` appended `--ignore DEP004`; rhiza-task adds it when the marimo
  tasks are registered **and the folder exists** — which is what `marimo-folder` above makes true.
- `rhiza-checks` — the make layer accumulated five checks via `+=` across three fragments;
  rhiza-task derives that exact set from `layers = ["python"]`. Confirmed identical.
- `python-version` — `.python-version` (3.12) wins over any value here, by design.

**Dropped with no equivalent, nothing depends on them:** `PROJECT_NAME_EXTRA` and `LOG_LEVEL`
(cosmetic, from the template's own `custom-env.mk` example). No `PREK_EXTRA_CONFIG` and no
project-level `LICENSE_IGNORE_PACKAGES` existed.

## Exclude list

This repo started at `exclude: []` — it had never opted out of anything, so there were **no
dead clone-relative entries to convert and none to drop**. `gh variable list` returns `[]`:
neither `MUTATION_ENABLED` nor `FUZZING_ENABLED` is set, so both gates are provably unopted,
and the house set was applied in full (confirmed with @tschm before deleting, since all five
paths are still shipped at v1.4.2 and this removes 8 tracked files):

| entry | why | file removed |
|---|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/rhiza_mutation.yml` | unopted; gate is in the caller, so it never started | yes |
| `.github/workflows/rhiza_fuzzing.yml` | unopted; gate is *inside* the reusable workflow, so it ran on every PR only to skip | yes |
| `.github/CONFIG.md` | contributor-facing meta doc, this repo's own | yes |
| `.github/DISCUSSION_TEMPLATE` | ditto (3 files) | yes |
| `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` | ditto (2 files) | yes |

The sweep classified all five as `NEW+TRACKED` — none `UNTRACKED` (no file a previous sync had
restored invisibly) and none `DECIDE` (no pre-existing exclusion whose intent was "I own my
version of this"). **No exclusions were added for the retired make layer:** v1.4.2 ships no
`Makefile`, `.rhiza/rhiza.mk`, `.rhiza/make.d`, `.rhiza/.env` or `.rhiza/.gitignore` in any
bundle, so such entries would be dead weight.

⚠️ Because these workflows are deleted as well as excluded, **re-enabling mutation or fuzzing
means restoring the caller, not just setting the repository variable.** Both reasons are
recorded in `.rhiza/template.yml`.

## Makefile shim

The old `Makefile` was template-owned (it is in the old lock's `files:` block), so it was
**regenerated** with `uvx rhiza-task shim` rather than restored from `HEAD`. Its two
customisations — `MARIMO_FOLDER` and `MKDOCS_EXTRA_PACKAGES` — are exactly what moved into
`[tool.rhiza-task]`, so nothing was lost. The generated shim already pins
`RHIZA_TASK ?= rhiza-task@0.3.1`, **matching CI's pin exactly** — no local/CI divergence.

One repo-specific addition was needed. `book` and `license` are both task names *and* root
paths here (`book/` is a directory; `license` matches `LICENSE` on a case-insensitive
filesystem, so it shadows on macOS but not on the Linux runners). Make's up-to-date check won,
so `make book` printed ``make: `book' is up to date`` instead of building. `.PHONY` alone is
**not** enough — make skips the pattern-rule search for phony targets, which turns that into
``Nothing to be done for `book'`` — so both get an explicit recipe. Verified:

```
make -n test     ->  uvx rhiza-task@0.3.1 test
make -n book     ->  uvx rhiza-task@0.3.1 book
make -n license  ->  uvx rhiza-task@0.3.1 license
make -n fmt      ->  uvx rhiza-task@0.3.1 fmt
```

To be clear about why, since the tempting reason is wrong: **this is not a CI fix.** At v1.4.2
the reusable workflow runs `uvx "$RHIZA_TASK" fmt`, not `make`, and the `check-makefile-targets`
/ `update-readme-help` hooks are gated on `^Makefile$` and skip when it is absent. The shim is
here because `README.md` documents `make install` / `test` / `fmt` / `marimo` / `book`, and it
keeps that true instead of leaving a docs PR behind.

## Nothing left unstaged

Working tree is clean. No `--no-verify` commit was needed — every hook ran and passed on all
six commits, including `check-toml`, `validate-pyproject`, `check-rhiza-config`,
`check-python-version-consistency`, and (once the shim was back) `check-makefile-targets` and
`update-readme-help`, neither of which rewrote anything.

**No gates were run.** `/rhiza:quality` scores; this command syncs.

## Drift this PR deliberately leaves behind

- **`.rhiza/make.d/releasing.mk` is now orphaned.** It is repo-owned (never in any lock), so
  the sync correctly left it — but `rhiza.mk`'s glob `-include` was the only thing reaching it,
  and it depends on `FORGE_
