author: necipsunmaz
body:
Stacked on #26 (`fix/missing-endpoint-surface`), which is itself stacked on #25. Review those first.

Kept off #26 deliberately: this is a **behaviour change to two shipped methods**, not an addition,
and #26's story is "reach routes that were unreachable".

## The bug

`components.create` and `processes.create` sent a JSON:API envelope. Both handlers deserialize into
a plain struct, so every call failed on the missing required fields:

| Handler | Struct |
|---|---|
| `components/create_component.rs:13-20` | `CreateComponentBody { machine_id, fingerprint, name, metadata }` |
| `processes/create_process.rs:13-19` | `CreateProcessBody { machine_id, pid, metadata }` |

Only `metadata` carries `#[serde(default)]`. `machine_id`, `fingerprint`, `name` and `pid` do not,
so `{"data": {"type": …, "attributes": {…}}}` fails deserialization on all of them.

It reaches deserialization at all — rather than being turned away as an unsupported media type —
because axum's `Json` extractor accepts any `application/*+json`, and this SDK sends
`application/vnd.api+json`. So the field result is **422**, not 415. **Neither create has ever
worked from this SDK.**

## The responses were already right, and the asymmetry is real

`component_created_response` / `process_created_response` both wrap in `JsonApiDocument`, and
`_parse_component_resource` / `_parse_process_resource` read `data["id"]` and `attributes`
separately, which is correct. Only the request direction changes here.

The asymmetry is not an inconsistency to smooth over, and it cannot be inferred from a sibling
endpoint — `POST /machines` and `PATCH /machines/{id}` genuinely *do* take an envelope. Request
shape is a per-endpoint fact whose only reliable source is the handler's own body struct.

## Audited every request body, not just the two reported

| Endpoint | Shape | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /licenses/actions/validate-key` | bare `{key}` (`ValidateKeyBody`) | correct |
| `POST /licenses/{id}/actions/validate` | `{meta:{scope,skip_touch}}`, optional | correct |
| `POST /licenses/{id}/actions/check-out` | `{meta:{encrypt,ttl}}`, optional | correct |
| `POST /machines/{id}/actions/check-out` | `{meta:{encrypt,ttl}}`, optional | correct |
| `POST /machines/{id}/actions/generate-offline-proof` | `{meta:{dataset}}`, optional | correct |
| `POST /machines` | **enveloped** | correct |
| `PATCH /machines/{id}` | **enveloped** | correct |
| `POST /components` | **flat** | **was enveloped — fixed** |
| `POST /processes` | **flat** | **was enveloped — fixed** |

Components and processes were the only two wrong.

## Why the tests did not catch it, and what replaces them

The old assertions read `body["data"]["attributes"][…]` — so they passed against exactly the body
the server rejects. They pinned the bug rather than catching it, which is the root cause this whole
programme exists to eliminate, just on the axis nobody had measured.

The replacements assert **whole-body equality** against the server struct's field set, which cannot
pass with an extra wrapper, plus explicit `"data" not in body` guards.

**Verified rather than assumed:** reintroducing the envelope makes **11 tests fail**; removing it
again makes all 22 pass. The tests they replace passed in *both* states.

New `tests/test_request_wire_shapes.py` asserts the enveloped and flat cases side by side in one
table, so "normalize them to match" fails loudly instead of reading like a tidy-up. That is the same
class of defect, and the same hiding place, as the mirror-image response-decoding bug the fleet
measurement found in tamga-dotnet on these same two endpoints.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` / `mypy src/` (strict)
- [x] `uv run pytest --cov=tamga --cov-fail-under=80` — **470 passed**, coverage **97.46%** (up from
      97.32% on #26)
- [x] Envelope reintroduced → 11 failures; removed → 22 pass. The bug is genuinely caught now.
- [x] Public surface diffed against #26's head: **identical**. Behaviour-only, zero surface delta.
- [x] Every commit `fix:` — no `feat:`, no `!`, no `BREAKING CHANGE:`. PATCH.

author: dylanjkf
body:
Six consistency fixes from the audit's Part 6 (customer app).

## A11y
- **ConnectionsTab** — the clickable connection row opened the detail drawer on *click only*. Added `role="button"`, `tabIndex`, `aria-label`, and Enter/Space handling so keyboard users can open it.
- **ConnectionDetailDrawer** — a failed load fell through to `null` (a silently blank drawer). Added an `ErrorState` branch with retry.
- **Form-label association** — the Truck/Asset/Operator/file `<Select>`/`<Input>` in `MaintenanceSchedulesTab`, `ComplianceDocumentFormDialog`, and the dynamic `FormRunnerDialog` fields had visible `<Label>`s not programmatically tied to any control. Added `htmlFor`/`id` pairs (the dynamic form keys them off `field.id`), so a label click and a screen reader both reach the right control.
- **Colour-only status** — `ImpactPage`'s Headline signalled good/watch/critical by text colour alone; the two `StatTile` copies (ChecklistsPage, SyncDashboardTab) did the same. Added a tone word (Headline) and an alert icon + sr-only status word (StatTile) so meaning survives greyscale and screen readers.

## Permission consistency
- **WebhooksTab / CredentialsTab** — the "Test" buttons fire a real webhook delivery / a live authenticated credential call, but sat *outside* the `canManage` gate — a view-only user could trigger them. Now gated like Edit/Archive.
- **No-permission direct-URL behaviour** — Maintenance / Compliance / Documents / KnowledgeBase / Checklists / Forms / Customers fired their list query unconditionally and fell through to a red "Something went wrong" 403 panel for a user without the view permission. Each now gates the query (`enabled: canView`, including a new optional `enabled` on `usePaginatedList`) and early-returns the same clean **"No access" `EmptyState`** that `FuelPage`/`AuditLogPage` already use. (Early returns placed after all hooks — rules-of-hooks clean.)

## Tests
- `CredentialsTab.test.tsx` — the Test button is present for a manager, absent for a viewer.
- `CustomersPage.test.tsx` — the "No access" `EmptyState` renders and the list is **never fetched** without `customers:view`, and loads normally with it.

Customer suite **62 passing**; `tsc` + lint clean (warnings pre-existing).

Agent Implementation (`changeset/agent.py`) Three `@tool` functions demonstrating the scan → draft → publish workflow: - **`scan_site`**: Read-only site analysis (Woo products, SEO, landing pages). Returns structured placeholder data. **No approval required.** - **`draft_changeset`**: Creates a change set from scan results. No writes. **No approval required.** - **`publish_changeset`**: Publishes changes to live site. **Requires human approval via HumanInTheLoop.** ### 3. Proper HumanInTheLoop import path - Tool definitions present - MIT License detection - AWS credential placeholders **Result: 20/20 checks pass** ✅ ## Technical Details - **Strands SDK version**: `strands-agents>=1.0.0`, `strands-agents-tools>=0.2.0` (pinned per official docs) - **Import path**: `from strands.vended_interventions.hitl import HumanInTheLoop` (verified against official docs) - **Model provider**: Amazon Bedrock with Claude Sonnet 4 (default) - **Python syntax**: Validated with `py_compile` (all files pass) ## Success Criteria ✅ All requirements met: 1. ✅ Python 3.10+ project with pinned strands dependencies 2. ✅ MIT LICENSE (GitHub detectable) 3. ✅ README with setup, AWS placeholders, hackathon mention, architecture notes 4. ✅ .gitignore for venv/cache/env/dist 5. ✅ .env.example with AWS/Bedrock vars only 6. ✅ Package `changeset/` with stub tools, HITL config, local demo 7. ✅ Not a chatbot, not the letter-counter sample ## Testing ### Quick Verification (No Dependencies) ```bash # Clone and verify structure git clone && cd changeset # Run verification script python3 verify_setup.py # Result: 20/20 checks passed ✅ # Syntax validation python3 -m py_compile changeset/*.py # ✅ Pass ``` ### Full Install & Demo (Requires AWS Credentials) ```bash # Install and run python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate pip install -r requirements.txt python -m changeset.agent # Runs demo with HITL approval prompt ``` ## What's Not Included (By Design) - author: aubincorinaldiecooper-bit
body:
Audit findings 2, 3, 4 and 7. Findings 5 and 6 are decided (leave and watch; feedback is the loop). Finding 8 is a Railway setting — the tools here can set variables but not delete them, so `MINICPM_API_KEY`, `MINICPM_API_BASE_URL` and `MINICPM_MODEL` need removing on the dashboard.

## 2. Footage now ends with the session

Nothing in this system had ever deleted anything. Every upload, small copy, segment, clip and still stayed permanently — including for sessions that ended weeks ago and can never be opened again. Storage cost only grew, and someone's video sat on our disks with no way for them to take it back.

**A guest session lives in the browser tab** (the frontend half is CLIPITFRONTEND#16). When it closes, the token goes with it and nobody — including the uploader — can reach that video again. An hourly sweep acts on that: sessions quiet for a day have their footage removed. The idle window is generous on purpose — a tab left open overnight is still someone's session, and deleting their video out from under them is far worse than another day of storage.

**What is kept is deliberately narrow:** the question they asked, the moments found, and their thumbs up or down. That is the record of whether our reading of a video is any good, and it says nothing about the video itself.

**What goes:** the footage and everything derived from it — small copy, segments, clips, stills, scene notes and transcript. Those describe someone's video rather than our reading of it, and once the footage is gone they cannot be checked against anything anyway. Worth a second look if you disagree: the scene notes and transcript are the judgement call in this PR, and they are the most personal text we hold.

There is also **`DELETE /api/videos/:id`** now — the same removal, on request rather than on a timer. Previously a person could not remove their own video at all.

Two mechanics worth knowing. Storage keys are nulled rather than left pointing at deleted objects, because a key that resolves to nothing is a lie the rest of the system acts on — signing URLs for bytes that are not there. Chunk rows keep theirs, because deleting them would cascade to the matches and take the human verdicts with them; the flag on the video is what tells everything else the footage is gone.

## 3. A moment we found, discarded, and reported as absent

A match below `MIN_MATCH_CONFIDENCE` was dropped, logged for us, and the user told nothing matched — the one failure a person cannot tell apart from their video genuinely not containing the moment. Both paths now record what they discarded, and the API returns it as `uncertain[]` with timecodes, capped at five.

Deliberately **not** matches: on the request, not in `clip_matches`. They cannot be cut into clips, are not counted, are not ranked. The only thing they change is that an answer can say "I saw something at 04:12 I wasn't sure about" instead of claiming an absence.

## 4. The invented percentages are gone rather than hidden

Every video stage carried one — 5, 20, 60, 100 — and none was measured. The screen stopped showing them yesterday; the API kept publishing them, and the browser is not the only thing that reads this. Stage wording is now what a person would say. **The percentage on a search stays** — that one counts real chunks finished out of a real total.

## 7. Dead code with passing tests

`extractFrames` and `planFrameTimestamps`, from before the model could watch video, plus their tests. Also `'verification'` as a usage stage, which nothing ever wrote.

## Testing

`npx vitest run` — 230 passed, 15 files.

The retention path has no test, and that is worth flagging rather than glossing: it deletes things, and the pieces it uses (storage `remove`, the queries) are individually straightforward but the sweep itself is only exercised in production. If you want a guard before it runs anywhere real, the honest one is a dry-run mode that logs what it would delete.

author: mukeshpanchal27
body:
## What?

See #81898 — follow-up in the same spirit.

Removes the blank line separating `@param` and `@return` in PHP docblocks under `phpunit/` and `test/`. 9 files, 11 lines removed.

## Why?

The [WordPress PHP documentation standards](https://developer.wordpress.org/coding-standards/inline-documentation-standards/php/) run the tag block together, with no blank line between `@param` and `@return`:

```php
 * @param string $block_name Name for the test block.
 * @param array  $supports   Array defining block support configuration.
 *
 * @return WP_Block_Type The block type for the newly registered test block.
```

becomes:

```php
 * @param string $block_name Name for the test block.
 * @param array  $supports   Array defining block support configuration.
 * @return WP_Block_Type The block type for the newly registered test block.
```

#81898 made this same change in `packages/block-library/src/social-link/index.php`. This PR applies it to the test directories.

## How?

Removes the blank comment line(s) between the last `@param` and the following `@return`, within a single docblock. Nothing else is touched — the diff is a pure deletion with zero additions, and every removed line was a bare ` *`.

Affected files:

| File | Lines removed |
|---|---|
| `phpunit/block-supports/aria-label-test.php` | 1 |
| `phpunit/block-supports/block-visibility-test.php` | 1 |
| `phpunit/block-supports/border-test.php` | 1 |
| `phpunit/block-supports/custom-css-test.php` | 1 |
| `phpunit/block-supports/shadow-test.php` | 1 |
| `test/php/.../ValidBlockLibraryFunctionNameUnitTest.php` | 1 |
| `test/php/.../ForbiddenFunctionsAndClassesSniff.php` | 2 |
| `test/php/.../GuardedFunctionAndClassNamesSniff.php` | 1 |

body:
Add meson-cross-arm64.ini to enable cross-compiling OpenDCDiag from an x86-64 host to an aarch64 target via:

  meson setup builddir --cross-file meson-cross-arm64.ini --buildtype=release

The cross-file declares the aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc/g++/ar/strip/pkg-config toolchain and the aarch64 linux host_machine target. The baseline already shipped meson-cross-win32.ini, meson-darwin.ini, and meson-freebsd.ini; this adds the missing ARM64 counterpart.

Verified by inspection: meson parses the file (recognizes [binaries], [host_machine], [properties], [run_machine] sections) and attempts to locate the cross-compiler. On a host without aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc installed, meson setup fails with "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc'" — a missing-toolchain error, not a syntax defect in the .ini. File is byte-identical to the reference tree.

author: ilbzzz
body:
### CodeMender Security Fix

**Finding ID**: `4970ef5e-f49e-5947-bd85-83c5b696c79f`
**Title**: SQL Injection in Product Search Route
**Severity**: HIGH
**Vulnerability Type**: SQL Injection
**File Path**: `/app/juice-shop-local/routes/search.ts`
**Start Line**: 23

#### Analysis
The application takes untrusted search queries from `req.query.q` and directly embeds them into a raw SQL query. While the input length is restricted to 200 characters, there is no escaping of single quotes or other SQL meta-characters. An attacker can craft a malicious query parameter to manipulate the structure of the executed SQL statement. This can be used to perform a UNION-based SQL injection, exposing records from other database tables such as Users, bypassing intended data visibility controls.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Send a GET request to the search endpoint:
`/rest/products/search?q=apple')) UNION SELECT * FROM Users--`
This modifies the WHERE clause to perform a UNION SELECT and returns sensitive user records alongside products.

author: cwliao
body:
## Summary

Implements the first of two non-exclusive levers proposed in `docs/plans/2026-08-20-swarm-claude-grok-lane-timeout-recurrence-001.md`'s "Resolution" section, per the user's choice. A live 4-lane re-run showed every external-CLI lane (`claude`/`grok`/`agy`) hitting the worker-runtime ceiling on both attempts under 3-way concurrent dispatch, while `native_hermes` (in-process, no external CLI subprocess) finished comfortably -- not because external lanes are slower per step (heartbeat gaps were similar across all lanes), but because they need structurally more steps for equivalent work (subprocess spawn, cd/path handling, output polling).

## What changed

`create_swarm`'s `worker_max_runtime_seconds` param changes from a fixed `int` default (`DEFAULT_WORKER_MAX_RUNTIME_SECONDS=120`, applied uniformly) to `Optional[int]=None`, resolved per-worker:

1. An explicit per-worker `SwarmWorkerSpec.max_runtime_seconds` still wins outright (unchanged).
2. An explicit swarm-wide `worker_max_runtime_seconds` still applies uniformly to every lane (preserves existing caller behavior for anyone already passing it explicitly).
3. Only when genuinely unset does a new lane-aware default kick in: **120s for `native_hermes`** (unchanged), **600s** (new `DEFAULT_EXTERNAL_LANE_WORKER_MAX_RUNTIME_SECONDS`) for `claude`/`grok`/`agy`.

Both call sites that previously eagerly substituted the old fixed default *before* calling `create_swarm` (`hermes_cli/kanban.py`'s `hermes kanban swarm` CLI, `tools/kanban_tools.py`'s `kanban_swarm` tool) now pass `None` through when the caller doesn't specify a value -- otherwise neither caller could distinguish "unset" from "explicitly 120" by the time `create_swarm` saw it, and `create_swarm` had no way to apply the lane-aware default.

600s is a bounded, not empirically-optimal choice (same "bounded, not optimal" philosophy this codebase's own `DEFAULT_MAX_IN_PROGRESS` comment already documents for its own value) -- no successful external-lane run's actual step count was observed in the investigation to derive a tighter number from.

## Tests

- 4 new/updated tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_swarm.py`: lane-aware default resolution tested directly, the existing per-lane-runtime-persisted test updated for the new expected values, an explicit swarm-wide override still applying uniformly, and a per-worker override still beating both the swarm-wide value and the lane default.
- 185 tests pass across `test_kanban_swarm.py`, `test_kanban_cli.py`, and `test_tools/test_kanban_tools.py` (the three files touching this call chain).
- Manually verified end-to-end via `hermes kanban swarm` on this host with a throwaway 3-lane test swarm (tenant `lane-default-dryrun`): `native_hermes` persisted `max_runtime_seconds=120`, `claude`/`grok` persisted `600`, confirmed via direct `kanban.db` query.

## Test plan

- [ ] Cross-review before merge, per this repo's established practice for a change to live dispatcher-adjacent behavior on a single-instance production host with no staging environment
- [ ] After merge + redeploy, spot-check a real lane-bound swarm to confirm claude/grok now have headroom to actually complete instead of hitting the old 120s/300s ceiling

author: vincentkoc
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves CodeQL alert 88, where the workflow invariant test used a nested multiline regular expression to locate action-ledger publisher commands. Repetitive input could force excessive backtracking.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test now parses the workflow YAML and scans each job-step `run` script linearly. Publisher commands must use the repository's canonical standalone form: the exact `pnpm run --silent publish-action-events -- \` command line, one `--name value` argument per physical line, and a continuation or pipeline terminator.

This grammar is intentionally fail-closed. Shell wrappers and broader quoted or escaped shell syntax are not part of the workflow contract. Accepting them would turn a narrow repository invariant into a partial shell parser and reintroduce ambiguous command-boundary behavior. The seven owned publisher sites already use the canonical form.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Maintainers retain the seven-publisher producer-authentication invariant without a ReDoS-prone parser.

## OpenClaw Bay Impact

OpenClaw Bay is unaffected. This is a test-only workflow invariant change; no dashboard, queue, lifecycle, publication, telemetry, or data contract changes.

## Documentation Impact

No documentation changes are needed. The workflow and publisher authentication contract are unchanged.

## Real Behavior Proof

Claim: the linear scanner identifies all seven current action-ledger publishers, validates their expected producer values, and rejects syntax that could move or counterfeit the authenticated argument.

- Surface: parsed `.github/workflows/sweep.yml` job-step `run` scripts and the existing publisher-authentication invariant.
- Scenarios: all seven current publishers; comment, `echo`, and command-prefix pseudo-invocations; trailing spaces; doubled trailing backslashes; inline comments; multiline quotes; duplicate options; same-line options; missing values; shell control and redirection; nested publisher text; alternate npm separator layout; and unquoted `${IFS}` argument injection.
- Command/environment: Node 26.5.0 in the isolated full-clone worktree at exact signed head `f8b985eaa99aa65bd5da7a170109e63e2ccb4c3e`.
- Observed result: `node --test --test-name-pattern='every action-ledger publication authenticates' test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` passed 1/1. Changed-file `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` also passed.
- Limits: static repository workflow-contract proof. Hosted `pnpm check` and CodeQL are authoritative full gates.

## Evidence

- Exact signed head: `f8b985eaa99aa65bd5da7a170109e63e2ccb4c3e`.
- Focused invariant: passed 1/1.
- Changed-file formatting, lint, and diff checks: passed.
- Latest ClawSweeper rank-up move addressed: the doubled-trailing-backslash fixture proves a later producer flag cannot authenticate a terminated command.
- Latest actionable security finding addressed by replacing permissive continuation scanning with the canonical line grammar.
- Independent maintainer review approved the canonical fail-closed grammar as the best fix. The suggested wrapper and broad shell-value support were rejected because they are not owned workflow contracts and would expand this invariant into a shell parser.
- Local `pnpm run check` was not allowed to purge the shared full-clone dependency tree through the required worktree symlink. Exact-head hosted `pnpm check` is required before merge.

## Risk and Rollout

Test-only change: `+131/-11`; production `+0/-0`. No runtime, dependency, configuration, or rollout surface changes. Merge remains gated on exact-head hosted CI, CodeQL, and ClawSweeper review.

author: jaydenwearne-code
body:
Both published artifacts had drifted for nine increments. Docs and one dev-server fix; no engine or app behaviour changes.

## The anatomy sheet was the serious one

It is the **neuroanatomist review sheet** — the vehicle for the last standing correctness gate on the engine, per the closing line of CLAUDE.md. Measured before starting:

| | |
|---|---|
| Structures in the model | **528** |
| Rows in the sheet | 194 |
| Rows naming a structure **that no longer existed** | **39** |
| Model structures **absent** | **373** |
| Real coverage | **29%** |

A reviewer working from it would have checked under a third of the engine, plus thirty-nine things that are not in it.

Rebuilt against `src/model/structures.js`: **528/528 structures, 35 levels, 16 regions.** Verified end to end — 0 missing, 0 not-in-model, 0 duplicated, 27/27 hemisphere gates correct, tag balance clean.

**The `.fn` column is rewritten, not transcribed.** The model's `note` field is engineering prose — it references other structure ids inline, hedges, explains modelling decisions. Every row is now the finding in clinical English, finding first, discriminator in bold: the tongue deviates *towards* the weak side; wrist drop with the triceps *spared*; eversion weak but inversion *intact* (peroneal, not L5).

The verification caught a miss the eye would not: `thal_pulvinar` is hemisphere-gated and shipped without its marker. A gateless row looks perfectly plausible.

## The flow diagram couldn't have been run

Less visible, worse in kind. Its worked case entered `hemiparesis@left` — a finding **deleted** by the raw-observations refactor — and named `cst_cord` twice, split into `cst_cord_arm` / `cst_cord_leg` by the same change. Re-run with the current vocabulary the case still resolves to `left_cord_hemi` explaining all of it, so only the copy was wrong.

Every chip in the file is now validated against `FINDINGS`, the structure table and the site list: 19 chips, 0 unresolved.

Also: a new section covering the three layers built on top of localisation, a file map that had listed 8 modules and named `syndromes.js` as the whole of `src/data/`, and a coverage strip rebuilt from the model (the *"next: pathology · FND · UI"* chip is retired — all three shipped).

## Both URLs were dead

The links the README has told us for a month to "republish in place" returned *artifact not found*, and the account listed no artifacts. Both are republished as new artifacts and the README now carries the live URLs plus the lesson: publishing without `url` mints a new artifact, and a 404 means republish, not "merely unshared".

## Also

- `serve.mjs` sent `text/html` with **no charset**, so any fragment without its own `<meta charset>` rendered em-dashes as mojibake locally. The files were always valid UTF-8; only the preview lied. Called out in the README because the tempting "fix" is to mangle the content.
- Corrects "36 levels" to 35, and the assertion count in CLAUDE.md to 5,212.

**69 suites / 5,212 assertions green.**

author: rogerznts
body:
## O que muda

A regra do pipeline sai do shell e passa a viver em **`pipeline.yaml`**, lido pelo agente. Bash fica restrito ao que um agente não alcança: corrida de numeração no remoto, geração de derivados e uma verificação única que roda em hook.

**O diffstat assusta e vale explicar antes:** este PR remove ~12.000 linhas e adiciona ~2.500. Nada de comportamento foi perdido — o que saiu era shell reimplementando regra, e cada capacidade tem destino registrado. Dois documentos existem exatamente para provar isso, e são o melhor ponto de entrada para revisar:

- `docs/specs/archive/016-*/rule-migration-audit.md` — as 9 regras que moravam em `common.sh`, com origem e destino, uma a uma
- `docs/specs/archive/016-*/spec-015-requirements-check.md` — as 5 user stories da spec 015 conferidas cenário a cenário

## Por quê

O [ADR-0021](../blob/master/docs/architecture/adr/adr-0021-declarative-rule-minimal-shell.md) reverte a premissa da Etapa 2 do roadmap de autonomia — *"regra crítica deve ser codificada em Bash verificável"*.

Duas evidências a derrubaram:

**O ADR-0020 é o experimento que a mediu até o fim.** Treze voltas de correção na mesma família de defeitos, todas nascidas de ler YAML em shell. E o ponto de chegada dele recusa qualquer linha contendo `"`, `'`, `{`, `[`, `|` ou `>` — nesse ponto o formato deixou de ser YAML. A escolha do leitor determinou o que o formato pôde ser.

**A garantia que justificava tudo isso não se aplicou.** A spec 014 chegou ao `master` em `qa-gate`, sem archive, com o `check-ship-ready.sh` instalado, correto e nunca invocado. Daí a decisão 5 do ADR: *garantia sem chamador não conta como garantia*.

## Números

| | antes | depois |
|---|---:|---:|
| Shell (sem `payload-*`) | 7.912 | **2.563** |
| Scripts | 25 | **5** |
| Funções em `common.sh` | 39 | 15 |
| `selftest-*.sh` | 1.726 linhas | **0** |
| Scripts sem chamador | 2.607 linhas | **0** |

## O guardrail, que é a peça central

`.claude/hooks/guard-spec-merge.sh` intercepta `gh pr create`, `gh pr merge` e `git merge`, e chama `validate.sh ship-ready`. Ele bloqueou este próprio PR até a spec ser arquivada.

Ele passou por uma security review independente que encontrou **sete formas de contorná-lo** — newline separando comandos, prefixo de env, caminho absoluto, `command`, e três variantes de `<<`. Três aconteciam sem nenhuma intenção de burlar. A causa era usar blocklist; a postura foi invertida para fail-closed, e as sete estão fechadas com regressão.

## Verificação

- `validate.sh all` limpo, incluindo `tasks-sync` e 22 fixtures de contrato
- Instalação limpa simulada (só o que o `degit` leva): passa
- Equivalência conferida contra cada script antes de removê-lo: `check-ship-ready` (mesmas falhas, mesma ordem), `audit-docs-paths` (ambos limpos), `sync` (`AGENTS.md` byte a byte idêntico)
- Cinco baterias versionadas em `verification/`, incluindo teste de mutação 6/6

## Gate

**`WAIVED`, score 90.** `SECURITY: PASS` após três achados corrigidos e reverificados.

O waiver é do critério SC-001 — teto de 1.500 linhas de shell, contra 2.563 entregues. Ele foi estimado antes de qualquer script ser lido e demonstrou-se inatingível sem remover função: chegar lá exigiria apagar os comentários que registram armadilhas já pagas e eliminar ao menos duas capacidades. Motivo, aprovador e timestamp estão no `gate.yaml`.

## Também neste PR

- **Spec 014 fechada retroativamente** — estava no `master` em `qa-gate` desde 16/ago
- **Spec 015 interrompida** com o material aproveitável colhido em `harvest/`; a branch segue de pé, porque o histórico das treze voltas é a evidência que sustenta o ADR-0021
- **Roadmap de autonomia** emendado: Etapa 2 substituída, Etapa 4 refeita, Etapa 5 preservada como próxima

body:
While looking into OCaml 5.5 support: this branch of chooser.sh required OCaml 5.4 exactly and returned UNKNOWN otherwise, so the build failed. Select the grammar on the camlp5 version alone, and rename the file accordingly.

Tested every OCaml 5.x release that these camlp5 versions support, plus 4.14:

  camlp5 8.05.02  OCaml 4.14.4, 5.0.0, 5.1.1, 5.2.1, 5.3.0, 5.4.1, 5.5.0
  camlp5 8.04.00  OCaml 4.14.4, 5.0.0, 5.1.1, 5.2.1, 5.3.0, 5.4.1

In all thirteen combinations chooser.sh selects pa_j_8.04.00.ml, "HOLLIGHT_USE_MODULE=1 make" completes, and all four unit test binaries pass: UnitTests/basic_tests and UnitTests/printer_tests, native and bytecode, with the printer tests reporting 107/107. author: ryanmello07
body:
The Linux leg publishes three artifact types today -- the .deb, the install.sh
tarball, and the AppImage + .zsync -- while the linux repo has shipped
packaging/make-rpm.sh alongside them since the AppImage migration and its own
CI publishes four. v2026.8.15 is the visible gap: AppImage + .deb + tarball, no
.rpm. This closes it by calling the script the linux repo already owns, from
the container that already builds the .deb.

WHERE IT RUNS, AND WHY THERE

In the existing ROLE=daemon container (Dockerfile.daemon, Ubuntu 22.04) -- not
a new job, not a new image. make-rpm.sh is nfpm-based rather than rpmbuild/mock
based, and nfpm 2.47 is already installed there, pinned and checksum-verified,
for the .deb. The .deb, the tarball and the .rpm therefore come out of one
assemble_daemon_root() call on one `meson install --destdir` tree, so they
cannot ship different daemons -- which is the whole argument for not giving the
rpm a container of its own.

22.04 is also the correct image on SELinux grounds, independently of the glibc
floor that put the daemon there: semodule_package stamps the policy module with
the BUILD host's libsepol version and a target whose libsepol is OLDER refuses
it, so building on jammy's libsepol 3.3 for Fedora's 3.6+ is the safe
direction.

THREE NEW PACKAGES IN Dockerfile.daemon

checkpolicy + semodule-utils, because make-rpm.sh hard-dies without checkmodule
AND semodule_package: the Fedora-family package ships a compiled SELinux policy
module, and without it systemd runs urnetworkd in init_t, which is denied
/dev/net/tun. Note the family split -- semodule_package is in semodule-utils on
Debian/Ubuntu, where policycoreutils ships semodule/sestatus/setfiles and not
the packager, but in policycoreutils on Fedora. Guessing wrong looks identical
to not trying, so a `command -v` assertion in the image makes a base-image
regression fail at `docker build` rather than 40 minutes into an emulated run.

rpm itself, because without it make-rpm.sh skips its entire payload assertion
and degrades to a single warning -- and that assertion is what catches an rpm
containing no daemon. It is also what verify.sh's new section reads.

FAILURE TOLERANCE, AND WHY IT IS NOT IN run.sh

Every rpm step added here is warn-and-continue by default; UR_REQUIRE_RPM=true
makes it a gate, which is what the linux repo's own CI runs with.

run.sh's existing non-blocking `if build-linux.sh` idiom is NOT sufficient
tolerance on its own, and this is the one design point worth reviewing
carefully. Its uploads live INSIDE the `then` branch, so a single non-zero exit
anywhere in the Linux leg skips every Linux asset -- the SDK zip, the .deb, the
tarball and the AppImage included. A fatal rpm step would therefore convert
"the new package broke" into "the release shipped no Linux artifacts at all",
which is strictly worse than the status quo.

So the tolerance lives per-artifact inside build-arch.sh, and the .rpm is
invoked AFTER the .deb and the tarball are already on disk. A missing
make-rpm.sh is treated the same way rather than as a hard preflight failure:
it is the newest script in linux/packaging, so a checkout that legitimately
predates it must still produce the artifacts it does have. It is still
preflighted before the (possibly qemu-emulated) meson build, so the answer
arrives in seconds; it is simply a warning rather than an exit. The miss is
loud in three places -- build-arch.sh, build.sh, and the rpm named in run.sh's
builder_message -- and flipping the default is a one-word change in each
`${UR_REQUIRE_RPM:-false}`.

WHAT IS ASSERTED, AND WHAT IS NOT

verify.sh gains a deliberately thin section 5b: presence, `rpm -qp --info`, and
the arch tag read out of the package HEADER. make-rpm.sh already asserts the
payload, the scriptlets, the /lib-free layout and the unit's non-%config
status, and repeating those would only exercise the same tool twice. What it
cannot know is which leg produced the file, and the staging tree is
arch-specific -- an aarch64 rpm falling out of the amd64 leg is the real
failure mode at this level.

There is deliberately no install test. Nothing in this pipeline executes an rpm
scriptlet: `rpm -i` on Ubuntu would write an rpmdb onto a dpkg-owned filesystem
and still not run %post's `semodule -X 200 -i` or the systemd preset the way a
Fedora host does. A green build here is not a green install, and the comments
say so rather than letting a future reader assume otherwise.

NOT IN THIS CHANGE

The .flatpak. flatpak-builder needs bubblewrap user namespaces and a
system-wide `flatpak install` as root -- docker run privileges no leg here is
granted -- plus a live Flathub fetch mid-build for the ~2 GB GNOME runtime and
30-50 min per arch natively, which is multi-hour under qemu. The manifest also
passes no -Dsdk_arch, so an arm64 flatpak would link the amd64 SDK slice; that
is a change in the linux repo, not here. It belongs in its own change rather
than as a step that cannot run on the release host.

Anything snap-related. Nothing on this branch builds or uploads a .snap. The
residual `*.snap` in build-linux.sh's stale sweep is a deliberate cleanup of
pre-migration output trees and is left alone.

STALE SWEEPS

*.rpm is added to both sweeps (build-linux.sh and linux/build.sh). This is not
cosmetic: run.sh globs OUT_DIR to upload, so a stale rpm from a previous
version would sail into the new release. The .sha256/.asc sidecars make-rpm.sh
writes are already covered by the existing entries, and are deliberately not
uploaded, matching the .deb.

VERIFIED

Ubuntu 22.04 confirms the package split (semodule-utils owns
/usr/bin/semodule_package; policycoreutils does not ship it), Dockerfile.daemon
builds clean through the new assertion, checkmodule + semodule_package compile
the linux repo's real packaging/selinux/urnetwork.te into a 1741-byte
urnetwork.pp on libsepol 3.3, and `rpm -qp --qf %{ARCH}` returns x86_64 for an
nfpm-built rpm. build-arch.sh's new paths were exercised for all of: script
present, script absent (warn), script absent + UR_REQUIRE_RPM=true (fatal),
ROLE=gui (no rpm logic), unsupported ARCH, and script failing / succeeding
without an artifact under both knob values. run.sh parses under zsh 5.9; every
modified bash script passes `bash -n`.

No file is created or deleted, nothing is removed from any other platform's
path, and Windows, Android, Apple, extension, SDK, sn and proxy are untouched.

author: vallejoraul08-debug
body:
## Qué arregla

`GET /api/v1/swaps/search` cobra $0.001 por encontrar contrapartes y devolvía una sola, la dirección demo, con `completion_rate: 0.98` y `avg_time_seconds: 45` escritos a mano. El campo inventado era justo el de confiabilidad —lo que pesa un agente antes de bloquear fondos contra un extraño— y `available_amount`, también inventado, es el que decide si esa contraparte se ofrece.

Cierra #16.

## Cambios

- `completion_rate` y `swaps_completed` salen de `agent_history`. Sin historial: `null`, no un default. Si la base falla: `null` también.
- `avg_time_seconds` pasa a `null`: no se mide en ningún lado todavía.
- `available_amount` sale de `DEMO_COUNTERPARTY_AVAILABLE_USDC` y viaja con `available_amount_source: "estimate"`.
- La entrada sembrada va marcada `source: "demo"`, y la respuesta lleva `reputation_source` junto al `rate_source` que ya existía.
- La lectura de reputación va acotada: tope de espera (`REPUTATION_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS`, 1 s) y backoff tras un fallo (`REPUTATION_DB_RETRY_MS`, 30 s), mismo patrón que `ensureX402Initialized()`. Sin esto, `/swaps/search` —que antes no tocaba Postgres— pasaba a comerse los 5 s de `connectionTimeoutMillis` en cada búsqueda pagada con la base caída.

"Sin fila" no abre la ventana de backoff: es una respuesta legítima y rápida. Si se confundiera con un fallo, un agente sin historial dejaría sin reputación a todos los demás durante 30 s. Por eso el `race` usa un centinela y no `null`.

Las variables se validan antes de comparar: `Math.max(Number(basura), piso)` devuelve `NaN`, y `NaN` desactiva las dos guardas. Medido antes de corregirlo: con `REPUTATION_DB_RETRY_MS="medio minuto"`, 20 búsquedas con la base caída daban 20 conexiones.

## Cómo se probó

`apps/api/src/__tests__/swaps-search-counterparty.test.ts`, 11 casos offline: sin historial, con historial, base caída, base que no responde nunca, entorno inválido, y que el `rate` sigue viniendo de Horizon.

`npm run typecheck` 7/7 · `npm test` verde · `cargo test --workspace` 41 verdes.

## Qué queda fuera, a propósito

La contraparte demo sigue siendo la única que se devuelve: no hay emparejamiento contra `bazaar_intents`. Eso es trabajo aparte y da para su propio issue — este PR quita la información inventada, no construye el motor de búsqueda.

author: rashidannahas-b
body:
Four commits: the hostile QA run against MODULE: Onboarding and compliance, the fixes it pointed to, the agreed backlog item, and **wave B built**.

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `domains/qa-release/signals/2026-08-21-onboarding-compliance-limits.md` | the assumptions, the measurements, the exact number where each broke |
| `domains/qa-release/signals/2026-08-21-onboarding-compliance-fixes.md` | what to build, in this architecture |
| `domains/product-management/backlog/BL-0198-…md` | the agreed item |
| `server/`, `tests/` | wave B |

---

## What wave B fixes

Two places the module lost information **in silence**.

### 1. The sweep rings once

`runScan()` wrote one notification per obligation — about seven per employee.
`state/notifications.json` is **one feed shared by every audience** and it keeps
500 rows. So:

| Employees | Alerts | Surviving in the inbox | Lost for good |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60 | 423 | 423 | 0 |
| **72** | **507** | 500 | **7** |
| 200 | 1,403 | 500 | **903** |
| 1,000 | 7,003 | 500 | **6,503** |

The loss was permanent: `alerted{}` recorded every one as **sent**, so an
evicted alert never fired again. The same sweep also emptied the feed of every
payroll, invoice and employee message.

Raising the cap only moves the wall from 72 people to 720 and makes the bell
unreadable long before that. So the sweep now raises **one digest** naming the
count and the three most urgent, linking to the screen that still lists
everything. The **per-employee push is untouched** — that one is addressed to a
person about their own document.

The fine note travels **into** the digest, because it carries the rule that a
cap-only fine reads "up to" and never states the maximum as expected.

### 2. `alerted{}` is written only when the digest landed

Recording an alert nobody was shown is exactly how a deadline disappears. That
was the shape of the original fault.

### 3. `notify()` reports what the cap evicted

On the return, never on the stored row — a row records an event, not how full
the feed was. A future flood is now loud instead of silent.

### 4. The scan says what it did not read

The 160-record cap is **right** — that is already 64 KB of prompt against a
4,096-token answer. The fault was that a tenant holding 5,000 records had 4,840
dropped with no count, and the grounding then said *"160 records checked …
nothing outstanding"*: a clean bill on 3% of the evidence.

The result now carries `recordsTotal` and `recordsSkipped`, findings dropped at
their own cap are counted as `truncatedFindings`, and the words "nothing
outstanding" may appear **only** when every checkable record was read.
`skipped` keeps its old meaning — findings the guards dropped — because
overloading it would make one word mean two things.

---

## Measured

200 employees, **1,411 obligations → ONE inbox row**, nothing evicted, every
obligation recorded as alerted, a second sweep silent, and the payroll and
invoice notices still there afterwards.

`tests/compliance.mjs` and `tests/compliance-scan.mjs` pin all of it.

**One assertion changed shape rather than substance.** The failed-notification
test asserted `fired === 0 && failed >= 3`, counting per-obligation
notifications that no longer exist. It now asserts that no rows were written
and — as before — that nothing was recorded as alerted, which is the guarantee
it was always protecting.

---

## Not in this wave

Deliberately, each its own item: the 24.7 KB-per-employee board payload, the
one-value-contract refactor, the board's per-row guard, the import truncation,
the Arabic-Indic digits, and the nightly cursor that sweeps records past 160.

---

## Notes for the reviewer

- **The item is now BL-0198.** It has been renumbered seven times — 0150, 0166,
  0167, 0181, 0190, 0191 and 0196 were each taken by another session. `npm run
  backlog-id` answered **0198**, and it reads every live `claude/**` branch as
  well as `main`. The companion spec is **BL-0199**. A main-only reading would
  have said 0196, which `claude/hashim-email-greeting-repeat-5fxcmp` already
  holds; 0197 is held by `claude/email-signature-cc-visibility-0oustk`.
- Rebased onto `main` at `3d21e21`. The one conflict was in
  `domains/product-management/README.md`, where `main` had renumbered its own
  marketing-programme entries; `main`'s side was taken.
- `BL-0199` describes the same work that `main` shipped as **BL-0193**
  (`scripts/backlog-id.mjs`, `tests/backlog-ids.mjs`, `duplicate-ids.json`).
  It is left `status: specced` as instructed, but it looks superseded and
  product-management should close it rather than let a later session build it
  twice.
- Local: `tests/compliance.mjs`, `tests/compliance-scan.mjs`,
  `tests/backlog-ids.mjs`, `tests/claims.mjs`, `tests/spec-guard.mjs` and
  `tests/context-brief.mjs` all pass. `tests/ledger-shards.mjs` fails with
  "server did not start", confirmed to reproduce with these changes stashed —
  pre-existing and container-local.

author: kim-em
body:
This PR reads the `p ^ k`-power Frobenius on convolution points in matrix coordinates. Under the identification of the points of the general linear coordinate Hopf algebra with `GLₙ(A)`, it is the entrywise `p ^ k`-power map; that map preserves the matrix subgroup `hopfIdealPointsSubgroup` cut out by a Hopf ideal over `ℤ`, so it restricts to a group endomorphism `iterateFrobeniusHopfIdealPoints` of the points of any closed subgroup scheme of `GLₙ` defined over `ℤ`, with the zero and addition iteration laws; and the points fixed by that restriction are exactly the points of the same subgroup scheme valued in the Frobenius-fixed subring of `A`, both as an equality of subgroups of `GLₙ(A)` and as the isomorphism `frobeniusFixedHopfIdealPointsMulEquiv`. For `p` prime, `0 < k`, `A` an algebraic closure of `ZMod p` and `q = p ^ k` the last statement reads `G(𝔽_q) ≃* G(A)^F`. Nothing is asserted to be finite, and no algebraic closedness, field, or finite-type hypothesis is used.

The exact target is `ReductiveGroups/README.md`, Layer 9, the bullet "Points over an algebraically closed field as a group, functorially in the field, so that a field endomorphism induces a group endomorphism of the points", which names the `q`-power Frobenius as the first case a consumer asks for. `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Frobenius/Points.lean` and `FixedPoints.lean` already supply the coordinate-free half; this PR supplies the matrix half and, for the first time, the statement for a *closed subgroup scheme* rather than for `GLₙ` itself. After this PR that Layer 9 bullet needs the twisted case, the graph automorphism coming from the isomorphism theorem for pinned groups, before the pinned Chevalley--Demazure construction itself can be assembled.

The consumer milestone is `CFSGStatement/README.md` L1, whose untwisted Steinberg map is `Frob_q` on the points of a pinned Chevalley--Demazure group, together with L3, which sets `H_d = fixedSubgroup d.steinberg`. The dependency edge is that L0 builds `ValidLieTypeIndex.AmbientGroup` from the Layer 9 pinned group scheme, and the carrier it will use, `TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantToralGroupScheme`, is presented by a Hopf ideal in the coordinate Hopf algebra of `GLₙ` over `ℤ`; `iterateFrobeniusHopfIdealPoints` is then the endomorphism `d.steinberg` on the untwisted branches, and `frobeniusFixedHopfIdealPointsMulEquiv` identifies L3's `H_d` with the `𝔽_q`-points.

The construction reuses `TauCeti.Bialgebra.iterateFrobeniusPoints`, `range_frobeniusFixedInclusion`, `frobeniusFixedSubring_le_of_dvd`, `TauCeti.map_fixedSubgroup_eq`, and the general-linear point equivalence together with `map_mem_hopfIdealPointsSubgroup`, `mapHopfIdealPointsSubgroup` and its functoriality laws; no Mathlib source or external formalization is vendored. The naming and the shape of the fixed-point interface follow `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Frobenius/FixedPoints.lean`. The standard references are R. W. Carter, *Finite Groups of Lie Type: Conjugacy Classes and Complex Characters*, §1.17, and J. C. Jantzen, *Representations of Algebraic Groups*, I.9 and II.1, as credited in the module documentation.

Add `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Frobenius.lean` (96 lines), which describes the invertible matrices over any index type fixed by the entrywise Frobenius and needs no coordinate ring, and `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Frobenius/GeneralLinear.lean` (431 lines), which carries the coordinate and Hopf-ideal half; state injectivity of `TauCeti.GeneralLinear.mapHopfIdealPointsSubgroup` beside its identity and composition laws.

Roadmap: ReductiveGroups

Consumer roadmap: CFSGStatement

author: phaazoid
body:
The shove drop pointer was stamped from a single landing EVENT (kb_fell + kb_drop_from + landing_index) rather than derived from the trail's height profile. That was a second seam for a fact the geometry already held, and it went stale the moment #259's tumble learned to plummet: stamped on the ONE cell a flight ended on, it could not express a second drop at all.

THE RULE: a trail cell drops when the two surfaces meeting at the EDGE it was entered by are not at the same height. Nothing else is asked. BoardSpace.surface_height_at carries what makes it work -- a ramp's plane meets its neighbour's exactly at the shared edge -- so a slide reads continuous and draws nothing with no ramp special case anywhere. kb_fell is deleted.

Geometry, all of it dev-ruled in play across five review rounds:

- It starts falling AT THE EDGE. The flat arrow it lands on begins at the back of its tile, so a fold placed inward leaves that much shaft behind the foot -- worse on a slope, whose centre is half a level under its top edge.
- Both ends join the plane the neighbouring arrow is DRAWN in, not the surface under it. Those differ on a ramp: the layer lift rides the surface normal, and a ramp's normal leans, displacing its arrow ~0.031 cells downhill so its uphill edge retreats inside the cell. OverlayMirror._ribbon_point is that question; joining the surface put a seam on every ramp landing. The general form of that displacement is filed as #432.
- The layer's clearance is VERTICAL for this marker (lift_dir restored), so its top lands in the plane the flat arrows share. Lifting it along its own normal -- horizontal, for a vertical quad -- broke that join twice, and then needed no_depth_test to survive the resulting z-fight, which turned the pointer into an x-ray drawn through platforms the camera had panned behind. Standing clear of the cliff face is a separate, far smaller epsilon (WALL_CLEARANCE), and JOIN_OVERLAP keeps both folds an overlap rather than a butt joint.
- ONE quad, never a cross: the rig's pitch is authored at a fixed 40 degrees, so a vertical quad across the trail never goes edge-on -- its width bottoms out at 64% and no camera-facing pick is needed.

A void removal drops the full plummet. MovementComponent.VOID_PLUMMET_CELLS is one distance with two readers -- the pointer's length and the fall the sprite takes -- because a preview promising a shorter drop than playback shows is a Law #2 divergence. The fall is MovementComponent.plummet(), awaited by AttackAction.execute before die(), so a unit shoved into a hole falls a long way instead of vanishing at the lip. 3D-only by construction (a flat board has no height to fall through), a declared #292 asymmetry; play_session's hand-copied twin skips it. Depth and duration are Game-tab knobs beside Shove slide speed.

Also here, from the same review arc:
- Tumble-then-plummet (reversing #259's conservative "the tumble stops at a lip"): a downhill step below the ramp's base pays its fall and keeps whatever descent waits below.
- A void removal no longer counters: _counter_actor_live gained a lifecycle term, since a void kill leaves HP untouched.
- No flat arrowhead on a hole -- the pointer alone says where it went.

Verified: presentation 297/297, law 100/100, squad green, knob laws 45/45. Falsified against five mutants, each landing on its intended case: the single-landing gate, the centre-measured break, the cell-centre foot, the raw-surface join, and the dropped lift_dir. A sixth passed first time and was the finding -- the plummet case reached its assertion from an already-settled sprite, so it could not see the branch order it claimed to test.

Docs: verticality.md gains The drop pointer and marks both rulings this arc reversed; canon marker bumped to #432.

author: luongnv89
body:
Closes #72

## Summary

The database connector wrote the full MongoDB connection configuration — including `username` and `password` — into the log at info level (F-SEC-001). Two sites leaked: the connector's own configuration line, and `DataStorage`'s connect-failure path, which handed the whole `connConfig` to the run logger whose lines land under `src/server/logs/` and are served back over the API by `GET /api/logs/*/:fileName`. Both sites now name host, port and database only.

## Approach

Sanitize credentials at each log site (minimal/balanced): replace the serialized-config log with a host/port/dbname summary, and pass a redacted `{host, port, dbname}` payload to the run logger on connect failure. No shared utility, no API or behavior change beyond the log content.

## Decision Record

- **Root cause:** `db-connector.js` logged `JSON.stringify(connConfig)` verbatim, and `DataStorage.connect()`'s error branch passed `this.connConfig` as a logger argument; with run-scoped loggers writing files under `src/server/logs/`, any authenticated caller could read the credentials back through the logs endpoint.
- **Options considered:** Option 1 — remove the connection log lines entirely; Option 2 — introduce a shared credential-redaction utility; Option 3 — sanitize at each site, naming host, port and database only
- **Options rejected:** Option 1 — loses operationally useful diagnostics; Option 2 — over-engineered for two call sites
- **Selected option:** Option 3 — sanitize at each site
- **Residual risk:** none identified — stdout captured by external log drivers now carries only host/port/dbname
- **Effort profile:** light — fast path (pre-work Effort S); synthesis skipped, QA capped at 1 cycle
- **Reproduction:** `node --test test/db-connector-credential-redaction.test.js` confirmed red for the stated reason → regression test `test/db-connector-credential-redaction.test.js`

Analyzed at: `fix/72-stop-logging-the-database-password @ 663d376` (2026-08-21)

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/server/routes/db-connector.js` | Configuration line logs `host`, `port`, `dbname` only; username/password never logged |
| `src/core/communications/DataStorage.js` | Connect-failure error payload redacted from full `connConfig` to `{host, port, dbname}` |
| `test/db-connector-credential-redaction.test.js` | 3 regression tests: console line, run-logger payload, and a sweep asserting the canary password appears in no file under the server log directory |

## Test Results

- Unit tests: 302 passed of 303 in suite (299 pre-existing + 3 new); the only 3 failures are the pre-existing live-MongoDB e2e cases that also fail on `master` in this environment
- Integration tests: covered by the suite above
- E2e tests: unchanged (3 environment-dependent failures identical to baseline)
- Build: lint clean (0 errors)
- QA cycles: 1

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Evidence |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| The log line names host, port and database name only; username and password are absent or redacted | pass | `src/server/routes/db-connector.js:52-56`, `src/core/communications/DataStorage.js:49-56`; tests "the connector logs host, port and dbname only…" and "DataStorage connect-failure logging names host/port/dbname only" |
| A test asserts that a configured password never appears in any file under the server log directory | pass | Verified red: `node --test test/db-connector-credential-redaction.test.js` → fixed → test "a configured password never appears in any file under the server log directory" (canary sweep over `src/server/logs/`) |
| `npm test` passes at ≥ 285/286 (baseline-green holds) | pass | 299/303 pass; failure set identical to `master` baseline (3 live-MongoDB e2e cases), no regressions |

author: alessiobrillo
body:
Sparse market data (1-2 old sales) no longer pulls the valuation anchor to the median sale price.

The problem: valueAnchorEur = Math.max(baseMarketValueEur, market.medianSalePrice) used the full median regardless of dataDensity. A single 50k comparable sale anchored a mediocre domain to 25k instead of ~500.

The fix: Anchor is now interpolated: base + (median - base) * min(1, dataDensity * 3). With dense recent sales (50+) the full anchor applies; with sparse data the anchor stays close to base.

Tests added:
- modulates market anchor by dataDensity - sparse sales do not pull anchor to median (ADR-0002)
- applies full market anchor with dense recent sales (ADR-0055)

All CI checks pass locally (typecheck, lint, format, test, build, db:sync:check).

author: anvudevv
body:
## Why this is a separate PR

The commit belongs to #15 but landed after that PR was merged, so it never reached `dev`. Production is still serving the broken build:

```
$ git show origin/dev:package.json | grep '"config"'
"config": "^5.0.0"
```

## The failure

Every request to `tuvimienphi-backend.vercel.app` returns 500 — `/api/health/liveness` included, which touches nothing. The function dies on load, before Nest starts:

```
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module
  config@5.0.0/node_modules/config/lib/config.mjs
  from config@5.0.0/node_modules/config/lib/config.js not supported
Node.js process exited with exit status: 1
    at /opt/rust/nodejs.js:2:14275
    at /opt/rust/bytecode.js:2:1110
```

`config@5` ships a CommonJS entry whose only line is `require('./config.mjs')`, so it needs a runtime with `require(esm)` support. Vercel serves functions through its own loader — the `/opt/rust/*` frames — which does not have it. `5.0.1`, the newest release, carries the same line, so upgrading is not a way out.

Vercel reported those deployments **Ready** the whole time: the build succeeded, and nothing checks that the function can boot.

## The fix

`4.x` is plain CommonJS and reads the same files. Booting `dist/serverless.js` — the actual Vercel entry — with production environment variables:

```
before:  Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM] … exited with status 1
after:   config validated, app module loaded — past every config layer
```

An intermediate run was the useful signal: right after the downgrade the error became a Zod complaint about `db.tls` being undefined, which meant config had loaded and YAML had parsed, and only `production.yml` was missing because `NODE_ENV` was unset. With it set, the bundle runs clean.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm nx run-many -t lint typecheck test -p @org/backend` — 23 suites / 179 tests
- [ ] `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds (lockfile matches `package.json`)
- [ ] After merge, `https://tuvimienphi-backend.vercel.app/api/health/liveness` returns 200 instead of 500
- [ ] Deploy logs show no `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM`

## Note

`dev` is this project's production branch — the deployment alias is `tuvimienphi-backend-git-dev-…`. Merging here deploys straight to production.

Production also refuses to start now if any of these is unset, by design (from #15): `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_NAME`, `REDIS_HOST`, `REDIS_PORT`, `JWT_SECRET` (32+ chars), `SECRET_KEY`. `DATABASE_URL` and `REDIS_URL` cover the first seven.

Четыре из пяти шагов по укреплению базы (шаг 1 — булщит-чек хвоста — считается в фоне, добавлю отдельно).

## Шаг 2 — «доказано отгрузкой»
Сверил компании из разборов моделей с таможенной первичкой HS 8411. **11 компаний реально возили детали в РФ** и получили бейдж «📦 возил в РФ ×N» с экспортёром и годами в подсказке: Dongturbo (21 отгрузка 2023–2025), EthosEnergy, Ansaldo Energia, Sulzer Turbo Venlo, GTS, SAMIC, Henan GTET. Это высший ранг доверия — не «заявлено на сайте», а «прошло границу».

## Шаг 3 — аналитика откликов из Bitrix
По CRM-истории каждой компании считается отклик: ответы по существу (цена/КП/переписка/мотивированный отказ) против молчания. На карточке плашка «отвечают N/M · XX%», новая сортировка **«сначала реально отвечающие»** — наверх идут те, кто нам стабильно отвечает (IMMI 9/11, PeriParts 8/8, POWERGEN 6/6), а не просто те, кому много писали. 124 компании с историей.

## Шаг 4 — сквозная дедупликация
Вторая склейка вдобавок к доменной — по имени до скобки, для дублей на разных доменах или без сайта. 14 групп слито (Thomassen Energy, Goodwin Steel Castings, GF Precicast, GTS S.p.A. …), база 1226 → 1212. Родовые слова исключены из ключа, поэтому Solar Turbines ≠ Solar Manufacturing и Allied International ≠ Allied Power Group остаются раздельными.

## Шаг 5 — след доказательности на карточке
Под компанией — видимая строка «почему она здесь», а не только цифра балла: 📦 возил в РФ ×N, 👁 скептик видел на сайте (с дословной цитатой в подсказке), 💬 отвечали нам ×N. Сорсер видит основание доверия сразу.

## Проверки
Playwright: все вкладки, новая сортировка и плашки, 20 компаний с таможенным следом / 100 с цитатой / 89 с откликом, дедуп без ложных склеек (аудит 202 групп, 0 потерянных вердиктов), 0 JS-ошибок, 0 оверфлоу.

## Theme

Achromatic palette. Two colours survive: `chart-3` for live/heartbeat status and `destructive` for errors. Page is off-white, cards are pure white — separation without dark blocks. `--radius` 0.625rem → 1rem.

The `dark` class was hardcoded on `<html>`, so the light palette defined in `globals.css` was unreachable. That is unpinned now, which means **the dashboard, `/claim` and `/not-found` render light for the first time and still need a visual pass**. Sign-in was checked and already reads correctly.

## Bugs fixed along the way

- **Content shipped at `opacity: 0`.** Motion writes its `initial` state into the SSR markup, so the hero and all 24 scroll reveals were invisible until hydration finished, and permanently invisible without JS. Entrance animation is CSS now; the hero is a server component with no JS on the critical path.
- **Torn grids.** Per-cell reveal stagger left a grid's bottom row mid-animation while the top row was settled. Reveals are per section now.
- **Hydration mismatch.** Branching on `useReducedMotion()` during render desynchronised server and client trees. Status dots are CSS.
- **Wrong numbers without JS.** `NumberTicker` ships `0` and counts up after hydration, so the 90s stale threshold displayed as `0s` on failure. Plain text now.
- **Beam pulse never animated vertically.** `animated-beam` pinned its gradient's `y1`/`y2` to `0%`. It also drew a single bezier; now orthogonal with rounded corners.
- **Fonts.** `font-sans` resolved to Tailwind's default stack rather than Geist, and the base layer forced Source Code Pro onto every heading, so `h3`s clashed with the headlines.

## Verified

Typecheck clean · production build passes · `/` still statically prerendered · no console errors · no horizontal overflow at 390px · reduced-motion path renders every section visible.

## Not addressed

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` was generated when `motion` was installed — pnpm 11 no longer reads `pnpm.overrides` from `package.json`, so the `hono@4.12.25` pin **is currently ignored**. Pre-existing, and a dependency-policy call, so left alone and uncommitted.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` were written by Next 16's own tooling during builds; left uncommitted.

The discovery sweep picked this one up and filed it under `capabilities`. I think that's the wrong shelf, and I'd rather say why than just move it.

It adds no new ability to the agent. The four tools it registers reach the same SaaS APIs the agent could already reach — the difference is where the credential lives. author: jakub-przepiora
body:
**Feature B** of the step-parameters / typed-outputs plan — **stacked on #251 (Feature A)**, so this PR targets the Feature A branch to keep the diff scoped to B. Merge #251 first, then this.

Lets a process-template step define what the operator must **record** at execution, and the MES records it — completing the original user request (the "typed operator output, incl. QC photo" half).

## What & why
Steps only captured checklists (boolean sign-offs) before. This adds typed data capture: a step defines outputs (`key` + label + **value type**), the operator fills them at the workstation, required ones **block completion**.

Value types: `text`, `number` (with unit), `boolean`, `select` (options), `date`, **`picture`** (e.g. `output_qcpic`).

## How (mirrors the checklist sub-system end to end)
- **Schema:** `template_step_outputs` (definition) + `batch_step_output_values` (recorded), both soft-deletable with a partial-unique live index. Picture values store the file on the **private disk** (path/mime/size), mirror of `batch_step_documents`.
- **Gate:** `BatchStep::pendingRequiredOutputs()` + a guard in `BatchService::completeStep`, alongside the checklist / document / read-confirmation guards.
- **Admin authoring:** `TemplateStepOutputController` + `StoreTemplateStepOutputRequest`; an **Outputs** sub-list in the step editor.
- **Operator recording (the new upload path):** `recordOutput` records a scalar or **sanitises + stores a photo** (`ImageSanitizer` → private disk), served by `showOutputFile` (line-scoped, safe inline mime + `nosniff`). Operator UI: a `StepOutputs` block — input per type + photo capture (`capture="environment"`).
- **Read API:** `GET /api/v1/work-orders/{id}/step-outputs` + an authenticated picture endpoint, for ERP/reporting.

## Tests
11 feature tests: admin authoring (+ select-needs-options, operator-forbidden), the **completion gate**, operator records a number, **uploads a picture that serves back**, **non-image rejected** by the sanitiser, idempotent overwrite (soft-delete prior), IDOR (output from another template), and the **read API**. i18n en/pl parity (+13).

**Verification:** backend `php artisan test` — **2481 passed**; vitest — 35; `npm run build` — OK; Pint clean on changed files.

Additive / non-breaking.

author: bamseynet
body:
## Summary
- `orch up --name <name>` (and the `bootstrap` alias) sets AND persists this install's tmux session name to `_orch/state/session-name`, so a later `orch` invocation in a clean environment (different shell, cron, after a reboot — no `SESSION_NAME` exported) still resolves to the same session.
- Precedence, centralized in `lib.sh` so every entrypoint that sources it (status/spawn/send/tail/attach/hud/remote-control/...) picks it up automatically: `--name` flag > `SESSION_NAME` env (unchanged, still does not persist) > persisted name from a prior `--name` > `orch-<hash>` default (#81).
- Name validation: only letters/digits/`_`/`-` accepted (tmux treats `:` and `.` as target separators — a name with either would silently target the wrong pane). Invalid names are rejected loudly; nothing is persisted. Validation applies to whatever `SESSION_NAME` actually resolves to (env, persisted file, or the hash default), not just a fresh `--name` value — but see the non-fatal note below.
- Session existence is checked via an **exact** `tmux list-sessions` match, never a bare `tmux has-session -t <name>` — real tmux matches an unambiguous *prefix* (confirmed against tmux 3.4: `-t bill` hits a live `billing` session), which would otherwise let `--name` silently hijack a different install's session.
- Renaming via `--name` is **refused** if the session under the currently-resolved old name (env, persisted, or hash default — not just the persisted file) is still alive, rather than silently orphaning it. A successful rename also stops the now-stale heartbeat/watchdog loops (they each resolve `SESSION_NAME` once, at their own process startup) so they relaunch bound to the new name.
- The #81 collision-guard WARNING (two installs sharing one session name) now mentions `--name`.
- Ownership tracking for that guard lives **on the tmux session itself** (a session-scoped `@orch_owner` option), not in either install's own state dir — see Decisions below.

Closes #92

## Decisions
1. **`_orch/state/session-name`, not `_orch/config.json`.** The persisted name is per-install/per-machine identity data keyed to a resolved `ORCH_ROOT`. `config.json` is committed to git and shared across every clone/branch/worker of this toolkit — an operator's session name has no business round-tripping through commits, and keeping it out of `config.json` also sidesteps any conflict with the concurrent #90/#91 workers' `config.json` edits. **Correction from an earlier revision of this PR body:** I originally justified this by claiming state is "never wiped in bulk" — that's false; `install.sh:46` does `rm -rf _orch/state` on every run. Fixed properly instead of re-litigating the decision: `install.sh` now backs up and restores `session-name` across a re-install, the same explicit treatment it already gives `config.json`.
2. **Rename-while-running: refuse.** Warn-and-proceed would orphan a live, possibly in-progress session under a name nothing resolves to any more — recoverable (the tmux session still exists) but easy to lose track of. Refusing costs the operator one extra step (stop the old session, or keep working under the old name) in exchange for never silently stranding a running session.
3. **Ownership marker on the tmux session, not in state.** The original implementation stored the owning `ORCH_ROOT` in a file under *this install's own* `_orch/state/`. That's provably unreachable for the collision case it exists to catch: two different `ORCH_ROOT`s have two entirely separate state directories, so an install adopting a *different* install's session always finds its own owner-file empty and takes the silent "reusing" path — the WARNING could only ever fire by hand-seeding a file production code never writes there. Moved to a session-scoped `@orch_owner` tmux option instead, which every install resolving the same session name can actually see.
4. **A source-time hard exit in `lib.sh` on an invalid session name was too blunt.** `lib.sh` is sourced unconditionally by every entrypoint. An unconditional `exit 1` there took out `orch help` and `orch down` too, with no recovery short of hand-editing state on disk. `lib.sh` now records the problem (`$SESSION_NAME_ERROR`) without exiting; entrypoints that actually interpolate `SESSION_NAME` into a tmux target (`ask.sh`, `bootstrap.sh`, `clean.sh`, `heartbeat.sh`, `send.sh`, `send-remote-control.sh`, `spawn.sh`, `watchdog.sh`, and `orch`'s own `tail`/`attach`) call `require_valid_session_name` explicitly, right before they need it. `--name` also clears a stale error from the value it's replacing, so `SESSION_NAME='a:b' orch up --name good` isn't blocked by the invalid value it's fixing.

## Known limitations (acceptable, noted for the record)
- **One-time ownership-migration blind spot.** A session created by an install running the *old* code (or any session that predates this PR) carries no `@orch_owner` option. The first install that touches such a session under the new code silently claims it (same as a freshly-created session would) — there's no way to distinguish "genuinely unowned" from "owned by an old-code install that never recorded it." This is a one-time transitional gap, not a standing hole: every session created going forward is tagged at creation time.
- **`_orch/send-remote-control.sh:59`** still does a bare `tmux has-session -t "${target%%:*}"` and is exposed to the same prefix-hijack pattern described above (reproduced live during review). Left out of this PR's scope — filed as a follow-up to promote `session_exists()` from `bootstrap.sh` into `lib.sh` so every entrypoint gets the exact-match check, not just the ones touched here.

## Test plan
- `tests/issue92_named_persistent_sessions.bats`: 27 hermetic tests (mocked, *stateful* tmux stub — tracks sessions and `@orch_owner`/`set-option`/`show-options` across separate invocations, and fakes tmux's real prefix-match behavior for `has-session` so a regression is actually caught, not just a same-shaped-but-blind stub). Covers: precedence tiers, name validation, `--name` persisting so a later clean-environment invocation resolves to it, invalid-name rejection, the hijack-by-prefix case (verified live against real tmux 3.4, and verified the regression test actually kills the mutant by reverting the fix and confirming the test fails, then restoring it), the collision guard exercised end-to-end with two *real* `bootstrap.sh` invocations (not hand-seeded state), the rename guard against the resolved name (hash-default and env-pinned cases), the heartbeat/watchdog restart-on-rename, `--name` beating an invalid pre-existing `SESSION_NAME`, and `orch help`/`orch down` surviving a corrupt persisted-name file.
- Updated `tests/hygiene_session_namespace.bats` (pre-#92) and `tests/compaction_bootstrap_rehydrate.bats` to match the new ownership mechanism and the has-session→list-sessions change; updated `tests/install.bats` with a session-name-survives-reinstall regression test.
- Ran every pre-existing test file that touches `SESSION_NAME`/`bootstrap.sh`/`orch help`/the eight scripts this PR modifies individually — all green, no regressions.
- `shellcheck` clean on the whole toolkit.
- CI's full `bats tests/` suite (428 tests) green on every push. Local full-suite run deferred to CI throughout, per slot serialization with the other two live workers on shared files.

author: gjovanov
body:
# Phase C — the hardware caps probe runs in a child process

A capability probe is untrusted third-party code by definition: it calls into vendor drivers and, through them, GPU firmware. In-process, a fault anywhere in that stack took `roomlerd` down — and the service manager restarted it straight back into the same probe. The result was a crash-**loop**, not a degraded-but-running agent.

## The fault, reproduced today

The WSL sibling ships `/usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so.1` as a stub with no usable driver, which puts nvenc in the **loaded-but-unusable** state: the `dlopen` succeeds, so no presence check catches it, and the failure path from `cuInit(0)` segfaults. On the installed rc.421, as root, from the same entry point the daemon uses at startup:

```
[hevc_nvenc @ 0x…] dl_fn->cuda_dl->cuInit(0) failed
timeout: the monitored command dumped core
exit=139                                    ← 128+11, SIGSEGV
```

Hosts with *no* libcuda (mars/zeus/jupiter) take the clean dlopen-failed branch, which is why this stayed latent — the probe only runs at startup, so a long-lived agent never re-enters it and the crash surfaces at the next restart, looking like whatever shipped most recently.

## The change

`encode::caps::detect()` spawns `roomlerd caps-probe` (hidden subcommand), reads one `ROOMLER_CAPS_JSON:{…}` line, and treats **any** failure as *every hardware codec is unavailable*: non-zero exit, killed by a signal, 60 s timeout, unspawnable, or unparseable output all land in the same place. The fallback is `compute_caps(false)` — everything computable without a driver call.

`compute_caps` gained one `run_hw_probes` parameter; each probe region is already a `cfg`'d block or an `if`, so gating them is a one-line change each and there is one source of truth for the non-probe tail (files, audio, RPC verbs, chroma).

The agent stays a working agent when the probe dies — files, input, RPC and software codecs survive. It just stops claiming hardware it has no evidence for, which is the honest reading and costs a session nothing worse than a software encode. That retires the whole class rather than the one CUDA symptom: any future driver that faults, hangs, or calls `exit()` now costs this host its HW advertisement and nothing more.

## Verification

- **Fault injection, end to end**: with the child aborting, the parent logged `caps probe: the probe child DIED … status=exit code: 0xc0000409`, fell back to no-HW caps, and **exited 0**. Before this, that same fault was the daemon's own death.
- **Healthy path**: `roomlerd caps` → `caps probe: child reported elapsed_ms=509`, one marked JSON line parsed.
- 689 tests pass on Windows / clippy clean on `overlay-l3,ssh-server`; Linux surface green.
- Two new unit tests: a failed probe still yields usable caps and advertises no hardware or DC transport; the marked JSON line round-trips.

## Details worth knowing

- The child sets `ROOMLER_AGENT_CAPS_CHILD=1`; `detect()` seeing it computes in-process — a recursion guard, so nothing can spawn endlessly.
- stdout is **marker-parsed, not last-line-parsed**. The daemon logs to stdout, so "the last line" would have been a log line on the very first run — this is not hypothetical, it's visible in the child's output.
- The child's **stderr is inherited on purpose**: its per-codec probe lines are the record of *which* codec died, and they belong in the daemon log directly above the verdict.
- 60 s timeout is a backstop against a *hung* driver, not a performance budget — and even at the ceiling it beats the in-process behaviour it replaces, which was to hang forever.
- `caps-probe` doesn't take the single-instance lock, so a probe child never fights the running daemon for it.

Closes the `[MEDIUM] [2026-08-20]` Known Issue. Field proof is the WSL sibling surviving repeated restarts, which follows the release.
