author: kasper0406
body:
#ai-generated

`chlo.erf` and `chlo.top_k` already survive StableHLO serialization as `stablehlo.composite` ops. `chlo.erfc` does not, so it is expanded into its full polynomial approximation at export time and downstream StableHLO consumers cannot recognize it.

Where I hit this: exporting `jax.nn.gelu(x, approximate=False)` (which lowers through `chlo.erfc`) via `jax.export`. With jax/jaxlib 0.9.1:

```
jax.scipy.special.erf          -> stablehlo.composite "chlo.erf" ...
jax.nn.gelu(approximate=False) -> ~90 StableHLO ops, no composite
```

This blocks the stablehlo-coreml converter (and any other StableHLO consumer) from recognizing erfc; it has to match a ~70-op polynomial or give up.

This adds `chlo::ErfcOp` to `ChloPreserveHighLevelOpsPass` and `ChloRecomposeOpsPass` so erfc round-trips exactly like erf. `chlo.erfc` has no attributes, so the existing builtin-attribute passthrough covers it.

On the compile path there is no `MHLO_ErfcOp`, so the recomposed `chlo.erfc` is left alone by `ChloLegalizeToHighLevelMhloPass` and expanded by `ChloLegalizeToStablehloPass` — the same path `chlo.acosh`/`cosh`/`sinh` already take. Verified end to end: the composite lowers to the identical 92-op expansion produced today, so numerics are unchanged.

Tests: erfc cases added to `chlo_preserve_high_level_ops.mlir` and `chlo_recompose_ops.mlir`, mirroring the existing erf cases. The preserve test's `preserve | recompose | diff` RUN line covers the round trip.

author: batonogov
body:
Closes #151, closes #150 — the issues asked to decide them together, and they resolve each other.

## The duplicate (#151)

`triggerMRPipeline` POSTed unconditionally, so every execution produced another merge request pipeline for the same MR: on a retried job, on a manual re-run, and on any later run against an existing MR.

Now the MR's pipelines are listed first, and the run skips when one already exists for the head commit:

```
Merge request pipeline already exists for commit abc123de (ID: 7, status: running): https://gitlab.example.com/p/-/pipelines/7
Skipping pipeline creation; pass --force-pipeline to create another.
```

The skip is printed rather than silent, so the behaviour is visible in the job log. `--force-pipeline` is the escape hatch the issue asked for, and it is rejected without `--trigger-pipeline` rather than quietly doing nothing.

**Failing to list is not a reason to skip.** If the list call errors, the tool warns and creates a pipeline anyway — a duplicate is a better outcome than checks that silently did not run. Same when the head SHA is unknown: nothing to compare against, so it creates.

## The update question (#150)

**Decision: trigger on update too**, and the README now says so instead of "after the MR is created".

Taken alone, the case against was that later pushes to a branch with an open MR already produce a merge request pipeline of their own, making an explicit trigger redundant or duplicated. But that argument is exactly what the per-commit check above answers: if GitLab already made one for this commit, this run skips. What is left is the case the flag exists for — a branch that moved and whose checks are worth re-running — with the redundancy removed rather than traded for a missing pipeline.

Keeping the flag's meaning simple ("this run should have a pipeline") also matches how it reads at a call site in `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

## Implementation note

`handleMR` returns the `*MergeRequest` instead of just its IID, because the comparison needs the head SHA. It is already in the create response and in the list response `getExistingMR` reads, so no extra API call — `MergeRequest` and `Pipeline` just gained their `sha` fields.

Adding a branch to `run()` pushed it to complexity 16, over the configured 15; the two `--create-only`/`--update-mr` precondition guards moved into `checkMRMode`, which they already formed in practice.

## Tests

- `TestTriggerMRPipelineDeduplicates` — six cases counting actual POSTs: existing pipeline for the head commit (0 created), existing pipeline for an older commit (1), no pipelines (1), `--force-pipeline` (1), unknown head SHA (1), unreadable pipeline list (1).
- `TestRunTriggersPipelineOnUpdate` — through `run()` with `--update-mr --trigger-pipeline`, asserting the update path does trigger.
- `TestForcePipelineRequiresTriggerPipeline`, `TestShortSHA`.

The existing `triggerMRPipeline` tests from #143 pass unchanged apart from taking an MR instead of an IID — and, since their MRs carry no SHA, they double as coverage for the unknown-SHA fallback.

```
$ go test -race ./...
ok  	gitlab-auto-mr	1.854s
$ golangci-lint run
0 issues.
```

Conflicts with #161 in `triggerMRPipeline`; mechanical to resolve whichever lands second.

author: zhiyuan-zhang0206
body:
## Summary

PR1 of the execute_code-out-of-thread work (issue #184, user ruling 2026-08-21): one disposable subprocess per exec call, cold start accepted, no warm pool. **Infrastructure only — the exec node is NOT wired to it yet; production behavior is unchanged.** PR2 switches the node over behind a flag, PR3 deletes the worker-thread machinery.

## File tree

```
agent/
├── exec_child.py                    (A)  ★ new subprocess entry (`python -m agent.exec_child`):
│                                          one exec per process. Reads the request envelope
│                                          (code + timeout + typed state snapshot), establishes
│                                          identity with owns_loop=True (ava.self lifecycle calls
│                                          keep working — their inbound INSERTs go over ava.DB),
│                                          init_subprocess_logger (file sink only, no stderr
│                                          pollution) + best-effort event-pipeline sink, loads
│                                          plugins, rebuilds the dynamic AgentState and injects the
│                                          snapshot into ava.state / ava.state_update, runs the
│                                          code under sdk_telemetry.recording(), writes the result
│                                          envelope (outcome kind / lifecycle class name / crash
│                                          traceback / plugin delta / security findings) on every
│                                          exit path. SIGINT→KeyboardInterrupt,
│                                          SIGTERM→TimeoutError; daemon watchdog os._exit(124)s
│                                          past timeout+grace+margin so an orphaned child cannot
│                                          run long; per-agent config overlay re-applied
│                                          framework-scope so SDK calls see the agent's settings.
└── graph/
    ├── _exec_protocol.py            (A)  request/result envelopes: cat-able JSON, 0600, under
    │                                     $AVA_HOME/run/exec/<agent_id>/, stale-file pruning,
    │                                     size ceiling, version/kinds validation. The state
    │                                     snapshot (parent→child) and the plugin delta
    │                                     (child→parent) ride as base64-wrapped
    │                                     JsonPlusSerializer.dumps_typed blobs (the checkpoint
    │                                     allowlist) — langchain messages round-trip
    │                                     field-for-field (AIMessage usage_metadata included;
    │                                     convert_to_messages loses it) and set deltas keep their
    │                                     type. Shared KILL_GRACE_S.
    ├── _exec_result.py              (A)  the _ExecResult sum type + _construct_exec_result
    │                                     moved out of _exec.py (the machinery needs them without
    │                                     importing _exec.py — that would close an import cycle).
    │                                     ExecChildError carries a child crash's type/message/
    │                                     traceback parent-side; _ExecCrashed gains an optional
    │                                     full_traceback for the child path.
    ├── _exec_subprocess.py          (A)  ★ parent machinery: spawn with start_new_session (own
    │                                     process group), stderr=STDOUT merged pipe into the
    │                                     existing StreamingTextIO (read1 — chunks stream live
    │                                     instead of waiting for EOF), 50ms poll loop with
    │                                     cancel=SIGINT / timeout=SIGTERM / 2s grace /
    │                                     SIGKILL(-pgid), child-env builder re-emitting the
    │                                     per-agent config overlay the boot popped. Maps the
    │                                     envelope onto the sum type with the parent's
    │                                     cancel/timeout flags authoritative.
    └── _exec.py                      (M)  re-exports the moved sum type (tests keep their
                                          imports); _ExecCrashed dispatch prefers the
                                          child-formatted traceback when present.
shared/
└── paths.py                          (M)  exec_run_dir() — $AVA_HOME/run/exec.
scripts/
├── lint_no_os_environ.py            (M)  allowlist entries for the two child-env handoff files
└── lint_clock_lattice.py            (M)  KILL_GRACE_S registered as an independent clock
tests/agent/
├── test_exec_protocol.py            (A)  envelope round-trips + exact typed round-trips
│                                          (AIMessage usage_metadata / ToolMessage kwargs / set),
│                                          perms 0600, pruning, ceiling, version/kind validation
├── test_exec_child.py               (A)  real child spawns: done / crash / lifecycle envelopes,
│                                          snapshot injection + plugin delta round-trip,
│                                          SIGTERM→timed_out envelope, watchdog exit 124
└── test_exec_subprocess.py          (A)  real child through the machinery: done / merged stream
                                           order / crash with child traceback / os._exit /
                                           timeout / cancel / incremental chunk streaming /
                                           state snapshot / process-group kill of a grandchild
```

## Data flow

```
exec node (future PR2)                parent machinery                    child (one per exec)
──────────────────────                ────────────────                    ────────────────────
write_request(0600 json+blob)  ──►   spawn [sys.executable -m            read request
                                     agent.exec_child],                      establish(owns_loop=True)
                                     start_new_session, stderr=STDOUT        import ava + plugins
                                     pipe ──► StreamingTextIO ──►            rebuild AgentState,
                                             50ms chunk publish              ava.state = snapshot
cancel_event ──► SIGINT ────────────►                                   ──► KeyboardInterrupt
deadline     ──► SIGTERM ───────────►   2s grace ──► SIGKILL(-pgid)      ──► TimeoutError
                                     read result envelope ◄─────────────  write result envelope
_ExecResult sum type (parent flags authoritative)                        exit 0
```

Invariants: the parent's cancel/timeout flags win over the child's envelope kind (except lifecycle, reconstructed from the class name); a missing envelope is never rounded up to a clean done; the child never writes framework logs to the output pipe (file sink only); request/result files are 0600 and cleaned up by the parent.

## Not tested

- End-to-end through the exec node — no wiring in this PR (PR2, flag-gated).
- Windows: the machinery is POSIX-first (process groups, signals); Windows paths are best-effort (terminate/kill, no process-group kill, signals skipped in the child). CI runs POSIX.
- Large-history snapshot latency (MB-scale serialization cost) — only small snapshots measured.
- MCP session semantics across exec calls (each exec child dials the daemon fresh) — to be verified at PR2.
- sdk_call event parity through the child's event-pipeline sink in a live cluster — unit-verified only.

author: michaelrobert9
body:
Ownership race: OrgForm decided access before auth finished restoring on a fresh page load (exactly what happens when a sport site links a user to the main site), so `user` was briefly undefined, ownerUserId !== undefined was true, and it set denied=true — and never reset it once auth loaded. The real owner saw "no access". Now it waits for auth (loading flag) before judging access and resets the denied flag each run. Ownership is read fresh every time.

Performance: every page was bundled up front (~851KB JS). Routes below the landing page are now React.lazy code-split — each page's JS loads only when visited. Main bundle drops to ~673KB (175KB gzip); Admin/OrgForm/Account/etc. are separate on-demand chunks. Suspense fallback added.

author: apollo600
body:
Fixes #1581.

## What was happening

`codegraph index` on a repo containing a deeply nested C/C++ file died with `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` — the whole CLI process, no error message, no index. Reproduced on `llvm/llvm-project`, where the trigger is `clang/test/Parser/parser_overflow.c` (16,384 nested braces).

`ccpp::visit_node` recurses once per parse-tree level, ~450 bytes of native stack per level. Parse workers were created as `new Worker(scriptPath)`, i.e. on Node's default **4MB** worker stack (the main thread gets 8MB), so ~9k levels exhausted it. The overflow is a SIGSEGV inside the addon and never becomes a JS exception, so:

- `parse-worker.ts`'s catch (which handles `memory access out of bounds` / `out of memory` by exiting so the pool respawns) never runs;
- `tryKernelExtractRaw`'s per-file `defer:` fallback to the wasm extractor never runs;
- and because worker threads share the process, the whole `codegraph` process dies.

Measured, with the worker stack as the only variable:

| worker stack | 4MB | 6MB | 8MB | 16MB | 64MB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parser_overflow.c` | SIGSEGV | SIGSEGV | ok | ok | ok |

Nesting depth at 4MB: 8,000 levels ok, 10,000 levels SIGSEGV.

Same file on the wasm path parses fine — `CODEGRAPH_KERNEL=0` indexed all 31,608 files of llvm-project in 1m48s. With the kernel on and only that one file excluded: 1m24s, and the node/edge counts match the wasm run except for that file's own 2 nodes.

## What this changes

`ParseWorkerPool` pins `resourceLimits: { stackSizeMb: 16 }`. A thread stack is reserved lazily, page by page, so this costs nothing on files of ordinary depth.

I want to be explicit that **this raises the cliff rather than removing it.** The complete fix is a depth cap in the kernel walkers that raises `defer:`, which routes the file to the wasm extractor that already handles it.

A third thing worth considering separately: when the pool sees a worker exit with a parse in flight, naming that file in the error would turn this class of bug from a bisect into a one-line diagnosis.

## Tests

New `__tests__/parse-worker-stack.test.ts`:

- the stack constant covers the deepest nesting seen in the wild, with headroom;
- `resourceLimits` actually reaches the worker thread, and the partial `resourceLimits` doesn't silently cap the V8 heap (parse workers legitimately reach ~1.4GB RSS on a large index);
- the kernel parses a 16,384-deep C file without dying — skipped when no `.node` is staged, matching `kernel-scaffold.test.ts`.

Both worker arms run in a **child process** deliberately: on a regression the parse segfaults, and a segfault in a worker thread would take the test runner down with it instead of reporting a failure. Verified by setting the constant back to 4 — the suite fails cleanly with `expected 'SIGSEGV' to be null` and the runner survives.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `__tests__/parse-pool.test.ts` (17 tests) still passes.

author: artokun
body:
Closes #1969.

**Four commits, and the review provenance differs between them** — please read that before the diff:

| commit | author | review status |
|---|---|---|
| `90d9cf6` — the mechanism | grok-swarm | **independently reviewed by me**, in a worktree I cut myself. Three defects found, fixed in the commits below. |
| `944caab` — a structural join is not a claim about intent | me | **NOT independently reviewed** |
| `c54470b` — two keys that fit equally well are a refusal | me | **NOT independently reviewed** |
| `0c792b5` — let the value settle a name tie before refusing | me | **NOT independently reviewed**, and it exists only because `c54470b` was wrong |

The three findings, in the order I found them, all instances of one principle — *say the true thing, not the decisive thing*:

1. **`944caab`** — the structural 1:1 rule guessed a target for any stray key on the 34 tools that take exactly one required key.
2. **`c54470b`** — the name-match rules broke a two-way tie by string length, inventing a winner on `panel_connect`.
3. **`0c792b5`** — fixing (2) by refusing on every tie silenced `panel_edit_node {node:5}`, which the original ranking got right. A tie is now settled by the value when the value can settle it.

Detail and mutation evidence for (2) and (3) is in the PR comments rather than repeated here.

## How this PR came to exist

grok-swarm claimed #1969 at 07:06Z, pushed `90d9cf6` at 07:22Z, and then stalled before opening a PR — its siblings from the same batch (#1972 → #1980, #1973 → #1981) both got PRs, this one did not. No live process, worktree idle and clean. Rather than duplicate it and repeat the #1887 loss, I reviewed it and finished it. The mechanism is grok's and is kept intact.

## What `90d9cf6` does (grok's, reviewed)

Ask 2 of #1969: a rejected call used to name the unknown key and the missing required one as **two separate issues** —

```
unrecognized_keys: ["group"]
expected number, received undefined at group_id
```

A frontier model joins those. A 2–4B fine-tune trained only on server-verified successes has never seen the error-to-recovery transition and cannot. So a Zod error map installed at `strictPanelSchema` puts the join in one sentence: `Unrecognized key 'group' — did you mean 'group_id'?`

It is a **suggestion, not an alias** — the call is still refused. That is the complement of #1985, which aliases four specific keys; this covers the other ~90 tools' keys, which nothing aliases.

**What my review confirmed:**
- **Both transports carry it.** grok's test only exercises the MCP SDK path (`registerPanelTools`, Codex backend). I probed the **Anthropic SDK path** (`createPanelMcpServer`, the Claude backend — the primary one) at runtime and the message arrives intact on the wire: `"message": "Unrecognized key 'group' — did you mean 'group_id'?"`. Measured, not read off the shared `strictPanelSchema` call.
- **`tools/list` is unaffected.** The emitted JSON Schema for `panel_remove_group` is byte-clean — `additionalProperties:false` preserved, no leakage of the error function. 95 tools still register.
- **Acceptance is unchanged** — the canonical key still reaches the handler.

## The defect I found — `944caab`

`pairUnrecognizedKeys` has three rules. Rules 1–2 match on the **name** (`group` → `group_id` by affix/edit distance). Rule 3 is a **structural** fallback: if exactly one unknown key and exactly one missing required key are left over, join them even when the names are nothing alike — which is how the reporter's `todos` → `items` gets caught.

Rule 3 fires on **counts, not meaning**, and I measured that **34 of the 95 registered panel tools take exactly one required key**. So before this fix, every one of them answered *any* stray key with a confident guess:

```
panel_remove_node { dry_run: true }
  → "Unrecognized key 'dry_run' — did you mean 'node_id'?"
```

Phrased identically to the true `group` → `group_id` case and **indistinguishable from it by exactly the 2–4B models this change exists to serve**. So the model acts on the wrong repair — moves the value into `node_id`, fails again on a type error. That is the failure this PR is supposed to remove, reintroduced one rule further down.

Worth naming: grok's suite *does* test "does not invent a target" — but against `panel_graph_outline`, an **all-optional** tool, which has no required key and therefore structurally cannot reach rule 3. The test picked the one case that cannot exhibit the defect.

**The fix splits the two claims rather than deleting rule 3**, because rule 3 is what serves the reporter's own case:

- Rules 1–2 matched on the name → stay `— did you mean 'X'?`
- Rule 3 → promoted to `did you mean` **only when the value the caller actually sent also parses under the target's schema**; otherwise it states the fact it knows: `— required key 'node_id' is missing`.

Both halves of the join still arrive in one sentence, which was the ask. The difference is that the sentence no longer asserts intent it cannot know.

`todos` → `items` survives as a confident suggestion, because the todo array they sent **is** a valid `items`. Measured across the surface, the value check suppresses **133 of 170** false joins while keeping every true positive.

## Evidence

- **Full suite on the PR head `0c792b5`: 615/616 files, 11,252 passed, 4 skipped.** Also run on grok's `90d9cf6` alone (11,240 passed) to separate its result from mine. The single failure is `package-hooks.test.ts > every entry in 'files' exists on disk`, and the missing entry is `dist` — a build output absent from a never-built worktree. Harness artifact, not grok's change, and named here rather than waved off.
- Typecheck clean. `check:vocabulary` OK (1758 files). `check:unknown-collapse` OK.
- **27 tests** in the file (15 grok's, 12 added by the review), all driving a real `McpServer` + `Client` rather than calling handlers directly — the string an agent reads is produced by the SDK's renderer, so a schema-level assertion would be checking a different sentence than the one that reaches them.

author: saranshisatgit
body:
Closes the last gap in JYT #1389 / #1418.

The partner has been able to mint a quote and copy a buyer link for a while — **that link rendered nothing**, as the partner UI's own success panel admits. This is the page.

## Design

**No login, no account.** The token in the URL is the whole credential, because asking a procurement contact to sign up before they can see a price is the wall this feature exists to remove. The link is deliberately multi-view — forwarding it to procurement is the use case, not an abuse of it.

**An unknown token and a revoked one are indistinguishable.** Both 404 on the backend so a prober learns nothing; the fetcher turns *any* failure into the same not-found rather than letting an error bubble into a stack-shaped 500 that says more than the 404 does.

🔑 **Every judgement is the backend's, not this page's.** The headline, the explanation, the disclaimer, the expiry nudge and which price columns render all come from the `compare` block, which already knows how to tell a dead link from a pre-freeze quote from one whose live price has moved. Re-deriving any of it here is how a page ends up contradicting its own header.

## Deliberately uncached, deliberately noindex

Every other fetcher in `lib/data` uses `force-cache` with a tag. This one uses `no-store` and the page is `force-dynamic`, because:

- the backend records `viewed_at` / `view_count` on read, so a cached page would silently stop the view tracking the partner relies on to know the buyer looked;
- a cached per-token document risks being served under another token's key.

`robots: { index: false, follow: false }` — the token *is* the credential.

## Details worth keeping

- Freight is presented as an **estimate**, and says so when the lane could not be quoted live.
- Where a weight came from travels with the number: a declared **product** weight over-quotes a lighter variant, and at bulk quantities that can cross a carrier slab.
- Totals are shown as **landed** cost — subtotal + freight, quoted as one consignment.

## Verify

`npm run build` — green, and the route appears as dynamic:

```
├ ƒ /[countryCode]/quotes/[token]      418 B     332 kB
```

The pre-existing React 19 `Suspense` type errors in `products/` and `store/` templates are untouched by this branch.

## Not in this PR

The partner-ui link change adding the `[countryCode]` segment — that lands in the monorepo, and without it existing links point at `/quotes/:token`, which 404s under this app's routing.

body: V3.1 keeps the Digash level-trading research direction and fixes/diagnoses implementation mismatches exposed by V3 without tuning to the observed result. It preserves the public period 20/30, one counted touch, tolerance uncertainty, and lifetime=0; no arbitrary level expiry is added. It adds top-5 activity lists including real quote-volume ranking, a one-sided/contracting breakout protorgovka proxy, causally confirmed 5m structure stops, gross-vs-net fee diagnostics, level-age/touch-error diagnostics, and a same-or-higher-TF structural-room measure. Horizontal target roles are not frozen to their original S/R label: a support above price after a break may act as resistance and vice versa, so targets remain the nearest already-known horizontal level in trade direction, with a second target that ignores lower-TF structure. Historical trade-count, order-book densities, private trend-line rules and private structure formations remain explicitly unreplicated. Cache-only, 16-process runner included.

author: j5ik2o
body:
Fixes #3404.

## 概要

`tests/gen-coverage-registry.ts` の function クラス列挙は dist の `amadeus-{lib,graph,state}.ts` のみが対象で、`packages/setup/**` の関数は列挙対象外でした。そのため setup 系テストが `covers: function:<name>` を宣言してもどのユニットにも join されず、buildRegistry は未 join の claim を黙って捨てていました（#3389 で実測）。

## 変更内容

1. **setup パッケージの function 列挙を追加**: `packages/setup/src/**` をソースから列挙（setup は dist 投影ではなくソース直配布のため）。トップレベル `export function|const|class` と `export namespace` メンバー（`function:<Namespace>.<name>`）の両形を対象。flat な id 空間で名前が衝突する場合（`main` 等）は 1 ユニットに集約し `source` に全宣言ファイルを記録。
2. **未 join covers claim の loud 化**: registry 自身の語彙（7クラスプレフィックス）で書かれた claim がどのユニットにも join しない場合、生成 registry の `unjoinedClaims` にコミットし、generate / `--check` 両方で stderr に報告。コミットされたリストが freshness diff の対象になるため、**新規**の未 join claim は `--check` を red にします（既存 367 件があるため即 fail ではなく advisory + diff ゲートの二段構え）。他台帳の語彙（`file:` / `domain:` / `modules:` 等）は対象外。

## 検証

- `bun tests/gen-coverage-registry.ts --check`: OK (fresh, guards green, ratchet held)
- `bun test tests/integration/gen-coverage-registry.test.ts`: 43 pass / 1996 assertions
- `bun run typecheck` / `bun run lint`: green

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the coverage-registry CI gate (freshness/ratchet) and expands the enumerated function universe; a generator bug could fail CI or hide coverage drift.
> 
> **Overview**
> Closes the silent gap where setup tests’ `covers: function:…` claims joined nothing, and where unmatched registry-vocabulary claims were dropped without a committed byte.
> 
> The `function` enumerator now walks `packages/setup/src` (top-level exports and `export namespace` members as `function:Ns.name`). Duplicate names across roots collapse to one unit. Unjoined claims in the seven class prefixes are listed in the committed registry and printed as `UNJOINED COVERS CLAIMS`; new ones fail `--check` via freshness, existing hundreds stay advisory. CLI dispatch is now an injectable `runMain` returning an exit code.
> 
> Covered function count ratchets 193→196; enumerated functions 362→475. Docs (EN/JA) and generator tests cover both export shapes, unjoined reporting, and in-process argv paths.
>

author: time4love
body:
## Two anonymous paid paths

`WRITE_TOOLS` was maintained as *"tools that persist something"* rather than *"tools that cost something"*. Two tools fell through that gap and ran with **no account at all**:

| tool | what a single call spends |
|---|---|
| `suggest_thesis` | embeds the topic, then one long-context `ThesisSynthesisAgent` call |
| `get_research_agenda` | embeds each gap, and with `includeSuggestions:true` runs `GapRevisionAgent` **once per open gap** — cost scales with thesis state, not a fixed price |

Neither writes a row, so both read as reads. On production that meant anyone with the URL could invoke LLM synthesis at the project's expense.

## And no cap, by accident of mount order

```js
app.use('/api/mcp', mcpRouter);      // line 119  ← matched and returned here
app.use('/api', generalLimiter);     // line 136  ← never reached
```

Express matched `/api/mcp` at the earlier mount, so the limiter never ran. **MCP was the only completely uncapped surface in the backend.**

The limiter is now attached to the mount directly rather than moving it below — moving it would re-gate the route behind `requireStagingAccess` and break external clients, which is exactly why it sits up there.

`generalLimiter` rather than `aiCostLimiter`: an MCP session spends requests on `initialize` and `tools/list` before any tool call, so a 10-per-15-min cap would exhaust itself on handshakes. The paid tools are gated by `resolveResearcher()` instead; the limiter bounds the anonymous read surface, where `search_evidence` still embeds a query per call.

**`search_evidence` stays open deliberately** — it embeds a query and nothing more, it's the core public read, and it's what the anonymous ChatGPT integration depends on. Gating it would break a working consumer to solve a problem it isn't causing. There's a test asserting that, so a future tightening pass has to make the trade-off consciously.

## The drift that hid it

The classification lived in **three places that couldn't see each other**: the `WRITE_TOOLS` set the gate reads, plus two hand-maintained literal arrays advertising the tool list in `GET /api/mcp`.

They had already diverged — **`suggest_thesis` appeared in none of them**, so the endpoint published 20 of its 21 tools and omitted the most expensive anonymous one.

Fixing that instance wouldn't prevent the next one. So:
- the advertised lists are now **derived** from the sets the gate reads
- `mcpToolClassification.test.ts` asserts the sets are **exhaustive and disjoint** against the server's real `server.tool()` registrations

A new tool cannot be added without being classified. Verified by re-introducing the original bug — the guard fails with two assertions naming `suggest_thesis`, and goes green when restored.

## Verification

- **851/851** backend tests (was 845), `tsc` clean, lint unchanged at 301
- Drift guard proven to fail against the original bug, not just pass against the fix
- No migrations

## Doc corrections

`docs/gf-cost-exposure-dev-plan.md` gains this as audit item **#9**, plus §0.1b on why the original audit missed it: it enumerated REST routes, and `/api/mcp` is one route multiplexing 21 tools behind a JSON-RPC body — it appears once in a route listing and looks like one endpoint.

Its status line also claimed Phase 1 was "not yet committed/pushed/merged". `rateLimiting.ts` **is** on `origin/master`; corrected.

body:
## Summary

Adds engine-side brass/horn/sax section transposition to Tab Translator Pro, so any decoded chart (PDF / GP / Power Tab / MusicXML) can be exported as transposed MusicXML or ABC for every standard section instrument. Fully additive — `engine.tsx` stays React-free and pure-ES; the existing `transposeScore` does the pitch shift, and the existing `scoreToMusicXML` / `scoreToABC` do the formatting.

## What's included

New engine surface (all listed in the single `export { ... }` block, per the two-file contract):

- **`BRASS_INSTRUMENTS`** — 15-instrument catalog with `transposeSemitones` (written − sounding), `clef` (`treble` / `bass`), and a General-MIDI `midiProgram`:
  - B♭ Trumpet / Cornet / Flugelhorn +2, F Horn +7
  - Trombone / Bass Trombone / Euphonium (BC) / Tuba 0 (bass clef)
  - B♭ Euphonium (TC) +14
  - B♭ Soprano Sax +2, E♭ Alto Sax +9, B♭ Tenor Sax +14, E♭ Baritone Sax +21
  - B♭ Clarinet +2, B♭ Bass Clarinet +14
- **`getBrassInstrument(id)`** — catalog lookup.
- **`scoreToBrassMusicXML(score, id, opts)`** — runs `transposeScore(concert, semitones, useSharp)`, feeds the shifted score to `scoreToMusicXML`, renames `<part-name>`, and (for bass-clef instruments) injects a `<clef><sign>F</sign><line>4</line></clef>` into the first measure's `<attributes>`.
- **`scoreToBrassABC(score, id, opts)`** — same but for ABC. Also shifts `opts.key` (or `analyzeKey(score)` if none supplied) by the instrument interval so the `K:` line matches the transposed pitches, injects `%%MIDI program N`, and adds `V:1 clef=bass` for bass-clef instruments.
- **`buildBrassSection(score, ids, opts)`** — one entry per requested instrument as `{ id, name, format, filename, content }`; unknown instrument ids are silently skipped (matches the sister-app UI's tolerance).

Family enharmonic default (B♭ · C# · E♭ · F# · A♭) is inherited from the existing `transposeScore` + `symbolForMidis` chain.

## Files

- `engine.tsx` — brass block inserted directly after `transposeScore`; exports added to the single `export { ... }` block. Zero React/DOM; passes the two-file transpile guard.
- `engine.txt` — mirror synced (per the CLAUDE.md convention).
- `tests/path-a-smoke.mjs` — 19 new assertions on the C-major MusicXML fixture (`C G | Am | F`): B♭ trumpet reads it in D (root steps D + A), E♭ alto in A (root A/E), F horn in G, trombone in C with F/4 bass clef; ABC trumpet has `K:D` + `%%MIDI program 56`, trombone has `V:1 clef=bass`; `buildBrassSection` returns one entry per instrument; unknown ids skip.

## Verification

- `cd tests && npm test` — **all pass** (Blue Sky 165 bars, verse + V + bridge, plus every pre-existing regression across GP/GP3/GP5/GPX/PTB/MusicXML/exports, plus the new brass block).
- Blue Sky, Confirmation, Peg, Kid Charlemagne, House of the Rising Sun etc. all still reconstruct byte-identically.

## How this is used

Users who want a UI-driven brass export can send the recognised chart to the finishing app via the existing **→ Chord Sheet Maker Pro** handoff, then open the new **🎺 Brass Section** panel there (paired CSMP PR).

## Test plan

- [ ] Recognise any chart (PDF / GP / Power Tab / MusicXML) in Tab Translator Pro.
- [ ] From the Node console / a headless probe, call `eng.buildBrassSection(score, ['trumpet-bb','alto-sax-eb','tenor-sax-bb','trombone'], { format: 'musicxml', title: 'Demo' })`.
- [ ] Open one of the resulting XMLs in MuseScore / Sibelius / Dorico — pitches and chord symbols should read correctly in each section instrument's written key.

author: ikscream
body:
## Problem
After the node resize, Grafana still returned **"no available server"**. Root cause is **not** capacity (node has ~4.7 GB free) — it's **Grafana 13.2.x** (the chart default) crash-looping on its new unified-storage / "secure values" subsystem:

- logs: `cleaning up inactive secure values: ... context deadline exceeded`, an **18.5s** `/api/health` request
- → liveness probe kills the pod → restart loop → endpoints `notReady` → Traefik 503 "no available server"

## Fix
- **Pin `grafana.image.tag: "12.4.9"`** (stable; no unified-storage subsystem).
- Raise Grafana memory limit 256Mi → 512Mi (node is 8 GB now).
- **Relax the readiness probe** (chart default `timeoutSeconds: 1` was flapping) → 5s / failureThreshold 6 / 20s initial delay.
- MEMORY.md: record the `cx33` resize and the Grafana-13.2 gotcha.

author: lagebj
body:
## Summary

Post-Phase-13 roadmap Group C1 (Phase 11 §68). Every sibling lifecycle status field in the schema is a real Prisma enum; `MatchRound.status` alone was a bare `String`, named by the audit as the confirmed root cause of an unreachable `NOT_GENERATED` branch in `round-status.ts`.

**Investigation before writing the migration found three real, confirmed bugs, not one** — full detail in ADR-0083:

1. `unfinalize-match-round.ts`/`unfinalize-single-match.ts` called `deriveRoundStatus()` (a display-only computation) with hardcoded inputs guaranteeing it could only return `"BLOCKED"` or `"READY"` — then persisted that value directly into `MatchRound.status` instead of the literal `"DRAFT"` it should have written.
2. A pre-existing `CHECK` constraint mirrored the full 5-value UI display vocabulary instead of the 2-value persistence rule, letting bug 1 succeed without ever violating a database constraint.
3. `resolve-or-create-match-round-for-date.ts` explicitly wrote `status: "NOT_GENERATED"` when creating a new round — a second, independent invalid write site.

## ⚠️ Requires a production migration after merge

This PR includes `prisma/migrations/20260821100000_match_round_status_enum/`. Per this repo's rules, **production migrations must be run deliberately from a local machine** (`npx prisma migrate deploy` with `DIRECT_URL` targeting Neon production) — never as part of the Vercel build. **This is not automated and will not happen on merge.** I have not run it against production myself; a real production DB connection for even a read-only check was already blocked by the sandbox's safety classifier earlier this session, so I expect the same for a write, and in any case a schema migration against production is a distinct action that should not happen without an explicit go-ahead separate from merging the code.

## Changes

- `prisma/schema.prisma` — new `MatchRoundStatus { DRAFT, FINALIZED }` enum; `MatchRound.status` now uses it.
- Migration: coerces any row with an unexpected value back to `DRAFT` unconditionally (a direct production data check was blocked, so the migration does not depend on knowing the actual extent of any corruption), drops the now-superseded `CHECK` constraint, converts the column.
- Fixed the three confirmed bugs above at their write sites.
- `get-assistant-command-centre.ts`: fixed the same class of bug — comparing `round.status` directly against values the database never actually stores. A round with zero draft selections fell through to the live-integrity branch and was incorrectly recommended as "Ready to finalize." Now checks `hasDraftSelections` explicitly.
- `round-board.tsx` / `domain/fixtures/service.ts`: both omitted `decisionRequiredCount` from `deriveRoundStatus()`'s blocked-signal count, unlike `finalize-match-round.ts`'s own combined treatment — a round with only Decision-required conditions displayed as READY despite its own "decisions need review" banner. Fixed to match the established pattern.
- `import-full-app-state.ts`: coerces any corrupted historical export value to DRAFT/FINALIZED rather than letting the insert fail.
- Removed a fully dead `_roundData` object and the now-unused `hasMatches` parameter from `deriveRoundStatus()` and its call sites.

## Verification
- `npm run lint` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` — pass
- `npm run docs:check` / `npm run terminology:check` / `npm run architecture:check` / `npm run policy:verify` / `npm run version:verify` — pass
- Full test suite (2630 tests) — pass, against local Postgres, migration applied and verified end-to-end locally (including a rollback/retry due to a `DROP DEFAULT` ordering issue caught before merge, not just before writing this PR)
- Version bump 0.14.2 → 0.14.3 (patch)

## Notes
Given the blast radius (`MatchRound`/`Selection` are both actively written via many code paths), this PR would benefit from a closer review pass before merging, not just green CI.

## 問題
無法匯入台新 .xls 檔。

## 根因（兩個）
1. **id 衝突**：記帳「檔案匯入」的 `<input id="import-file" accept=".xls,...">` 與設定頁「JSON 備份還原」的 `<input id="import-file" accept=".json">` **同 id**。`getElementById('import-file')` 只回傳第一個（.json 的），所以點檔案匯入其實開到只收 .json 的選擇器 → .xls 被擋、選不了。
2. **iOS 重複讀檔**：合併入口後 `file.arrayBuffer()` 被讀兩次（偵測一次、解析一次），iOS Safari 對同一 File 第二次讀取常失敗。

## 修正
- 記帳匯入 input 改名 `rec-import-file`（與 JSON 匯入不再衝突）
- `handleImportFile` 只讀一次 arrayBuffer，偵測到台新後用**已解析的 workbook** 呼叫新的 `startRichartImport(wb)`，不再重讀檔案

author: aryali1996
body:
## Ticket 46: Fix Track List Localization – "Accompaniment" and "Vocal" Remain in English When Chinese Language Is Selected

### Root cause

- **Playback/Monitor** (`PlaybackMonitorView.tsx`): separated-stem tracks were created with `makeTrack('stem', key, buffer)`, where `key` is the raw identifier returned by the Python separation engine (`vocals`, `accompaniment`, `lead_dry`, `harmony_dry` — see `engine/separation.py`). The track-list renderer's `trackLabel()` helper explicitly special-cased `'stem'` tracks to display that raw, untranslated identifier verbatim instead of running it through `t()`.
- **Audio Tools** (`AudioToolsView.tsx`): the per-stem download buttons used a local `STEM_LABELS` constant of hardcoded English strings (`'Vocals'`, `'Accomp.'`, `'Lead'`, `'Harmony'`) for both the on-screen button text and the button's `title` attribute (which also hardcoded the English word `"Download "`).
- **Cover Creation** (`CoverView.tsx` / `StemPlayer.tsx`) was already correct — it maps stem keys through `t('cover.labelVocals')` etc., so no changes were needed there.

### Fix

- Added `src/renderer/src/utils/stems.ts` with a `stemLabelKey(stemKey)` helper that maps the engine's raw stem identifiers to a new shared `tracks.*` i18n namespace (`tracks.vocal`, `tracks.accompaniment`, `tracks.harmony`, `tracks.other`), added to both `zh-CN` and `en-US` bundles in `i18n.ts`.
- `PlaybackMonitorView.tsx`: `trackLabel()` now renders `t(stemLabelKey(tr.label))` for stem tracks instead of returning the stored raw label.
- `AudioToolsView.tsx`: stem download button text/title now use `t(stemLabelKey(key))` and the existing `common.download` key instead of hardcoded English. The old `STEM_LABELS` map is kept (renamed `STEM_FILE_SUFFIX`) purely for generating ASCII-safe downloaded `.wav` filenames, which are intentionally left untranslated.

Since both views already use `useTranslation()`/`t()` inside their render function, stem names now re-render immediately when the language is switched — no track reload needed.

### Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json` — passes.
- `npx vitest run` — all 60 existing tests pass.
- Manually traced both code paths (Playback/Monitor separation flow and Audio Tools batch download flow) to confirm `t(stemLabelKey(...))` is used everywhere a stem name is rendered.

### Acceptance criteria coverage

- [x] Chinese mode shows 伴奏 / 人声 / 和声 for track list stem names.
- [x] English mode shows Accompaniment / Vocal / Harmony.
- [x] Names update instantly on language switch (driven by `t()` in render, no stored/cached label).
- [x] No hardcoded English stem names remain in Playback/Monitor or Audio Tools UI components.
- [x] Cover Creation already correct; verified unaffected.

author: h0x91b
body:
## Summary

When dev3 is viewed over remote access, the header can now say **with a number** whether the connection is slow — and where the wait goes.

One sample is the round trip of a `ping` RPC through the same `/rpc` WebSocket every other request already uses, sampled every 5 s while the tab is visible (~27 bytes/s, under a thousandth of the terminal stream). The server stamps its own span, so the panel can split *our* time from the network's. A stalled request counts as a loss, never as a huge sample.

**Where it lives.** A healthy link is not news, so it buys no header pixels: the readout sits as a `Connection` row in the header's overflow menu, next to `Memory left`, and only climbs into the slot the desktop QR icon uses once the verdict stops being good — median past 150 ms, or jitter/loss bad enough to feel. Same earned-visibility rule the memory pill already uses; net header controls unchanged. If the socket is open but nothing answers, it shows a dash in red rather than disappearing.

**Why the tunnel looked innocent.** A measured 331 ms round trip turned out to be neither Cloudflare nor our pipeline: the host's VPN exits in Ireland, so every frame crossed it twice per direction, and our own share measured 0 ms. Hence the opt-in `DEV3_CLOUDFLARED_EDGE_BIND=en0`, which lets cloudflared dial the edge from a chosen interface — 340 ms → 25 ms on that machine. Off by default, because it routes a whole working session around a VPN somebody installed on purpose.

## Also in here

- The open/pin/hover/positioning machinery this widget shares with the memory readout is extracted into `useHeaderFlyout` + `HeaderFlyoutPanel`; both components shed ~200 duplicated lines and keep only their own content.
- **Help mode bug fix:** `HelpOverlay` froze its zone list at mount and held the DOM node. Any conditional readout that unmounts and remounts underneath an open help mode left a detached node, whose rect is all zeros — so the outline, badge and card collapsed into the top-left corner of the screen instead of sitting beside the control. Zones now resolve their element at render time, and a zone whose element left the screen drops its marker.
- The route label no longer names Cloudflare for a hostname it cannot classify (a bare LAN name, a Tailscale host); bracketed IPv6 loopback is recognised as local.
- Released a leaked `visibilitychange` listener and a per-sample deadline timer, and an interface name is now looked up as an own property so `DEV3_CLOUDFLARED_EDGE_BIND=__proto__` cannot reach `Object.prototype`.

Decisions: `decisions/2026/08/20/remote-connection-quality-definition.md`, `decisions/2026/08/20/cloudflared-edge-bind-escape-hatch.md`.

author: kujopht
body:
Post-R1 Completion Program, Phase 3.

## P3-A: 500 vs 422 on invalid Content-Type
Investigated against current code, not the old report. Could not reproduce — ran 356 requests (89 POST/PUT/PATCH routes x 4 malformed-body shapes) against a local mock-mode server, all correctly 422/400/403, zero 500s. No fix needed. Added `server/tests/test_content_type_validation.py` as a regression guard.

## P3-B: account deletion
No account-deletion endpoint existed at all before this — the only prior path was an operator calling Appwrite's own `DELETE /v1/users/{id}` directly, orphaning every other collection. Adds `DELETE /api/account` (self-service only), cascading in a fixed order (app data → R2 objects → identity last) so a mid-cascade failure never strands data with no owner and is retriable at every step.

Data-retention policy (full detail in `MetadataStore.delete_account`'s docstring):
- **Deletes**: novels/chapters (including published ones with an audience — deliberate, no placeholder-author mechanism), tts_jobs/audio_tracks/job_claims/job_locks, posts/comments/post_likes/notifications, user_follows (both directions), story_follows, author_stats, gamification state, translation projects + BYOK provider connections.
- **Retains untouched**: `moderation_events` (append-only by design), `listen_credits` where this user is the listener (already counted toward another author's standing).
- **Retains, anonymizes**: `author_applications` (keeps decision history), `content_reports` where this user is the reporter.

body:
## Summary

화면에서 앱 타입을 **web** 으로 골라도 리포에는 이것 하나만 들어갔다:

```dockerfile
FROM nginx:alpine
EXPOSE 8080
```

배포는 성공한다. 열어 보면 **"Welcome to nginx"** 가 뜬다. 개발자는 파이프라인이 다 돌고 주소가 열린 뒤에야 그 안에 앱이 없다는 것을 알게 된다.

스캐폴딩이 앱 타입을 아예 몰랐다 — `scaffold.Input` 에 그 필드가 없었다.

## Changes

**React 앱 소스** (`react_app.go` 신규)
- `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `index.html`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`, `.dockerignore`
- 버전은 **플랫폼 자신이 쓰는 조합**에 맞춘다 — React `^19.2.4`, Vite `^8.0.0`, `@vitejs/plugin-react` `^6`, TypeScript `~5.9.3`. 함께 도는 것이 이미 검증됐고 팀이 아는 스택과 어긋나지 않는다. "최신" 을 따로 추적하면 서로 맞지 않는 조합을 사용자에게 떠넘기게 된다

**Dockerfile — 빌드와 서빙을 나눈다**
- node 이미지를 그대로 배포하면 개발 서버가 프로덕션에 뜨고 이미지도 수백 MB 가 된다
- nginx 설정에 `try_files` 를 넣는다. SPA 는 새로고침하면 서버가 그 경로를 찾으므로, index.html 로 되돌리지 않으면 **첫 화면 말고는 전부 404** 가 된다
- 포트를 배포 매니페스트가 가리키는 값으로 맞춘다. 기본 80 으로 두면 Service 의 `targetPort` 와 어긋나 endpoints 가 비고, 원인이 멀리 떨어진 503 이 된다
- 첫 스캐폴딩에는 lock 파일이 없으므로 `npm ci` 대신 `npm install` 을 쓴다

**배선**
- `scaffold.Input.AppType` 추가, 파이프라인 생성 → 저장소 프로비저닝 → 스캐폴딩으로 이어지게 했다
- 웹이 아닌 앱은 예전 그대로다 — 백엔드 리포에 React 소스를 넣지 않는다

## Testing

먼저 실패(RED)를 확인한 뒤 구현했다.

- `TestScaffold_WebAppGetsReactSources` — 파일 목록과 버전. `package.json` 을 실제로 파싱해 검사한다(깨진 JSON 이면 빌드가 첫 줄에서 죽는데, 문자열 포함 검사로는 그것을 놓친다). react 와 react-dom 이 같은 버전인지도 본다
- `TestScaffold_WebDockerfileBuildsThenServes` — 2단계 빌드, `try_files`, 포트
- `TestScaffold_NonWebKeepsPlaceholder` — 백엔드 무영향
- `TestProvisionAppProject_WebAppCommitsReactSources` — 사슬이 끊기지 않는지. 앱 타입은 세 단계를 거쳐야 스캐폴딩에 닿고, 어디서 끊겨도 증상은 "배포 뒤에야 앱이 없다"로 같다
- `go build ./... && go test ./internal/... ./deploy/...` 전체 통과

## 적용 범위

**새로 만드는 파이프라인부터**다. 기존 리포는 이미 있어서 스캐폴딩을 건너뛴다(`scaffoldSkipped := !project.Created`) — 확인하려면 새 이름으로 web 타입 파이프라인을 하나 만들면 된다.

Scope: 웹 앱의 스캐폴딩 내용과 앱 타입 배선. 배포 매니페스트·파이프라인 정의·라우팅은 그대로다.

body: ## Summary Updates the speedtest plugin display to show proper byte-denominated throughput units (B/s, KB/s, MB/s, GB/s) instead of bare numbers. ## Changes - Added `SpeedtestMetrics.formatThroughput()` to convert Mbps values to bytes/s and format with auto-scaled units - Updated download/upload labels to display formatted values with units (e.g., `↓16 MB/s`, `↑5.6 MB/s`) - Increased label widths from 42 to 74 points to accommodate the unit text - Each metric (download/upload) is formatted independently for clarity ## Technical Details - **Conversion**: 1 Mbps = 125,000 bytes/s (since 1 Mbps = 1,000,000 bits/s ÷ 8 bits/byte) - **Auto-scaling**: Values are displayed with appropriate units based on magnitude: - < 1 KB/s: Shows as "X B/s" - < 1 MB/s: Shows as "X.X KB/s" or "XX KB/s" - < 1 GB/s: Shows as "X.X MB/s" or "XX MB/s" - ≥ 1 GB/s: Shows as "X.XX GB/s" ## Examples | Before | After | |--------|-------| | `↓125 ↑45` | `↓16 MB/s ↑5.6 MB/s` | | `↓800 ↑200` | `↓100 MB/s ↑25 MB/s` | | `↓8 ↑2` | `↓1.0 MB/s ↑250 KB/s` | ## Context Builds on PR #2 which introduced the compact speedtest UI. The plugin was showing unlabeled numbers that appeared to be Mbps values. This PR adds truthful byte-denominated units to make the display more informative and scannable while maintaining the compact layout.

## Problem / Motivation

JSON-RPC method-not-found responses used the reserved `-32601` code through a private ACP client constant and duplicate literals in the multiplexed session and MCP stdio paths. That made protocol parity depend on manually keeping several copies aligned.

## Why it matters

A single public protocol constant makes the reserved code discoverable and prevents ACP-compatible request handlers from drifting while preserving their existing error messages and behavior.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

The duplicated reserved code was the source of drift risk, so this change makes `acp/types.py` the ACP protocol owner and reuses `JSONRPC_METHOD_NOT_FOUND` in the legacy ACP client, multiplexed session handle, and shared MCP stdio dispatcher. The builtin auto-improvement app remains self-contained rather than gaining a cross-layer dependency.

author: twillis45
body:
The competitive audit wanted the Vocabulary pattern — *"you outrank 4% of learners"*, a percentile over a distribution curve. I said I wouldn't build it. **This is what I said I'd build instead.**

## Why not the percentile

A percentile needs a population. There's no server and no telemetry here **by design**, and both store filings say so — so the only way to print one would be to invent a distribution and present it as though it described other players.

That's a fabricated statistic on a reward surface. Worse than showing nothing, and it would be the first thing in this product that wasn't true.

## What's true instead

Every board already has a finite, known answer set: six grid words plus its bonus list — **26 to 105 words depending on the wheel, median 41**. So *"23 of 41 words found"* is a fact about the board rather than a claim about anybody else.

It does the job the percentile was wanted for — telling a player how much is still there, which is what makes somebody keep looking. **Spelling Bee prints exactly this.**

It gives away no answers. A count is not a word.

## Tests

Three, and the middle one matters most: found words are stored per puzzle, so a caller passing the wrong set would inflate the numerator past the denominator and print **"7 of 6"** — which reads as a bug to a player, and is one.

(One test failed first with my own bad arithmetic — I'd written 5 where the union was 4. The code was right.)

267 tests; check:ranks, check:marks, check:tiles, check:rail pass.

**Stacked on #52** — merge that first.

author: zeshuochen
body:
## 内容

| | |
|---|---|
| 修复 | **别把「令牌对不上」当成僵尸** —— daemon 无声消失的真凶，会硬杀一个健康进程（#20） |
| 修复 | `--doctor` 的端口探测没跟着 `--port` 走（本 PR 新增） |
| 版本 | 0.3.3 → 0.3.4（三处） |

## doctor 探错端口

`_url()` 认 `--port`，而 `_doctor()` 里的 `_port_in_use()` / `_pid_file_is_ours()` 不接参数、永远打默认端口：

```
$ nekoro-browser --port 28503 --doctor          # 28503 是空的，28417 上有别人
[WARN] Daemon : http://127.0.0.1:28503 is held (pid file says 2424, unverified) but not answering
```

指着空端口说被占着，还点了个不相干的 pid。`--stop` 和 `_ensure_daemon` 都传了 port，**只有 doctor 漏了** —— 是 0.3.3 加这个 WARN 分支时漏的，**已随 0.3.3 发出去过一版**，由发布前独立复核发现。

修复后：`[INFO] Daemon : not running on http://127.0.0.1:28503`

mutation：去掉两处 port 参数 → `test_doctor_probes_the_port_it_reports_on` 转红（`探测没用上 --port，实际打的是 {None}`）。

## 发布前独立复核结果（针对 0.3.4 产物）

- **拒杀外部 daemon 7/7**：A 日志留下 `/exec rejected: bad token` ×6、**零条 `/shutdown rejected`** —— 连「尝试停对方」都没发生。对比 0.3.3 同一日志的前半段（`/exec` ×2 + `/shutdown rejected` + A 消失），前后对照干净
- **自愈没被挡**：同令牌真僵尸仍走 `Stale daemon detected`，且是**优雅停**（僵尸日志里有 `shutdown requested`），不是硬杀
- **`--stop` 新警告**：对外部 daemon 先警告再强制结束；正常 `--stop` 输出不含 Warning
- **13.9 分钟 / 40 次采样受控监视，daemon 存活 40、消失 0**，其间刻意施压（6 次外部数据目录起 daemon、两轮僵尸清理、20 秒阻塞 exec、完整 MCP 会话）。对比 0.3.3 同条件下死过两次（6.5 / 10.5 分钟）
- wheel ↔ 源码树逐字节一致；37/37；MCP 53 工具、失败均 `isError`

## 仍未修（发布说明如实写）

- **`click_index` 静默空点**：复核冒烟里又撞到一次，间歇性、与窗口前置强相关，`0×0` 防护抓不到。非本版回归，单独跟。
- **daemon 无声消失**：已知的那条杀人路径已封死并有用例守着；但复核者在架起监视之前有 **1 次**无法归因、无法复现的消失（操作序列原样重跑后安然无恙，且不排除是与我并发测试的干扰）。样本不足以断言「不存在其它路径」，所以措辞仍是「根因已定位其一 + 加了留痕」。

body:
NO-DECISION: @zach picked the ladder 2026-08-18; this finishes the BLIND and GAP conversions #490 and #491 began


#491 said it covered "the eleven scripts that still spelled BLIND as 3". That
count came from grepping for `3 BLIND` in exit-code tables, so it only found
scripts that DOCUMENT the code there. Six more spell it in code with no table,
and I only went looking because two cases had been scoped out by hand.

They were not one thing. 3 meant four different things:

  BLIND -> 6   directive-prose.sh   "the range or the diff could not be read"
               session-marker.sh    resolve_blind
               selfdev-credentials.sh  "could not reach $CRED_HOST at all"

  GAP -> 4     shellcheck-lint.sh   "the tree is not clean, it is HELD" --
                                    in scope, not done yet, the same argument
                                    #490 made for its three
               install-honey-plugin.sh  missing installs under --check

  BLIND, spelled 2 -> 6   deploy-drift.sh. Its heredoc returns 3 to its own
               reader, which translated that into `exit 2` while SAYING BLIND
               in the message. That is #490's usage/blind collision again, in
               a script that had no usage exit to collide with -- so nothing
               ever surfaced it. The remote 3 STAYS: it is private between the
               heredoc and its reader and never reaches a caller.

A THIRD ASSERTION OF THE SAME CODE, in a suite I would not have run:
`conf.test.sh` pins session-marker's BLIND independently of
`session-marker.test.sh`. One exit code, two suites. Only a full-glob sweep
finds that, and my earlier sweeps had the wrong glob -- `*.test.sh`, where
this repo also has `*-test.sh`. Fixed in #491; the lesson repeated here.

STILL NOT CONVERTED, and each needs its own change rather than a sweep:

  gh-sign.sh          3 on a grammar refusal is REFUSED, which is 7. It is an
                      agent-facing contract on EVERY write path in the estate,
                      so it moves deliberately or not at all.
  sunset-coordinator-files.sh   spends 3 on both `die()` and a --help path.
                      Those are BROKEN (5) and usage (2), two codes, and
                      picking one for both is what got us here.

Suites: every suite in bin/tests green under CI's glob, including the six
touched here and conf.test.sh. Prose at parity, paid from directive-prose's
own pattern-derivation table.

author: jmccrae
body:
## Summary
- Adds `Lexicon::resolve_deprecation`, which follows `deprecations.csv` merge chains to whatever synset currently holds an id's content, resolving multi-hop merges and staying existence-aware at every hop (needed to safely handle a real cycle in `deprecations.csv` where one of the two mutually-deprecated ids is actually still live).
- `/synset/{id}` (content negotiation), `/rdf/synset/{id}`, `/ttl/synset/{id}`, and `/xml/synset/{id}` now permanently redirect (308) a deprecated id to the superseding synset's URL, e.g. `en-word.net/synset/01916702-v` → `en-word.net/view/synset/01923704-v`, matching the example in the issue.
- `/view/synset/{id}` gets the same redirect via a new axum middleware (`synset_view_redirects_and_404` in `main.rs`), since the SSR page component has no way to set the HTTP response status/redirect itself.
- An id that doesn't resolve to any synset now returns a real 404 status on all of the above, instead of a "Not found"/"No synset found" page served with 200.

Closes #40.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p ewe_lib` — includes 7 new unit tests for `resolve_deprecation` (single/multi-hop chains, dead ends, both cycle variants, and a regression test reproducing the real `deprecations.csv` cycle found during manual testing)
- [x] `cargo test` for `ewe_dioxus` with `--features server`

author: cgreeno
body:
Re-lands the test from [#57](https://github.com/cgreeno/temporalex/pull/57), which **never reached main** despite GitHub marking it merged.

#57 was stacked on `fix/defactivity-arg-shapes`. That branch merged to main at 09:44:31; #57 merged into it at 09:44:41 — ten seconds later, into a branch that was already dead. GitHub reports "merged" because it merged into its *base*, which by then was not on the path to main.

So main currently has the weak version of the test:

```elixir
test "an ignored arg does not collide with a real one of the same name" do
  assert Temporalex.Testing.run_activity(Shapes, :collides, [:ignored, :kept]) == {:ok, :kept}
end
```

That asserts through `Temporalex.Testing.run_activity/4`, which applies `activity.implementation` directly and never touches the generated dispatch wrapper — and the wrapper head is where the collision was. It passes with the bug present, which I proved by reverting the fix.

This restores the workflow-driven version, which fails with `expected a scheduled activity, but no commands are queued` when the fix is reverted, and keeps the direct call as its own test for what it genuinely covers: the implementation still sees the author's argument names.

Verified: 49 tests, 0 failures in the activity surface suite.

body:
## Summary

S4 PR2 (issue #191) — the materialized-aggregates half of S4, second slice after PR #340's `event_consumer.py` + `repo_events` table (merged). Adds `repo_event_daily_counts`, a per-tenant/repo/event_type/UTC-day rollup, upserted by the same consumer that writes `repo_events`.

**Schema change included:** migration `0037` adds one new table (`repo_event_daily_counts`), composite primary key `(tenant_id, repo, event_type, day)` (no surrogate id/sequence — this table is purely an upsert target, nothing references it by foreign key), RLS-enabled (ENABLE only, no FORCE, matching migration `0036`'s precedent), plus conditional grants for `clevis_worker` and `clevis_api` mirroring `0036`'s pattern exactly. Purely additive, zero data-loss risk — nothing reads this table yet.

## What changed and why

- **`apps/api/alembic/versions/0037_add_repo_event_daily_counts.py`** — the migration described above.
- **`apps/api/src/core/db.py`** — `RepoEventDailyCount` SQLAlchemy model mirroring the migration.
- **`apps/worker/src/event_consumer.py`** — `_process_entry`'s `repo_events` insert now uses `RETURNING id`, and only when a row was actually inserted (not a deduped redelivery) does it upsert the matching `repo_event_daily_counts` row (`ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET count = count + 1`), in the same transaction. This gating is what keeps the aggregate idempotent — GitHub redelivering the same webhook must not double-count it.
- **`docker/provision-api-role-existing-deployment.sh`** and **`docs/self-hosting.md`** — extended with the same grant pattern already established for `repo_events`, for the same reason (CI runs `apps/worker/tests` under `clevis_api`, since there's no `clevis_worker` CI provisioning).
- **`apps/worker/tests/test_event_consumer.py`** — new tests: fresh event produces a `count=1` row, a second distinct event on the same day increments to `2`, reprocessing the same `delivery_id` leaves the count unchanged, and events on different UTC days produce separate rows.

**Deliberately out of scope, discussed and decided directly with the requester:** no dashboard or API endpoint reads these aggregates yet (that's S6's job) — `repo_events` has no backfill yet (S5) and webhook config is optional per self-hosted org, so repointing any read now would show a misleadingly thin result for orgs without webhook history. Per-actor rollups (useful later for Collaborators dashboards) are also not added speculatively — no concrete consumer for them yet.

## Test plan

- [x] `alembic upgrade head` applies cleanly on top of `0036`; `alembic check` reports no model/migration drift
- [x] `pytest -q apps/worker/tests/test_event_consumer.py` — 30 tests pass, including the 4 new aggregate cases
- [x] Full `pytest -q` — 680 passed, 3 skipped, 3 xpassed, against a freshly reset local Postgres + a locally-mapped Redis
- [x] `bun run check` (typecheck + lint + build) — clean, enforced by the `pre-commit`/`pre-push` hooks on this PR's commit

## Summary

Add a concise design philosophy to `commands-src/AGENTS.md`, the source of truth already read by the repository-local `canonicalize-skill` workflow when creating or editing `q-*` skills.

The principles establish that a skill should:

- govern recurring consequential decisions or state transitions, not re-teach ordinary agent work;
- default to agent freedom and add only justified constraints;

author: origami74
body:
## The problem

Wi-Fi Aware carried exactly one peer. Not a chipset limit — a Pixel 7 Pro advertises 8 concurrent data paths and a Galaxy A52s 2, against the one Myco held.

The lane had **one UDP socket**, and `Network.bindSocket` marks a socket for exactly one `android.net.Network`. Every NDP is its own network, so the most recent bind blackholed every other peer with its data path still established. Given that, `dataPathBlockedBy` refused a second NDP outright — correct behaviour for a design that could not have carried it.

Investigation: `reference/aware-multipeer-limit.md` (gitignored, local).

## What this does

**A pool of UDP transport instances**, `aware0…aware<n>` on ports 4872+, bound at node start and unconditionally on Android — so the Wi-Fi Aware toggle still never rebuilds the node. Fixed rather than grown on demand because fips builds its transports from config at start and cannot add one at runtime.

**Sized to the chipset.** Kotlin reads `Characteristics.getNumberOfSupportedDataPaths()` and reports it; the core persists it and binds that many, clamped 1–8. The A52s stops holding sockets it can never use; the Pixel gets all 8.

Persisted rather than applied live, because the pool is bound when the node starts and the capability is not readable then — `getCharacteristics()` returns null with Wi-Fi off, and the call needs API 33 against our minSdk of 29. Last launch's answer off disk is what makes the number available at the one moment it is needed. A first launch that cannot read it uses 4.

**A socket per peer.** `AwareRadio` holds a `UdpSocketPin` per instance; `AwareSlotPool` gives each peer a slot; that slot's socket is pinned to that peer's data path. The peer is pushed under the lane label `"aware<slot>"`, which the core turns into the qualified transport `"udp/aware2"` — so fips dials the socket marked for *that* peer's network and refuses rather than substituting another.

**The local gate came out.** `dataPathBlockedBy` now refuses only when the pool is full, with the framework's availability count still a backstop (it reported `dataPaths=7` free throughout a run of instant refusals, so it is not trusted alone). A slot is claimed when a data path is *requested* and surrendered when it drops or is given up on, so a peer that walks out mid-negotiation does not keep a socket.

## The part that needed a protocol decision

Each pooled socket has its own port, so a slot cannot be a purely local choice — **the peer has to be told which port to dial**.

It rides the existing `"<npub>|<port>"` identity payload. The shape is unchanged, so builds from before the pool still parse it, and a peer that advertises no port at all is still dialled at the legacy port.

A peer discovered before its identity is known (the Aware match carries no npub) is told the **base port, which is slot 0**. So a pair of phones is exact with no correction at all; a third is corrected one message later; and a correction that lands after the data path is already up re-pushes the peer at its new address — `platform_peers` suppresses re-pushes by `(npub, address)`, so a changed port is not swallowed.

Both sides now answer an identity, which needed a termination rule: the answer is sent **only when our port changed or theirs did**. An echo gets nothing back, so the exchange ends on its own — without a marker in the payload that older builds could not parse — and a peer that restarted its radio and is reintroducing itself at the base port still gets an answer rather than the silence a stale entry would earn it.

## One subtlety worth reviewing

`wifiAware.slots` in the state reports the pool the **running node bound**, not what the settings would produce. The radio allocates slots from that number, so reporting a pending larger value would have it pin `aware5` — an instance never bound, whose fd never arrives and whose dial fips would refuse. A capability arriving under a running node therefore changes nothing until the next start, which also keeps a live mesh from being torn down for it.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p myco-core` — 152 pass. New: lane→instance mapping for every slot, the legacy bare `"aware"` label, unknown-lane fallback, lane-family strip, the capability clamp table, and a persistence test that asserts a report does *not* resize the running pool but does size the next one.
- `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` — 8 new `AwareSlotPoolTest` cases (no two peers share a slot, a full pool refuses rather than reusing, release/re-acquire, first peer lands on slot 0).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `./gradlew assembleDebug` — clean. `Cargo.lock` unperturbed.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on `main` already (`content.rs`, `remote_backend.rs`, `lane_observation.rs`, `runtime.rs:985`, vendored fips). No new findings in the changed code; left alone as out-of-footprint.

## On-device

Verified on a Pixel 7 Pro with one peer — all instances bound, the slot-qualified transport routed the dial, and the Noise session established:

```
UDP transport started name=aware0 local_addr=[::]:4872
telling npub1ne8uwap… to dial us on 4872 (slot 0)
Aware NDP up to npub1ne8uwap… at [fe80::7d:65ff:feed:6b16%379]:4872 (slot 0)
pinned aware0 UDP socket to 1222
API connect … transport=udp/aware0
Session established (responder, XK) src=npub1ne8u…8v94
```

**Not yet exercised: more than one concurrent Aware peer.** Two phones both land on slot 0, so the correction path and pool exhaustion are untested on hardware — that needs a third device. Host tests cannot cover any of it; the NDP lifecycle and identity exchange only regress on physical devices.

**Also still unexplained:** the framework's ~3ms `onUnavailable` for a second peer, seen before this change. It was attributed to a `dumpsys` metrics field that turned out to be a high-water mark, not a limit. This removes *our* ceiling; whether an Android policy limit sits behind it is now measurable, since every NDP log line carries `slots=<held>/<pool>` next to the framework's `dataPaths=<free>`.

Implements Phase 10 of the generalized Evidence Graph.

- adds a typed `DeviationAdapter` over normalized installed-game Deviation evidence
- canonical identity is exact `deviation_base_data` source ID (`ds-dev-<id>`); display names are browse aliases only
- preserves same-name source variants as distinct entities and exposes browse-family membership without promoting the name into proof
- proves abilities only when exact `skill_ids` resolve to `deviation_skills_data`; embedded skill text without IDs stays PARTIAL
- preserves containment, mood, temperature, quality/power/balance coefficients from source records without inventing formulas
- preserves raw `territory_effects` and `meme_ids` as PARTIAL evidence only; no player-facing trait edge is created without a typed definition owner
- keeps acquisition UNRESOLVED until a typed vendor/drop/reward owner is found
- keeps scenario availability UNRESOLVED; `meme_ids` are explicitly not scenario proof
- registers/searches Deviation variants directly from `published/data/deviations.json`, independent of compact web publication
- adds false-proof tests for same-name variants, name lookup rejection, exact skill ownership, embedded-text partial state, raw trait handles, scenario gating, acquisition, registry routing, and publication-authority isolation

No generated outputs, `tools/miner.zip`, raw snapshots, or website publication authority are changed.

author: adamsalah13
body:
Four Phase-G producer / data-integrity findings from `docs/tasks/cupe-review-findings-2026-08-19.md`, taken together because they are one theme: **a run that declined to do work could say so in a way nobody could read.**

## 1. The `clusters` snapshot was write-once and the draft was not

The row was built on FIRST INSERT and never touched again, while step 6 re-authored the canonical on every run. So re-ordering `templates_harmonized` flipped a mixed cluster's draft from JDFN to WJQ and left the snapshot claiming the **old form and the old member list** — and the Library reads that snapshot to answer *"which documents is this role drawn from?"*.

HR would have read a CUPE role whose sources were listed as **APSA documents**, with nothing saying the two disagreed. Both rows are derived from the same members on the same run: they move together or the provenance is a lie (NN #6).

Pinned by an integration test that runs twice with the order reversed and asserts the row follows the canonical. It cannot reach a human artifact — the composer mints its rows under `uuid4` with `origin: composed` while this id is content-derived, and every skip path returns long before step 5.

## 2. The counters partition, and the identity is a validator rather than a sentence

The docstring claimed `persisted + refreshed + skipped + failed == clusters_seen`. True when written; false by the time it was read, because two skip counters were added underneath it. Three cluster shapes also fell through every counter, so a run could decline work and report a total that looked complete.

Both identities are now `model_validator`s:

```
clusters_seen       == the six outcome buckets
clusters_recomputed == entered + the four explicit reasons for not entering
```

with `clusters_no_authorable_template` / `clusters_no_members_loaded` added for the shapes that had no name. **A docstring can go stale; a validator goes red.**

Two more in the same family:
- `clusters_mixed_jdfn_wjq` counted mixed only when the winner was *not* WJQ — so putting `wjq` first would have reported every mixed cluster as un-mixed. It now counts by membership.
- `wjq_members_authored` was incremented off the cluster's **form**, before the cluster was processed — so a resumed pass that skipped everything still reported thousands of members "authored". It now counts only members that fed a draft this run **wrote**, with the remainder in `wjq_members_unwritten`.

## 3. `--resume --allow-downgrade` is refused instead of silently doing nothing

The two flags ask opposite things about the same rows: `--resume` skips every cluster holding a landed rewrite, which is exactly the set `--allow-downgrade` exists to overwrite. Resume was tested first, so it won every time, the re-baseline never happened, and the run **exited 0**.

There is no correct winner to pick — picking one would be guessing which half of a contradiction was meant — so the CLI exits 2 with an explanation.

## 4. ⚠ The fourth finding is NOT reachable — measured while writing the test for it

*"A member dropped by `load_member_jds` is invisible per cluster"* describes a path that cannot be taken. Both loaders read the same `parsed_jds` rows through `SFUJobDescription.model_validate`, but `load_signed_corpus` (clustering) must **also** build `JobSignals`, so it accepts a strict subset: a row that fails the member load already failed to *sign* and was never in a cluster to be dropped from.

So `member_rows_dropped_unvalidatable` is **structurally zero** for the producer — the same class of dead parameter as `thresholds.wjq.duties_max: 12`. The loss is real but happens earlier and is already counted as `documents_unsignable`, which an integration test now pins (corrupt row → `unsignable=1`, member drops=0, `clusters_recomputed=0`).

A per-cluster `members_unloadable` is added to the snapshot anyway as defence in depth: the two loaders are separate functions with separate validation, and only their current coupling makes this safe.

**Recorded as measured-unreachable rather than closed, because nothing was fixed** — what changed is that we now know why it never fires.

## Verification

- **Gates: 2,839 passing, 94.23%** — full suite incl. integration, re-run locally.
- No rulebook change: `rules_version` untouched, no register entry. None of this decides how a JD is scored or approved; it decides what a run is able to tell you.

⚠ CI is currently blocked repo-wide on GitHub Actions billing, so the local run is the evidence.
