author: os-zhuang
body:
Fixes #10832

`content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx` handed the reader a **method, a path and a payload
contract** for a route that is not mounted. That is the same defect class as #10710, one
level worse: the earlier card advertised a *behaviour*, this one advertised an *endpoint*.

## The three facts, re-measured at this base (`origin/main` @ `5f2e54cc66`)

| Claim the pages make | What the tree says |
|:---|:---|
| `POST /graphql` is a servable route | **Not mounted.** `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts:2026` is the whole of it: `// /graphql removed — GraphQL is not in the product plan (#2462 follow-on).` |
| the platform serves it when a plugin is installed | **No `createGraphQLDomain`** anywhere in `packages/*/src` (0 hits); the fifteen domains at `http-dispatcher.ts:556-574` do not include one. |
| `src/api/` contains a GraphQL module | **Zero graphql files** in `packages/spec/src/api/` (re-measured: 68 files, 0 named graphql). The one string hit is `protocol.zod.ts:105`, a docblock naming GraphQL as an industry *design style* — not a module. |

## Remove vs. rewrite — reasoned per site, not applied uniformly

`packages/runtime/src/domains/unavailable.ts` draws the line: **404** = "the route is not
there"; **501** = "the route is there, the implementation is not", and every 501 domain is
mounted *unconditionally*. `/graphql` is in **neither** state. So a construct whose job is to
*enumerate servable routes* must lose the entry entirely — rewriting it to "not available"
would still assert GraphQL was a surface worth listing. That is why #10710 deleted its
status-table row.

But the card is right that a mermaid node and a prose enumeration are not the same object,
so the sites split two ways:

**Deleted — the construct itself asserts a surface that does not exist:**

- `api/plugin-endpoints.mdx` — the entire `### GraphQL (/graphql) — Plugin Required` section
  and its `POST /graphql` method/path table, plus GraphQL from the frontmatter enumeration
  at `:3`. A table headed *Method | Endpoint | Description* is a promise that the row is callable.
- `api/declarative-endpoints.mdx` — `/graphql` from the exemplar list pointing at that
  catalog. The two survivors (`/auth`, `/automation`) are real mounted domains.
- `protocol/diagram.mdx` — the `GQL[GraphQL]` node **and both its edges** (`CLIENT --> GQL`,
  `GQL --> KERNEL`). Deleting only the declaration would not have been enough: **mermaid
  materialises an undeclared node from a dangling edge**, so the box would still render, now
  without its label.
- `protocol/diagram.mdx` — GraphQL from the `src/api/` layer-table cell.

**Rewritten — the surrounding claim is true; only the enumeration was wrong:**

- `protocol/diagram.mdx:163` sequence label → `HTTP Request (REST)`. The request is real; the
  parenthetical listed one transport too many.
- `protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx:70` → `Start HTTP server`. Phase 6 genuinely starts a server.
  ASCII box width preserved (all Phase-6 rows remain byte-identical in length to their siblings).
- `protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx:10` → `(HTTP, WebSocket)`. The error protocol does span
  the remaining surfaces.

Wording precedent followed: `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx:53`, which already
says `/graphql` now 404s and is left untouched.

## Sibling PR

**#10828's diff was read before editing** (its three files: `api/index.mdx`,
`data-modeling/fields.mdx`, `getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`). It is **disjoint by file**
from all five files here — no overlap, no shared hunk. One correction to the dispatch premise:
that PR is **still open and unmerged** (base `a7ea3289eb`, the previous `main`), so its changes
are *not* in `origin/main` @ `5f2e54cc66`; the three `api/index.mdx` GraphQL sites this branch
leaves alone are its work, not residue.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` derived **15 families** from the changed paths — including
`check:error-status-conformance`, which the dispatch clue list did not name and which matches
only via `protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`. All 15 green at **`451fe92153`**, the head of
this branch. Exit codes captured by redirect before any pipe, never off a `tail`; each log
verified to carry real output, so no `pnpm --filter` zero-match could pass as green. Their own
verdict lines:

- `check:doc-anchors` — *"272 internal #fragment link(s) across 408 source file(s) all resolve to a real heading"* — the deleted `###` heading broke no anchor (independently confirmed: no `#graphql` fragment exists anywhere in `content/`).
- `check:error-status-conformance` — *"every derivable runtime status is documented, and every documented status is reachable."*
- `check:doc-authoring` — *"389 files clean — no bare metadata literals."*
- `check-doc-frontmatter` — *"403 page(s) under content/docs parse with yaml@2.9.0"*
- `check:docs-audit-scope` — *"scope is in sync with content/docs/: 189 hand-written doc(s)"*
- `check:docs-redirects` — *"OK (apps/docs/redirects.mjs: 92 entries ...)"*
- `check:doc-formula-expressions` — *"self-test: 30 cases passed"*, *"22 record-scoped formula example(s) ... judged clean"*
- `check:role-word` — *"OK, no new occurrences of the reserved word."*
- `check:published-readme-links` — *"165 outbound link(s) across 60 published markdown file(s)"*
- plus `check:cross-package-test-inputs` (×2, pnpm + direct node) and `spec/check:{empty-state,liveness,strictness-ledger,variant-docs}`.

`check:quick-reference-counts` is **not** in the derived set here — it keys on
`quick-reference.mdx`, which is #10828's file and not in this diff.

No ablation applies: this is a docs-only change with no guard under test.

**No changeset** — decided from the real file list, not defaulted. All five files are under
`content/`, which matches **no** glob in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`packages/*`, `apps/*`,
`examples/*`, …), and its only consumer `apps/docs` (`@objectstack/docs`) is `private: true`.
This publishes nothing ⇒ `skip-changeset`.

## Deliberately not touched

- `packages/**` — out of scope for this card. The code is correct; the docs were wrong.
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx:724` — a comparison to other ecosystems, not a claim
  about our surface.
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx:53` — already correct; it is the precedent.
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx:17,97` and `getting-started/index.mdx:99` —
  already correct: they state GraphQL was *removed*.
- `content/docs/references/**` — generated, filed against the generator during #10710's triage.
- `skills/**` and its mirror `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx:156` — GraphQL residue found
  in five places, but the source of truth is `skills/**`, which is governed/human-merge-only.
  Filed separately rather than patching the consumer page into disagreement with the skill it
  catalogs.

author: gbcreation
body:
## Summary
- `resume_watch` has its own 600s `MAX_WAIT` safety timeout, and Claude Code appears to re-fire `permission_prompt` periodically as a nudge while a prompt sits unanswered.
- Every repeat was correctly treated as a no-op (consistent with the same repeat-leaves-timers-untouched logic that already protects `idle_timer` for `Waiting`/`Done`/`Compacting`), but that meant nothing ever noticed `resume_watch` quietly dying at the 600s mark.
- Once dead, nothing was polling the screen for that session anymore, so the tab stayed stuck on `permission` indefinitely, until some unrelated hook happened to supersede it.
- Confirmed live twice: one session stuck 14+ hours (`Stop` finally fired the next day), another stuck 20+ minutes with 11 repeated nudges arriving after `resume_watch` had already given up.
- `Permission` is now excluded from the "leave repeats untouched" rule (`old_state == Some(state) && state != State::Permission`). A repeated `permission_prompt` falls through to the same abort-then-arm path a genuine transition takes, restarting `resume_watch` fresh every time so it can never die while Claude Code keeps asking.

## Test plan
- [x] 65 tests pass (new: `repeated_permission_message_restarts_resume_watch`)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] Verified live end-to-end against the real daemon: entering `Permission`, a repeat (now logged as "session state updated" rather than "repeated, timers untouched"), and resolution all worked correctly

author: mizu-jun
body:
## What

Third and last code part of the #62 follow-up (after #69 and #70): the close-window dialog's Kill/Cancel buttons, and the consent dialog's selected-button fill.

| Site | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Kill at rest | `[0.75, 0.25, 0.25]` | `danger_fill(tokens, 0.55)` |
| Kill selected | `[0.95, 0.40, 0.40]` | `danger_fill(tokens, 0.85)` |
| Cancel selected | `[0.95, 0.85, 0.40]` | `caution_fill(tokens, 0.85)` |
| Consent selected | raw `semantic_warning` | `caution_fill(tokens, 0.85)` |
| Selected-button label (both dialogs) | `[0.10, 0.10, 0.10]` fixed | `on_surface_text(fill)` |

## Why Kill does not reuse #70's helper

`danger_button_colors` answers *"is this button focused"* — it steps from a barely-tinted rest state to a mid blend, which is right for a settings delete button that only turns red once you land on it. Kill has to read as the destructive choice **before** it is selected, because it sits next to Cancel. So it steps from that same mid blend to a strong one. Sharing the blend and *not* the focused/unfocused rule is what keeps both readings intact.

## What the measurement changed

The labels are the substance here. A fixed near-black label is wrong on any dark fill, so labels now come from `on_surface_text` (added in #69). Measuring that across all nine built-in schemes turned up something no fixed blend strength can fix:

| Fill | Scheme | Best either extreme manages |
|---|---|---|
| `semantic_error` at 0.85 | Nord | **4.42:1** ❌ |
| `semantic_warning` used raw | Solarized | **4.37:1** ❌ |

Both are middling luminances — neither a near-black nor a near-white label has anything to contrast with. (This is also why `caution_fill` blends instead of passing the token straight through.)

`semantic_fill` therefore walks the blend back toward `surface_1` until the label clears `MIN_TEXT_CONTRAST` — the same shape as `row::ensure_readable`. It terminates because `surface_1` derives from the scheme background, the end of the range a label can always be read against. The trade: some schemes get a slightly quieter fill than requested. An unreadable label on a destructive button is worse.

The consent dialog's 3 px top stripe and its title keep the raw warning hue — a line and text, not a fill.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean through every crate
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — all pass, 0 failures (909 in this crate)
- [x] Re-verified after rebasing onto merged `master`
- [x] Two new tests. One pins **every fill/label pair the dialogs paint, across all nine built-in schemes, at 4.5:1** — this is the test that forced `caution_fill` to exist, and it fails on Nord if the adaptive step is removed (verified by removing it). The other pins that a stronger blend always reads as redder, since that ordering is what carries both "dangerous" and "selected"
- [ ] **On-device visual check — not run.** Joins the accepted-unverified backlog in `docs/plans/ui-ux-modernization-v3.md`. Worth a look: whether the adaptive step-back leaves Kill visibly red enough on Nord, and the Cancel-selected fill now that it is blended rather than a flat yellow

## G11 follow-up after this PR

Everything the plan listed is now migrated except two items, both deliberate: `picker.rs`'s purple/green macro & SSH branding (its comments call it intentional — needs a product decision, not a mechanical migration) and `color_util::resolve_color`'s no-palette fallbacks (unreachable outside tests, explained in #69). A plan update recording this follows separately.

author: hiddenitachi0
body:
## Summary
- A cheap/status-only recovery run that hit the `resumeRequiresNormalModel` guard while trying to file an approval had no way forward — it just got refused, wrote a comment, and the issue sat `blocked` for days with finished, unmerged work behind it (this happened for real on 19 August).
- Every place that guard blocks a mutation now automatically hands the action off: it schedules a normal-model follow-up run on the same issue/agent, and leaves a plain-language comment recording that it happened, how many times, and roughly what it cost. This is fully automatic — the agent doesn't need to know about or call anything new.
- `PATCH /issues/:id` additionally catches every attempt by a cheap/status-only run to set an issue to `blocked`, and redirects it into the same hand-off instead of ever persisting `status: "blocked"` for that reason.
- The hand-off is bounded so it can't loop: it's idempotent per (issue, source run) — a repeat attempt from the same run never enqueues a second follow-up — and capped at 3 escalations per issue for its whole lifetime. Once capped, blocking is allowed again, but with a distinguishable reason an operator can tell apart from "needs a bigger model."
- Signal used (and why the classification side of this wasn't touched): the ticket also asked to stop classifying a wake as "cheap" in the first place when the next step is an approval/PR/merge. I looked at doing this via a heuristic (recent-comment text matching "PR"/"approval"/"merge" phrasing), but decided against it — it's the kind of thing that's easy to get subtly wrong in either direction, and the reactive hand-off above already fully closes the loop regardless of how the run was classified going in. So this PR relies entirely on the reactive fix rather than a classification-time guess.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] New unit tests for the decision logic and the DB-touching orchestration (`cheap-run-escalation.test.ts`, plus additions to `model-profile-hint.test.ts`) covering: enqueue on first block, idempotent no-op on repeat attempts from the same run, capped-at-lifetime-limit behavior, and graceful failure (no throw, no partial state) if scheduling the follow-up wake errors.
- [x] Route-level tests added to `approval-routes-idempotency.test.ts` proving a blocked approval creation triggers a real escalation wake and that a repeat attempt doesn't double-enqueue.
- [x] Full existing suites for the touched routes (`approval-routes-idempotency.test.ts`, `issue-agent-mutation-ownership-routes.test.ts`) pass — one pre-existing, unrelated timeout failure confirmed present on `custom` before this change too.

author: hiteyy
body: ## Problem Mainnet deploy [run 32485466353](https://github.com/PIXELZX0/SERIES9DEX/actions/runs/32485466353) reported **failure** after deploying the full stack successfully and passing every on-chain assertion. The failure was `exit code 22` — curl's "HTTP error". `forge verify-contract` submits verification as an **async job**. The readback loop queries the contract straight afterwards, gets `404` while Sourcify is still processing, and `curl -sf` returns non-zero. Under `set -euo pipefail` that aborts the step. All eight contracts were verified (`match`) when queried a few minutes later — nothing was actually wrong. ## Fix - Drop `-f` so an HTTP error returns the body instead of a non-zero exit - Tolerate a failed request (`|| true`) and a non-JSON body - Retry up to 6 times with 10s backoff, breaking as soon as it matches - Add `--max-time 20` so a hung endpoint cannot stall the job Unverified contracts still produce a `::warning`, exactly as before. Verification is discoverability, not correctness — the on-chain wiring and ownership assertions in the previous step are what gate the deploy, and those already passed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? author: oleksiitsybulskyi-sima
body:
## Summary

- add `ensure_edgematic_studio_installed()` beside the Model Compiler extension step, offered directly after it and honouring `-y` / `--noninteractive`
- install from the production Vulcan artifact `edgematic-studio/<arch>@main` with no `sima-cli login` step, since Vulcan artifacts are unauthenticated
- publish Studio's HTTP port when the Neat SDK container is created, and print the reachable URL in the setup summary
- start Studio after a successful install so the printed URL is live; a failure to start warns and prints the command instead of failing setup
- add `--no-edgematic-studio` (alias `--no-studio`); `--minimal` and `--no-insight` skip Studio too
- add `edgematic-studio` to `DEFAULT_REPOSITORIES` and `NEAT_INSTALL_REPOSITORIES`

## Why the port is published at create time

Docker port maps are immutable after create, and the extension prompt runs later, in `configure_container`. So the mapping cannot be conditional on the user's answer — it is published whenever Studio _may_ be installed, gated only by `--no-edgematic-studio` / `--no-insight` / `--minimal`. A declined install leaves one idle binding, which is harmless, and publishing unconditionally also makes a hand-installed Studio reachable — today that requires a separate `socat` forwarder container.

This only affects the create path, which is where it matters: the existing-container branch of `setup_and_start` calls `configure_container_user`, never `configure_container`, so extension installs and port publishing always happen together.

The install outcome is relayed back through `configure_container` so a declined prompt does not leave the summary advertising a URL nothing is serving — the same idiom as the existing `code_ui_supported` flag.

## Notes

- **Studio's host port may drift** to the 18000-30000 range if 8088 is taken. Verified safe: Studio's WS origin guard compares `Origin` against the request's `Host`, so a remapped host port passes and a spoofed one is refused.
- **Auto-start needs `bash -ic`, not `bash -lc`.** The installer defines `activate-edgematic-studio` as a shell function in `~/.bashrc`, and the stock `.bashrc` returns early when non-interactive (`case $- in *i*) ;; *) return;; esac`), so a login shell does not see the function. `-t` gives it a PTY, which suppresses bash's job-control warnings.
- **The terminal sidecar range (8761-8770) is not published.** Those ports are handed to the browser container-side and only work identity-mapped; publishing ten more is a separate decision. The summary states the limitation rather than leaving the feature to fail silently.
- **Unrelated pre-existing doc drift:** `python -m scripts.generate_cli_markdown_docs` also rewrites `sima-cli-device.md`, `sima-cli.md` and `index.md` from a `device` docstring change that was never regenerated. Those are reverted here to keep the diff focused; `--check` already exits 1 on a clean `develop`.

## Validation

- `pytest -q tests/unit` — 568 passed, 26 subtests (`develop` baseline: 539 passed). The 46 `test_vulcan.py` failures are pre-existing and identical on a clean tree — they assert `exit_code == 0` while the CLI's self-update check reports 2.1.15 → 2.1.16.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_sdk_image_detection.py -k "edgematic or studio"` — 29 passed
- `python -m compileall -q sima_cli`, `git diff --check` — clean
- `python -m scripts.generate_cli_markdown_docs` — `sima-cli-sdk-setup.md` regenerated

End to end on a real host (`ghcr.io/sima-neat/sdk:latest`, amd64, deliberate non-identity map `18088 -> 8088`):

- install resolved and completed from production Vulcan; auto-start reported success
- `GET /` and `GET /version` returned 200 from the host browser
- `/version` reported `studio 2.1.2.1-main.e969d8461d35`, `sima_cli 2.1.16`, `sdk platform 2.1.3`
- re-activation stayed idempotent — one daemon, same pid
- WS origin guard checked directly: no Origin -> 101, matching host port -> 101, spoofed container port -> 403, foreign origin -> 403

Still worth confirming on a machine with agent credentials: that a Studio agent chat turn completes end to end. Everything up to and including a correct `/version` is verified above.

Closes #157

author: wkalt
body:
Two bugs in Node's reading of the embedding_functions schema metadata.

First, parseFunctions keyed its result map by function name, so a table whose metadata configures the same function for two vector columns came back with only the last one. It now keys by the vector column, the convention Python's parser already uses.

Second, Node could not read metadata written by the Python bindings at all, which spell the keys snake_case: configs parsed with both columns undefined, breaking embedding application on add() and leaving only query-side embedding working. The parse now accepts both spellings.

Both fixes land in one shared parser used by every reader -- parseFunctions and the makeArrowTable schema validator, which had its own private camelCase-only parse -- so the wire contract cannot fork between entry points. A config naming no source or vector column is an error at the boundary rather than a default downstream, as are two configs claiming one column. The "vector" fallback remains only on the optional field of user-supplied configs.

Breaking: parseFunctions is exported and its map keys change from function name to vector column.

author: ocrosby
body:
## Summary

Two commits, one feature:

1. **Branch detection** — introduces [`github.com/jedi-knights/go-lua-parser`](https://github.com/jedi-knights/go-lua-parser) as a bounded dependency, adds `cover.FindBranches` that parses Lua source and walks the AST to locate branch points (`if`/`elseif`/`while`/`repeat`/`for`), returning `[]Branch` with per-arm body-first-line info.
2. **BRDA emission** — extends the domain with `BranchCoverage` + `BranchArm`, adds `cover.PopulateBranches` that derives per-arm taken counts from existing line hits, and teaches the LCOV reporter to emit `BRDA:<line>,0,<arm>,<taken>` plus `BRF`/`BRH` totals. CLI wires `PopulateBranches` between test execution and report emission.

## Model choices worth flagging

- **Unknown vs. zero.** `Taken == -1` means the arm's hit count cannot be derived from line coverage alone (implicit fall-through in an `if`-without-`else`, or a loop's exit path). LCOV renders these as `-`; they count toward `BRF` but not `BRH`. `Taken == 0` means the arm's body was instrumented but never executed — a real miss.
- **Short-circuit `and`/`or` deferred.** Per-arm hits for short-circuit ops cannot be honestly derived from line coverage, so emitting them would inflate BRF without a matching BRH signal. Skipped until instrumentation exists.
- **Populate ordering.** Runs after `CoverageData.Normalize` (which rebuilds `FileCoverage` and would drop branches) and before `emitReports`. Documented at the call site so the ordering isn't accidentally inverted.

## Docs

- `CLAUDE.md` swim-lane rule gains a carve-out for source-derived coverage analysis.
- `docs/adoption-strategy.md` gets a BRDA note under differentiators and a new \"Companion repos\" section explaining the three properties that justified extracting the parser to its own repo.

## Coverage

- Overall: 91.7% (above the 90% floor)
- New files: 100% (`populate.go`, `branches_test.go`, `populate_test.go`)

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -race -count=1 ./...` — all packages pass
- [x] `golangci-lint run ./...` — 0 issues
- [x] Detector: if/elseif fall-through arms point at the right next-body line
- [x] Detector: if without else leaves the else arm's FirstLine as 0 (unknown)
- [x] Populate: known miss (line hit 0) → Taken=0; unknown arm (FirstLine=0) → Taken=-1
- [x] Populate: missing source file silently skipped, line coverage preserved
- [x] Reporter: BRDA renders \`-\` for unknown arms, integer for known
- [x] Reporter: files with no branches emit no BRDA/BRF/BRH block
- [x] Reporter: BRDA sorted by line then column for deterministic output

author: davidquarel
body:
## What

Content pages (worksheets, homepage, 404) now ship **zero framework JS**. The App Router unconditionally emits, per page, an inline RSC flight payload — a JSON-escaped duplicate of the entire rendered page, ~62% of a worksheet's bytes — plus ~650 KB of React runtime chunks, all to power a sidebar toggle and a checkbox. This PR replaces that with server-rendered markup and ~1.5 KB of vanilla JS.

**Built site: 28.4 → 10.9 MB (−62%).** Singular-learning-theory: 9.45 → 2.85 MB raw, **162 KB gzipped**; AIXI: 8.64 → 2.72 MB.

## How

- **`perf(katex)`** (first commit): KaTeX renders `output: "html"`, dropping the hidden MathML duplicate of every formula (`$A$`: 385 → 194 bytes). Visual tree byte-identical; screen readers get the TeX source as an `aria-label` on the wrapper instead (the visual tree is permanently `aria-hidden`, so MathML was their only path — now the label is). `\gdef`-only macro blocks stay unlabelled.
- **`feat(nostack)`** (second commit):
  - `NavContext`/`NavToggle`/`ModulePageShell`/`SidebarNav`/`DownloadsRow` become server components. Both sidebar layouts live in the served markup; the mode is a `nav-open` class on `<html>` (persisted in localStorage, restored pre-paint by an inline script) with `#page-shell` rules in `globals.css` doing what the conditional JSX did.
  - `public/site.js` is the site's entire client JS: sidebar toggle, close-on-mobile, and the with-solutions href swap (`data-sol`/`data-nosol` pairs on each link).
  - `scripts/strip-hydration.mjs` runs after `next build` (wired into `npm run ci`, standalone as `npm run strip`) and removes the flight-payload scripts and `_next` bundle tags from every page **except `/admin/status`**, which keeps React for the InFlight live-PR overlay. It fails loudly if an unknown script pattern survives, and never touches markup or stylesheets.

## Behaviour changes

- `<Link>` soft navigation is gone on stripped pages — links are plain full-page loads. On a static document site this is arguably correct, and it stops the homepage prefetching multi-MB payloads for links nobody clicked.
- The hamburger no longer renders on pages with no sidebar to toggle (it used to show, inert, on `/admin/status`).
- `/admin/status` is byte-for-byte untouched; its React chunks stay in `out/_next/static/` and are only downloaded by visitors to that page.
- The per-page `index.txt` flight files are still deployed (admin's router expects them); nothing links them from stripped pages, so they cost deploy size, not visitor bandwidth.

## Verified

17 CDP checks against headless Chrome on the stripped export: sidebar toggle/persistence/pre-paint restore, two-column layout, solutions swap, toggle hidden on homepage, `/admin/status` still hydrating (InFlight strip renders, table intact). `next dev` / `run.sh watch` are unaffected — the strip only runs on the static export.

## Risk

A Next upgrade could change the emitted script patterns — that is what the strip script's fail-loudly check is for: the build breaks rather than half-strips.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Description

Raises the supported Python floor from 3.11 to 3.12.

numpy 2.5 and scipy 1.18 already require Python 3.12, so a 3.11 install could only run on a frozen older scientific stack; SPEC 0 dropped 3.11 in Q4 2025. Bumping the floor also lets every CI job share the same interpreter features (in particular coverage's `sys.monitoring` core, which the upcoming CI speed-up PR turns on) and removes the last reason to import `Self` from `typing_extensions`.

Changes:

- `requires-python = ">=3.12"`; the 3.11 classifier is dropped.
- The min-deps matrix in `.github/actions/load-shared-vars` tests 3.12 and 3.14 instead of 3.11 and 3.14, so every claimed version is still exercised.
- Ruff's `target-version` becomes `py312`. Its autofix moved `Self` from `typing_extensions` to `typing` in nine modules. The PEP 695 rules it newly enables (`UP040`, `UP046`, `UP047`, ten sites) are ignored for now so the generics-syntax migration can be a change of its own.
- Two comments that justified workarounds by the 3.11 floor are updated, and `environment.yml` pins `python>=3.12` so the conda dev environment cannot solve to an interpreter pip will then reject. The floor is deliberately not repeated in prose docs (they go stale); `pyproject.toml` is the one statement of it.

Verified locally on a fresh Python 3.12 environment: full suite (`12278 passed`), doctests (`203 passed`), and `pre-commit run --all-files`.

author: zackees
body:
## Summary

soldr#2469 step 2.2. A 29-line inline polling state machine in `release-auto.yml` becomes `.github/scripts/verify_pypi_wheels.py` with unit tests. The inline-run ratchet drops **187 -> 160**.

Two behavioral improvements come with the move, both aimed at the 0.9.0 failure class:

**The expected count now comes from the contract.** The inline block carried `expected=8` with a comment explaining which matrix rows it counted. Step 2.1's point is that the target contract is the single source, so the script asks `release_completeness` instead — adding or removing a target updates the gate for free.

**Wheels are checked by name, not by count.** The inline block compared `len(urls)` against `8`, so eight *wrong* wheels satisfied it. That is precisely how 0.9.0 went wrong: PR #2455 shrank the matrix, the canonical targets, the npm selector, and the tests together, and nothing noticed five targets vanishing because every consumer agreed with the smaller number. A gate that checks names against the contract is independent of the thing it is checking. There is a test for exactly this — the right *number* of wrong wheels must not satisfy the gate.

Both bounds from the inline block are kept (attempt cap and wall-clock deadline) with a test for each, plus one proving the poll stops on first success rather than always exhausting its budget. A 404 still reads as "not yet" rather than an error, since that is the ordinary state while PyPI's read-through cache catches up.

## One existing assertion re-pointed, not dropped

`test_release_musllinux_wheels` asserted `"expected=8" in workflow`. I did not delete it. It now asserts the *derived* value and that the literal is gone. The property that line always cared about was "8, not the 5/6/7 of the incident" — its own stale-marker list spells that out — and the property is now stronger, because it is checked against the contract and by wheel name. Both musllinux wheels are asserted present in the derived set.

## Verification

- full Python suite: **755 passed, 5 skipped**
- `ruff`, `black`, `loc_ratchet`: clean
- ratchet test confirms 160 with zero slack

`tests/test_wheel_lane_policy.py` is excluded from the local run only — it needs PyYAML, which the bare `--no-project` env lacks, and it fails identically on unmodified `main`. CI has it.

Advances #2469.

author: cyrilb1531
body:
Closes #315. No code and no corpus, which is what that issue says closes it:
[ADR 0050](docs/decisions/0050-the-sentencepiece-bpe-lineage-stays-a-bpe-model.md).

## Reading the files answered a question the issue had not asked

#315 asks *"one tokenizer or two, and where `Metaspace` lives"*. Before deciding I read
what the two named models declare, from two ungated mirrors:

| | Llama-2 | Mistral v0.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `normalizer` | `Sequence[Prepend "▁", Replace " "→"▁"]` | `null` |
| `pre_tokenizer` | `null` | `Metaspace{…, prepend_scheme "first", split false}` |

**They do not declare the same thing.** Llama-2 never says `Metaspace`. A design that
taught `BpePreTokenizer` about `Metaspace` — which was my first recommendation — would
have loaded Mistral and **still refused Llama-2**: the half-a-view failure this lot
exists to prevent, invisible from the issue text and cheap to find. Reading a
declaration is not freezing a corpus, so this did not need #318.

What unifies them is `split: false`: Mistral's `Metaspace` does not split, it prepends
and replaces. That is why the normalizer spelling is equivalent, and why the transform
belongs in one place rather than in the pre-tokenizer.

## What the ADR decides

1. **The lineage stays a BPE model** — `LoadBpe` → `BpeVocabulary` → `BpeTokenizer`,
   because that is what `model.type` declares. The loser is a `SentencePieceBpeTokenizer`
   named after the lineage: it was argued from 0017 §3's own worry about picking the
   nearest-sounding class, and it loses because a type name contradicting the file moves
   that ambiguity rather than removing it.
2. **Metaspace is one internal transform**, and **the loader builds it from either
   spelling**. `remove_extra_whitespaces` becomes a flag, because that is what separates
   the existing unigram path from these two — the current ten lines do it and neither
   model asks for it, so sharing them unchanged would apply a transformation nobody
   declared.
3. **`byte_fallback` is reproduced, not refused.** Stated as a decision rather than left
   to #317: an ADR keeping 0017's refusal would describe an endpoint #175 contradicts.
4. **A normalizer `Sequence` that is not exactly `Prepend` + `Replace` stays refused** —
   0017's rule surviving while two of its clauses fall.

## Sequencing, chosen by risk

#316, then #317, then #318 — not the parent's numbering. #316 carries an extraction, and
an extraction must return exactly the same answers; the unigram oracles prove that for
free, but only while nothing else moves in the same lot.

**After #316 both files are still refused**, on `byte_fallback`. The ADR says so, because
otherwise that lot reads as a failure.

## Two things checked rather than assumed

- **`fuse_unk: true`** is declared by both and is *not* a third refusal — already carried
  by `BpeVocabulary.FuseUnk` and pinned by `BpeFuseUnkTests`.
- **`BpeVocabulary` is publicly constructible** with `init` properties, which tests
  already use, so each lot reaches its own code without waiting on the other's refusal —
  #208's constraint that a lot check its corpus reaches the code it is about.

Also corrected in passing: the decisions index said *"All forty-five carry `accepted`"*
for fifty entries.

author: lisascheers
body:
The Toshiba NVMe currently holds the disposable Squid cache while the smaller Kingston SATA SSD holds the projects tree. The desired layout reverses those roles so projects can use XFS over compressed VDO and Squid fits on the SATA SSD.

This change moves the Squid cache declaration to the Kingston SSD, reduces its configured maximum to 190 GB, and declares the Toshiba disk as the `projects` LVM PV. It enables VDO support and adds a manual XFS mount for `/dev/projects/data`. The VDO logical volume remains an explicit migration step because the pinned Disko revision cannot model it safely.

The migration will not run Disko's full destroy graph. The live cutover follows the reviewed migration runbook, including verified file and filesystem-image backups before either disk is reformatted.

Testing:

- `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.nook.config.system.build.toplevel --no-link`
- Alejandra formatting check on both changed files
- targeted Statix and Deadnix checks on both changed files
- inspected the generated fstab, Squid unit, Squid configuration, VDO tooling, and XFS tooling
- `nix flake check` still fails at `flake-parts/hosts/default.nix:229` because `nixosConfigurations.nook.system` does not exist; the same failure reproduces on the base commit

author: boyney123
body:
## What This PR Does

Clarifies that the built-in federation workflow is a paid feature by placing `packages/core/src/federation/` under the EventCatalog Commercial License, shipping the mixed-license terms with the `@eventcatalog/core` package, and enforcing the existing Scale entitlement inside the federation module for every configured run.

## Changes Overview

### Key Changes
- Add a Commercial License file at `packages/core/src/federation/LICENSE` and a license header to every source file in the federation module
- Update the root `LICENSE` and `README.md` to document the mixed-license model (MIT plus commercial directories), and add a package-level `packages/core/LICENSE` so the published npm package carries the full terms
- Add `packages/core/src/federation/entitlement.ts` exposing `isFederationEnabled()`, backed by the existing Scale entitlement (`isEventCatalogScaleEnabled` from `@eventcatalog/license`)
- Move the entitlement check from an injected `isFederationEnabled` option on `federateCatalog` into the federation module itself, so the CLI no longer wires it in and the check cannot be bypassed by omitting the option
- Exclude `LICENSE` files from the tsup build entry glob
- Add `federation-license.spec.ts` verifying every federation source file carries the license header and the LICENSE files exist, and update `federate.spec.ts` for the internal entitlement check
- Add a changeset (`curly-pandas-federate.md`) releasing `@eventcatalog/core` as a patch

## How It Works

`federateCatalog` now calls the module-internal `isFederationEnabled()` before running any configured federation, throwing the existing Enterprise-feature error when the entitlement is missing. The entitlement helper deliberately keeps callers plan-agnostic so federation can later move from the Scale entitlement to an Enterprise offline entitlement without touching the workflow. Cleanup of previous federation output still runs without an entitlement, so a catalog with no federation config is unaffected.

## Breaking Changes

None for MIT-licensed usage. Running `eventcatalog federate` with configured sources now always requires the Scale entitlement — previously the check depended on the caller passing it in (the CLI already did).

## Additional Notes

No corresponding change is needed in the editor repository — this only affects the core package's federation module and repository licensing docs.

author: felipedefensor
body:
Grouping components derived from a pasted hierarchy subtree failed with
`Grouping failed: Grouping component would overlap with existing component.`

Closes #396.

## Reproducing

Reported against a real file. In a hierarchy timeline:

1. Copy the top-level hierarchy of one timeline.
2. Paste it into a single hierarchy of another with **Paste complete**.
3. Create a child in one of the pasted components.
4. Decrease that child's level.
5. Split the child in two.
6. Try to group the two halves.

Expected the halves to be grouped; got the overlap error instead.

## Cause

`_create_child_from_paste_data` rescaled each copied component with arithmetic
that differed between its start and its end: the start was taken relative to the
source parent's **start**, the end relative to the source parent's **end**. A time
appearing in two components — as one's end and the next one's start — therefore
went through different operations and came out a few ulps apart. Nesting
compounded this, since every level re-derived its scale factor from the
already-rounded bounds of the level above.

In the reported file the pasted `Modulation` component starts at
`134.18723783376336` while its left-hand neighbours end at `134.1872378337634` —
4e-14 further right, so arithmetically *inside* the group span. Since the
grouping validators compare boundaries with exact float operators, that
sub-ulp gap read as a real overlap.

## Fix

Three commits, one per concern:

**`fix: keep hierarchy paste-complete boundaries exact`** — build a single affine
map at the root of the paste and apply it to the absolute times of the whole
subtree, so the same time maps to the same float everywhere it occurs. This is
mathematically identical to the old per-level nesting (composing affine maps
over nested intervals yields the root map) but without the intermediate
rounding. Endpoints are anchored exactly so the pasted subtree lines up flush
with the target.

**`fix: tolerate float drift when comparing hierarchy boundaries`** — compare
boundaries with a 1 ns tolerance instead of exact operators. Needed
independently of the above: files saved before this fix already contain the
drifted values, and exact comparison is fragile for any rescaling operation.
1 ns sits far above the float noise (~1e-13) and far below any meaningful
musical interval, so genuine overlaps are still rejected.

The tolerance is applied to *every* boundary comparison that runs over stored
geometry, not just the two grouping validators, so the helpers cannot disagree
about whether the same timeline is valid:

- `get_parent` / `get_children` — a parent whose start sits a few ulps after its
  child's start was not found, silently orphaning the child. Everything
  depending on the parent link then misbehaves: delete cascade, level changes,
  copy-with-children, and the `has_same_parent` check inside grouping itself.
- `get_boundary_conflicts` — reported the very grouping unit the validators had
  just accepted as conflicting with its drifted neighbour.

Each comparison keeps its original strictness; only the equality test changes.

Checked `scale_segmentlike` (media-duration changes) for the same class of bug —
it applies `t * factor` uniformly to starts and ends, so shared boundaries stay
identical. Paste-complete was the only offender.

**`fix: report paste-complete child creation failures to the user`** — a child of
the pasted subtree that could not be created was skipped with only a log line,
so the user saw a silently incomplete paste. It now goes through the same
`COMPONENTS_PASTE_ERROR` dialog as the other paste-complete failures. Pasting
stays best-effort — a failed child is skipped along with its own subtree and the
remaining siblings are still pasted — so the reasons are collected across the
whole operation and reported once at the end rather than one dialog per failure.

Also folded into the paste commit: the unused `children_of_element` accumulator
is gone, and a failed `create_component` no longer flows into
`get_component_ui(None)`.

## Tests

Each new test was confirmed to fail without the corresponding fix and pass with it.

- Three tests asserting exact float equality of shared boundaries after
  paste-complete — for siblings, for grandchildren (where the old error
  compounded), and for an identity rescale. Two of them fail on `dev` with the
  visible drift `3.8999999999999995` vs `3.9000000000000004`.
- An end-to-end test walking the whole reported flow through commands
  (paste-complete → create_child → decrease_level → split → group), which fails
  on `dev` with the exact reported error message.
- Two backend tests for the grouping tolerance: one where a neighbour's end sits
  a few ulps inside the group span (must succeed), one where it sits well inside
  (must still be rejected).
- Three more for genealogy and conflict detection: a parent whose start drifted
  past its child's start, one whose end drifted before its child's end, and
  coincident-but-drifted boundaries that must not be reported as conflicting.
- Guard tests against the tolerance being too coarse: a genuinely too-narrow
  parent is still not adopted, an overlap well past a boundary is still
  reported, and a drifted duplicate on the same level is still a conflict.
- Two tests for the paste-complete failure dialog: it fires with the creation
  failure's reason, and it stays silent when every child is created.

Every commit is green on its own. Full suite: 1844 passed, 13 skipped.
`pre-commit` (black + ruff) clean.

If the root node itself were passed (admittedly unusual), the existing implementation would indirectly throw since `Root::getParent()` throws `NotFoundException`, because the filesystem root has no parent and  the `do` loop executes unconditionally.

This defensive edge-case fix better aligns the implementation with the `getParent()` contract while treating the root as a

author: mjfisrttime
body:
💡 What: Replaced `Math.sqrt` and `Math.pow` inside `applyRulesToImageData` with direct squared distance calculations (`dr*dr + dg*dg + db*db`). The tolerance is also squared prior to the loop.
🎯 Why: `rgbDistance` was being called for every non-transparent pixel in every frame. `Math.sqrt` and `Math.pow` are expensive operations inside such a hot loop, causing unnecessary CPU bottleneck during processing.
📊 Impact: Math operations in the pixel loop are now simple multiplications. Micro-benchmarks show the squared distance approach is approximately 20x-25x faster than using `Math.sqrt` and `Math.pow` for 10 million iterations.
🔬 Measurement: Verify the improvement by processing a large GIF file. The time taken from clicking "Apply" to the files finishing processing will be noticeably shorter.

author: matheusz98
body:
## O bug

Selecionar parcelas e clicar em "Pagar Selecionadas" derrubava o modal antes de renderizar qualquer campo:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'valorPago')
  at PagarModal.tsx:199
```

`PagarParcelas` monta o `PagarModal` desde o início da página, com `parcelas=[]`. Como `parcelasData` era inicializado por `useState(parcelas.map(...))`, nascia vazio — e `useState` só roda na primeira montagem. Quando a seleção chegava, `parcelasData` continuava `[]` e `parcelasData[i]` era `undefined`.

**Por que só apareceu agora:** a tela de Parcelas estava sempre vazia, então nunca houve parcela para selecionar. Gravar as parcelas (Relay 61) tornou este caminho alcançável pela primeira vez — o item 8.2 do checklist nunca chegou a rodar de verdade.

## A correção

Espelha o padrão que **já existia** no `EditarParcelaModal` (`parcelaCarregadaId`), em vez de inventar solução nova:

- `selecaoCarregadaRef` guarda a seleção já carregada (ids concatenados)
- efeito sincroniza `parcelasData` quando a seleção muda
- ao fechar, o ref é limpo — reabrir a mesma seleção repopula do saldo, descartando edição abandonada (o modal fica montado no pai, o ref sobreviveria)

Preserva juros/multa/desconto digitados enquanto a mesma seleção estiver aberta, mesmo que o react-query refaça o fetch da lista.

## Dois reforços no mesmo arquivo

1. **Render:** cai para o saldo da parcela quando `parcelasData` ainda não alcançou a prop. O efeito roda *depois* do render, então o primeiro frame após a seleção mudar veria o array anterior.

2. **`handleSubmit`:** passa a buscar por `id` em vez de indexar posicionalmente. Se a seleção mudasse entre render e submit, o índice gravaria o valor de **outra** parcela — falha silenciosa em pagamento, pior que o crash.

## Varredura: um terceiro caso, de subtipo diferente

Procurei outros modais com estado derivado de prop. Encontrei um, mas **não é o mesmo bug** — reportando conforme combinado, sem corrigir:

`RegistrarRecebimentoModal.tsx:27` — `useState(titulo.saldo?.toString() || "0")`.

Os três pais (`TitulosTab:657`, `RenovarContratoModal:809`, `Dashboard:489`) montam **condicionalmente** (`{selectedTitulo && ...}`), então o `useState` só roda quando já existe título. O crash não acontece.

Resta uma diferença sutil: `TitulosTab` e `Dashboard` limpam a seleção ao fechar (desmontando o modal e reinicializando), mas `RenovarContratoModal` usa `titulosVencidos[0]` — derivado de query, nunca limpo. Se a lista mudar com o modal montado, `valorReceber` fica com o saldo do título anterior. É estreito e não observado; fica anotado, não corrigido.

**Placar:** 1 corrigido antes (`EditarParcelaModal`), 1 corrigido agora (`PagarModal`), 1 de risco menor anotado (`RegistrarRecebimentoModal`).

## Testes

`src/components/contas-pagar/__tests__/PagarModal.parcelas.test.tsx` — 2 testes, vermelho antes do verde, reproduzindo o `TypeError` exato da linha 199. Cobrem montar vazio e receber parcelas depois, e trocar a seleção com o modal já aberto.

- `npm test`: **350 passed** (52 arquivos)
- `npm run typecheck`: limpo
- `npm run build`: ok
- 1 arquivo de produção

author: yeojz
body:
## Problem

Publishing created the tag as a side effect of `gh release create --target main`. `--target main` resolves to main's HEAD **at publish time**, not the release commit. The publish job's checkout had no `ref:` either, so it built from main's HEAD too.

That left two windows open between merging the release PR and dispatching publish:

1. **Tag drift** — anything landing on main in between silently moves where the tag points.
2. **Content drift** — npm gets a tarball containing those commits, under a version number that never corresponded to any reviewed tree. Unlike a tag, a published version can't be corrected.

History has stayed clean (`v13.5.0` → `97069d8`, `v13.4.1` → `1d997b0`) but that's release discipline, not construction.

## Changes

**New: `.github/workflows/tag-release.yml`**

Fires on `pull_request: [closed]`, gated on `merged == true` plus the `ci-release` label. Tags `merge_commit_sha` directly, so the tag is a deterministic function of the merge rather than of when someone gets around to publishing.

Guards, all failing loudly rather than skipping:

- **PR author account id is `41898282`** (github-actions[bot]). From the event payload, so it reflects the token that opened the PR and can't be set by the PR itself. Ids are immutable across renames; logins are not. The `ci-release` label alone is not an identity signal — anyone with triage access can apply it.
- **Release commit author email** matches the constant in `version-release-pr`. Explicitly *not* an identity proof: git author metadata is unsigned (head commit reports `verified: false`) and anyone who can push may set it. It's a canary for that hardcoded identity drifting out of sync.
- Branch matches `release/<group>-v<version>`, group is `packages`, and the version matches `packages/otplib/package.json` at the merge commit.

Tag creation is idempotent (same sha → no-op) and refuses to move an existing tag.

**Changed: `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml`**

- Dispatched **against the release tag** rather than taking a tag input. The ref selects both the source published and the workflow that publishes it.
- Both jobs reject anything that isn't a `vX.Y.Z` tag matching the committed version. The dispatch dropdown pre-selects the default branch, so without that guard an accepted default would publish main's HEAD — the exact drift this removes. Rejecting on `ref_type` also closes a gap the input design had: a branch named like a tag.
- `--target main` dropped from both `gh release create` calls — the tag pre-exists, so `gh` attaches to it.
- Removed the dead `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')` clause (the workflow was `workflow_dispatch`-only, so its first clause was always true).

Publish stays manual. The human gate before npm is worth keeping, and it sidesteps the fact that tags pushed with `GITHUB_TOKEN` don't trigger other workflows.

## Environment policies (done)

Deployment policies were updated alongside this, since a tag dispatch is refused by default:

| Environment | Policies | Serves |
|---|---|---|
| `general` | `branch: main` + `tag: v*.*.*` | prepare-release, smoke-test, publish-docs (main); publish dry-run (tag) |
| `production` | `tag: v*.*.*` + required reviewers | publish only — no branch path exists |

`production` is deliberately tag-only. It is used by exactly one job, and under dispatch-from-tag an old tag runs its own copy of the workflow, predating the `ref_type` guard. The environment policy is enforced by GitHub before the job starts, so it is the one check that applies regardless of which workflow version runs.

`tag: v*.*.*` rather than `v*` because these are glob patterns, not regex — requiring the three-part shape is as precise as the policy layer gets. Exact validation stays in the workflow.

Related: `tag-release` deliberately carries **no** `environment:`. It runs on a `pull_request` ref (`refs/pull/N/merge`), which no branch policy matches, and it needs nothing beyond `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Design decisions

**Dispatch-from-tag over a `tag` input.** Trade-off is real: workflow fixes stop applying retroactively, since publishing an old tag runs that tag's copy of the file, pinned action SHAs included. That only bites when republishing something old, and self-heals from the next release. In exchange, recipe and source come from one ref, and there's nothing to type.

**No "is this tag an ancestor of main" check.** It would guard against publishing an off-branch tag, but closes the door on hotfixes — and if we branch from a tag to backport, checking against main is actively wrong. Tag-matches-version is the invariant worth enforcing; reachability from main is not.

## When tagging fires

On merge of the release PR, and only then. `prepare-release` is `workflow_dispatch` and touches no tags. A release PR closed without merging skips the job.

For `pull_request` events the workflow file comes from the merge ref — head merged into base — and the base is main. So once this lands, main's copy runs regardless of whether the release branch contains it, including for a PR cut from main beforehand.

`pull_request` has no label-based event filter, so the workflow is evaluated on every closed PR and skips via `if:`, leaving a skipped run in the Actions tab each time.

## Verification

- Both files parse; the folded `if:` collapses to a single valid expression.
- Branch-name resolver exercised against real and adversarial inputs: correct version accepted; wrong version, wrong group, non-release branch, and a `; rm -rf /` injection attempt all rejected. Untrusted values go through `env:`, never interpolated into script bodies.
- Dispatch guard: `tag v13.6.0` accepted; `branch main`, `branch v13.6.0`, `tag v13.4.1`, `tag latest` all rejected.
- Identity checks validated against real data — account id `41898282` on #819/#854/#881, bot email on the `v13.5.0`/`v13.4.1`/`v13.4.0` squash commits, and a human-authored commit correctly rejected.
- `PREV_TAG` still resolves to `v13.4.1` with `v13.5.0` present.
- No backfill needed — `v13.5.0` already exists on the remote at the release commit.

author: eldara-cruncher
body:
Closes #605.

## The failure

`RepoStore.Pull` fetched a chart tarball with one `client.Get` and treated any
non-2xx as fatal, with nothing on disk to fall back to. The error is not scoped
to the release that could not be downloaded — it travels
`Pull` → `repoSource.Load` → `planRelease` → `PlanApply` — so a release-asset
host answering `504 Gateway Timeout` for a couple of seconds failed three
applications' entire reconcile and sent each into an escalating backoff, for
charts that were version-pinned, digest-published and already deployed from
those exact bytes.

Three calls earlier, `EnsureRepos` already makes the opposite decision for the
*index*, and says why: refreshing is best-effort because every version in the
manifest is pinned, so a stale cache can only fail to resolve a chart and never
resolve one wrongly. The index — mutable — falls back. The tarball — pinned,
immutable, covered by a sha256 the index just published — did not.

## What changed

**A content-addressed cache**, `<store>/cache/charts/<sha256>.tgz`, consulted
before the network. The read is gated by `verifyDigest` against the entry the
caller just resolved: the same check the download path runs, against an index
`EnsureRepos` has just refreshed. So the dangerous cases miss rather than
mislead — a chart rebuilt and re-uploaded under one version, a truncated write,
a hand-edited file all fall through to a download. An entry publishing no digest
is never cached, because nothing could validate the read; keying on name and
version instead would mean trusting a version to be immutable, which is exactly
what a repository is free to break.

The URL, scheme and plaintext checks stay ahead of the lookup, so a repository
this store refuses to download from is not one it serves out of cache either.

**Bounded retry** on 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 and transport errors — two
retries, 0.5s then 2s, each announced through `Warnf`. `Pull` takes no context,
so an uninterruptible wait is one the caller is owed a reason for. 404 and 403
are the repository's answer about the chart and are not retried. This is what
covers a cold cache: a first deploy, a version bump, an application just added.

**Bounding the cache**: a hit refreshes the file's mtime, and a write sweeps
archives nothing has read for 30 days — so what ages out is the versions a
pinned release has moved past, and the cost of ageing out something still wanted
is the one download that would have happened anyway. Under `swarmcli-cd` the
cache sits in `<data>/charts/<app>/repositories/`, which `reclaim` already
deletes when an application leaves the set.

`writeCache` gained a second caller and its doc's first sentence stopped saying
"index"; nothing else in it changed.

## Cost

A persistent transient failure takes ~2.5s longer to report, and up to three
times the 30s client timeout against a blackholed host. In exchange the steady
state stops touching the network at all: a `swarmcli-cd` controller with six
chart applications on the 3-minute default was re-downloading six byte-identical
archives every three minutes, roughly 2,880 a day.

## Testing

`go test ./...`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint run ./charts/...` — all clean.

New coverage in `charts/repo_test.go`, each case mutation-checked (the guard was
confirmed to fail when the behaviour it asserts is removed):

- a second pull does not download again, and **a second `RepoStore` at the same
  directory reuses the cache** — the shape `swarmcli-cd` actually has, since it
  builds a fresh store per reconcile
- the cache answers when the repository is down (the reported failure)
- a moved digest misses, and the download it falls through to is judged by the
  new digest
- an entry with no digest is never cached, and leaves no cache directory
- a corrupted cache file falls through to a download
- a hit keeps an archive from ageing out of the sweep
- a 504 that clears is ridden out; a persistent 504 gives up after the schedule;
  a 404 is not retried
- `cacheKey` normalisation: prefixed, bare and uppercase hex accepted; absent,
  `sha512:`, short, non-hex and `../`-bearing digests refused

Not run: no chart repository outage was available to reproduce against, so the
504 path is exercised by an `httptest` server rather than by the real one.

Machine-generated by an AI agent (Claude Opus 5) and not human-reviewed. Claims carry a file, a line or a reproducible check so they can be verified cheaply.

author: kelseyrmonson
body:
The findings had accumulated into the README, which had grown to ~1,500 words of
prose kept in sync with six analysis chains by hand. This adds the layer that was
missing above the chain reports, and cuts the README back to navigation.

## What's here

**`00_Key_Results.qmd`** — every headline result across all six chains, with n and
the multiplicity correction, then a separate *What does not hold* section, then
the caveats. It reads the committed `output/` tables and recomputes nothing, so it
renders in seconds and cannot drift from the chains it summarises.

**`01_TRB/05_export_key_numbers.R`** — `01_TRB` was the only chain with no

author: diegoesqui
body:
Añade un botón discreto en la esquina superior derecha de cada bloque ` ``` ` que copia el código al portapapeles.

## Qué hace

- Copia **solo el código**: sin las vallas ` ``` ` y sin la sangría del markdown cuando el bloque está anidado en una lista.
- Al pulsar, cambia a un check y dice «Copiado» durante 1,4 s; si falla, una equis en rojo.
- Tenue al 50 % hasta que el ratón pasa por encima, para no competir con el código.
- No roba el foco al editor ni mueve el cursor.
- Los bloques vacíos no llevan botón.

## Decisiones

- **Va en su propio `ViewPlugin`** (`src/editor/copy-code.ts`) y no dentro de `live-preview.ts`: si alguna vez generase un rango inválido, CodeMirror desactiva en silencio el plugin *entero* que lo aportó, y ahí se perderían encabezados, viñetas, checkboxes y enlaces de golpe.
- **Icono SVG de trazo, no emoji**, por lo mismo que el resto de la interfaz: los emojis los dibuja el sistema operativo y la app se vería distinta en Mac y en el Windows del trabajo.
- **`position: relative` en `.cm-line.cm-codeblock`** para anclar el botón. No cambia la altura de la línea, así que no le afecta el problema que sí tienen los márgenes con la caché vertical de CodeMirror — verificado navegando con flechas.
- **Plan B para el portapapeles**: si la API moderna no estuviera disponible (contexto no seguro o política corporativa), cae al `textarea` oculto con `execCommand` en vez de fallar sin más.

## Verificado en el navegador

Cuatro casos, comprobando el texto exacto que se copia:

| Caso | Copiado |
| --- | --- |
| Bloque ` ```python ` | `def saluda(nombre):\n    return f"Hola, {nombre}"` |
| Bloque ` ```bash ` anidado en una lista | `npm run build\ncd dist` |
| Bloque sin cerrar al final | `select 1 from dual` |
| Bloque vacío | sin botón |

Además: el texto se actualiza al escribir dentro del bloque, navegar con las flechas a través de un bloque sigue yendo línea a línea (sin saltos), tema claro y oscuro, y sin errores en consola. Probado también sobre el `opensidian.html` de producción ya construido.

body:
## What this changes

A row a component laid out is clipped on a resize rather than refolded, because
whatever arranged it into columns is no longer there to arrange it differently.
That is right for a table or a diff and wrong for the opening: it is drawn from
facts read once at launch — the directory, the recent sessions, the login — and
those are held for the whole session, so what laid the card out is still here.
The record now takes what lays it as well as what it laid, and a resize replaces
those lines with the same card drawn for the window there is now. It is the one
block that gets this, and it says so in its own prose.

## How you verified it

`a_window_that_narrows_mid_session_redraws_what_is_live_at_the_new_width` is a
whole-screen snapshot that already covered exactly this and was asserting the
bug: at 52 columns the card showed the left half of a two-column layout and the
box's right edge was missing. Its snapshot now shows the one-column form, and
the comment that said a card cannot be laid out again says which one can.
`the_opening_is_laid_out_again_when_the_window_changes` fails without the change;
`a_card_that_changes_height_leaves_the_reader_on_the_line_they_were_on` and
`a_reader_inside_a_card_that_was_laid_out_again_is_left_at_the_top_of_it` pin
where a scrolled reader ends up when the card's line count moves under them.
`scripts/check.sh` is green.

author: com-junkawasaki
body:
⚠️ **Draft on purpose — this must not be merged as-is.**

Opened as a draft so GitHub itself blocks the merge. On 2026-07-26/27, 17 PRs of
exactly this shape were merged by an automated pass because the body's warning was
advisory and the PR looked mergeable; ~913 lines were deleted from `main` before
the damage was found and 8 of them restored.

To use this: keep the additions, drop any deletions, or re-cut the branch from
current `main` so it only adds. Then mark it ready.

These rewrite files that already exist on `main`, and the working tree they
came from may be far behind it. Merging blind can silently roll `main` back.

Precedent: cloud-itonami's working tree was 1381 commits behind `main`; applying its
`legal/terms.md` would have reverted owner-approved public legal pages to a DRAFT.

author: godlikedh
body:
## Why

Durable job settlement and stale recovery were split between the generic queue repository and the owning Inbox, Library, and Publisher state machines. That duplicated policy, required raw JSON inspection in generic code, and made external-effect cancellation and terminal recovery difficult to reason about.

## Scope

- Keep claim, heartbeat, fencing, and low-level queue transitions generic.
- Route typed settlement and stale recovery to Inbox, Library, Publisher, and Cleanup owners.
- Commit domain and queue mutations together where they must agree.
- Validate a claimed command against the locked queue row before domain mutation.
- Preserve storage/publication ambiguity, generation/revision fences, safe non-consuming cancellation, and malformed-payload recovery.
- Document the ownership boundary and add focused state-transition/concurrency regressions.

## Out of scope

- Schema changes, new tables, services, workflow frameworks, or product behavior changes.
- Production deployment or production-data validation.

## Testing

- `just check`
- `DATABASE_URL=postgres://... cargo test -p sooqa-persistence --tests -- --ignored --test-threads=1` — 58 passed
- `DATABASE_URL=postgres://... cargo test -p sooqa-worker --test publication -- --ignored --test-threads=1` — 15 passed
- `DATABASE_URL=postgres://... cargo test -p sooqa-worker --test storage_shutdown -- --ignored --test-threads=1` — 7 passed
- `git diff --check`

All PostgreSQL verification used a disposable local test database. No production systems or data were accessed.

## Risks

Settlement now performs typed routing and locked-row identity validation. Focused tests cover mismatched leases, forged commands, expired cancellation replay races, caption bounds, malformed payload recovery, and publication/storage terminal paths.

## Stack position

Based on current `main`; independent of the remaining retention issue except that retention should build on this ownership model.

Closes #126

author: kaluli123123
body:
Fixes half of #15645 — the missing-upstream symptom.

## Root cause

`performAddWorktree` has two branch-creation paths: a new-branch path (`--no-track -b`) and a claim-existing-branch path (`options.checkoutExistingBranch`, no `-b`). Only the new-branch path called the `push.autoSetupRemote` config helper. The claim path — exactly the scenario #15645 reports (`git worktree add <path> <branch>` where the local ref already exists) — skipped it entirely, so the branch was left with no upstream and the first plain `git push` failed until the user set one by hand.

## Fix

Extracted the existing config-setting logic into `ensurePushAutoSetupRemote()` (byte-identical body, confirmed via `diff -w` against the original inline code) and call it from both sites so the claim path gets the same treatment the new-branch path already had.

## What this does NOT fix — #15645 is not fully closed by this PR alone

- **The misleading refresh-warning/toast text** (the "does not exist" / "cannot be fast-forwarded" / "check for local-only commits" claims table in the issue) is untouched. Independent review confirmed this symptom is not addressed by this diff.
- **SSH/relay parity gap**: `src/relay/git-handler-worktree-ops.ts`'s `checkoutExistingBranch` branch still early-returns before reaching the equivalent `push.autoSetupRemote` block, so worktrees claimed through a remote/SSH host still lack it. Left as an explicit follow-up rather than expanding this diff's scope; flagged in code with a comment naming the gap.
- #15331 (branch-absent case, different code path) is related but distinct per the issue's own text and is not a dependency of this fix.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/main/git/worktree-add-creation-config.test.ts` — 15/15 passed (new test asserts the claim path's full `mock.calls` sequence, confirmed to fail red before the fix via `toEqual` array-length semantics).
- `pnpm run typecheck` — exit 0.
- Independently reviewed by two reviewers (Claude + Codex, neither the implementer), each pulling the diff and re-running tests/typecheck themselves rather than trusting the implementer's report. Both confirmed the extraction is behavior-preserving and the new call site is correctly parameterized; both independently flagged the incomplete-closure scope above.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet (OpenTelemetry)</summary>

### [`v1.18.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/blob/HEAD/RELEASENOTES.md#1180)

Release details: [1.18.0](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/releases/tag/core-1.18.0)

- **Breaking change:** The maximum size of a single OTLP export request is now
  64 MiB by default instead of 128 MiB to conform with the OpenTelemetry specification.
  Raise the value of the new `OtlpExporterOptions.MaxRequestSizeBytes` property
  to increase the capacity.
- Added `OtlpExporterOptions.MaxRequestSizeBytes` to configure the maximum OTLP
  request size limit, as required by the OpenTelemetry specification. The default
  is the recommended 64 MiB. A batch whose serialized payload exceeds the limit
  is not sent and is dropped in its entirety. The maximum supported value is
  256 MiB.
- Added `OtlpExporterOptions.MaxResponseSizeBytes` to configure the maximum size
  of a response the exporter will accept, as required by the OpenTelemetry
  specification. The default is the recommended 4 MiB. A response exceeding the
  limit is discarded and treated as a non-retryable failure.
- Added the `otel.sdk.processor.log.processed` and  `otel.sdk.processor.span.processed`
  SDK self-observability metrics.
- Added support for serializing attribute values that are key/value lists in
  the OTLP, console and Zipkin exporters.
- The OTLP exporter will now export the logger version, if it was specified.
- Add new `ITelemetryHostInitializer` interface for applications that do not
  support hosted services, such as Blazor, to use to manually initialize the
  OpenTelemetry SDK as part of application startup.
- `BatchActivityExportProcessor` and `SimpleActivityExportProcessor` no longer
  forward spans to the exporter once Shutdown has been called, and
  `BatchActivityExportProcessor.Shutdown` now waits for in-flight `OnEnd` calls
  to finish enqueueing before flushing.
- Fixed self-diagnostics log lines being silently dropped when an event message
  was too long to fit in the internal buffer. Such content is now truncated.
- Fixed activity creation throwing when multiple tracer providers returned a
  sampler attribute with the same key.
- Fixed logger, meter and tracer providers leaking background threads if an
  exception is thrown by their constructor after resource creation.
- Avoid formatting exceptions and creating exception attributes when
  `RecordException` is called on a span that is not recorded.
- Fixed `UseOtlpExporter` to respect options configured with
  `services.Configure<OtlpExporterOptions>(...)`.
- Clamped the server-supplied OTLP/gRPC retry delay (`RetryInfo.retry_delay`) to
  a minimum value of 100 milliseconds.
- Fixed serialization failures leaving failed trace, metric, and log batches in
  the serializer's per-thread state.
- Fixed the persistent-storage retry thread terminating permanently on an
  unexpected exception.
- Fixed the OTLP exporter from retrying certain non-transient HTTP failures.
- Improved OTLP log attribute serialization performance by avoiding unnecessary
  boxing.
- Improved OTLP histogram serialization performance by avoiding a redundant
  scan of explicit bucket bounds.

author: toddmitchell
body:
All of Cat 3 — declaration **and** enrolment, in two commits.

> Originally scoped as just the declaration half (3.1–3.5). The enrolment half landed on the same branch and the branch is force-push protected, so the two ship together. They are pointless apart anyway: the pipeline queries `GrantOn = Connect` and finds nothing until an app declares, and a declaration sits inert until something queries it.

**Commit 1 — declaration (3.1–3.5).** **Stacked on `app-registrations-to-table` (#1662)** → `circle-definitions-to-table` (#1661) → `review-stamp-cat1` (#1649).

This is PR (2) of three. PR (1) was the plumbing (#1661, #1662); PR (3) is the enrolment pipeline and the owner toggle.

## What an app can now declare

```jsonc
"defaultCircles": [{
  "id": "…",                    // app-supplied; what an update matches on
  "name": "Chat-only",
  "driveGrants": [ /* ChatDrive Write|React */ ],
  "grantOn": "connect",         // none | connect | ownFlowConnect | review
  "designation": "personal",
  "emoji": "💬"
}]
```

It belongs in the registration payload rather than a later call for the two reasons part 2 gives: a grant-on-connect circle enrols **ambiently**, so the first connection after install must already know about it; and the install consent screen is where the owner agrees to it.

## Create-or-update, matched on circle id

Replaying a registration updates the circle rather than duplicating it (3.3). An app may only touch circles it owns — another app's, or an owner circle, is refused with `CircleNotOwnedByApp` (3015) rather than taken over.

Circles an app *stops* declaring are deliberately left alone. People may be in them, and a changed registration payload is no reason to silently revoke membership.

## The deposit-only invariant (3.5)

Enforced at definition-write time and re-run on **every** update, so it holds whenever `GrantOn` changes. Two rules, following the decision that permission keys stay on circles:

| A `Connect` / `OwnFlowConnect` circle | |
|---|---|
| permission keys | rejected — `CannotGrantKeysOnAmbientCircle` (3013) |
| read grants | rejected — `CannotGrantReadOnAmbientCircle` (3014) |
| read on an `AllowAnonymousReads` drive | allowed — a member gains nothing a stranger didn't have |

Checked at **write**, not at grant, for the same confused-deputy reason as part 1's drives-it-can-already-read rule: an app can plant a definition, and the next owner-driven grant would mint it with the master key in scope.

This is what turns "an unreviewed connection holds zero read keys" from a convention into an enforced property.

## The `[JsonIgnore]` fix has moved

This PR originally carried the fix for a bug #1661 introduced — `[JsonIgnore]` on the promoted circle fields made every client-side circle update silently reset `GrantOn`. **That fix now lives in #1661 itself**, so #1661 is safe to land on its own rather than only as part of this stack. It arrives here by merge.

## Testing

5 integration tests in `AppDefaultCircleTests`: declared circles become real rows owned by the app; re-registering updates rather than duplicates; an ambient circle is rejected for permission keys and for a read grant; a `Review` circle accepts both.

Two of them failed on the first run and are what surfaced the `[JsonIgnore]` bug.

Full solution suite green: **2,547 passed, 0 failed** (68 skipped, all pre-existing `[Explicit]`).

## Commit 2 — enrolment (3.6–3.13) and the system apps declaring

**The pipeline.** `ResolveEnrollmentCirclesAsync` runs wherever a connection's circles are resolved: system circles exactly as before, plus every grant-on-connect circle belonging to an app the owner has left enabled. `TableCircle.GetByGrantOnAsync` hits `Idx1Circle (identityId, GrantOn)` — that query is the whole reason `GrantOn` is a column, and until #1661 moved definitions into the table it could not have been written.

**The toggle.** A `Dictionary<Guid,bool>` on `TenantSettings`, set via `POST register/connect-enrollment`. An app absent from the map counts as enabled — which is exactly the install-consent seeding the spec asks for, and it sidesteps a circular dependency, since `TenantConfigService` already depends on `IAppRegistrationService`. Turning an app off affects future connections only.

**The declarations.** Chat, mail and feed each declare a deposit-only `Connect` circle in `SystemAppConstants`, carrying that app's slice of what the system circles hand out today. `v15 → v16` backfills existing installs and validates through the pipeline's own query path rather than a direct read.

## Transitional by design

The system circles still enrol every connection, so one formed now lands in **both** and the same drive grants arrive twice. Redundant, not harmful.

It also means **"an unreviewed connection holds zero read keys" is still false** — the system circles still carry read grants. That becomes true when they retire, which is the next phase. Worth stating plainly rather than leaving implied.

Retiring them is a bigger job than it looks: feed distribution, `AllowIntroductions` and ShardRecovery all key off the Confirmed circle and have no replacement built, and `odin-js` still posts the two hardcoded circle GUIDs.

## A design bug the new circles exposed

`UnreviewConnectionAsync` started rejecting *every* contact, because they all now hold an app default circle. But being in one is not evidence the owner reviewed anyone — it happened automatically. The rule now ignores any circle with `GrantOn != None`, so only a circle the owner deliberately chose stands in the way. Both directions are pinned by test.

## Two existing tests changed

`SystemInitializeConfigTests` and `CircleDefinitionTests` asserted exact circle counts. They now assert presence. The set of circles after init genuinely grew by three, so the old assertions were checking a number that no longer means anything.

## Still not here

`AppRegistrationRequest` has no `AppSlug` field — an app declaring its own address arrives with drive addressing. And 3.7 (an app-context accept bypassing the default set) needs the V2 explicit-accept path from #1599.
