body:
* MH-190: Render markdown in streaming bot messages on arrival (#154) (#155)

The complete broadcast was sending bot_message as plain text, causing finalizeStreamingBubble to set textContent (raw markdown displayed as-is). Page refresh worked because the ERB partial uses render_markdown.

- Expose MarkdownHelper.render_markdown as a module_function
- Render and sanitise bot_message HTML before broadcasting the complete event
- Switch bubble.textContent to bubble.innerHTML in the Stimulus controller (safe: HTML is pre-sanitised server-side with the same allowlist as render_markdown)

* Merge main into IAT (#183)

* MH-176: Update principal address card via Turbo Stream after linking a document (#177)

* MH-176: Update principal address card via Turbo Stream after linking a document

The complete broadcast only updated the linked-documents table and modal; the address card stayed stale until a full refresh, even when linking a proof-of-address document populated it server-side.

Extract the address card into its own partial with a stable dom_id, and replace it in the create.turbo_stream.erb response so the address appears immediately.

* MH-176: Extract Kyc::PrincipalPresenter for the address card

The address card partial was doing raw kyc_principal attribute checks/joins directly in the view, unlike the rest of the app's Applicant/Kyc show pages which lean on presenters (ApplicantPresenter, Kyc::ExecutiveSummaryPresenter, etc.). Move the presence check and city/postcode join into a small presenter, matching that convention.

* MH-176: Move address line building fully into the presenter

The view still branched on address_present? and address_line2.present? after the first presenter extraction — still deciding what to show, not just rendering. Kyc::PrincipalPresenter#address_lines now builds the full ordered list (including the address_line2 inclusion rule), so the view just loops over it with a single presence check for the overall block vs. the "not provided" fallback.

* MH-160: Add plain-text transcript export (#178)

* MH-160: Add OnboardingSessionPresenter#plain_text_transcript

* MH-160: Add plain-text format to the transcript show action

Also add a format.text branch to ApplicationController#user_not_authorized — without it, a :text request rejected by Pundit hit ActionController::UnknownFormat (406) instead of a proper 403, since that shared handler's own respond_to only covered html/json. This benefits any future .text response across the app, not just transcripts.

* MH-160: Add download link and copy-to-clipboard button for transcripts

* MH-160: Add download attribute to transcript text link

Without it the browser displays the text/plain response inline instead of saving it, which didn't match the "Download as text" label.

* MH-192: Add AGENTS.md with git workflow, testing, and architecture guidance (#179)

* MH-189: Fix duplicate document requests for the same person (#180)

* MH-189: Update existing principal instead of duplicating on re-declaration

* MH-189: Deduplicate document checklist items by principal name

* MH-192: Document Jira workflow and status transition guardrails (#181)

* MH-154: Allow applicants to defer missing document uploads (#182)

* MH-154: Add deferred document tracking to DocumentCollectionService

* MH-154: Add document deferral route, controller, and Turbo Stream response

* MH-154: Guard nil onboarding session and malformed index in document deferrals

* MH-154: Add document checklist strip with defer buttons above the composer

* MH-154: Pass computed outstanding items into checklist partial instead of re-deriving from session

* MH-154: Show a welcome-back notice when outstanding documents remain

* MH-154: Share one DocumentCollectionService instance in ConversationsController#show

* MH-154: Show document checklist status on the admin transcripts page

* MH-154: Move document status badge into presenter, add i18n, memoize checklist items

* MH-154: Lock the session row when deferring a checklist item

defer_item! did a read-modify-write on document_checklist with no row lock, so two concurrent requests deferring different items could each read the same pre-defer state and the second write would silently overwrite the first, losing a deferral. Wraps the operation in with_lock, matching the pattern already used in
DocumentFeedbackService#complete_session_if_finished.

* Merge Maian into UAT (#195)

* Build(deps): Bump solid_queue from 1.4.0 to 1.5.0 (#185)

Bumps [solid_queue](https://github.com/rails/solid_queue) from 1.4.0 to 1.5.0.
- [Release notes](https://github.com/rails/solid_queue/releases)
- [Commits](https://github.com/rails/solid_queue/compare/v1.4.0...v1.5.0)

---
updated-dependencies:
- dependency-name: solid_queue dependency-version: 1.5.0 dependency-type: direct:production update-type: version-update:semver-minor ...





* MH-201: Fix addresses.addressable_id schema drift and harden business address creation (#189)

db/schema.rb declared addresses.addressable_id as bigint while the create_addresses migration specifies uuid. Because schema.rb's version already matched the latest migration, a fresh `db:migrate` (CI's DB setup path) loaded schema.rb directly rather than replaying migrations, silently truncating UUID owner ids via integer casting.

Also hardens Kyc::BusinessAddressPopulationService against the check-then-create race CI caught: a RecordInvalid from the uniqueness validation on primary is now treated as a no-op rather than propagating, since a primary business address already existing is exactly the invariant the service is trying to guarantee.

* Build(deps-dev): Bump simplecov from 1.0.2 to 1.0.3 (#184)

Bumps [simplecov](https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov) from 1.0.2 to 1.0.3.
- [Release notes](https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/releases)
- [Changelog](https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- [Commits](https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/compare/v1.0.2...v1.0.3)

---
updated-dependencies:
- dependency-name: simplecov dependency-version: 1.0.3 dependency-type: direct:development update-type: version-update:semver-patch ...





* Chore/mh 202 deprecation warnings (#190)

* Fixes MH-203, SimpleCov warning

* Fixes MH-205, :unprocessable_entity warning

* Fixes MH-204, RubyLLM warning

* MH-182: Add missing schema-path tests for ClaudeAdapter (#191)

Structured output support (schema:, with_schema) already landed via MH-184, but no test exercised that path directly.

* MH-157: Fix stuck "Sending" label on applicant chat messages (#193)

* Security: bump Rails 8.1.3 -> 8.1.3.1 for CVE-2026-66066

activestorage 8.1.3 has a possible arbitrary file read / RCE vulnerability in variant processing (GHSA-xr9x-r78c-5hrm). Updating the whole Rails gem family within the existing ~> 8.1.3 constraint to pick up the fix.

The patched activestorage now eagerly loads its Vips transformer at boot, which requires the ruby-vips gem (previously only needed lazily). Add it explicitly; libvips is already present in the Dockerfile's apt-get install list, so no image changes are needed.

* CI: install libvips for scan_js and test jobs

The activestorage 8.1.3.1 security patch made ruby-vips a hard runtime dependency (loaded eagerly at boot, see previous commit). The GitHub Actions runner doesn't have libvips installed like the app's Docker image does, so any job that boots Rails (scan_js via bin/importmap, test via zeitwerk:check/db:migrate/rspec) failed with a LoadError. scan_ruby and lint don't boot the app and were unaffected.

* MH-157: Fix stuck "Sending" label on applicant chat messages

onboarding_chat_controller.js reused the same DOM id (onboarding_pending_applicant_message) for every applicant message bubble and never cleared it after finalizing. Once a second message was sent in the same page sess

body:
## 1. Summary

This PR changes:

- Bumps `charts/home-apps/vaam-store-prod-pg/values.yaml`'s `cluster.imageName` from `ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgis:16-3.4-86` to `ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgis:17-3.4-15` (PostGIS stays on the 3.4 track)
- Rewrites the surrounding comment to record this as a deliberate decision (PG 17 is the newest major with a proven-track postgis operand; PG 18 exists but has no 3.4/3.5 postgis image and no patch-pinnable tag), so the next person doesn't re-guess this the way the original PG 16 pin was guessed

It solves:

- The `vaam-prod-pg` CNPG cluster is bootstrapping right now with zero rows (`status.phase = "Setting up primary"`, initdb mid-flight, no `-app` secret ever consumed by any service, no database ever created). Bumping the major here costs a free re-bootstrap; bumping it after real data lands would require a `pg_upgrade` migration. The owner made the deliberate call to take the bump now.

---

## 2. Intent

The owner asked why this chart pinned PG 16 when Postgres is at 18. Answer, confirmed by re-enumerating the full live GHCR tag list for `cloudnative-pg/postgis` (4,359 tags, fully paginated via the `Link` header, not a truncated first page): the `postgis` repo tops out its patch-pinnable, proven-track images at PG 17 — `17-3.4-{1..15}` and `17-3.5-{1..177}` exist with numeric patch tags. PG 18 does have *some* postgis image now (`18-3.6-{standard,system}-{bookworm,trixie}`), but only on the newer PostGIS 3.6 track, with **no** PostGIS 3.4 or 3.5 variant for PG 18, and **no** numeric-patch tag to pin to (only floating OS-flavour tags) — breaking this chart's own patch-pin convention. PG 16 was never a deliberate choice: the chart's git history (`dba2889` → `c9637cf` → `c0b208a`) shows it originally used the CNPG operator default (blank `imageName`); 16 arrived only as a side effect of adding the postgis pin.

Source of truth: https://github.com/WhyThatFunction/home-os/pull/124 (the tag-fix PR that immediately preceded this one, and whose "Out of Scope" section explicitly flagged the PG-major question as deliberate future work — this PR is that follow-up).

---

## 3. Scope

### In Scope

- The one `imageName` tag bump in `charts/home-apps/vaam-store-prod-pg/values.yaml`
- The comment recording the PG17 decision and the PG18/postgis gap for future readers

### Out of Scope

- **The identical stale `postgis:16-3.4-system-trixie` pin in `vaam-store/platform`'s `deploy/charts/delivery-gateway/values.yaml`** (`database.cnpg.imageName`, `database.cnpg.enabled: false` by default — inert, unused in production). Different repo; not touched here. Worth noting: that pin is doubly stale — still PG 16, *and* still using the `-system-trixie` suffix convention that this fleet's PR #124 already proved doesn't exist on the `postgis` repo (only `postgresql` uses that suffix). Flagged for a follow-up in that repo, not fixed here.
- Any other unverified value in this chart (storage size, resource sizing, backup schedule, PostGIS 3.5/3.6) — not touched.

---

## 4. Verification

I verified this change by:

- [x] Running automated tests
- [ ] Running manual tests
- [ ] Checking logs
- [ ] Checking metrics
- [ ] Testing error cases
- [x] Testing rollback or failure behavior, if relevant

Commands run:

```bash
# Enumerate the FULL live tag list for the postgis operand (paginated via
# the Link header, anonymous GHCR pull token) -- 4,359 tags total
TOKEN=$(curl -s "https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:cloudnative-pg/postgis:pull&service=ghcr.io" | ...)
# looped GET .../tags/list?n=1000 following rel="next" until exhausted

# Confirm 17-3.4-15 is genuinely the newest 17-3.4-* patch tag
# (17-3.4-1 .. 17-3.4-15, nothing higher)

# Prove the NEW tag resolves (manifest GET, OCI image-index Accept header)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json" \
  "https://ghcr.io/v2/cloudnative-pg/postgis/manifests/17-3.4-15"
# -> 200, application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json

# Render the chart offline (no cluster contact, KUBECONFIG=/dev/null)
cd charts/home-apps/vaam-store-prod-pg && KUBECONFIG=/dev/null helm dependency build \
  && KUBECONFIG=/dev/null helm template vaam-store-prod-pg . -n vaam-store-prod

# Grep proof: no other PG-16 assumption left in the chart
grep -rn "16" charts/home-apps/vaam-store-prod-pg/
```

Results:

```text
New tag (17-3.4-15) manifest GET: 200 OK, application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json — confirms the tag resolves

helm template output (Cluster.spec):
  imageName: "ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgis:17-3.4-15"

helm template exit code: 0, no errors

grep "16" in charts/home-apps/vaam-store-prod-pg/: 4 hits remain, all inside
values.yaml comments (historical "the old tag was 16-3.4-86" / "3.5 is
available for both 16 and 17" text) -- no live imageName, no
postgresql.parameters block, no bootstrap stanza, no barman/extension
setting anywhere in the chart depends on PG major 16.
```

**Nothing here is proven against a live cluster.** Per this task's hard rule, no `kubectl` (including `--dry-run=client`, which still does API discovery against the current context — verified separately with a `KUBECONFIG=/dev/null` control test) was run against any cluster, live or otherwise.

### Post-merge sequence (for the owner to run — not run by this PR)

Changing `imageName` on a bootstrapping cluster does **not** by itself replace the in-flight PG16 initdb Job — a Kubernetes Job's pod template is immutable, which is exactly why PR #124 needed the stuck Job deleted before CNPG would recreate it on the corrected image. The same applies here, with one addition: a PG16 data directory is **not** readable by a PG17 binary, so if initdb already wrote anything to the PVC under the old image, the PVC itself must go too, not just the Job.

1. Merge this PR and let Argo CD sync `charts/home-apps/vaam-store-prod-pg` (picks up the new `imageName` on the `Cluster` object).
2. Check whether the PG16 initdb Job already wrote to `PGDATA` before reacting:
   ```
   kubectl get pods -n vaam-platform -l cnpg.io/cluster=vaam-prod-pg
   kubectl get job -n vaam-platform -l cnpg.io/cluster=vaam-prod-pg
   ```
   - If the initdb Job/pod is still `Running`/`Pending`/`ContainerCreating` (never completed a step that formatted PGDATA) → deleting the Job and PVC is still the safe default, since CNPG's initdb write starts almost immediately once the pod is scheduled.
   - If phase was ever anything past `Setting up primary` (e.g. any WAL/data activity), PGDATA is PG16-formatted and MUST be discarded.
3. Delete the stuck initdb Job so CNPG recreates it on the new image (Job pod templates are immutable):
   ```
   kubectl delete job vaam-prod-pg-1-initdb -n vaam-platform
   ```
4. Delete the PVC(s) CNPG already provisioned for instance 1 (and any other instance that got far enough to claim storage) — a PG16 PGDATA directory will make a PG17 postgres binary refuse to start (`database files are incompatible with server` / a version-mismatch crash-loop that does not name PG16→17 as the cause):
   ```
   kubectl get pvc -n vaam-platform -l cnpg.io/cluster=vaam-prod-pg
   kubectl delete pvc <vaam-prod-pg-1> -n vaam-platform   # repeat per matching PVC
   ```
5. Let CNPG reconcile: it recreates the PVC (empty), recreates the initdb Job on `postgis:17-3.4-15`, and initdb runs fresh against the new major.
6. Watch for `Cluster in healthy state`:
   ```
   kubectl get cluster vaam-prod-pg -n vaam-platform -w
   ```

No data-loss risk either way: this cluster has never reached `Cluster in healthy state`, no `vaam-prod-pg-app` secret has been consumed by any vaam-store/platform service, and none of the 7 `databases:` CRs (`auth_db`, `catalog_db`, `delivery_db`, `order_db`, `payment_db`, `upload_db`, `vendor_db`) have ever actually been created inside a running cluster.

author: woojubb
body:
The four INFRA items an agent cannot complete. That much was already recorded; what was not is **what exactly each waits on**, and whether the record was still true.

Re-measured rather than repeated — and one of them was wrong.

## INFRA-046 — half its evidence was stale

The 2026-07-28 audit says `REGRESSION_RED_PROOF_ENFORCE` is **"set in no workflow"** and concludes **"nothing can fail on it"**.

Both have been false since 2026-08-04. The flag is set in `ci.yml` with the owner decision recorded at the line, and the job is named `regression-red-proof (enforcing: accidental-green only)`. That gate *can* fail.

Corrected in place with the correction **visible**, not by rewriting the original — the audit's reasoning is still worth reading, and so is the fact that it aged.

**What still holds, verified:** it is not registered in `run-all-scans`. That is *correct rather than a gap*: it reads `PR_BODY` and a merge-base diff, so it has no hermetic tree to judge. Registering it would put a check that cannot reach a verdict into a suite whose passes are read as verdicts — which is exactly why `promotion-closes` is excluded, and says so.

**Remaining action:** one `gh api -X PUT` against `protect-develop` (id `18715844`; nine required contexts today, neither of these among them). Needs repo-admin scope. And it should not run yet, on the item's own reasoning: `accidental-green` has never fired on a real PR, so requiring it would put an untested refusal in the merge path. **Blocked on evidence first, a credential second.**

## INFRA-097 — one candidate action re-examined and declined

`scan-workflow-provenance` *does* accept `--base-ref`, and wiring it into CI is the only step short of trusted provenance an agent could take. So it was examined rather than left unmentioned.

Declined, and for the item's own reason: it improves **detection**, and it does not make the control plane trusted — the guard would live in the same file the PR under test can edit. Landing it would close no part of the objective while making the item *look* closer to done.

## INFRA-104 — measured again, not assumed

`develop` is 70 commits ahead of `main`, and every closing reference it carries names an issue that is already closed — checked against live issue state. A promotion today derives an **empty block for the second time**.

Manufacturing a candidate by reopening one of the issues this session hand-closed was offered and declined: satisfying a checkbox by arranging the evidence is the shape this repository refuses everywhere else.

## INFRA-054 — the block restated as three decisions

None technical; the load-bearing one is whether losing the promotion PR (and CodeQL's annotations on it) is acceptable. Once settled the implementation is ordinary and an agent can do it — its vehicle is `workflow_dispatch`, so unlike INFRA-042 and INFRA-065 it is **not** blocked by the 2026-08-04 cron directive.

`pnpm harness:scan` — 129 passed, 3 skipped.

author: cprussin
body:
The chrome is one texture drawn over every app surface, so a window can be above it or below it but never **between two pieces of it**. That is what stops a shell putting a wallpaper under a window and a panel over it, and it is the last thing about CSS on a window that does not work the way a page would.

> **Guidelines audited:** `docs/guidelines/TESTING.md`, `docs/guidelines/ERRORS.md`, `docs/guidelines/CONTROL_FLOW.md`, `docs/guidelines/FUNCTIONS.md`, `docs/guidelines/FILES.md`, `docs/guidelines/RUST.md`. Change complies with all rules.

## The mechanism

A texture carries no per-fragment depth, so it cannot be sliced by z. It **can** be sliced by region: drawn once confined to the parts that belong under the windows, again confined to the parts that belong over them, with the windows drawn in between.

`Layer::clip` is that region — a list of `[x, y, width, height]` rectangles, empty meaning the whole quad. `render_texture` already takes them as instances (it is all `render_texture_from_to` converts its damage into); `draw_layers` was passing `None`.

**In the unit square's own coordinates**, not output pixels, because that is the space the shader's instances are in:

```glsl
vec3 position = vec3(vert * vert_position.zw + vert_position.xy, 1.0);
v_coords = (tex_matrix * position).xy;
gl_Position = vec4(matrix * position, 1.0);
```

`matrix` here is `matrix3(surface_to_output)`, which maps the unit square rather than a destination rectangle — so an instance is a fraction of the quad. `v_coords` comes off the same `position`, which means the texture follows the clip without being told about it.

An empty list draws **everything**, not nothing. `Some(empty)` would be a layer that draws no pixels — a plausible reading of "clip to nothing", and the wrong default for every existing caller.

The shadow is **not** clipped: it is drawn from a larger quad of its own, so it would need its own rectangles in that quad's space. The only layer that is banded is the chrome, and the chrome casts nothing. The field's docstring says so.

## Scope

This is the renderer's half only. Nothing builds bands yet: `present` still draws the chrome once, last, and every caller passes an empty clip. The half that decides *where* the bands are — deriving them from the page's `z-index` — comes next, and this is the piece that had to be proved against real pixels first.

## Testing

`cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

**`e2e-compose.sh` passes 24 pixel tests** through a real GLES stack, up from 23. The new one is the point: a full-output texture drawn into two disjoint bands, asserting both are painted **and that the gap between them is still black** — that gap is where a window goes, and it is the assertion the whole feature rests on.

The second band is deliberately **not full width**. Two full-width bands are drawn identically by a renderer that discards `x` and `width` altogether, so a picture made of those alone agrees with the code being half wrong.

**Mutation-verified**, run through `e2e-compose.sh`:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| instances forced back to `None` | banding test fails at the first band boundary |
| `x` and `width` discarded (`[0.0, r[1], 1.0, r[3]]`) | banding test fails — the narrow band runs the whole way across |

## Why this was uncertain until now

The design doc previously claimed `render_texture_from_to` was the path to use. It is not — that call appears in `compose.rs` only inside `#[cfg(test)]`, as the deliberate Smithay-comparison helper, and `compose.rs` already records why it cannot be used on a y-inverted texture: Smithay flips by negating the coordinate, which on a clamped wrap mode samples the first row for the whole quad. The chrome is y-inverted. Using it would have drawn the desktop as one smeared row.

author: cybilresistance
body:
Phase 1 of `plans/engine-availability-and-install.md`. Read-only status: a new `GET /api/engines` and a status card on every tab of Settings → API. **No install affordances** — recipes, refresh, one-click install and path overrides are Phases 2–4.

## Why this shape

The naive version of this feature is dishonest. Four of the five engines ship inside the Callboard npm package, so an "installed ✓/✗" column would print ✓ forever and teach nobody anything. Decision 1 of the plan is therefore three orthogonal facts per engine — **runtime, version, credentials** — never one boolean.

Most of the review effort went into that honesty, and it caught real lies:

- **`credentials.configured` is `boolean | "unknown"`.** It started as a plain boolean hardcoded `false` for every ACP vendor — so a machine with a valid `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` rendered "Not configured", and an ACP tab's dot could never go green. `false` now means only "Callboard looked where this engine keeps credentials and found none", which is true for Claude Code and Codex alone.
- **Pinned dependencies no longer get a remedy that does nothing.** `@cline/sdk` and `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` are pinned *exactly*, so "updating Callboard picks it up" was false — the runtime now carries `dependencyRange`/`pinned` and says "newer than the version Callboard pins (`0.0.69`), which only moves when Callboard's manifest does".
- **The credential chain covers `apiProvider`.** Bedrock/Vertex/gateway users have every other account field absent, and were being told to run `claude login` while fully authenticated.
- **The ACP tab degrades to `systemInfo`** when `/api/engines` is unavailable, rather than losing the vendor name and the "`opencode` not found on PATH" hint it still holds.

## Facts corrected against the tree

The plan was written from a reading of this tree; implementing it found four places where the tree disagreed. All four are corrected in the plan doc (#354) and reflected here:

- `require("<pkg>/package.json")` **throws** `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` for every engine package but `@openai/codex` — they ship `exports` maps with no `"./package.json"` entry. Manifests are read via `require.resolve.paths()` instead.
- `account.tokenSource` is absent on subscription logins, so keying on it reported a signed-in Max account as unconfigured.
- `opencode --version` must not live on `AcpProviderAvailability` — that type is serialized into `/api/system-info`, and the probe spawns a third-party binary.
- `/api/system-info` is **byte-identical**; the whole `index.ts` diff is one import and one `app.use`. Decision 3 requires it — older browser bundles read its existing fields.

## Robustness

- **`execFileSync`'s `timeout` is advisory.** A TERM-trapping child ran 30003ms against a 2000ms sync timeout, because Node never escalates to SIGKILL — and these are sync calls on a single-threaded server, so the stall would hit every SSE stream and in-flight chat. The new version probes are async with `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` (2005ms on the same child). `which` stays sync and is noted: making it async ripples into `/api/system-info`.
- Registry lookups degrade to an absent `latestVersion`, never a thrown route; stale entries carry `checkedAt`/`stale` and render "Last checked 3 days ago" instead of a confident "up to date".
- `?refresh=1` has in-flight dedup so it is never served the load it asked to bypass.

## Pre-existing bug found, not fixed here

`CodexSessionProvider.checkSdkVersionOnce` is **dead code** — its `require("@openai/codex-sdk/package.json")` throws into a bare `catch {}` on every boot, so the `EXPECTED_CODEX_CLI_VERSION` drift warning has never fired and cannot. A rollout-format change would land as silent parse corruption. Confirmed by execution by two independent sessions; assigned to Phase 4 in the plan.

## Gate

`npm run build` clean. `npm test` repo-wide: **177 files passed, 2702 tests passed, 32 skipped.** Rebased onto `896eb0c` (#355) and re-run green on that base. Verified live against an isolated daemon: auth 401 without a cookie, correct per-engine data, `/api/engines` aborted and `/api/agent-settings` aborted both degrading correctly.

author: fmurodov
body:
Raises retention now that syslog ingestion is live, and drops the volume to two replicas.

- `retentionPeriod: 365d`. Measured steady state is ~55 MiB/day (6.74M rows → 415 MiB, ~64 B/row), so a year projects to ~20 GiB.
- `retentionDiskSpaceUsage: 25GiB` as a backstop. Daily volume swings ~3x (520k–1.42M rows/day), so a size cap that evicts oldest-first is what keeps a noisy log source from filling the volume and wedging the pod.
- New claim at 30Gi on `longhorn-2replicas`. `storageClassName` is immutable, so two replicas cannot be an in-place edit. Saves ~30 GiB across the nodes; log data is reconstructible enough not to warrant a third copy.

Retention is instance-wide: container logs dominate the volume, syslog is a rounding error at current rates.

**Migration already done.** Flux was suspended, the pod scaled down, and data copied to the new claim — 35,489 files / 438,501,708 bytes identical on both sides, and all 8 days of history verified present after restart. The service is already running on the new claim, so merging reconciles Git to the cluster rather than changing it.

On apply Flux prunes the old `victoria-logs-data` claim, which deletes the old Longhorn volume. That is the intended cleanup.

## What changed

Follow-up to #10, which merged just before this commit landed on the branch — this PR carries the one remaining commit.

### The draft plan (new engine + draft-sheet section)
- **`buildDraftPlan()`** (`artifacts/api-server/src/lib/draft-plan.ts`, pure, 6 table tests): one slot per remaining pick, several options each (best first, no player repeats across the plan). Scoring is market-fit first — reaches beyond ~2 rounds are punished — blended with positional-percentile quality, walking need (the round-4 slot assumes round-3's primary was taken), take-him-now-or-lose-him urgency, and survival odds from consensus ADP + spread.
- Keeper-consumed rounds and traded picks are honored (a round-1 keeper removes the R1 slot); kept/drafted players come off the board; kicker/defense rounds are planned as streaming notes on the final picks since the ranked 250 doesn't cover them.
- **`GET /draft/plan`** (spec → orval codegen → route). The plan cache invalidates on every keeper change and draft pick, so uploading the keeper sheet immediately regenerates it.
- **Draft sheet**: "The plan — a target for every pick, with fallbacks": `R#·overall`, primary with position/ADP/survival-odds/role, then the if-gone alternates. Print-first styling.

### Stat Lab: real breakdowns, honest scopes
- The selected player is held by **id** and re-derived from the live query each render — a refresh mid-session updates an open breakdown instead of showing stale data.
- Every breakdown row carries a **`PLAYER`** or **`TEAM · XXX`** scope chip; all-team stages (trenches, scheme) get an "inherited — every {team} player shares these" banner; the guide view tags each stat's scope. Shared team context no longer reads as duplicated player data.

### Tooling
- `api-server/tsconfig.json` gains `noEmit` + `allowImportingTsExtensions`: engine files can now import siblings with the `.ts` extensions node's test runner requires (tsc there is typecheck-only; esbuild does the emit).

## Notes for review

- Verified live: baseline plan reads sensibly (pick 12 → Ashton Jeanty at ADP 16 with 91% survival, QB proposed where the market prices one), keeper import reshapes it correctly, and the Stat Lab shows 27 player-chips / 17 team-chips on a WR breakdown with a clean console.

author: prodigystudios
body:
## Problemet

`crm_quotes.amount` och `crm_work_orders.amount` är `computePricing(...).total`, alltså **subtotal + moms**. Rapporteringen och översikten summerade det fältet rakt av.

Följden var inte bara att talen låg för högt — de **adderade två olika sorters kronor**. En order med omvänd skattskyldighet (byggmoms, `vat_percent = 0`) räknades ex moms medan en privatkundsorder räknades inkl 25 %.

Det värsta var rankningen, inte totalerna: eftersom påslaget bara träffade de momspliktiga raderna fick en säljare som säljer till privatkunder 25 % gratis mot en som säljer till byggföretag. "Per säljare" och topplistan rankade delvis på kundmix, inte på prestation. Veckomålen mättes mot ett brutto, så samma säljare nådde sitt mål ~20 % för lätt.

## Mätt mot drift (2026-08-21, senaste 12 mån)

| | Före | Efter |
|---|---|---|
| Offertvärde | 6 130 106 kr | 5 205 674 kr |
| Ordervärde | 1 723 702 kr | 1 441 177 kr |
| Fakturerat | 673 596 kr | 542 071 kr |
| Aktiva offerter (översikten) | 4 484 409 kr | 3 809 300 kr |
| Öppna ordrar (översikten) | 1 026 718 kr | 899 106 kr |

Beräkningen är **per rad**, inte en schablon: de 34 momsfria raderna är oförändrade rad för rad, de 135 momsade räknades om.

## Lösningen

`netAmount()` i `pricing.ts` — hos `computePricing`, som skapade bruttot. Den läser `pricing_summary.subtotal` när summeringen beskriver samma belopp som raden, annars härleds nettot ur `amount` och `vat_percent`. Mätt: 168 av 169 rader går den primära vägen.

`toAmount` är borta. Den fanns bara för att läsa `amount` rått, vilket är precis det som var fel.

Avbrutna order räknas inte längre som omsättning (18 710 kr ex moms i drift). De faller bort i `partitionOrders` respektive veckofönstret, så de försvinner samtidigt ur ordervärde, antal, tratt och kundtabell. Regeln bor hos vokabulären i `work-orders.ts` och är **avsiktligt** inte härledd som "det som saknas i `BOARD_FILTER_STATUSES`" — den dagen någon lägger till en Avbrutna-flik hade en sådan härledning tyst börjat räkna avbrutna order som omsättning igen.

## Granskningen fångade en riktig bugg

`netAmount` kunde redovisa en riktig offert som **0 kr**. Den litade på `pricing_summary.subtotal` så snart fältet fanns — men quotes-schemat defaultar varje fält i `pricingSummarySchema` till 0, så en offert sparad utan `pricing_summary` får `{subtotal: 0, vat: 0, total: 0}` bredvid ett riktigt `amount`. En tyst nolla, den värsta sorten.

Summeringen godtas nu bara när `total` matchar `amount` inom ören — samma vakt som systerfunktionen `resolveQuoteVatBreakdown` redan hade.

## ⚠️ Att ta ställning till efter merge

**Veckomålen mäts nu mot netto.** `crm_goals` har mål satta i kronor (500 000 kr offertvärde/vecka på 36 rader), satta under den gamla bruttoregimen. Jämförelsen är konsekvent nu, men målnivåerna kan behöva ses över. Det är ett affärsbeslut och rörs inte här.

## Utanför scope, medvetet

"Senaste offertlägen"/"Senaste ordrar" på översikten visar rått `amount`. De listar enskilda dokument, och ett dokumentbelopp har en egen etablerad regel (`quoteAmountDisplay`: privat inkl moms, företag ex + moms) — det är beloppet kunden ser. Värt en egen titt: listorna följer i dag varken regeln, utan visar bruttot rått.

## Verifiering

`type-check`, `lint`, `build` (exit 0) och hela sviten — **1701 tester**, varav 31 nya. Ingen SQL.

## Objective
EPIC 30 Sprint 30.26: remove stale implementation history and dead maintenance noise while preserving durable technical rationale. Closes #223.

## Implementation summary
- **`BD30-F075` (fixed, wider scope than originally documented)** — a prior sprint attempted removing dead CSS from a superseded card-menu interaction pattern and reverted after discovering the real scope was larger than 6 initially-visible locations. This sprint mapped it completely before touching anything: 15 locations in `cards.css` (2 needed surgical substring removal from minified lines with live content interleaved, 2 were mixed comma-groups where only the dead selectors were removed from the list — CSS comma-grouped selectors don't share cascade with each other, so this is safe by construction, not luck), plus 3 more files discovered along the way: a dead `:has()` rule in `dragdrop.css`, orphaned `.card-action-menu`/`@keyframes` in `app.css`, and a 57-line orphaned JS module (`beeday-card-menu.js`) — all leftovers from `BeeDayCardMenu.razor`'s removal in an earlier sprint that never got fully cleaned up. Verified via grep (zero remaining references), a clean build, and 118 real E2E test runs (`AccessibilityQualityTests` 18/18, plus 100 institutional/experience-system/home tests) with no regression.
- **`BD30-F076` (fixed)** — a global CSS rule for `.beeday-hero__eyebrow` only "worked" because a scoped rule in `BeeDayHero.razor.css` happened to outrank it in the cascade (previously fixed a real WCAG-AA failure this way). Confirmed by reading both rules in full that the scoped rule already supplies every property the global one did — removing the global entry (and a second, previously-undocumented onboarding-specific override that was also fully shadowed) has zero visual effect, just removes the fragile cascade dependency. Verified with the same accessibility suite, including the COR0-COR9 scenarios that originally caught the WCAG bug.
- **`BD30-F005` (fixed)** — 29 stale documentation path references across 20 files (recount found slightly more than the original 27/19 estimate). Key finding that made this mechanical rather than an editorial guess: the 5 "moved" docs were archived to `docs/history/` with their original section numbering preserved intact — confirmed by reading each target before fixing anything, so every fix repoints only the file path, not the section citation.
- Also removed ~10 comments that only labeled a sprint number with no other content (pure noise, confirmed by reading each in full — the vast majority of ~188 sprint/epic-referencing comments checked turned out to be durable rationale, not noise, consistent with prior sprints already having cleaned most of it).
- `BD30-F059`/`BD30-F093`/`BD30-F071`/`BD30-F087`/`BD30-F088` reverified without new evidence or attempted fix — none are code-hygiene-shaped this sprint (an unresolved defect with no new lead, a policy call on a new logging convention, and coverage/performance work respectively) — forwarded per the Ledger.

## Architecture impact
None. No public contracts, no schema/migration changes.

## Test coverage
No new tests — this is a removal/correction sprint. Existing suites (E2E accessibility, institutional/experience-system/home) run for real to prove no regression from the CSS/JS removal.

## Validation results
- `dotnet format BeeDay.slnx --verify-no-changes` — PASS
- `dotnet build BeeDay.slnx --configuration Release --warnaserror` — PASS, 0 warnings
- `dotnet test BeeDay.slnx` (Debug, full) — PASS, 1555/1555
- `dotnet test BeeDay.slnx --configuration Release` (full) — 1 isolated failure on first run (`ActivityFilterBarTests.SharedSearchInputPreservesTheDebouncedFilterContract`, unrelated to any file this sprint touched), confirmed `TRANSIENT/FLAKY`/`CHANGE-CAUSED = NO` via isolated retry (3/3) — matches the exact mechanism `BD30-F042` (Sprint 30.24) documented for concurrent test-project execution under a single `dotnet test BeeDay.slnx` invocation. Clean re-run: PASS, 1555/1555.
- `dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes` — PASS, no pending model changes
- `git diff --check` — PASS

## Deployment/environment considerations
No schema, migration, or public-contract changes. No HMG/production database mutation executed or required.

## Rollback considerations
Standard revert.

## Known risks / follow-up
- `BD30-F059` (Wallet card interactivity, root cause still unknown) and `BD30-F093` (LoggingBehavior EventId convention) remain open per the Ledger — neither had new evidence this sprint.
- `INV-021`'s naming-consistency half (`beeday`/`BeeDay.*`) is Sprint 30.27's dedicated scope, not touched here.

Full findings and evidence: `docs/epics/30-system-integrity/README.md` §33.

## Summary by Sourcery

Remove dead card-menu assets, obsolete CSS, stale documentation links, and non-informative historical comments while preserving durable technical rationale.

Bug Fixes:
- Remove obsolete card-menu CSS and JavaScript remnants left behind after the card-menu component was removed.
- Eliminate the obsolete global hero eyebrow styles and shadowed onboarding override while preserving the scoped accessibility styling.

Enhancements:
- Update stale documentation references to their current or archived locations while preserving section citations.
- Remove comments that contain only historical sprint labels and update the integrity ledger with the completed hygiene findings and validation evidence.

Documentation:
- Refresh application and system-integrity documentation to record corrected historical references, completed cleanup findings, and remaining follow-up scope.

Chores:
- Delete unused card-menu assets and purge dead CSS, JavaScript, and maintenance noise without changing public contracts or persistence behavior.

author: randomparity
body:
Closes #156

## What this changes

Four clause-level reconciliations in `skills/detect-evil/SKILL.md`, one per finding recorded in the issue, so each rule in the claim-reproduction section carries exactly one reading:

1. **Finding bar states the refuted-claim precedence.** A paragraph after the bar's four questions names the refuted-claim finding as the one finding that need not name a boundary or category, and says its four questions are answered by the claim, the observation, the command, and the environment the refuted bullet already requires in `body`. The scan no longer chooses between dropping a valid refutation and inventing a boundary to fit the bar.
2. **A red guardrail run refutes; it is not routed to not-checkable-here.** "Any failure routes the claim..." now reads "A failure of any of those three conditions routes the claim...", and the sentence adds that a guardrail which does run under those conditions and comes back red refutes the claim.
3. **The claim-set sentence is an ordering, not a narrowing.** "take those first — they order the work, they do not bound it: every load-bearing claim still gets named and a state", so `$trial-loop`'s *sound with record notes* exit cannot be reached on a shrunken claim set.
4. **The static-inspection bound no longer contradicts guardrail running.** *Hard constraints* bullet 2 scopes the bound to proving a vulnerability and points claim reproduction at the section's own three conditions.

Bumps the manifest version to 1.0.14 per ADR 0022.

## Verification

- `just verify` passes (records gate, lint, format, public-safety, skill shape, ripgrep config, plugin/version checks, 17 test suites, actionlint, zizmor, prek dry-run). Prose only — per the acceptance criteria no gate asserts on this text.
- One adversarial review iteration: one finding (medium) — an accidental deletion of the *Hard constraints* read-only bullet by a line-anchor slip in the first commit — fixed in ba2656e by restoring the bullet verbatim; no other findings.
- Security pass: not triggered — prose-only skill-contract change; no entry point, trust boundary, secret, or dependency surface.

author: josemarluedke
body:
Makes `<DocfyLink>` compatible with Embroider's `splitAtRoutes`.

## The problem

`RouterService#recognize()` resolves the matched route handlers, and resolving a route that lives inside a split bundle is what makes `@embroider/router` fetch that bundle. `DocfyLink` called it from its `routeName` getter, which both `href` and `isActive` read — so **merely rendering a link downloaded the page it pointed at.**

A docs sidebar or homepage that links across every section therefore pulled the entire documentation site up front, which defeats the split. Traced with a stack:

```
get href → get routeName → RouterService#recognize → applyToState → get route → getRoute → fetch bundle
```

This is specific to resolving a *URL*, which is how Docfy addresses pages. Plain `<LinkTo @route="...">` is unaffected — it is addressed by route name, needs no `recognize()`, and renders the same href without loading anything.

Worth noting `@embroider/router`'s README documents the opposite intent: it declines to support `Route#serialize` precisely so that "linking to a route" need not load it, and `_getQPMeta` is overridden with a comment about avoiding "premature loading of lazy routes when we are merely trying to render a link-to". `recognize()` looks like an unguarded path in that same story, but the practical fix belongs here, where the URL-addressing happens.

## The change

`@to` is already the router's path, so nothing needs resolving to render:

- `href` is built from `router.rootURL` + `@to`
- `isActive` compares `router.currentURL` instead of route names
- `recognize()` moves into `navigate()`, where the bundle is about to be loaded anyway

An unrecognised `@to` still falls through to the browser, and `@anchor` links are still left alone, both as before.

**One behaviour difference needed handling.** Docfy gives index pages a trailing slash (`/docs/getting-started/`) where `urlFor` never rendered one, so building `href` straight from `@to` would have changed every index link to a trailing-slash URL. On hosts with "pretty URLs" (Netlify, for one) that is a 301 on every cold page load, and it moves a site's canonical URLs. The path is normalised so hrefs stay byte-identical. There is a test for it.

## Measured

Verified against a real `splitAtRoutes` app ([frontile.dev](https://frontile.dev)'s docs site) by linking it at this build. Homepage, which links to ~40 docs pages across every section:

| | stock | this PR | app-local workaround |
|---|---|---|---|
| Split route chunks fetched on `/` | **3** | **0** | 0 |
| Homepage JS (uncompressed) | 2146 kB | **932 kB** | 913 kB |

Navigation still works: clicking transitions client-side, the URL/title/heading update, and exactly one chunk loads on demand.

(The third column is a hand-rolled link component that app added to work around this. With this fix it can delete it, which is the point.)

## Testing caveat, please read

`DocfyLink` had no component tests, so this adds 8 integration tests covering href construction, the trailing-slash case, anchors, active state, click-through, and the unrecognised-URL fallback.

**I was unable to run them: `test-app-vite`'s suite is already broken on `main`.** `vite build` fails to resolve `sinon`, which three existing tests (`docs-layout-test`, `page-headings-test`, `intersect-headings-test`) import without it being declared in `test-app-vite/package.json`. Adding it gets past that and into a second pre-existing failure — `ReferenceError: define is not defined` from `@embroider/virtual/test-support.js`. Both reproduce on a clean `main` checkout.

So this PR includes `sinon` as a `test-app-vite` devDependency (it is genuinely missing), but the new tests are **unverified**, and the `define` problem is left alone as out of scope. The component change itself is verified in the real app above. Happy to split the dependency fix out, or to look at the test harness separately if you want it in the same pass.

author: fagenorn
body:
## Problem

`select_phase_action` treated an unknown turn count or context-token count as a
budget signal on every non-direct run:

```python
if turn_count is None or context_tokens is None:
    return "handoff"
```

`from-issue`'s phase gate tells owners the opposite — *"Do not fabricate usage:
omit unavailable `--turn-count` or `--context-tokens`"* (`from-issue/SKILL.md:198`)
— and the Claude Code harness exposes no authoritative context-token count. So a
truthful owner omitted it and the helper handed it off at its **first** phase
boundary, at Phase 0, with turn usage nowhere near its ceiling.

That alone stalls a dispatched run. Control then refuses to resume it: a Phase-0
handoff owns no worktree yet (Phase 1 acquires it), and an absent recorded
worktree is only accepted for reserved direct run ids. An orchestrated run
cannot hold such an id, so every issue deadlocked — forced to hand off, then
unresumable.

Observed on run `orch-78-94-20260821`: issues 80 and 81 both handed off at
Phase 0 and could not be resumed. Issue 80's recorded `phase_inputs` show the
mechanism plainly — `turn_count: 22` against a ceiling of 120, with
`context_tokens: null` as the sole trigger.

## Fix

Guard the ceiling comparisons with `is not None`, as the direct branch already
does, so an unknown count is simply not near-ceiling.

Preserved deliberately:

- **`delegate` still requires measured usage** below both ceilings — the intent
  of `test_delegate_requires_measured_usage_below_both_ceilings`.
- **Measured near-ceiling reports still hand off.**
- **The direct branch is byte-identical.**

## Not in this PR

Widening control's resume gate so a Phase-0 handoff with an absent worktree
resumes under any run id. I implemented it, and it broke two tests that guard
that gate on purpose — including
`test_zero_sequence_direct_shaped_dispatcher_rejects_absent_resume_without_mutation`,
an anti-spoofing case for a direct-shaped id with a zero sequence — so I
reverted it. Dropping a tested guardrail deserves its own decision. With this
fix a Phase-0 handoff is a rare genuine near-ceiling event rather than the
default, so that gate is no longer load-bearing for this failure.

Consequence worth knowing: issues 80 and 81 stay unresumable **within** run
`orch-78-94-20260821` even after this lands. A fresh run id drives them from
scratch, or `/from-issue` picks them up from their handoffs.

## Verification

Full `just agent-workflow-tests`:

- `test_workflow_state.py` — **96/96 OK**
- other eleven files — **281/281 OK**

Plus a direct check against issue 80's recorded `phase_inputs`: `continue` now,
`handoff` before. `test_unknown_usage_continues_a_dispatched_run_across_phase_gates`
pins the new behaviour with its own test rather than only relaxing existing
assertions.

No `.nix` files touched, so `just build` is unaffected.

author: mandeepashf-collab
body:
## What this does

Turns the tenant CMS from an AI-only site builder into a template-driven one, and fixes the reason the existing template library never shipped.

**The finding that shaped the work:** `TEMPLATE_REGISTRY` / `TEMPLATE_LIST` / `seedPageFromTemplate` in `src/lib/tenant-cms/templates/index.ts` had **zero importers anywhere in `src/`**. The five starter templates were dead code, and the "template picker" their comments referenced did not exist — only the AI-generation path reached the UI.

### Phase 0 — wire the library
- `POST /api/tenant-cms/pages` accepts `{ templateId, slug?, title? }` and seeds a homepage plus its inner pages as **drafts**, through the same `resolveAgencyEditor` gate. Empty-page creation is unchanged.
- `/business/website` renders a gallery: industry filter, brand-color swatch per template, page + placeholder counts, one click to seed and open the editor.

### Phase 1 — design system (backward compatible)
- `blockStyleSchema` gains optional `variant` / `animation` / `maxWidth` / `preset` / `schemaOrgType`, each defaulting to the pre-Phase-1 value, so stored configs parse and render unchanged.
- `presets.ts`: six presets (`clean-corporate` reproduces the original look, plus `bold-editorial`, `warm-local`, `dark-tech`, `soft-medical`, `high-contrast-trade`).
- `BlockSection` is the single place a preset resolves: section rhythm, content width, how brand bands are painted, and `--lf-*` CSS variables that `HeroBlock` and `FeaturesGridBlock` read via `var(--lf-*, <original value>)`.
- `FeaturesGridBlock` implements the `cards` / `bordered` / `icon-left` / `bare` variants (the only variants the templates use: 27 bordered, 15 cards, 1 icon-left).
- Animations are pure CSS behind `prefers-reduced-motion`. No new dependencies, no `next/font/google`.

### Phase 2 — 22 industry templates
The 18 verticals from `industry-pages.ts` plus insurance, mortgage, real-estate, solar. Each carries a homepage plus two inner pages, per-page meta title/description, a schema.org `@type` the renderer emits as server-side JSON-LD, and its own preset + color pair. The five per-file templates are superseded by the inline registry and removed.

## Correctness notes

- **Seeding parses before insert** (`blockConfigSchema.parse(block)`), so stored config is total and an invalid template fails loudly instead of persisting a half-filled block.
- **Authoring vs parsed types.** Templates author against `z.input`; the renderer keeps `z.infer` output types. Without this split, every `style: {…}` literal fails because zod `.default()` makes the output field required — that was 300 build errors.
- **JSON-LD escapes `<`.** The brand name is tenant-controlled; `</script>` in a company name would otherwise break out of the script block.
- **No new block types**, so `tenant_page_blocks.block_type`'s CHECK constraint (mig 165, widened by 293) needs no migration. No migration in this PR at all.
- **Reserved slugs.** The `saas` template originally used the slug `register`, which mig 165 CHECK-blocks — it would have 23514'd at insert. Renamed to `get-started`, and the test now asserts the rule for all 22.

## Honesty rules

No fabricated testimonials, logos, or review counts. Every numeric claim is a `[[…]]` placeholder (104 across the registry) and the seed response returns the count so the editor can surface it before publish. Three `"24/7"` claims remain as literals in trades templates — worth an owner's eye.

## Tests

New `src/lib/tenant-cms/__tests__/templates.test.ts`: all 22 registered, each with a homepage plus two inner pages; every block validates against `blockConfigSchema`; every block type is in the DB CHECK list; every slug passes the reserved-slug rule; every icon name exists in `lucide-react`; no hardcoded company names.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `npx vitest run src/lib/tenant-cms` — 13/13 pass.
- `next build` — compiles successfully; its page-data stage then fails on `supabaseUrl is required` because this checkout has no `.env.local`. The same failure reproduces on `main`, so it is environmental, not from this diff. **A preview deploy is the real check here.**
- Not yet verified by eye: no rendered screenshots, because rendering a seeded page needs a white-label agency org and Supabase env. Worth a look on the preview URL before merge.

## Known gaps

- Variants are implemented for `features_grid` only. Hero variants (`split`, `image-right`, `minimal`) parse and validate but render as the original layout — no template uses them yet.
- `item.icon` (a lucide name) is still not rendered — `FeaturesGridBlock` draws one hardcoded sparkle glyph, as it did before this PR. The icon-name test guards data that nothing displays yet.
- No onboarding auto-suggest: `organizations` has no `industry` column anywhere in `src/` or the migrations, so template-by-industry is exposed through the gallery filter rather than a stored industry.

author: leoliu-spruce
body:
## Description

Users that only need CAIP-2 blockchain ids had to pull in the whole crate, including `ssi-jwk`, `linked-data` and `xsd-types`. The `caip2` module only ever needed `thiserror`.

Every dependency besides `thiserror` is now optional and gated behind the new `caip10` feature, which implies `caip2`. The existing account verification features (`eip`, `ripemd-160`, `aleo`, `tezos`) imply `caip10`, and `default` now includes it, so the default build is unchanged.

This is a breaking change for dependents using `default-features = false`, which previously still got both modules.

## Breaking change

`ssi-caips` is bumped to **0.4.0**

Affected: crates depending on `ssi-caips` directly and with `default-features = false`. They previously got both modules regardless of features; they now get an empty crate unless they opt in.

Migration:
```toml
ssi-caips = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["caip10"] }
```

author: jumaelmartins
body:
## Media page — manage uploaded images

Admin **Media** page: a gallery grid to list, upload, safely delete, describe, and inspect the usage of uploaded images. Built TDD, task-by-task, from `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-16-media-page-design.md` and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-16-media-page.md`.

### Backend (`images` module — no Prisma migration)
- **Usage in the image list** — `GET /images` now returns each image's `usage`: the projects that reference it (`{ id, title }`) and whether it's the profile picture. Derived from existing relations, no schema change.
- **In-use-guarded delete + orphaned-file fix** — deleting an image referenced by a project or set as the profile picture returns **409** (human message, file left on disk). For an unused image, the DB row is now removed **before** the file is unlinked (fixes an orphaned-file bug where a failed unlink could leave a dangling row). Ordering is locked by a real sequence assertion.
- **`PATCH /images/:id`** — owner-guarded description edit (max 200 chars; `NotFoundException` if not owned).

### Frontend (`features/media` slice + `/media` route)
- Image `usage` types + `normalizeImage` usage-default; new `MediaImage` type.
- Media api client, React Query hooks, and a `PATCH /api/images/[id]` BFF route (mirrors the projects route: `backendFetch` → `toBffResponse` → `revalidatePortfolio` → normalize; malformed body → 400).
- **Gallery grid** (`MediaView` + `MediaCard`): search by description, "unused only" filter, inline description edit, usage badges, and a safe-delete confirm dialog that surfaces the 409 message via toast.
- `/media` dashboard page (Suspense + client content, mirrors `projects`) and the **Media** nav item enabled.

### Testing
- Backend: `npx jest` — **211/211** green.
- Frontend: `npx vitest run` — **393/393** green; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on the new slice.
- Ownership verified on every images endpoint (list JWT-derived; PATCH checks `f_userId===sub`; DELETE ownership enforced in `uploads.controller`). Description max-200 enforced on DTO, zod, and backend.

### Notes
- Usage intentionally counts archived/soft-deleted projects too (the FK exists regardless of soft-delete state) — spec-mandated, safe for restore.
- No database migration required; `f_images.description` already existed.

author: yue-here
body:
Closes WP-1112 (v1.1, refinement speed). One session, nine commits, all measured on the main-checkout venv `[dev]`, darwin/arm64.

## What landed

- **The derivative bases build is batched** (`CompiledPhase.batch` index planes; one kernel per symmetric block, one per frozen FCJ node count in the bucket layout; vectorised node generation via `fcj_offsets_weights_batch` beside its scalar authority). The ragged `entries` contract survives as a lazy derived view, so every consumer runs unchanged.
- **The column accumulation is batched** (`_accumulate`): contributions laid out row-major and scattered through one `bincount` — the pre-batch loop's addition order exactly, so it is bit-identical unconditionally. The proof is that the ten backend goldens passed **un-recaptured** after this commit.
- **Windows are sized by a stated discarded-area bound** (`WINDOW_AREA_TOL = 2e-2`, solved per peak from its own (η, Γ)) instead of a fixed ±30 FWHM whose η-dependent bias was unstated. The tolerance was chosen by sweep: on the IUCr QPA round-robin the fractions are flat in the tolerance from 5e-3 to 5e-2 (deviations vs weighed truth 0.6/2.9 wt % — the fits' own systematics; bands ±2/±6) while the protocol fits run ~2× faster. The 1e-3 the plan proposed is unreachable: the Lorentzian tail gives k ≈ η/(π·tol), so lab windows would *grow*.
- **The window's two jobs split**: tail coverage is k(η)·Γ; capture range is the new `Stage.window_slack_deg` (mirrored on `StageSpec`, `SCHEMA_VERSION` 0.2 → 0.3, textdoc key, GUI highlighter + committed dist rebuilt). The indexing Le Bail validation derives its slack from the pattern range (2·tanθ_max·1 %, clipped [0.3, 6]°), so a wrong-metric candidate reads as *displaced*, never *absent*.
- **The one-hot FCJ sizing gate**: nodes are allocated only when both apertures can be positive this stage. Discovered en route: the QPA protocol carries no FCJ physics at any stage (`axial_hl` never leaves 0), and its late stages were paying full node cost for exact identity fallbacks.

## Measured (vs WP-1111's opening baseline, quoted not re-run)

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| trigger cold | 50 s | 28.25–28.85 s |
| trigger series, warm/pattern | 4.5–22.4 s | 2.06–15.04 s |
| cpd-2 QPA protocol | ~17.5 s (1109) / 15.6 s (pre-WP, this session) | 8.20–8.51 s |
| cpd-1a | 9.7 s (pre-WP, this session) | 4.73–4.95 s |

Rwp identity held (cpd-2 0.13290 in sweep and harness). Equivalence bars: symmetric bit-identical (pinned against the pre-WP loop body kept verbatim in `tests/test_derivative_bases_batched.py`); FCJ ≤ ~1e-15 rel with the golden re-baseline ritual (`tests/data/README.md` § backend_goldens records both events); window re-sizing justified by the recorded area tolerance with QPA bands unretuned. Never an Rwp comparison.

## Deliberately not done / filed elsewhere

- Forward-loop batching, GPU, series `vmap` (WP fences); evaluation count → **WP-1113** (its Inherited now carries the `x_scale` lead and this session's re-measurements — counts held at 540/420 nfev/njev on cpd-2, the LM-basin numbers predate the new windows); peaks buffer → **WP-1114** (Inherited states the new denominator: Σ windows still 34.6× n_points on the trigger, kernel at ~11 ns/element).
- Suites: fast 2580 passed + 117 skipped (6 tests added, no new skips); full fired once on the final tree, 27:53, with four independently-converged-fit bars recalibrated to measured numbers (capillary χ², Stephens cone counts/face, corundum noise ratio) — every core claim held. The misfit-injection texture tests now pin the *stronger* claim (honest windows cut the extraction leak; phantom texture R² 0.66 → 0.012) with the cap logic unit-tested directly.

author: ramouchostar
body:
Deux constats du 21/08 sur Kraainem, et une demande à laquelle je réponds à côté — volontairement.

## 1. « Tous » ne voulait pas dire tous

`sendBroadcast` résolvait la cible en identifiants d'équipe, puis sélectionnait `memberships.team_id IN (…)`. L'option « toutes les équipes » ne touchait donc que les membres qui en ont une. À Kraainem : **13 membres sur 16 sans équipe**.

Un envoi « à tous » aujourd'hui partirait à **3 personnes** avant le filtre de consentement, et à **1** après.

C'est le défaut de l'ADR 0034 retourné : là, une configuration sociale absente coupait l'entrée des tickets ; ici, elle coupe la sortie des messages.

`resolveAudience` sélectionne désormais par `restaurant_id`. Les ciblages **par équipe** et **par type** restent bornés aux équipes — c'est leur objet (ADR 0014). Seul le canal général retrouve le sens que son libellé annonçait.

## 2. Le consentement marketing bloquait des messages qui n'en sont pas

Le filtre `marketing_push` s'appliquait à tout, y compris à « ton ticket du 18 n'est pas passé, c'est réparé ». Ce message n'est pas une publicité : il exécute le programme auquel le membre a adhéré.

**La demande initiale était de faire porter le consentement marketing par l'acceptation de la politique de confidentialité. Ce chemin est fermé** : le RGPD exige un consentement **spécifique, séparé et non groupé** (art. 4.11 et 7.2) ; un consentement empaqueté dans l'acceptation d'un document général est nul, et une politique de confidentialité est un document d'**information** (art. 13), pas un véhicule de consentement. C'est le grief le plus courant dans les décisions de l'APD sur le marketing direct.

Mais l'intuition derrière la demande est juste — **l'essentiel de ces messages n'est pas du marketing**. C'est cette distinction qu'on formalise, et elle donne le même résultat pratique :

| Nature | Contenu | Base légale | Public |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service` | cadeau prêt, ticket non passé, incident, changement de règle | exécution du contrat (art. 6.1.b) | **tous les membres visés** |
| `promo` | offre commerciale, promotion du jour | consentement (art. 6.1.a) | membres ayant accepté les offres |

Défaut : `promo` — le plus restrictif, et le comportement historique.

## 3. Deux enveloppes anti-spam séparées

`admin_service` et `admin_broadcast` sont deux `trigger_type` distincts, plafonnés chacun à 2 par semaine et par membre. Sans cette séparation, la nature `service` deviendrait mécaniquement une façon de doubler la fréquence publicitaire.

## 4. La politique de confidentialité dit les deux régimes

Le tableau des bases légales distingue les informations du programme (contrat) des offres commerciales (consentement), et la politique écrit noir sur blanc que **l'accepter ne vaut pas accord pour les offres** — case séparée, décochable à tout moment sans rien perdre du programme. C'est la moitié légitime de la demande : informer dans la politique, oui ; y enfouir un consentement, non.

## Effet mesurable

À Kraainem, un message de service passe de **1 destinataire à 16**. Les canaux restent inégaux — 4 abonnements push, 1 seul numéro avec consentement marketing — donc la majorité le lira **in-app** à sa prochaine ouverture. C'est très supérieur à rien, et ça ne prétend pas être un push.

## Étape manuelle

`docs/migrations/20260821-1840-broadcast-canal-general.sql` — j'applique dès la fusion (règle de collaboration n°5). Le code est **fail-open** sans elle : un message de service est alors journalisé en `admin_broadcast`, et une annonce programmée repart en `promo`.

## Vérification

`npm run check:naming`, `npm run type-check` et `npm run build` verts. Le comportement d'envoi n'a pas été exercé en prod : le faire enverrait de vrais messages à de vrais membres.

body:
Dois defeitos achados em **teste real no host**, nenhum deles visível pelos
gates ou por teste offscreen.

## 1. Sessão órfã travava a biblioteca inteira (`4dcf438`)

Jogo encerrado anormalmente (crash, `kill -9`, OOM) não passa pelo watcher, e a
linha de `game_session` fica em `running` para sempre. Como
`idx_game_session_one_active_owner` admite uma única sessão ativa por dono,
**todo lançamento seguinte** falha com `E-TX-LOCKED`.

Não havia recuperação: `session recover` espera AppID de Steam, não o id da
biblioteca de emulação, e o diretório de locks está vazio porque o bloqueio vive
no banco. Trava permanente onde a regra é degradar (AGENTS.md §8).

`_reap_dead_game_sessions` encerra, antes de criar a próxima sessão, toda sessão
ativa cujo processo já não exista. `start_ticks` protege contra reuso de PID.
Reusa `_process_alive`, `active_game_sessions` e `transition_game_session` —
nenhum caminho novo. Teste confirmado nos dois sentidos.

## 2. O fluxo governado nunca conseguia baixar (`b34213d`)

`component apply` **roda no daemon** — provado apontando o cliente do
repositório contra o daemon instalado e recebendo
`E-API-GENERATION-MISMATCH`. E a unit fixava `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX`.

Sem `AF_INET`, todo install que precisasse baixar falhava com
`[6] Could not resolve hostname`. O executor era proibido de alcançar as fontes
que ele mesmo declara no manifesto.

Descartado por teste: rede do host (curl → 200), sandbox do agente
(`dangerouslyDisableSandbox` falha igual), argv (o mesmo argv roda rc=0 fora do
daemon) e binário (`/usr/sbin` e `/usr/bin/flatpak` são o mesmo inode).

O DuckStation só instalou pelo fluxo porque o AppImage já estava em cache desde
12/ago — nunca houve download bem-sucedido pelo fluxo.

`AF_INET`/`AF_INET6` liberados; todo o resto do endurecimento permanece, e o
teste novo exige cada diretiva para que afrouxar a rede não vire porta de
entrada para afrouxar o resto.

## Gates

4756 passed / 10 skipped; ruff, format, mypy (239), boundaries, independence e
status-check verdes.

## Efeito

Destrava instalar Cemu, RPCS3, Flycast, melonDS, Azahar, PPSSPP e os cores do
RetroArch **pelo fluxo governado**, e devolve a biblioteca depois de qualquer
encerramento anormal.

author: jaspercurry
body:
Closes #2813.

A speaker whose **saved** topology is a **roleful** composite (dual-Apple 4-ch
with declared drivers) now **parks with a named reason** when only some of its
declared children are present, instead of quietly letting the surviving dongle
take the box over. A saved *passive* composite, a saved single, or no saved
topology is untouched — full-range stereo is legal there.

---

## 1. Evidence first — the issue's open question, answered

The issue asked whether per-channel `startup_muted` / tweeter protection still
applies when a declared-active box degrades to `apple_usb_c_dongle`. **It does
not — and the premise that question was attached to is also wrong, which
matters more than the answer.** Both halves are stated because the second one
would otherwise be repeated forward as fact.

### (a) `startup_muted` is topology intent, not a runtime mute

Every production reader treats it as a *validation / sound-test* field:

- `jasper/output_topology.py::evaluate_output_topology` — topology blocker
  `tweeter_must_start_muted`
- `jasper/output_topology.py::channel_identity_report` — feeds
  `sound_test_blockers`
- `jasper/active_speaker/profile.py::ActiveChannelMap.validate_for_way` —
  refuses an un-muted preset output
- `jasper/active_speaker/path_safety.py::topology_target_signature` — signature
  match only

The mute that actually reaches the emitted graph is role-keyed and
unconditional (`jasper/active_speaker/camilla_yaml.py::_emit_filter_definitions`
→ `_driver_mute_name(role)`), and `jasper/active_speaker/graph_evidence.py::software_guard_evidence`
says so in as many words: *"There is no per-role startup mute to check
anymore."* So no, that field carries no protection on the degraded path.

### (b) The degraded path never reaches a flat full-range graph

The issue states the box "degrades to ordinary full-range stereo". That is true
of the **outputd/ALSA wiring** and false of the **DSP graph**:

- Graph selection reads the saved topology and nothing else.
  `grep -c 'output_hardware' jasper/active_speaker/runtime_contract.py` → **0**.
  `safe_graph_for_current_topology` takes no observed-hardware input at all.
- A roleful topology structurally cannot select flat:
  `runtime_contract.py::_flat_graph_allowed` raises
  `flat_full_range_graph_illegal_for_roleful_topology` — *"Normal playback can
  send full-range signal to the protected driver."*
- `runtime_contract.py::flat_graph_muted_outputs` returns an empty set for a
  roleful topology, and the flat emitter
  (`jasper/sound/camilla_yaml.py::emit_flat_outputd_cutover_config`) carries no
  crossover, protective HP, or limiter in the first place.

So today the box goes **quiet**, not loud. This PR does not claim to be
stopping audible full-range-into-a-tweeter, and the code comments say so
explicitly rather than repeating the shorthand.

### (c) The hazard that IS real, and why the park is still correct

The box goes quiet **silently**, and only by the coincidence of four
independent refusals in layers that know nothing about each other
(`topology_allows_flat_dac_graph`, `_flat_graph_allowed`,
`_outputd_endpoint_width`, and outputd's ring allowlist). Meanwhile
`apply_observed_single_policy` really does set `OUTPUT_DAC_RECOGNIZED=1` and
`apply_audio_runtime_env` really does write a **live** `JASPER_OUTPUTD_BACKEND=alsa`
edge onto the surviving dongle.

Two consequences, both bad:

1. **Nothing decides the outcome, so nothing can state it.** No reason on
   `/state`, no cue, no household-visible explanation for a dead speaker.
2. **Every one of those four refusals is load-bearing safety held somewhere
   else.** The day any is relaxed — a flat-graph allowance, a width-cap change,
   an outputd allowlist change — this shape becomes full-range content into an
   unknown driver with no gate anywhere in its own path.

Against the stop-condition in the brief: protection does **not** fully apply,
and the remaining safety is a four-layer composition that no single test pins.
That is not "provably driver-safe", so the ruling stands and is implemented
below.

---

## 2. The ruling (as amended by the panel round)

Saved topology is a **roleful** composite (declared drivers needing per-driver
DSP) + only a subset of its declared children observed ⇒ **park with a named
reason**. A saved passive composite, a saved single, or no saved topology ⇒
**today's behaviour, unchanged**. Per AGENTS.md's composite doctrine
("fail-closed partial states").

**Rolefulness, not `kind == "composite"`, is the gate** — the fix round's SF-1.
`kind == "composite"` is profile vocabulary: it says a device has children, not
that those children carry declared drivers. A passive composite can legally
place every declared speaker on one child's outputs (the live jts.local shape),
and unplugging the child that carries nothing must not park a working stereo.
This is the same calibration `jasper-doctor` already makes when
`check_active_speaker_output_hardware` downgrades a non-roleful saved/attached
mismatch from `fail` to `warn`.

The predicate has one owner and is not re-derived here:
`active_speaker.runtime_contract::active_topology_requires_roleful_graph`,
reached by deferred import — same circularity, same predicate, same fix as
`active_speaker.playback_route`, and paid only on the rare arm that reaches it.

## 3. The seam

`jasper/output_hardware.py::apply_saved_topology_policy`, applied in `main()` —
the single publisher of the output-hardware record.

Why there and nowhere else:

- **It is where the single/composite policy is actually decided.** The
  reconciler's `apply_observed_single_policy` already gates on
  `OBSERVED_OUTPUT_PROFILE_STATUS != "ready"`. Publishing `partial` makes that
  existing gate decline, `apply_observed_composite_policy` returns early
  (profile is not the composite), `OUTPUT_DAC_RECOGNIZED` stays `0`, and the
  existing `park_output_audio` fires. **The park itself needed no bash change**
  — the only shell edit in this PR is SF-3's journal field, which carries the
  reason outward and does not participate in the decision.
- **One record, one writer.** `python -m jasper.output_hardware --write` is the
  only producer of `/run/jasper-output-hardware/output_hardware.json`, which is
  what the reconciler, `/state.audio.output_hardware`, `jasper-doctor`, and
  `/sound/` all read. Applying the policy at the publisher means no consumer
  re-derives it.
- **`classify_output_cards` stays pure.** It remains a side-effect-free
  function of observed cards; the topology-aware refinement composes on top,
  exactly like the existing `usb_data_role` step in `main()`.
- **Registry-driven, not dual-Apple-specific.** The trigger is
  `DacProfile.kind == "composite"` **and** the saved topology needing a roleful
  graph, so a future composite profile inherits the fail-closed behaviour with
  no new code — and inherits the passive-composite exemption with it.
- **SF-3's journal field rides the same record.** The reconciler lifts blocker
  codes out of the payload inside the interpreter spawn it *already* makes to
  validate it, so naming the reason on `output_parked` costs no extra process
  on any pass.

On single-source-of-truth: the file read is **not** duplicated.
`_load_dual_apple_topology_children` was refactored onto a new shared
`_read_topology_hardware`, so this module still has exactly one reader of
`output_topology.json`. `_observed_dual_apple_hardware_issues` (the existing
owner of the mismatch fact) could **not** be called directly —
`jasper/output_topology.py` imports `jasper/output_hardware.py`, so the reverse
import is circular. Its equivalent branch there
(`dual_apple_observed_profile_mismatch`) remains what `clock_domain_report`
serves to the wizard and doctor; this PR does not touch `output_topology.py`.

**Out of scope, untouched as instructed:** `jasper/output_topology.py` (read-only
use), `jasper/control/audio_health.py`, `jasper/web/*`.

---

## 4. Where the reason actually surfaces

The park w

author: dakejahl
body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/28359

`i2c_launcher start -b N` with no `-t` now defaults the INA battery index to the bus number, and the instance table is large enough for 1-based bus `N`.

## Problem
[#24865](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/24865) added `-t` but the ctor tested uninitialized `_batt_index` instead of the parameter. Typical `start -b 1` therefore stored `-1`, and after [#28316](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/28316) INA226 rejects that. `instances[]` is indexed by physical bus number but was sized as the bus count, so `bus == I2C_BUS_MAX_BUS_ITEMS` (I2C6 on RT117x, I2C4 on v6x) wrote one past the end.

## Solution
Initialize `_batt_index` from the parameter (default to bus when `-t` is omitted). Size `instances` as `N+1` and reject bus `< 1` or `> N`.

author: luongnv89
body:
## Summary

Upgrades ESLint from v8.57 to v10.9 and replaces the legacy `.eslintrc.json` with flat config (`eslint.config.js`). Completes MODERNIZATION_PLAN Task 3.1 (closes F-DEP-009). Closes #25.

## Approach

Direct flat-config rewrite preserving all rule severities. `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` moved 4.6.2 → 7.1.1 in the same atomic change (4.x cannot run on ESLint 9+); `typescript-eslint` stays on ^8.67.0 (already declares ESLint ^10 peer support). Vitest untouched at 3.x.

### Spike: migration guide findings (breaking changes applied)

Source: [ESLint Configuration Migration Guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) + [`@eslint/migrate-config`](https://npmjs.com/package/@eslint/migrate-config) codemod docs.

- **Flat config is the only format** since v9; legacy eslintrc loading was removed entirely in v10 — `.eslintrc.json` deleted.
- **CLI flags removed**: `--ext` (dropped from the lint script), `--env`, `--ignore-path`, `--rulesdir`, `--resolve-plugins-relative-to`; `--no-eslintrc` → `--no-config-lookup`.
- **Predefined configs**: `eslint:recommended` now comes from the `@eslint/js` package (added as dev dep).
- **Config shape**: `env`/`globals`/`parserOptions` consolidate under `languageOptions` (browser globals via the `globals` package); `ignorePatterns` → top-level `ignores`; plugins/parsers are imported objects, not strings; `root` no longer exists.
- **Codemod note**: `npx @eslint/migrate-config .eslintrc.json` output was consulted, but the config was hand-written in CommonJS because this package.json has no `"type": "module"` (the codemod emits ESM).
- **New recommended rules in v9/v10** (`preserve-caught-error`, `no-useless-assignment`, `no-constant-binary-expression`) flag pre-existing code; they are explicitly disabled to keep this upgrade behavior-preserving. They can be re-enabled with code fixes in a follow-up.

## Decision Record

- **Selected option**: balanced — direct hand-written flat config mirroring eslintrc semantics, rather than codemod output or adopting react-hooks' new compiler-rule presets.
- **Why**: identical lint behavior minimizes blast radius; react-hooks 7.x `flat.recommended` enables React Compiler rules by default, which would add unrelated findings to a toolchain PR.
- **Rejected**: staying on FlatCompat shims (defeats the migration); disabling rules via inline comments (scatters config).

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `eslint.config.js` | New flat config: `js.configs.recommended`, `tseslint.configs.recommended`, browser globals, hooks/react-refresh plugins, preserved custom rules |
| `.eslintrc.json` | Deleted |
| `package.json` | eslint ^8.57→^10.9.0; add @eslint/js, globals, typescript-eslint; react-hooks ^4.6.2→^7.1.1; lint script drops removed `--ext` flag |
| `package-lock.json` | Lockfile sync |

The four custom rules are preserved with identical severities: `react-refresh/only-export-components` (warn + allowConstantExport), `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` (warn), `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` (error, `^\_` ignore patterns).

ESLint does not appear in the `index.html` importmap, so per AGENTS.md the two-place dependency rule needs no importmap change.

## Test Results

| Gate | Result |
|------|--------|
| `npm run lint` (--max-warnings 0) | ✅ 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| `npm run typecheck` | ✅ |
| `npm test` | ✅ 97/97 passed (12 files) |
| `npm run build` | ✅ |

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status |
|-----------|--------|
| Migration guide retrieved; breaking changes listed above | ✅ |
| `eslint.config.js` replaces `.eslintrc.json`; four custom rules preserved with identical severities | ✅ |
| `npm run lint` exits 0 with `--max-warnings 0` | ✅ |
| `npm test` passes (97/97) and `npm run build` exits 0 | ✅ |
