body:
## Objetivo
Auditoría y reconstrucción completa de la documentación para que describa únicamente el producto vigente y pueda usarse como fuente suficiente para mantener/reconstruir el sistema.

Este PR es **solo documentación** y parte del `main` que ya contiene el PR #27 (un Cargo máximo por Usuario).

## Fuentes revisadas
- `.specify/memory/constitution.md`
- `README.md`
- `PROMPT_RECONSTRUCCION.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md`
- todos los documentos de `docs/`
- Specs 001–012
- todos los `plan.md`
- todos los `checklists/acceptance.md`

## Contrato actualizado
- Constitución **2.11.0**.
- IAM: `Permiso → Rol → Grupo`, Usuario con máximo un Rol por Grupo.
- Rol pertenece a un solo Grupo y la membresía se deriva del Rol asignado.
- No hay permisos individuales ni Roles operativos sin Grupo.
- Cargo es metadato organizacional, no concede acceso, y es máximo uno por Usuario.
- `config:read` es lectura; `config:manage` permanece system-only; `areas:manage` es gestión de clasificación.
- Inicio = trabajo personal; Seguimiento = carga del equipo, solo lectura.
- Nueva solicitud depende de `requests:create`.
- Accesos usa staging + `Guardar cambios` y no muta por cada click/select.
- Rutas privadas sin sesión vuelven a Login.
- No polling agresivo; GET duplicados se deduplican y mutaciones invalidan caché.
- Neon pooled usa schema explícito, sin startup `options=-csearch_path`.
- Cadena Alembic vigente: `0001 → 0002 → 0003`.

## Limpieza
- Se retira la Spec 006 anterior que describía herencia Cargo/Posición → Rol, arquitectura ya sustituida.
- Se crea `specs/006-group-scoped-role-access` con el contrato actual.
- Se eliminan de la documentación normativa conceptos/modelos retirados, ramas ya mergeadas, cadenas Alembic antiguas y vías de autorización que el backend actual rechaza.
- Se eliminan referencias de dominio retiradas de la documentación vigente; por ejemplo, conceptos de apartamentos/propiedad no forman parte del producto ni de su reconstrucción actual.
- HISTORY/CHANGELOG quedan como resumen de evolución sin enseñar diseños sustituidos como opciones válidas.

## Detalle agregado
- Nuevo `docs/CURRENT_PRODUCT_CONTRACT.md` como mapa rápido entre Constitución, código y Specs.
- Nuevo `docs/FRONTEND_RUNTIME.md` para sesión, rutas privadas, request governor y política de polling.
- Política documental actualizada para exigir que futuros cambios retiren reglas sustituidas de las fuentes normativas.

## Validación
El diff contra `main` contiene únicamente archivos Markdown. No se modifica backend, frontend, migraciones ni infraestructura en este PR.

body:
This PR is for [OSUI] - Implement Design for Content Patterns v1 ([ROU-12874](https://outsystemsrd.atlassian.net/browse/ROU-12874)).

### What was happening

- Card, Card Background, Card Item, Card Sectioned, Accordion, AccordionItem, Alert and Blank Slate weren't yet aligned with the new theme's Figma designs (radius, typography, color model, and Card Sectioned's layout).

### What was done

- **Card**: border-radius now uses the "elevated surface" token (`--border-radius-softer`) instead of the flat-surface one, matching Figma; dropped the unused `box-shadow` (Figma's Card has a border only, no elevation).
- **Card Background**: added a border (new `--osui-card-background-border-*` CSS API), aligned radius. Overlay gradient/opacity intentionally left as-is — set dynamically by the developer, not prescribed by this pattern.
- **Card Item**: title font-size corrected to the `heading/h2` scale used in Figma.
- **Card Sectioned**: Vertical orientation now renders title → content → footer → image (image last); `.layout-native` styling restored with updated tokens; `UsePadding=False` now removes all padding including the image's, regardless of `ImagePadding`; "Last" image-position variation is out of scope for this pass. Fixed RTL spacing (Horizontal orientation's image/content padding is now correctly mirrored under `.is-rtl`).
- **Accordion / AccordionItem**: every item now gets the full 16px radius + clipping, matching Figma's per-item default.
- **Alert**: re-skinned to Figma's solid/filled look (per-type solid background, pill radius, light text on the three darker types, dark text kept on Warning's lighter yellow for contrast). The "Light" (subtle+border) variant is explicitly deferred, not part of this pass.
- **Blank Slate**: spacing switched from auto-distributed (`justify-content: space-around`) to an explicit token-based `gap`. Illustration/icon mechanism intentionally unchanged.
- Regenerated `stories/CssApiReference.mdx` for the new/changed CSS API properties.

### Test Steps

1. `npm run build` — build succeeds, ESLint clean.
2. Open Storybook → `Patterns/Content/Card`, `.../Accordion`, `.../Alert`, `.../BlankSlate` — verify each story against the corresponding Figma frame.

### Screenshots

_See Storybook/Chromatic for the visual diff on each affected story._

- [x] documented the code
- [x] clean all warnings and errors of eslint

- [ ] requires new sample page in OutSystems (if so, provide a module with changes)

body:
Replaces the home hero with a full-viewport, live-rendered ASCII mascot, and
lifts the wordmark into a shared site header on the way there.

Two commits, reviewable in order — the site header lands first because the
hero's `calc(100svh - var(--nav-height))` depends on it.

## 1. `feat: move the wordmark into a shared site header`

The wordmark and member badge were rendered per page, so the mark and the route
home only existed on `/` and were hand-copied onto `/account`. Both move into a
`SiteNav` in the root layout. `MemberBadge` still resolves the session in the
browser, so this does not make the pages under it dynamic.

## 2. `feat: replace the hero with an interactive ASCII mascot`

The hero is now one viewport tall and led by the Puff — a fluffball with ear
tufts and a red marker loop curling off its head, rendered live as ASCII by a
sphere-traced signed distance field. No 3D dependency; the model and the
marcher are ~700 lines of plain TypeScript.

The loop is the point: it is the same hand-drawn gesture the wordmark is made
of, which is what makes the mascot read as HAM's rather than as a generic
character.

Non-obvious decisions, all commented at the call site:

- **Fur is split in two.** The coat carries displacement coarse enough to matter
  to the silhouette; the pile is a shading term applied afterwards. Carving fur
  into the geometry finely enough to *read* as fur is self-defeating — the
  displacement's own gradient swamps the ball's, and the mascot shades like
  television static.
- **The ramp is short and inverted.** This is paper, not a terminal: a heavy
  glyph lays down more ink, so lit surfaces take the sparse end. Longer ramps
  are not finer ramps; their light end is a run of apostrophes and colons that
  all weigh the same and collapse the mid-tones.
- **Eyes are painted where a ray lands, not modelled.** Modelling them pushes
  two dark spheres out through the coat and reads as googly.
- **The grid adapts to the machine.** The design budget costs ~9ms/frame on a
  current laptop and ~39ms at 4× CPU throttle, which pins the main thread for a
  decorative animal. The loop times its own render and coarsens the grid until
  it keeps up. It only ever steps *down* — stepping back up oscillates around
  the threshold and the mascot visibly pulses between two resolutions.
- **Both `<pre>` layers are absolutely positioned**, and the ink layer has to
  be. A `<pre>` in normal flow has a min-content width of its longest line,
  which a grid item's automatic minimum honours — so an in-flow layer widens the
  column it is being measured against, and the `ResizeObserver` feeds that
  straight back into the sizing.

Interaction is gaze only: it rests turned toward the headline and follows the
pointer, with no accumulated rotation, so it can never end up facing away.
Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it holds a single pose.

## Brand

The Puff and its type requirement are now recorded in `BRAND.md` on
`organization-docs@main` (PR #3, merged 2026-08-21), so this PR no longer
departs from the brand doc:

- **§1** previously read "No Mascot"; it now records the Puff, and notes the
  marker loop echoes the wordmark without alluding to the origin of the name.
- **§2** previously read "exactly two font families"; it now carries a
  character-art exception naming this exact platform monospace stack, scoped to
  character artwork and barred from headings, copy, controls and the wordmark.
- **§5**'s reduced-motion rule was extended to cover mascot motion, which this
  implementation satisfies by holding a single static pose.

## Verification

| | cells | fps | main thread |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop | 11,448 | 30 | 33% |
| Desktop @ 4× CPU throttle | 3,906 | 30 | 52% |
| Mobile (390×844) | 5,000 | 30 | 16% |

- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` — clean; 114 tests, 10 new
  ones covering the renderer and the model, including that the distance field
  never over-states distance (sphere tracing silently drops pixels if it does).
- Driven live over the DevTools Protocol: gaze tracking moves ~3,900 characters
  between hard-left and hard-right pointer, reduced motion is completely static
  over 900ms, no console errors.
- Checked at 1440×860 and 390×844; the whole hero fits one mobile viewport.
- Each commit typechecks on its own.

**Not verified: `npm run build`.** It shares `.next` with a running dev server
and the preflight script wants env the build step does not hand it. Worth a
green CI run before merge.

author: jeg5y7
body:
v1.10.1's `setMaxResults(0)` fix extended runtime from minutes to ~40 minutes, but the field unit still stopped reporting — continuous BLE scanning fragments the heap until TLS handshakes can't get contiguous blocks. Two structural fixes instead of another symptom patch:

- **Duty-cycled scanning:** 3-second passive bursts every 30 seconds (walk-up latency unchanged; ~10% of the radio/heap pressure), plus a low-heap guard that skips bursts under 70 KB free.
- **Self-healing watchdog:** 5 consecutive failed uploads → self-reboot into the known-good boot sequence (WiFi → OTA check → BLE last). Whatever the root cause, the monitor can never silently stop reporting for more than ~10 minutes — and because the OTA check runs before BLE starts, a rebooting unit always remains updatable.

Requires the #46 semver fix (already merged) for the fleet to see this patch-level release. Binaries in `esp32/builds/` (1.10.1 images removed), OTA image at `public/firmware/smartfilter-1.10.2-usb.bin`.

author: d-cs
body:
## Summary

Adds the shard-selection stage of run-id minting. `resolveMintShard(env)` returns which run-ops database an environment mints its new run roots into: the active shard list, then a fleet-wide override, then a per-environment or per-organization pin, then a rendezvous hash of the environment id.

That half is inert. Nothing calls `resolveMintShard`, no deployment has any of the new flags set, and an empty active list returns the current answer without reading anything.

**The other half is not inert, and it is where review effort belongs.** To stamp a grace window this needs a read-then-write under a lock, so it rewrites the global feature-flag write path that `runOpsMintKind` already depends on in production. See below.

## Placement

Resolution reads the active list from a global flag, applies the grace window, and then picks:

- a fleet-wide override if one is set, which is how a cutover completes without visiting each organization. `new` holds the whole fleet on the current id format.
- otherwise a per-environment or per-organization pin. `new` holds one organization back while the rest move, which is how a canary works.
- otherwise a rendezvous hash, so adding a shard moves only about 1/(N+1) of environments and removing one moves only its own.

Two hash details are load-bearing. Scores are 64-bit `sha256(envId \0 key)`, because a 32-bit score collides at our environment count and an undetected tie would resolve by iteration order. The parsed key list is sorted, because otherwise two deployments listing the same shards in a different CSV order would place environments differently.

A pin or override naming a shard that has left the active list falls through to the hash and reports once. Honouring it would leak the drain the active list exists to perform, and throwing would fail triggers whenever a pinned shard drains.

## Why the active list is a flag and not an environment variable

A deploy rolls for hours, so two pods hold two different environment values at the same time. A list held in the environment therefore splits the fleet for the length of the rollout, with new pods placing an environment on one shard and old pods on another. A grace window measured in seconds cannot cover that, and the same knob times the existing mint-kind flip so it cannot simply be lengthened. An environment variable also cannot record its own flip time, and an operator cannot know a rollout's end in advance.

So the list, its grace stamp and the override are global flags, written server-side against the control-plane clock under an advisory lock. This branch adds no environment variables.

## The write path, which is live

Stamping generalises to any number of graced flag groups in one transaction under one lock. That has three consequences a reviewer should look at directly:

- It closes a real bug. `runOpsMintKind` is an editable control on the global flags page, and that page previously wrote it with a bare upsert: no lock, no stamp. An operator flipping mint kind through the UI got an ungraced flip, so every pod crossed the cutover at a different moment. Verified against a running instance, before and after.
- A graced group is all-or-nothing. Submitting its primary writes the group with a fresh stamp; omitting it deletes the primary and its stamp together, because a stamp left without its primary keeps being served and would mint into a shard just removed.
- The advisory lock takes the previous id as well as the current one, in a fixed order, so writers on an older release still serialise during a rollout. The legacy id can be dropped one release after this ships.

This folds with #4751 rather than replacing it: its `unlockLockedFlags` rule decides what the sweep may delete, and the graced groups keep their stamp under the lock. Both sets of tests pass.

## Notes for review

Determinism is a property of the pure core for fixed inputs. The wrapper supplies the clock, the same split `effectiveMintKind` already uses. A failed read of the list falls back to the current id format rather than guessing.

Six flags appear in the admin pages immediately. The two pins are per-organization, so they render read-only on the global page. The list, its stamp and the override are deployment-wide, so they render read-only in the organization dialog.

Nothing bounds the active list against shards that actually exist. That is safe while nothing mints, but the change that carries a shard key into an id must land after the shard descriptors bound the list, or bound it itself.

author: astroid435
body:
Implementación de dbo.tbl_opo_negocios_estados con EF Core Database First

Map the legacy table dbo.tbl_opo_negocios_estados with EF Core Database First and implement its repository, closing phase 2 of the construction plan.

The table is reused exactly as it exists: no DDL, no constraints and no migrations.

Mapping (F2.1 - F2.4)

BusinessStatusRow: represents a row of the legacy table with the real nullability of its columns. Four of the five columns admit NULL. Reading a NULL into a non-nullable property makes SqlClient throw for the whole query, so the tolerance lives in the entity and mapper, never in the aggregate.

Named Row rather than BusinessStatus so the type does not collide with the context namespace.
This corresponds to DESVIACION-1 in the plan, pending Tech Lead sign-off.

BusinessStatusRowConfiguration:

Uses the exact legacy column names.
Configures HasMaxLength and IsUnicode only so EF emits parameters that fit the real schema.
Does not use IsRequired.
Defines no navigations towards the three incoming foreign keys; their only effect here is the 547 raised on delete.

BusinessStatusRepositoryMapper:

Performs the single decimal-to-int conversion required by the service.
A persisted value that is not an exact whole number is read as "no percentage".
The value is never rounded, preventing a stray 0,4 from classifying a status as "Perdido" because of a conversion artifact.

ApplicationDbContext exposes the corresponding DbSet.

Repository (F2.5 - F2.7)
Reads
Queries use AsNoTracking.
Results are always ordered by:
Percentage ascending.
ID ascending.
A single ordering criterion is not a total order. Without the secondary ID ordering, OFFSET/FETCH can repeat or skip rows between pages.
Pagination happens directly in the query.
The following filters are optional:
Name.
Activity.
Stage kind.
A row without a percentage remains among the intermediate stages, matching the domain behavior and EF's null semantics.
GetAllAsync

Delegates using an empty filter.

GetActiveTerminalsAsync
Returns every active candidate.
Does not resolve the ambiguity of a tenant with two active "Ganado" records; that decision belongs to the provider.
Never returns an inactive record.
This eliminates the non-deterministic behavior of the legacy implementation.
Writes

CreateAsync

Commits inside the repository.
Returns the identity generated by the database.
The legacy procedure returned that identity as a return code, which the monolith discarded.

Update

Marks every mapped property as modified.
An omitted field therefore cannot erase an existing stored value, unlike the legacy SET without COALESCE.

RemoveAsync

Resolves the row before deleting it.
If it does not exist, fails with the context's NotFound instead of silently doing nothing.
Service registration

AddBusinessStatusServices registers only the repository.

Each HTTP slice adds its own use-case registration as it is built, ensuring that no slice blocks another.

Decisions worth reviewing
1. Aggregate identifier after creation

The aggregate exposes no identifier mutator because Entity.Id has a protected setter.

Therefore, CreateAsync returns the aggregate rehydrated from the inserted row instead of assigning the generated ID in place.

The alternative would have been adding an AssignId method to a phase 1 file, which is outside the scope of this step.

2. Exception handling on writes

The plan asked for three catches on every write. Only the catches that can actually fire are retained.

AddAsync and Update never reach the database:
The key is an IDENTITY.
Update only changes state in the change tracker.
Therefore, a DbUpdateException or SqlException can only originate from the commit.
UnitOfWorkAdapter already classifies those exceptions.
The 409 for the foreign key still arrives classified.
No write allows an exception to reach the caller unclassified.

Both calls are recorded in the plan.

Tests

Added 48 new unit tests covering:

Mapper in both directions.
The dirty-data rule.
Model mapping of the legacy table.
Repository behavior using the in-memory provider.
Write failures through a SaveChangesInterceptor.
Results
456/456 tests passing
97.3% overall line coverage
94.7% repository line coverage

The two catch (SqlException) blocks are unreachable from a unit test because SqlException has no public constructor. Phase 9 covers those paths against a real server.

Phase 2 status

Phase 2 is complete, with the legacy table mapped without schema changes and its repository implemented according to the construction plan.

author: puritysb
body:
## Problem

Upgrading a ChatGPT plan (Plus → Pro Lite) blanked every Codex gauge on every surface. Measured on the daemon wire: `codexRateLimits: { planType: "prolite" }` — a block with no windows at all.

The void rule itself was right. A snapshot stamped with a plan the account no longer holds is *meaningless*, not merely old, and neither freshness axis can retire it (`stale` waits on `resetsAt`, which stays days in the future on a weekly window; `capturedAt` only dims). The defect is that voiding ran **after** the snapshot was selected, so the one snapshot guaranteed to be discarded won the selection on every build.

Codex stamps `plan_type` from the auth token its process started with. A session opened before the upgrade therefore keeps writing the retired tier for as long as it stays open — and, being the busiest session, keeps minting the newest timestamps too.

Measured 2026-08-22:

| source | plan | when |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.codex/auth.json` (live tier) | `prolite` | token refresh 01:35 KST |
| rollouts, 8,314 lines, 07-31 → 08-22 | `plus`, never once `prolite` | up to 01:40 KST |
| a session started *after* the refresh | `prolite`, 7d window, valid | 01:43 KST |
| `codex app-server` live read | `prolite`, valid | now |

So a valid snapshot was sitting unread on disk while a mismatched one was picked and voided, over and over.

The rescue path was blocked twice over:

- `shouldQueryCodexRateLimitsLive` skipped the live query whenever the passive read was under 2 minutes old — i.e. whenever Codex was being used at all.
- `pickFresherCodexRateLimits` compared only `capturedAt`, so a live answer that did arrive lost to the newer mismatched passive one, and was then voided as a mismatch.

## Fix

Plan agreement becomes the **primary** key and age the tie-break, via `codexSnapshotOutranks` in the shared SSOT. It orders snapshots and never rescues one: a mismatched snapshot that wins for lack of a peer is still voided downstream, so the explicit windowless payload carrying the live tier is preserved (clients merge retain-on-absent — omitting the key would pin the retired gauge forever).

- `shouldQueryCodexRateLimitsLive` takes `passivePlanMatchesAccount`. A mismatch defeats the freshness skip but **never** the spawn throttles — a mismatch is a reason to prefer the live read, not a licence to spawn a subprocess on every usage build.
- `pickFresherCodexRateLimits` → `pickBestCodexRateLimits` (the old name no longer described the rule).
- Both daemons key their rollout cache on the account tier as well as the files. A files-only key served the pre-upgrade winner until some rollout happened to be touched again.
- **One tier per usage frame**: the plan that ranks the snapshots is the same one that voids them, read once per build on both sides. Two reads a moment apart can straddle a token refresh.
- The plan display table moves to the shared SSOT (`CHATGPT_PLAN_DISPLAY_NAMES` / `formatChatGptPlanName`) and the hand-written Swift `ChatGPTPlan` becomes generated. `prolite` added; separators are stripped before lookup, so `prolite` / `pro_lite` / `pro lite` are one plan. Fixes the subscription row reading "ChatGPT Prolite".

## Why both daemons

Either daemon can own port 9120 and both PRODUCE the wire snapshot, so the rule is generated from the SSOT rather than hand-mirrored (`pnpm generate-codex-freshness-rules`, vitest drift gate). Kotlin gets no copy — Android only consumes the wire.

The Swift daemon is the real beneficiary: sandboxed, it cannot spawn `codex app-server`, so the rollout tree is its **only** source. Node has the live query as a second source; Swift has nothing, so a plan-blind picker leaves it with no recovery path at all.

| mode | path | covered |
|---|---|---|
| Node daemon | plan-aware passive + live rescue | ✅ verified on the wire |
| Node session bridge | plan-aware passive (no subprocess) | ✅ same code path |
| Swift standalone (App Store) | plan-aware passive, tier in the cache key | ✅ XCTest |
| both running (one binds, one relays) | one generated rule, two producers | ✅ drift gate |

## Review round (3 commits)

The first commit was reviewed and two of its findings were real defects, not polish. Both are fixed here rather than deferred, because each reproduced the very failure the PR exists to close:

- **Android was formatting the raw tier itself.** `TopologyRail.codexSubtitle` reads `codexPlanType`, not the pre-formatted `subscriptions[].name`, and carried its own copy of the table — so the same account read "ChatGPT Prolite" on Android and "ChatGPT Pro Lite" everywhere else. `ChatGPTPlan` is now generated for Kotlin too and the drift gate asserts both mirrors carry every SSOT entry. Consuming the wire for one field is not consuming it for all of them.
- **The fix contradicted itself on normalization.** `formatChatGptPlanName` stripped separators; `codexSnapshotMatchesAccountPlan` — which now drives *selection* as well as voiding — still compared raw strings. The two operands come from different producers (auth token vs rollout stamp), so a spelling the display table exists to absorb would still land every candidate in the mismatch class: nothing to prefer, winner voided, and `passivePlanMatchesAccount` permanently false, respawning `codex app-server` every 5 minutes forever only to void its answer too. `normalizeChatGptPlanKey` is now the one comparison form, with a single `CodexPlanRules.planKey` in Swift — and the gate asserts the stripping appears **exactly once** there, not merely that it appears.

Two smaller ones: the generator's "build shared first" guard only covered a *missing* `shared/dist` (a stale one threw an opaque `TypeError` inside the emitters — verified fixed by removing the export and re-running), and the zero-argument `UsageAPIClient.codexRateLimits` was left with no callers while resolving its own tier, which would reintroduce across the pair the hazard the parameterized signature closes within it.

## Known follow-up, deliberately not in this PR

`bridge/src/daemon-server.ts` (~3372) broadcasts a session bridge's usage event **verbatim** when it carries Claude percentages, so the account half — `codexRateLimits` included — comes from the bridge. Session bridges have no live-query path by design, so when *no* plan-matching rollout exists at all, the daemon can hold a valid live snapshot while the bridge relays a voided one, alternating on successive events.

Pre-existing (the bridge/daemon asymmetry predates this change), narrow (needs zero valid rollouts), and not reproducible locally — and the fix would touch the most flicker-sensitive path in the daemon, the one whose comment documents a Claude-gauge regression. Left as a follow-up rather than changed blind.

## Verification

- On a copy of the real two-session tree: plan-blind picks `plus` (→ voided), plan-aware picks `prolite`. The instrument distinguishes the two branches on real data.
- After a daemon restart, on the wire: `codexRateLimits.secondary` 7d 1% / resets 2026-08-28, `planType: prolite`, subscription row "ChatGPT Pro Lite".
- vitest 3,268 passed · macOS XCTest `ProtocolTests` 71 passed · Android JUnit 378 passed · generated mirrors in sync · docs / design-system / coverage gates green.
- CI green on all three commits (7/7 checks each).
- Re-measured under the adversarial condition an hour after the fix landed: the pre-upgrade session is *still* writing `plus` with the newest timestamps (17:08 vs the valid session's 17:04), and the wire still carries a real window — so the ranking is load-bearing right now, not masked by the old session having ended.

Test fixtures are the real 2026-08-22 rollout lines, byte-identical on both daemons — a line composed from what the parser expects cannot fail the way a real one does.

Adds `AppFileInfo.pluginCalls` (every `<name>Plugin(` call) to the project context so rules can check any plugin's presence.

author: bernatmv
body:
## Summary
- Añade el producto privado NSFW en paralelo: auth con usuarios admin, shell Empty Spaces, Story/Chat/VN, envelope engine, agencia (reroll/fork/secuela), Studio/Hub/Biblioteca y legado.
- Integra RAGs editoriales (`narrative-rag-v2`), prompt builder ampliado, quality pipeline, catálogo semilla 12/12/8 y tres modelos LM Studio configurables.
- Términos personales de intereses/límites (privados por usuario; admin puede promover candidatos deduplicados).
- Play: SessionSheet discreto, continuidad de beats, loading anti-doble-request, normalización de envelopes LM Studio y rail navegable sobre overlays.
- Mantiene SFW intacto; el trigger oculto redirige a `/private/login`. Incluye E2E privados y ajustes de regresión SFW.

## Rediseño de la zona privada
Aplica el rediseño de Claude Design («Zona Privada – Rediseño») a las 15 rutas privadas. La jerarquía cambia: la prosa sale de la tarjeta y vive sobre el canvas, el chrome se retira y queda **una sola acción coral por pantalla**.

- **Lenguaje visual**: paleta afinada, hairlines de `.09`/`.13`, Newsreader como serif estructural (fallback Georgia, se carga solo dentro del ámbito privado), campos subrayados, rejillas hairline, filas de lista, pestañas subrayadas, prosa a 62 ch.
- **Creación en 3 pasos**: origen → forma de contarla → intereses y límites, con resumen vivo a la derecha. Los atajos precargan todo y aterrizan en el paso 2 para poder revisarlo.
- **Director**: el SessionSheet pasa a pestañas Dirección / Biblia / Plan / Estado / Reparto / Uso, con opciones avanzadas plegadas al pie.
- **Players**: story con aside de escena (escena, presentes, tensión, próximo en el plan), chat con burbujas y narración centrada, VN con caja de diálogo y un panel superpuesto Backlog / Galería / Extras.
- **Hilo del chat aplanado**: un solo `v-for` con clave `beat:índice` en lugar de `<template v-for>` anidados, que descolocaban el patcher de Vue al crecer la lista tras aceptar un beat.
- **Studio** a dos paneles (lista + detalle) para personajes, lugares y Experiences.

Sin pérdida de funciones: bifurcar, ramas, re-roll, comparar modelo, finalizar, secuela, archivar, colecciones, seguir, comentar, compartir, sprites, fondos, publicar, semilla y probe de latencia siguen accesibles.

## Cambios de producto que trae el rediseño
- **Predominantes limitados a 3** (constante compartida, aplicada en cliente y servidor). Excluir y «si encaja» siguen sin límite.
- **Catálogo público de intereses**: nueva migración (esquema 18) que siembra 40 términos aprobados. Sin ella solo se veían las etiquetas privadas. El listado ordena arriba lo ya clasificado, después las privadas y luego el resto.
- **Recursos públicos en la creación**: nuevo `POST /api/private/studio/import` que copia a tu Studio un personaje, lugar o Experience publicado (idempotente por nombre). En el paso 2 aparecen bajo «Publicados en el Hub».
- **Las historias que no empiezan no se guardan**: solo se listan las sesiones con al menos un beat; las vacías se purgan a las 24 h. Siguen accesibles por URL mientras juegas.
- **Accesibilidad**: contraste revisado — todos los tonos ≥ 4.9:1 sobre canvas y sobre el panel del Director. `color-scheme: dark` para que los desplegables nativos no salgan en claro. `aria-label` explícito en el gate.
- **Sin PII en pantalla**: el saludo de inicio usa el nombre de escena del perfil, no la cuenta.

## RAGs editoriales v2 (calidad de prosa)
Revisión de las guías narrativas de la sección privada. Todo vive en `server/services/nsfw/`; **la zona SFW (`app/lib`) queda intacta**.

- **Detalle sensorial y mundo**: escenario estratificado (clima, hora, luz, texturas) con el olfato como ancla recurrente y concreta («café quemado y madera húmeda», nunca «un olor agradable»). Personajes descritos por detalle visible, no por adjetivos valorativos.
- **Cuerpo y escena**: lenguaje corporal tejido en el diálogo (nada de cabezas parlantes), onomatopeyas fonéticas para gemidos y jadeos, especificidad anatómica visualizable y reanclaje de posiciones en cada movimiento significativo.
- **Anti-slop**: fuera la hipófora y la estructura «no es X, sino Y»; léxico prohibido compartido (`BANNED_PHRASES`, lista semilla ampliable) inyectado en el prompt; la prosa de un beat nunca cierra con una pregunta del narrador — las decisiones van en `choices`.
- **Personajes no complacientes**: pueden mentir, negarse o tener agenda propia, siempre coherentes con su caracterización.
- **Tonos `hardcore` y `dark`**: vocabulario sexual directo y crudo de forma proactiva y consistente, sin retroceder a eufemismos ni a registro clínico, manteniendo consentimiento, ritmo, reacciones creíbles y consecuencias.
- **Interioridad**: en story, pensamientos del personaje focal según focalización activa; en chat/RP, pensamiento privado ocasional de un NPC como especia, no como ingrediente de cada beat.
- **Prohibición absoluta de menores** en el system prompt, innegociable e independiente de la configuración de sesión (antes solo existían las exclusiones por sesión, editables por la persona usuaria).
- **Validadores deterministas**: el critic penaliza léxico prohibido y narración que acaba en pregunta, sin coste de LLM.

Versionado: `RAG_VERSION` pasa a `narrative-rag-v2`; skills `anticliche` y `sensualidad` a `1.1.0`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] Units de RAGs v2: léxico prohibido, tonos crudos, prohibición absoluta y penalizaciones del critic (18/18 en `server/services/nsfw`)
- [x] Units NSFW + storage (términos privados, envelope suelto, LLM reasoning)
- [x] Units nuevos: orden del catálogo de intereses y tiempo relativo
- [x] E2E privados: auth, story, chat, vn, agency (7/7)
- [x] E2E SFW con `--retries=1` (40 pass, 4 flaky en VN timing)
- [x] Recorrido manual de las 15 rutas privadas sin errores de consola
- [x] Recorridos de actualización sin errores: pasos del creador, pestañas de biblioteca y Hub, reordenado del catálogo, paneles de los tres players y entrada/salida del player (colapso del rail)
- [x] Sin desbordamiento horizontal a 320 y 390 px
- [x] Contraste medido en navegador sobre canvas y panel
- [ ] Smoke: generar con LM Studio real (Moonlight) y aceptar beat
- [ ] Smoke: importar un personaje publicado por otra cuenta y usarlo en el reparto
- [ ] Medición latencia real con mock desactivado en Ajustes

> Nota: los E2E no se han vuelto a ejecutar en esta última tanda porque la máquina no tiene los navegadores de Playwright instalados (`npx playwright install`). Los selectores de `private-auth.spec` se verificaron a mano.

> Pendiente previo a los RAGs v2: `storage.test.ts` y `nsfwStudio.test.ts` fallan ya en la rama sin estos cambios — esperan `schemaVersion` 17 y el código va por 18 tras la migración del catálogo de intereses. Hay que actualizar esos asserts en un cambio aparte.

author: vineethsaivs
body:
## Title

fix(responses): stop closing a message item the tool-only stream never opened

## Relevant issues

Fixes #37852

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added a testing section to describe the changes below
- [x] The unit tests added here fail before the change and pass after it

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

`POST /v1/responses` with `stream: true`, against an Anthropic-family model that returns a **tool call with no accompanying text**, emits three events that close a message item that was never opened:

```
response.output_text.done    item_id=chatcmpl-<uuid>   <-- never had content_part.added
response.content_part.done   item_id=chatcmpl-<uuid>   <-- never had content_part.added
response.output_item.done    id=chatcmpl-<uuid>        <-- never had output_item.added
```

Note the id prefix: `chatcmpl-`, not the `msg_` id used when a message item is opened normally.

### Root cause

`_ensure_output_item_for_chunk` has an explicit tool-first branch that opens **no** message item:

```python
# Tool-first
if hasattr(delta, "tool_calls") and delta.tool_calls:
    # Tool calls already handled via _queue_tool_call_delta_events
    # DO NOT create message item
    return
```

The end of the stream did not mirror that. `return_default_done_events` emitted the message `.done` triple unconditionally, and each `create_*` helper falls back to `self._cached_item_id`, which `_transform_chat_completion_chunk_to_response_api_chunk` had already filled in with the chat completion chunk id. So the ids in the `.done` events are ones no `.added` event ever introduced.

Per the Responses API contract every `*.done` must be preceded by its `*.added` for the same `item_id`. Clients that track output items by id reject the stream: the Vercel AI SDK (`ai`, used by CopilotKit and OpenCode) raises `text part <id> not found` and aborts the run **before the tool result is delivered**, so agentic tool-calling loops break on the first tool call. The same request is well formed as soon as the model emits any text alongside the tool call, which is what makes this look intermittent in normal agent use.

### Fix

Skip the message `.done` triple when no message item was opened and the turn has no assistant text to report, latching the three sent flags so `is_stream_finished()` still reports done and the stream proceeds to `response.completed`.

The guard is deliberately narrow, so the paths that do open a message item are untouched:

- `sent_content_part_added_event` is set only where the message item is actually opened, so it is the direct record of "a message item exists".
- The `content` / `reasoning_content` check means a turn that has something to report always keeps its `.done` events, including the reasoning-then-tool-call shape where `create_output_content_part_done_event` emits a `reasoning_text` part.
- `tool_calls` must be present, so this only applies to the tool-only turn.

## Testing

Three tests in `tests/test_litellm/responses/litellm_completion_transformation/test_tool_call_streaming_transformation.py` drive the sync iterator over a whole stream and assert that no `.done` event carries an item id that no `.added` event introduced.

```
# unpatched
1 failed, 8 passed
FAILED test_tool_only_turn_does_not_close_a_message_item_it_never_opened

# patched
9 passed
```

The other two are controls that pass either way: tool call **with** text, and a plain text-only turn, both of which must keep the full message item lifecycle.

Wider control, same tree:

```
python3 -m pytest tests/test_litellm/responses/ -q
469 passed in 59.04s

python3 -m pytest tests/test_litellm/test_responses_streaming_container_ownership.py -q
7 passed
```

`ruff check` on both touched files reports exactly the same findings before and after this change (the 12 in `streaming_iterator.py` are pre-existing on the base branch; the test file is clean).

**What I did not verify:** I do not have a live proxy with real Anthropic or Bedrock credentials, so this is not confirmed end to end against a real provider. The evidence above is unit-level, driving the real `LiteLLMCompletionStreamingIterator` over a chunk sequence shaped like the one in the issue. Reviewers with proxy access may want to re-run the `curl` from #37852 before merging.

## One thing deliberately left alone

`response.completed` also lists an empty message item in `response.output`:

```json
{"type": "message", "id": "chatcmpl-...", "status": "completed", "role": "assistant",
 "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": ""}]}
```

That item is built by `LiteLLMCompletionResponsesConfig.transform_chat_completion_response_to_responses_api_response`, which is shared with the **non-streaming** path. I checked, and a non-streaming `/v1/responses` call for the same tool-only completion returns the identical empty message item, so this is not a streaming bug and removing it would change the response shape for every provider on both paths. It is out of scope here and left for a separate decision. This PR fixes the streaming event pairing, which is what breaks the clients in the report.

### Motivation
- Provide administrators a dedicated tool to manage final entries on behalf of participants even when public/team registration is locked. 
- Improve robustness of result publication by verifying writes and surface public-result feed/visibility errors to the UI. 
- Add small UI/UX and rendering fixes across admin and public pages (team ID SVG, public view settings, ordering and empty-state messaging).

### Description
- Introduces an Admin Final Entry Manager with UI and logic: new modal and controls, helper functions (`adminEntryMemberLimits`, `adminEntryEventRows`, `adminEntryNextSlot`, `adminEntryEligibleForEvent`), and CRUD operations for admin-managed registrations (`openAdminEntryEvent`, `saveAdminEntrySlot`, `deleteAdminEntrySlot`, `renderAdminEntryManager`, `renderAdminEntryModal`), plus bindings in `admin-main.js` and new selectors in `admin.html`.
- Hooks the new manager into live data listeners so `students`, `events`, and `registrations` updates call `window.renderAdminEntryManager?.()` where appropriate and adds admin action handlers for entry-manager buttons in the global click dispatcher.
- Adds post-publish verification to publishing flows: single publish now checks the saved `results` doc and bulk publish verifies each committed `results` document and surfaces verification failures to the user (`publish.html`).
- Enhances public results UI and feed handling (`results.html`) by tracking feed errors and timestamps, showing a public-result status banner (`renderPublicResultStatus`), better empty-state messages, robust timestamp comparisons/sorting, and improved Firestore listener error handling for the published `results` feed.
- Miscellaneous: tweaks to team ID SVG generation (`teamIdSvg` clipPath/filter changes), tweaks to public view settings rendering and help block, and assorted small UI wiring improvements (icons, ordering, and guard clauses).

### Testing
- Automated tests: none were executed for this change.

author: reneleogp
body:
## Intent

Full rollback of the Telegram integration from `reneleogp/firstmate`, preserving Git history and the local bot token.

This is a **pure history-preserving revert** of the three merged Telegram PRs, applied in reverse dependency order:

1. Revert "feat: add bounded Telegram mirror mode (#8)"
2. Revert "fix: harden private Telegram request handling (#3)"
3. Revert "feat: add private Telegram transport (#2)"

All three reverted cleanly with no conflicts, so no manual conflict resolution was needed.

## History and PR state

- PRs 2, 3, and 8 remain merged and fully preserved in history. Nothing was reset, force-pushed, rewritten, or deleted.
- PRs 9, 10, and 11 are closed and unmerged; none of their commits were cherry-picked or otherwise reused.
- Only this task branch was pushed, to the fork `reneleogp/firstmate`. Upstream was never targeted.

## What is removed

Every tracked Telegram artifact introduced by those PRs:

- Python transport `bin/fm-telegram.py` and helper `bin/fm-telegram-agent-request.sh`
- Pi extension `.pi/extensions/fm-telegram-mirror.ts`
- Response skill `.agents/skills/telegram-respond/`
- Docs `docs/telegram.md`, `docs/verification/telegram-mirror.md`, and their `docs/documentation-audiences.json` and `docs/scripts.md` entries
- Telegram tests, plus the Telegram test-family and changed-path routing in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`
- The Telegram wake-migration branch in `bin/fm-session-start.sh`
- Telegram branches in the guard, turn-end guard, and supervision tests
- `README.md` Telegram reference

After the reverts, a case-insensitive search of the complete tracked tree for `telegram` and `FM_TELEGRAM` returns no matches.

The only remaining near-matches are unrelated and preexisting, untouched by this branch: `sendUserMessage` (Pi extension API) and the Herdr `LaunchAgent` handling in `bin/fm-remote-doctor.sh` (added upstream in #1623).

## Local token

`.env` was never read, printed, edited, or removed. The bot token stays local and outside Git for the later approved rebuild. No private `config/`, `state/`, or service-manager state was touched.

## Checks run

No no-mistakes pipeline was run, as instructed.

- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` - pass (`surfaces=69 local_links=253`)
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` - pass (ShellCheck 0.11.0, actionlint 1.7.12, 3 workflow files valid)
- `tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh`, `tests/fm-guard-stale-banner.test.sh`, `tests/fm-turnend-guard.test.sh` - pass (3 suites, 0 failed)
- `tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh` - pass, run 3x for stability

Two failures to flag for review, both understood:

- `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` - fails with `ruby is required to parse .github/workflows/ci.yml as YAML`. This is environmental (no `ruby` on this host) and **reproduces identically on unmodified `origin/main`**, so it is preexisting and unrelated to this change.
- `tests/fm-session-start.test.sh` - fails with `MISSING diagnostic did not appear at all`. This one **passes on `origin/main` and fails here**. Cause: PR 8 had changed that fixture from `rm -f "$fakebin/node"` to `rm -f "$fakebin/chrome-devtools-axi"`, with the comment "without depending on whether the host ships Node in /usr/bin". Reverting restores the pre-Telegram fixture, which is host-dependent and fails on any host that ships Node in `/usr/bin` (this one does). The failure is in test scaffolding only, not in reverted product behavior.

For reviewer awareness, the reverts also naturally remove two non-Telegram changes that had ridden along inside those PR patches, since this branch is a pure revert and preserves nothing beyond the patches:

- the zombie-process rejection in `fm_harness_pid_alive` (`bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh`) and its regression test
- the arm-ready timeout budgets and the direct read-only `ensureArmed` assertion in `tests/fm-pi-watch-extension.test.sh`

These can be re-landed separately if wanted.

## Merge

Not merged here. Merge authority is held outside this branch, subject to repository checks.

author: cataggar
body:
Closes #471.

## Summary

Replaces all production use of `openssl`, `sbsign`, and `sbverify` in Ubuntu and Azure Linux image construction with in-tree, Zig-only cryptography. X.509 certificate handling, local-key Authenticode signing, and Secure Boot signature verification are now native and fail closed.

## Native crypto (`packages/vmiz/src/authenticode.zig`)

- Bounded PEM/DER X.509 parsing and normalization with chronological validity enforcement (`notBefore <= notAfter`).
- Native RSA private-key decoding (PKCS#8 and PKCS#1, PEM or DER).
- Native RSA-SHA256 Authenticode signing (`signPeRsaSha256Alloc`), which self-verifies the produced signature before returning.
- Full native Authenticode verification (`verifyRsaSha256`) that fails closed on signer substitution, certificate-digest mismatch, PE certificate-table/layout defects, digest-coverage mismatch, unsupported algorithms, and invalid validity.
- Native certificate-details formatting for provenance.

## Signing/verification wiring

- The shared release signer (`scripts/uki_signing.zig`) and both build scripts (`build_generalized_ubuntu2604.zig`, `build_generalized_azurelinux4.zig`) drop all external signing/verification tools; local-key signing and the production verify path are native.
- Artifact Signing (external provider) integration and provenance `certificate_details` wiring are preserved unchanged.

## CLI

Two native subcommands used by the release workflows:

- `vmiz uki fingerprint <cert.pem>` — prints a certificate's canonical DER SHA-256.
- `vmiz uki verify --certificate <cert.pem> <signed-pe>` — full native Authenticode verification that additionally asserts the embedded signer is **exactly** the enrolled certificate.

## Workflows

- Ubuntu and Azure Linux release **build** jobs no longer install or invoke `openssl` or `sbsigntool`; certificate fingerprinting uses `vmiz uki fingerprint` and the end-to-end signing probe uses `vmiz uki verify`.
- The optional external **acceptance oracle** (Ubuntu) is intentionally retained (`openssl`/`sbverify`) as an independent redundant check; it never feeds production crypto.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Production Ubuntu (and Azure) image construction does not install or invoke `openssl`, `sbsign`, or `sbverify` — the builders emit an unsigned UKI via `ukify` and sign/verify natively. ✅
2. Local and external signatures are verified natively against the exact enrolled certificate. ✅
3. Tampering, signer substitution, invalid validity, and malformed certificate tables fail closed. ✅
4. Provenance and certificate fingerprints remain byte-compatible (`certificate_details` + canonical DER SHA-256). ✅

## Tests

- `authenticode.zig` standalone: **18/18** (sign/verify roundtrip against the enrolled cert; fail-closed on tampering & signer substitution; rejection of malformed/encrypted keys; rejection of inverted validity).
- Full suite `zig build test`: **1822/1836 passed, 13 skipped** (not-root env skips). The only failure is the pre-existing, unrelated `commands.qemu` AArch64 firmware test (`qemu.zig`, untouched here and unrelated to signing).
- `zig build test-cli`: **115/116** (same single pre-existing qemu firmware failure).
- `check-/test-generalized-ubuntu2604` and `check-/test-generalized-azurelinux4`: all pass.
- Real-binary end-to-end (openssl absent from the environment): `vmiz uki fingerprint` matched an independent Python DER SHA-256 exactly; `vmiz uki verify` returned `0` for the enrolled cert and `1` for wrong-cert, tampered, unsigned, missing-file, and missing-argument cases.

## Notes

- The `commands.qemu` AArch64 firmware test failure is pre-existing and environmental (unchanged since before this branch; not touched by this PR). It is unrelated to signing and left as-is.
- Real Azure Artifact Signing provider output cannot be exercised in this environment, but the production verify path reuses the same parser proven by the tests above and accepts `rsaEncryption` + `sha256WithRSAEncryption`.

author: rasuvaeff
body:
Raised from 85, measured rather than guessed. A fresh Infection run on this
package's current master, on PHP 8.4 -- the version the `Coverage & Mutation`
job pins -- reports MSI 99.53 over 215 mutants, 1 of
them escaping. The gate stood at 85, so the package could have lost a large
share of its killed mutants and still gone green.

The new value is `floor(100 * (killed - 1) / tested)`: one mutant of slack, so
a single hard-to-kill line from an unrelated change does not turn the build
red, then floored to a whole percent.

No tag follows: `infection.json5` is `export-ignore`d, so the Composer dist is
byte-identical and no consumer can observe this.

The mutation job in this PR is the verification: it runs Infection on PHP 8.4 against the new gate.

author: souhailbourhim
body:
Continues the Phase 3 branch after PR #3. Delivers **3.C — entity resolution** (SPEC §7.2),
plus 3.B.4, which landed after #3 was cut.

`entities` has been reporting *"300 labeled, awaiting a decision function to score against"*
since 3.A. It now reports a number, and `evals/thresholds.toml`'s floors move off `0.0`.

| | precision | recall |
|---|---|---|
| train (fitted on) | 0.900 | 0.667 |
| **HELD OUT** | **0.833** | **0.556** |
| full set | 0.868 | 0.611 |

## What it does

Decides which company a name refers to — `Comcast` → `CMCSA`, `Mishpacha Fund, LP` → a
minted id for a company nobody has indexed, `Amazon` in *"oil discovery near Amazon river"* →
nothing at all. 246 of the 300 hand-labeled mentions are correctly **unlinked**, so abstaining
well is most of the work, and `score_entities` counts a correct abstention as a true negative
so a resolver that links nothing cannot look perfect.

Four channels, most certain first: a **CIK** the filing states next to the span, a **complete
name** in the dictionary, a **name prefix**, and a **minted slug** for a span declaring a legal
form. Below the fitted floor the answer is unlinked, and `Resolution.reason` records which way
so failure modes can be read off a run rather than guessed at.

`entities/resolve.py` is the single decision seam — the Spark job and `evals/score.py` both
call it, the same contract `dedup.decide` keeps — and mention *detection* moved out of the eval
harness into `entities/mentions.py` for the same reason. The 300 labels were drawn against
those spans at those offsets; a second detector in the pipeline would mean the published
accuracy describes spans nothing ever produces. Verified: 298 of 300 labels re-detect.

## Tables

- `silver.entity_mentions` — a function of (article, dictionary, algorithm), so re-resolving
  **replaces** the day partitions. Deliberately *not* keyed by the resolve window: a cluster
  belongs to the window that produced it, but a mention resolves the same way whichever window
  asks.
- `silver.dim_entities` — **SCD2**, the only table here where a row is superseded rather than
  replaced. An article published the day before Facebook became Meta did not retroactively
  become an article about Meta, and the labels are drawn that way. This is also why the
  dictionary is a committed snapshot with a `built_at`: a live SEC call has no `valid_from` to
  give.
- `airflow/dags/resolve_dag.py` — 04:30 daily, half an hour ahead of `cluster`, so 3.D finds
  both tables rebuilt from the same day's silver.

## Three findings worth the review time

**A CIK is negative evidence too, and it was the biggest precision win.** EDGAR Form 4 and 144
filers are people filing under their own names, surname first — and surnames start company
names constantly. `Matthews Mark E.` resolved to Matthews International, `GEE DAVID NICHOLAS`
to GEE Group. The filing states the filer's CIK and no company owns it, so that vetoes the
link. A legal form overrides the veto, because a private fund also holds a CIK no ticker claims.

**A rollup silently disabled the CIK channel for the company it rolled up to.** A Wikidata
subsidiary was emitted as an `Entity` carrying its *parent's* id; entities are keyed by id, so
`Transamerica Corporation` overwrote `AEGON LTD.` and took cik `0000769218` out of the lookup.
A filing that stated its own CIK then fell through to minting a slug. Nothing raised — accuracy
just dropped. Fixed three ways (rollups become aliases of the parent, `build` is
first-writer-wins, parents matched through the name index rather than by slug equality, because
`paypal` never equals `paypal-holdings`), each pinned as a regression test.

**More data was wrong, and the notability floor was mislabelled.** With every business Wikidata
knows down to 5 sitelinks, held-out precision was 0.762 — *below* the SEC-only 0.812 — and
`Carver Passed Away` linked to a company called Carver. An alias index is only as precise as
its rarest junk entry.

| sitelinks | entities | size | train P/R | held-out P/R |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 39,200 | 1,075 KB | 0.800 / 0.593 | 0.762 / 0.593 |
| 10 | 19,782 | 607 KB | 0.800 / 0.593 | 0.762 / 0.593 |
| **20** | **11,835** | **388 KB** | **0.900 / 0.667** | **0.833 / 0.556** |
| 40 | 8,771 | 286 KB | 0.889 / 0.593 | 0.824 / 0.519 |

A third of the size and better on both axes. `MIN_SITELINKS` had been documented as "a knob on
dictionary size, not on the decision" — that was wrong, and wrong in the direction that
flatters a bigger download. At 388 KB it also fits inside the repo's own 512 KB large-file
guard, so no guardrail was loosened to hold a generated artifact.

## The fitting changed, and the held-out half is why

Two procedures were tried and rejected because the split caught them, both looking fine on the
column they were chosen on:

| procedure | train | held out |
|---|---|---|
| max recall s.t. precision ≥ 0.75 | 0.760 / 0.704 | **0.615** / 0.593 |
| the same, with `COMMON_WORD_RANK` also in the grid | 0.905 / 0.704 | **0.727** / 0.593 |
| the same, grid point chosen by 4-fold CV inside train | 0.792 / 0.704 | **0.667** / 0.593 |
| **max F1 s.t. precision ≥ 0.75, one constant fitted** | 0.900 / 0.667 | **0.833** / 0.556 |

Maximising recall under a precision floor *rides* the floor — it took the point whose train
precision was 0.760, barely clearing 0.75, while a knee sat one step away at 0.900 for a single
mention of recall. The constraint did not move; the objective inside it was wrong. And two
constants over 27 positives is fitting noise, so one is fitted and the other is set on a stated
rule. That F1 is right here and wrong for dedup is a real difference, not an inconsistency: a
false merge deletes a story the reader never learns was missing, while a mention filed under
the wrong company is something they see.

## Deliberately not done

- **`Meta` and `Apple` are unlinkable** on the word alone — they are ordinary English words, and
  the labels contain both readings. That is SPEC §7.2's embedding stage, deferred by decision at
  the top of the runbook and carried into ADR-0009. Largest share of the 21 false negatives.
- **Three channels are inert at the fitted floor** (prefix matching, corroboration, and the
  common-word rank above 2,000). Documented and pinned in tests rather than left to imply the
  system does more than it does — they are what a *lower* floor would use once embeddings make
  one defensible.
- Three false positives survive, each a different kind of hard: `BofA Finance LLC` → a rollup
  Wikidata does not record, `USA Today Sparking` → a masthead rather than a company, `FlyWire` →
  a fruit-fly connectome sharing a name with a payments company.

## Checks

`make eval` green with floors raised to 0.82 / 0.58 · `make lint` clean · full suite passes,
including 9 new Spark tests over the two tables and the SCD2 rename history.

## Summary by Sourcery

Deliver entity resolution and its production data pipeline while correcting cluster recency ranking and establishing reproducible evaluation thresholds.

New Features:
- Add deterministic entity resolution using SEC CIKs, complete and prefix names, legal-form minting, and confidence-based abstention.
- Build and commit a reproducible SEC/Wikidata entity dictionary with aliases, parent rollups, common-word data, and primary ticker selection.
- Add Spark pipelines and a daily Airflow DAG for resolved mentions and SCD2 entity history.
- Move shared mention detection into the production entities module and use it for both evaluation and Spark processing.

Bug Fixes:
- Rank clusters by their latest trusted coverage rather than their earliest canonical article, preserving both first-seen and last-seen timestamps.
- Prevent entity rollups and duplicate identifiers from displacing SEC canonical records and CIK mappings.
- Correct entity evaluation to count abstentions and wrong links accurately, and replace zero accuracy floors with measured thresholds.

Enhancements:
- Add offline en

author: apriendeau
body:
`SearchOpts::limit_per` diversifies by attribute value. Nothing diversified by vector space,
so five near-identical passages could fill the top five, including five chunks of one parent
document, which parent rollup cannot fix either.

`SearchOpts::diversity: Option<f32>` is a Maximal Marginal Relevance lambda. Over an
over-fetched window it greedily selects the candidate maximising
`lambda * score - (1 - lambda) * max_similarity_to_already_selected`. Pure arithmetic over
vectors the store already holds: no new dependency, no format change, Miri-clean.

## Where it lives

One seam. `Store::finish` is already the single tail every ranked surface funnels through, so
the new order is **cap -> MMR -> page cut**: `limit_per` is a hard constraint and runs first,
leaving MMR to reorder only legal survivors, and both precede pagination because reshaping a
page moves the boundary rather than what crosses it. That one placement is why it composes
with `limit_per`, `rank_by`, ANN, quantization, the segment indexes, `text_search` and the
rerank stage without any of them knowing about it.

## Four things that are load-bearing

- **Cosine, not dot.** Vectors are unit-normalized on insert only when `Config::distance` is
  `Cosine`, so redundancy is computed from each candidate's real norm. Otherwise a
  `DotProduct`/`Euclidean` store would measure magnitude as similarity.
- **Determinism.** Candidates are walked in ranked order and replace the incumbent only on a
  strictly greater MMR score, so a tie resolves the way the ranking already did and SPEC 7's
  total order (and pagination with it) still holds. `lambda` is validated finite, so no NaN
  can enter the comparison.
- **A documented window bound.** MMR is O(W^2 * dim), so it reorders at most 512 head
  candidates and a deeper page keeps its score order. A diversified search over-fetches
  `(offset + top_k) * 4`; where a cap is also asked for, the larger factor wins rather than
  the two multiplying.
- **Vectorless records.** A text-only doc reachable through `text_search` has nothing
  measurable to be redundant with, so it carries no penalty rather than being dropped.

`None` is the default and provably a no-op: it skips the pass and does not deepen the scan.

## Surfaces

Core, HTTP (`/search`, `/search/similar`, `/text-search`, `/collections/{}/recall`, and
`/search/batch` for free), CLI (`search`, `similar`, `text-search`, `recall`), MCP (`recall`,
`text_search`, `related`), all three SDKs, and the docs. `HybridOpts` gets nothing, exactly as
it has no `limit_per`: its fused list is cut inline and carries per-leg detail. `hybrid_search`
is asserted **not** to advertise the knob, so the MCP schema cannot promise what the handler
cannot honour.

`0.0` is a meaningful lambda (pure spread), which is a trap in three encoders at once: Go's
`omitempty` on a bare `float32` would drop it (hence `*float32`), and `RecallOpts` uses zero as
its "unset" sentinel for `top_k`/`min_score` (hence `Option<f32>`). All three SDKs assert the
key is **absent** when unset rather than null, and present when zero.

## Tests

Every assertion names what would be wrong without the feature, not that a query ran. Verified
by neutering `Store::diversify` to a no-op: five behavioural store tests go red, and the four
that stay green are the ones that should (the no-op test, the over-fetch-depth test, the
top-hit-never-moves test, the tie-order test).

Behaviour is asserted at every level: the greedy selection in isolation, a near-duplicate
corpus where the returned ids demonstrably change, ANN (HNSW and IVF) and int8/binary
quantization, `limit_per`, `rank_by`, pagination, an unnormalized `DotProduct` store, a
text-only hit, a file-backed reopen, over real HTTP, through the real binary's `--diversity`,
and over MCP. A lambda outside `[0.0, 1.0]` is a 400, not a 500.

## Rebased onto #217, which changed two things here

`recall_reranked` arrived with #217 at 10 arguments plus
`#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`, and `diversity` would have made 11. It now takes the
`memory::RecallArgs` struct this branch already introduces, which brings it to 6 and **deletes
the allow**. `diversity` threads into its `SearchOpts` and composes with `--rerank` for free
through `search_reranked`, the same seam the HTTP and MCP recall paths use.

`TextSearchRequest`, the CLI query arms and the three SDKs now carry both `diversity` and
#217's `rerank`. `/search/similar` deliberately has only `diversity`, matching #217's decision
to keep rerank off that route.

## One hunk that is not MMR, declared rather than hidden

`.claude/skills/nidus/SKILL.md:174` documented the Review step as
`nidus-check laws --pr <n>` (or **`--base main`**, or bare). With a stale local `main` that
reports **green over the wrong range**: in this clone `--base main` examined 93 files where the
real diff is 43, the other 87 coming from twelve already-merged commits (#208 through #217).
It bit two sessions independently today, and the vulnerable invocation is the documented one,
so nobody slipped. Changed to `--base origin/main`.

This is one line and unrelated to MMR. It rides here at the maintainer's explicit direction
rather than by accident; the checker-side guard (and the `lanes` half of the same bug, which
is worse) stays in **nidus-qko**. `nidus-check selftest` is 112/112, and the skill change owes
no automated lane.

Refs nidus-qko (the stale-`--base` guard this documents the cheap half of).
Refs nidus-33g (the CLI `text-search --limit-per` gap this uncovered but did not fix).

Closes nidus-tx2

author: lobinuxsoft
body:
## Qué pasa

Bazzite 44 trajo `bazzite-updater` (repo **Terra**, upstream [rfrench3/bazzite-updater](https://github.com/rfrench3/bazzite-updater)) y el menú quedó con **dos actualizadores** uno al lado del otro: el nuestro (`system-update.desktop`, terminal + `ujust update`) y el suyo, rotulado *"Bazzite Updater"* y marcado como nuevo.

Detectado en la F1 Pro sobre `yaguarete-deck-44.20260820`.

## Qué hace este PR

Se queda con el de ellos y oculta el nuestro, **no al revés**. Es una GUI Qt que corre la misma actualización por `uupd-manual.service` y suma dos cosas que el nuestro nunca tuvo: **rollback** y **notas de versión**. En una consola portátil que se maneja con los dedos eso no es cosmético. Sus dos dependencias ya están en la imagen (`uupd-manual.service`, `bazzite-rollback-helper`).

El rebrand **no necesita fork ni parchear binarios** — al contrario de la cirugía del asar de hhd-ui. Upstream dice explícitamente que la app es *"configurable for any Linux distro"* y lee su identidad de dos archivos:

| Archivo | Qué cambia |
|---|---|
| `/etc/bazzite-updater/KAboutData_OS.json` | nombre, descripción, homepage, bug tracker, créditos |
| `/etc/bazzite-updater/config.ini` | el feed de releases apunta a este repo |
| `io.github.rfrench3.bazzite-updater.desktop` | `Name=Yaguareté Updater`, `Icon=yaguarete-update`, `TryExec` |

El arte dentro de la app **ya era nuestro**: `build.sh` symlinkea los SVG de `/usr/share/ublue-os/bazzite/`, y `programLogo` resuelve a `distributor-logo.svg`, que es byte-idéntico a `yaguarete-logo.svg` (mismo md5).

## Por qué el gate está en el Containerfile y no en build.sh

`COPY system_files/overrides /` corre **después** de `build.sh`, así que en build.sh todavía no existe nuestro rebrand para condicionar nada.

Y el gate importa: `bazzite-updater` viene del repo Terra vía la base de Bazzite, y está verificado sólo en la variante **deck**. Si alguna variante llegara sin el paquete, ocultar nuestro lanzador dejaría esa imagen **sin ningún actualizador en el menú** y con un `.desktop` apuntando a un binario inexistente. En ese caso el rebrand se descarta y la entrada de consola queda visible. `TryExec` cubre el mismo caso en runtime si alguien desinstala el paquete en un sistema vivo.

`ujust update` sigue existiendo; sólo se oculta su lanzador.

## Verificación pendiente

- [ ] Build verde en las 4 variantes, y confirmar en el log de cada una qué rama del gate tomó (`[updater] …`)
- [ ] Smoke en la F1 Pro: una sola entrada en *Sistema*, nombre e ícono correctos, y el "acerca de" con nuestros datos
- [ ] Que el feed RSS traiga las releases de este repo

author: ntshgarg
body:
A coach could not reschedule a session from a desktop or tablet browser. Found during a UI audit and confirmed by measurement against a running app, not by eye.

## The bug

Expanding **Replace session** in the calendar day pane renders a form whose required `Venue` input and `Create replacement` button sit outside the visible area, with no scrollbar to reach them. Since `Venue` is `required`, the form cannot be submitted at all.

Three things combine to cause it:

- `.coach-occurrence-actions details > div` was `grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(110px, 1fr))` with 12px gaps and 18px padding — a hard **512px minimum width**.
- That grid sat in a non-wrapping flex row beside `Cancel session`, inside `.coach-calendar-workspace`'s day pane, which is sized `minmax(340px, 0.82fr)` — **340 to 450px** in practice.
- `.coach-day-view` uses `overflow: hidden`, so the excess was silently destroyed rather than made scrollable.

The rules that would have fixed it (`flex-direction: column`, `grid-template-columns: 1fr`) existed but were gated behind `@media (max-width: 760px)`. Fitting the original grid would need a viewport around 2000px wide, so it was broken across the entire practical desktop and tablet range.

## Measured evidence

Day pane width, and whether each control was inside the clip boundary:

| Viewport | Day pane | Venue | Create button |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1440px | 447px | clipped | clipped |
| 1100px | 380px | clipped | clipped |
| 820px | 340px | clipped | clipped |
| 760px | 744px | visible | visible |

After the change, all four widths report both controls visible.

## The fix

- An open disclosure takes its own full-width row (`details[open] { flex: 1 1 100% }`) instead of sharing one with `Cancel session`.
- The field grid uses fluid `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(120px, 1fr))` tracks, so it adapts to whatever width the pane has and cannot overflow again at some future size.
- `flex-shrink: 0` on the trigger buttons stops `Cancel session` collapsing into a two-line sliver.

`overflow: hidden` on `.coach-day-view` is left alone deliberately — the form is now intrinsically fluid so nothing overflows, and changing overflow on a `position: sticky` element risks unrelated layout regressions. Worth a separate look, since it is what turned a layout overflow into an invisible failure.

## Behaviour preserved

The closed state is unchanged: `Cancel session` and `Replace session` still share one row, verified at 1440px with both at the same y offset. Only the open form reflows.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm test` — 568 tests across 129 files, all passing
- Before and after captured from a live dev server on the 40-player demo fixture at four widths, with programmatic clip-boundary checks rather than visual inspection alone.

## Related

Styling-only fixes from the same audit are in #17. This PR is independent of it.

Also found and not yet addressed: the staff attendance register opens on 1 January instead of today (`initialIndex: 0` / `scrollOnReset: false`, where the player register correctly derives both from today), and `jumpToToday()` needs two clicks from another year.

author: rasuvaeff
body:
Raised from 85, measured rather than guessed. A fresh Infection run on this
package's current master, on PHP 8.4 -- the version the `Coverage & Mutation`
job pins -- reports MSI 98.04 over 102 mutants, 2 of
them escaping. The gate stood at 85, so the package could have lost a large
share of its killed mutants and still gone green.

The new value is `floor(100 * (killed - 1) / tested)`: one mutant of slack, so
a single hard-to-kill line from an unrelated change does not turn the build
red, then floored to a whole percent.

No tag follows: `infection.json5` is `export-ignore`d, so the Composer dist is
byte-identical and no consumer can observe this.

The mutation job in this PR is the verification: it runs Infection on PHP 8.4 against the new gate.

PR #1 ported the Cursor `automate-me` skill under the assumption that no structured multi-choice question tool existed on this host, so Step 2 was drafted around plain numbered-chat text. That assumption was wrong: a real `AskUserQuestion`-equivalent tool is confirmed available, supporting multiple-choice (with an implicit free-text escape hatch) and free-form answers, but only **one question at a time** — no batching, no `allow_multiple`.

## Skill authoring
- Added `automate-me/SKILL.md.tmpl`, listing `AskUserQuestion` as a first-class `allowed-tools` entry (not a commented-out note).
- Rewrote Step 2 to use `AskUserQuestion` as the primary mechanism: a sequence of individual questions (broad round → scoped follow-up(s) → free-form catch-all) instead of a batched multi-select round. Dropped all `allow_multiple`-style phrasing; free-form custom answers now do the work of capturing multiple areas in one reply when needed.
- Reframed the "don't depend on a structured tool" language to "use this tool, one question at a time" as the default, with plain numbered-chat kept only as a fallback if the tool is ever unavailable.
- Ported the remaining steps (history mining via session search instead of file globs, drafting through this repo's own `SKILL.md.tmpl` → `gen:skill-docs` → `skill:check` pipeline instead of `create-skill`, inlined prose-discipline checklist instead of external `unslop`/`poteto-mode` references, worktree/PR landing).

author: bendrucker
body:
## Description

New extension for [Screens 5](https://edovia.com/en/screens) by Edovia, a VNC/RDP/SSH client for macOS.

Three commands:

- **Search Connections** lists your connections grouped by type, ordered by how often and how recently you connect. Connect normally, or on a VNC connection in Observe Mode or as a guest. Add, edit, and remove connections, and filter by type from the search bar.
- **Import Connections** reads a `.screens` archive exported from the app and lets you pick which connections to keep.
- **Quick Connect** opens a VNC or SSH session to a machine that isn't in your list, taking the host straight from the root search bar (`desk-imac.local`, `admin@10.0.0.4:5901`, `ssh://192.0.2.10`) or from a form.

Two design decisions shaped the rest.

#### Importing as a Command

Screens keeps its library in CloudKit with no local store to read, and exposes no scripting interface. The only way in is an archive the user exports. That archive also holds every host Screens discovered on the local network, which for a real library is mostly machines the user would never open. Importing is therefore a deliberate step where you choose what to keep, defaulting to the connections you have actually connected to.

#### Direct Addressing

`screens://` addresses a saved connection by name or hostname, and neither is unique. In the library this was built against, one name was shared by three entries resolving to three different machines.

When a name identifies exactly one connection, the extension opens it through Screens, keeping its stored settings and credentials. When it doesn't, the extension connects to the machine's address instead, marks the row, and shows the address as the subtitle. Editing a connection lets you override either choice.

The extension reads only the archive you select. It never touches the app's container or any credential material.

The Screens icon is used with the makers' permission.

## Screencast

Metadata screenshots are coming in a follow-up commit to this branch.

## Remaining Before Review

- [ ] Add `metadata/` screenshots at 2000x1250, one per view command
- [ ] Run `npm run build` and test the distribution build
- [ ] Exercise the three forms end to end in Raycast
- [ ] Confirm the Quick Connect host field rejects the right inputs without getting in the way
- [ ] Mark ready for review

## Checklist

- [x] I read the [extension guidelines](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store)
- [x] I read the [documentation about publishing](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/publish-an-extension)

- [x] I checked that files in the `assets` folder are used by the extension itself

author: ag2trust-dev
body:
## Confirmed failure

The v57 migration in `migrate()` (`quorum-core/src/db.rs`) rebuilds `role_assignments` (DROP + recreate to widen the role CHECK to admit `arbiter`). Four child tables — `agent_runs`, `task_decompositions`, `review_collection_runs`, `routing_attempts` — hold `REFERENCES role_assignments(id)` foreign keys.

rusqlite's **bundled SQLite defaults `foreign_keys` ON** (no explicit enable in the open path — `apply_pragmas` never sets it, the default is the source). With enforcement on, the `DROP TABLE role_assignments` fails with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` (extended code 787), the entire `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` migration rolls back, `user_version` stays at 56, and **the daemon cannot start on the new binary** on any real database.

The existing test `migrates_v56_widens_role_assignment_check_to_admit_arbiter` missed this: it created `role_assignments` in isolation with **no child tables referencing it**, so the DROP succeeded even with FKs on.

## Fix

`PRAGMA foreign_keys` is a no-op inside a transaction, and `migrate()` wraps all migrations in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so the toggle must straddle that transaction:

1. After the `current == SCHEMA_VERSION` early return (i.e. only when a migration is pending), **capture the connection's current `foreign_keys` state** (`fk_prior`), then set `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` **before** `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`.
2. Run the existing migration body/commit unchanged (extracted verbatim into `migrate_txn`, preserving `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`).
3. **Restore `foreign_keys` to `fk_prior` on every exit path** — the restore runs before `outcome?` propagates any error, so enforcement is never left disabled on a live connection after a failed migration.
4. Safety net on success: run `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` under re-enabled enforcement; if it returns any row, fail loud (`SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY`). The rebuild preserves ids/data via `INSERT…SELECT`, so this is a guard, not expected to trip.

`ensure_schema_supported` / newer-DB refusal and all other migration steps are untouched.

## Test now reproduces the real failure

The migration test now seeds a child table with a real `… REFERENCES role_assignments(id)` FK and a row referencing an existing parent id, and enables `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` explicitly to mirror the runtime. It asserts: migration reaches `SCHEMA_VERSION`, the parent (id=9) and child rows survive, the connection still has FK enforcement on, `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` is clean, and the widened CHECK admits an `arbiter` row.

- **Pre-fix:** panics with `Db(SqliteFailure(..., 787, "FOREIGN KEY constraint failed"))` at the migration open.
- **Post-fix:** passes. Existing behavior stays green.

## Verification

`rtk proxy ./preflight.sh` — PASS (fmt + clippy + full tests, all 4 gates green, 1082 tests). Pre-push hook not bypassed.

## For reviewers to scrutinize

- Restore ordering: `conn.pragma_update("foreign_keys", fk_prior)?` runs before `outcome?`, so a migration error still restores enforcement.
- The FK-on source is the rusqlite bundled default, not an explicit pragma.
- `foreign_key_check` guard only runs when `fk_prior` was true.
