body:
## What this is

Round-1 **isolated PoC deploy** of CrossWatch (github.com/cenodude/CrossWatch, AGPL-3.0) into the `media` namespace — the first step of the `crosswatch-implementation` roadmap (P0 Trakt watch-history rescue). The Trakt live API is permanently gone (app disabled, proven; last scrobble 2026-07-29), so CrossWatch replaces the dead Trakt sync as the primary watch-state tracker, seeded from the Trakt ZIP export (5639 events: 310 movie / 5329 episode, 174 unique movies / 4688 unique episodes / 249 shows).

### Commits
- `e9f6def29` — round-1 manifests (ks.yaml, app/{kustomization,helmrelease,httproute}.yaml), registered in media kustomization
- `72d106809` — drop the no-op `external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/controller: none` annotation (envoy-internal routes are invisible to ExternalDNS, which only watches envoy-external)
- `e48b69114` — docs: Trakt-API-disabled fact, Jellyfin backfill, phase order

## What is deliberately NOT in this PR (round-1 isolation)
- **No provider credentials, no ExternalSecret** — SIMKL/Plex/Jellyfin are not wired. Nothing that can write into the real libraries runs until the import + round-trip are green.
- **No zeroscaler** — the pod stays warm during the import + measure PoC; add it back for sibling consistency once green.
- **No app-level CiliumNetworkPolicy** — baseline `allow-cluster-egress` only (in-cluster, no internet). The importer does not call TMDB (verified in `services/importer.py` v0.11.2); the Trakt export itself carries trakt/imdb/tmdb/tvdb IDs, so matching needs no external call.

## Posture (evidence-backed, not guessed)
- Image pinned `ghcr.io/cenodude/crosswatch:0.11.2@sha256:52ee...a337` (tag has NO `v` prefix; `v0.11.2` = MANIFEST_UNKNOWN) + renovate annotation.
- `/config` PVC via the shared VolSync component (local-hostpath, 5Gi, not NFS); ks.yaml `dependsOn` onepassword-connect + democratic-csi.
- HTTPRoute **envoy-internal only** (`crosswatch.${PUBLIC_DOMAIN}`) — LAN-only, off the public internet while the import is unverified.
- non-root 10001, `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, emptyDir `/tmp` (Starlette multipart spool), TCP probes matching the upstream Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK.

## Verify-at-PoC (after deploy, not pre-fabricated)
- Generated Service name / liveness path / egress need / `/tmp` writability — confirm on the live pod.
- **UID 1000 hypothesis** (not pre-flipped; 10001 is the repo-dominant convention): the image builds its own user at UID 1000. If the pod log shows `pwd.getpwuid() -> KeyError: getpwuid(): uid not found` or a permission-denied writing under the appuser home, the fix is one line `runAsUser: 1000`. Let the log decide.
- **Measurement interpretation**: memory limit is 512Mi for 5639 events into SQLite — an OOM is the LIMIT, not a CrossWatch bug (check OOMKilled). If "unmatched" rows appear, look at the NETWORK first (no app CNP round-1), not the software.

## Next step
Push + reconcile, then run the 3-step import API (`GET /api/import/options` → `POST /api/import/preview` → `GET /api/import/preview/{id}` → `POST /api/import/commit`) from the Mac over the envoy-internal LAN route, and measure the preview row count against the P0 ground-truth baseline (5639 events). Reaching the import is the gate for everything else.

## Flux deploy note
Flux watches `refs/heads/main` only (`kubernetes/apps/flux-system/flux-instance/app/helmrelease.yaml:28`). This PR does not deploy on push; the deploy starts when this PR is **merged** to main (webhook Receiver / 1h poll).

author: eod
body:
Unify the e2e scenarios by housting them into bot/lib.js as summarizeInventory and dbInventory, plus rconAsk and setDbLatency on the harness.
This drops multiple lines of duplicated code and leaves each scenario stating only what it is about.

lib.js also gains the helpers for driving the stack itself - run, compose, composeFile, containerId, logCount, dataVolume and loadedModConfig - so a scenario that has to recreate a server under a different config starts from shared code rather than from a fresh copy of `docker compose` plumbing.

Both servers also shared one toxiproxy proxy, so a latency toxic slowed both of them at once and could never single out one server's database traffic - which is exactly what a scenario about one server's writes racing the other's needs. Give server-b its own proxy on 3307 (config/server-b now points at it), and make setDbLatency take the server whose traffic it slows, so a caller cannot forget which one it meant.

author: gald33
body:
15 commits. The experiment now runs on the real substrate, and a round of it actually worked.

## The standing decisions, written down

`CLAUDE.md` at the repo root. Two rules I violated repeatedly across this session, now recorded with the failure modes named rather than just the principles:

- **The board is the only surface.** No tool API, no action schema, no `produce()`/`offer()`/`accept()` methods. The economy exists only as a manager function that reads formatted board messages and settles them.
- **There is no scheduler.** Every agent is its own long-lived concurrent session that reads and writes when it chooses. No turn-taking, no waves, no batching, no waiting. *"If the design starts to need a 'turn', stop — something has gone wrong."*

I built the forbidden thing twice after we settled it in conversation. The file exists so the next session inherits the decision instead of my drift.

## v3

**Agents use the native Switchboard MCP server and nothing else** — `agent-switchboard` was already pinned in 002's requirements the whole time; I found it by writing my own board file and having the package name collide with it. Six tools: `say`, `history`, `inbox`, `dm`, `roster`, `whoami`, plus `checkin` as the loop tool and `sleep`.

**The manager joins the same channel through the Switchboard client**, as one more participant. It reads history, settles `PRODUCE` / `PROPOSE` / `APPROVE`, says receipts back, and enforces only timing, format and scoring. A near-miss is refused with a reason and never repaired.

**Agents schedule their own wake-ups.** `checkin` is Switchboard's own main-loop primitive — heartbeat, returns what arrived, blocks up to 25s on `wait`. No supervisor, no relaunch, nothing touching an agent.

**One workspace per arm**, because roster, inbox and `dm` are workspace-scoped and separate channels alone would have let two arms see each other.

## The run

`bare`, 1 round, 8 episodes, 2 agents. 95 messages on the board, committed at `results/v3/board-island6-bare-1.json`.

```
eff_round 0.530   floor 0.823   per-episode [0.00 0.00 0.58 0.58 0.58 0.58 0.58 0.58]
settled 31   refused 2   talk 0   ack 2/2
```

Both traders acknowledged the schedule in their own words. They specialised — T1 into cloth, T2 into salt — found one cloth-for-salt exchange by episode 3 and repeated it unchanged for six episodes. Episodes 1 and 2 score zero because a proposal was made and never approved before the bell.

The two refusals are agents learning the surface: a two-good bundle written with a space instead of a comma, and an `APPROVE` of a lapsed proposal during the production window. Neither mistake was repeated.

**`talk 0`** — not one line of conversation. They coordinated by pattern-matching on settlements, in the arm with no protocol and no hint.

## Four harness faults found and fixed, all mine

1. `--append-system-prompt` caching, then a leaked `SWITCHBOARD_KEY` in the child env making every MCP call fail with `hub_unreachable`.
2. The same key in the *parent* env making the manager encrypt a workspace the agents had no key for — so their writes were rejected while reads worked. An agent diagnosed this better than I did: *"read operations work… the hub's signing service is not responding to write requests."* Nothing was wrong with the hub.
3. A guard that raised when an agent *chose* to stop, conflating agent behaviour with a session that could not start. The two are now told apart by what the runtime said.
4. `history(limit=1000)` against a hub that caps at 500 — which killed a completed run at the one moment its results existed only in memory.

## What this is not

**Not a result.** One round, one arm, two agents, scoring below the autarky floor, and there is no v3 pre-registration. It demonstrates the instrument runs end to end on the real surface. The v2 record and both its amendments are preserved; the v2 pilot that ran under the old structure is superseded and its harness-failure record was deleted rather than left in `results/` to be mistaken for a measurement.

The mark under a new score becomes the score itself: the number is set in --fresh-ink, the same red .model-new gives a new model's name, and the gradient stroke goes. It needs !important to land, over the grey ramp renderRow writes inline on the cell and over the blue of a top score, which .top-score also claims with !important — a cell that is both now reads red on the blue wash, which is the precedence the palette comment already described.

The stroke faded as a score aged, over a week, and a colour cannot carry that the same way: fading the number toward the background would dim data, not decoration, and mixing it back toward the text colour would stop it being the same red new models get. So the table's mark is now yes/no. scoreFreshness() still returns the graded value — the Recently Added panel fades a day's dot with it — but the score cells no longer carry --fresh, so that is dropped from renderRow rather than left dangling.

body:
## Контекст

PR #685 (мёржен, `1edee13`) починил редирект на канонический URL проекта задачи. В комментарии к тому PR автор явно пометил один пункт приёмки как непокрытый тестом:

> Пункт 4 — закрыт чтением кода, а не тестом... Автотеста на этот путь нет.

Внутренняя карточка была переназначена мне через fleet-balancer (checkout lease истёк без heartbeat у предыдущего исполнителя) уже ПОСЛЕ того, как #685 был смёржен. Функциональный фикс уже в `main` — новых правок в `task-detail.tsx` в этом PR нет. Этот PR закрывает единственный обнаруженный пробел: тест на негативный сценарий.

## Что сделано

`web/src/pages/__tests__/task-detail-canonical-project.test.tsx`: добавлен кейс `does not redirect for a taskId that does not exist, under any slug` — рендерит `TaskDetailPage` с несуществующим `taskId` и проверяет, что `navigate()` не вызывается ни при каком слаге (эффект должен молчать благодаря guard'у `!currentTask`).

Мутационный контроль: убрал `!currentTask` из guard'а — новый тест падает красным (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'project_id')`), остальные 3 теста остаются зелёными. Значит тест ловит именно отсутствие проверки, а не что попало.

## Проверка приёмки (все 4 пункта исходного требования)

| # | Статус | Чем закрыт |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Чужой слаг → адрес сам становится каноническим | ✅ | тест `redirects a task opened under a foreign project's slug...` (из #685), прогнан локально — зелёный |
| 2. Правильный слаг → без редиректа, без цикла | ✅ | тесты `does not redirect when the slug already matches...` + `settles after one redirect...` (из #685) |
| 3. «Назад» ведёт на доску настоящего проекта | ✅ | не изменялось этим PR; `handleBack` резолвит проект через `task.project_id`, подтверждено чтением (см. #685) |
| 4. Негативный контроль: несуществующий taskId | ✅ **закрыт этим PR** | новый тест `does not redirect for a taskId that does not exist, under any slug` + мутационный контроль |

## Прогон

- `npx vitest run` (весь web-пакет): **660/660 зелёных** (69 файлов)
- `npx vitest run src/pages/__tests__/task-detail-canonical-project.test.tsx`: **4/4 зелёных**
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: чисто
- `git push` прогнал pre-push хук `make ci` — прошёл

## Скриншоты §1k — не приложены, причина

Функциональных правок в `task-detail.tsx` нет (уже смёржены в #685), диф — только тест. Живой стенд требует аутентификации; у меня нет валидной сессии/учётных данных для него (не пытался обходить логин — запрещено правилами безопасности), а поднимать локально полный стек (Go-бэкенд + Postgres) ради скриншота одного текстового теста посчитал избыточным для этого PR.

body:
Sophie got a third Claude account.

**The tab row** grows a third account tab, and the accounts are labelled with bare **digits** instead of "Account 1" (her ask — four tabs across a 390pt phone leave ~97px each, which "Account 3" plus a badge does not fit in). The word is not lost: it is each tab's `aria-label`. The sliding line already measures the lit tab, so the row needed no layout work.

**The App/Web switch** on the title line is a three-position control now: one digit slot per account, left → right = 1 · 2 · 3, the lit one being the account she is signed into on the phone. Every other account's chats keep routing to the web via `#no_universal_links`, which already worked for any account value. An on/off switch had nowhere to put a third state.

**One list of accounts.** The digits were hand-written in four places (tab row, the row's account mark, the thread's picker, the header switch); they all come from one `ACCOUNTS` array now, so a fourth account is one entry.

### The switch was measured, not eyeballed

The masthead is the one row in this app that has run out of room before (five controls plus the title put the bookmark button under the word "Chats", so tapping the title opened Bookmarks). Measured on the real page:

- controls fill **205.8px**, the title takes what is left
- a bordered three-slot track came to **57px** (vs the old switch's 42) and put the controls back over the title at her own 390
- three trackless 16px digit slots = **48px**, plus `.hctl`'s gap tightened 6px→4px, comes to **205.8px** — the header is exactly where it was

The marker is **ink, not the old ON-state red**: with three positions one slot is always live, so red would sit permanently in the masthead. Same reasoning that took the red off the account tabs.

### Tests

`node scripts/test-chats-accounts.js` now covers account 3 end to end, the three-way switch (including that a chat on an account she is *not* signed into routes to the web and that tapping the live slot is a no-op), the tab badges, and a hit-test of the title against the header controls at 375/390/430. `test-chats-news.js`, `test-chats-tab-lines.js` and `test-chats-title-back.js` updated for the fourth tab and the three switch slots.

author: tya5
body:
**[e2e-coder]** — part of #5028

## What / Why

`test_plain_path_survives_flowview_absence` spawns
`sys.executable -c ...` with no `env=` override, so the subprocess
inherits ambient `sys.path` resolution instead of pytest's own
`pythonpath = ["src"]` (which is in-process only). On a machine whose
ambient interpreter/venv carries a foreign editable `.pth` — this
repo's own real incident (#5028): `sandbox_2`'s install shadows
`reyn.interfaces.repl.read_model`, `ImportError: cannot import name
'LOCAL_CHAT_READ_CAPABILITIES'` — the subprocess silently reads a
DIFFERENT checkout's `reyn`.

This is exactly the class `out_of_process_reyn` (`tests/conftest.py`,
already an established fixture used by 20 files — verified, not
assumed after an earlier wrong "unused" claim of mine on the issue)
exists to close. Fix: request the fixture, pin its returned src root
as `PYTHONPATH` in the subprocess's env — the same pattern already
used by `tests/llm/test_llm_run_async_client_cache_scope_3434.py` and
others.

## Scope

- **This one test only** — #5028's own instruction was not to sweep
  other files.
- **Does not touch `./conftest.py`'s #3233 in-process guard** — a
  separate, already-correct mechanism for a different half of the same
  divergence class (in-process is protected by `pythonpath`; a
  subprocess is not, which is exactly why this fixture exists).

## Witnessed both directions on real contamination (not "should")

My own machine independently carries the identical contamination
lead-coder found (same `sandbox_2` `.pth` in pyenv global
site-packages) — used it directly rather than constructing a synthetic
repro:

```
① RED, before the fix:
   python3 -m pytest tests/interfaces/test_textual_chat_phase1_3273.py::test_plain_path_survives_flowview_absence
   (bare pyenv global, no venv)
   -> ImportError: cannot import name 'LOCAL_CHAT_READ_CAPABILITIES'
      from 'reyn.interfaces.repl.read_model'
      (.../sandbox_2/src/reyn/interfaces/repl/read_model.py)
   — same shape as the incident report, reproduced independently.

② GREEN, after the fix, same invocation, same machine:
   python3 -m pytest tests/interfaces/test_textual_chat_phase1_3273.py::test_plain_path_survives_flowview_absence
   -> 1 passed

   GREEN, unchanged, under .venv/bin/python -m pytest (no regression) —
   also confirmed the file's other 4 tests still pass.

③ Test's own purpose preserved (its clean-interpreter isolation guarantee
   is unaffected by PYTHONPATH): the subprocess installs its OWN
   sys.meta_path blocker before importing anything (`_Block`, raises
   ModuleNotFoundError for textual/textual_flowview by name) — that's a
   FINDER, evaluated at import time regardless of what's on sys.path,
   not a path-visibility question. Pinning the src root cannot widen
   what the subprocess can import; it only fixes WHICH reyn checkout it
   reads. The test's own internal assertions
   ("flowview imported at module load" / "flowview imported during
   plain run") still ran and still passed in both ① and ② above.
```

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/interfaces/test_textual_chat_phase1_3273.py::test_plain_path_survives_flowview_absence` (contaminated env) — RED before, GREEN after (shown above)

- [x] `ruff check` — clean

author: maxrink
body:
Hardware-found base bug (surfaced while bench-testing #114, but present on master). When the camera is powered off or out of range, Control::disconnect() polled a completion loop on the caller (UI) task for up to 30 s while Camera::disconnect() never cleared m_Connected for a gone peer (onDisconnect only fires at the supervision timeout, or never in-window). Result: the on-screen UI froze ~30 s, then force-completed leaving a stale target (state idle, targets 1).

Fix: interactive disconnect (forRestart == false) is now non-blocking. It aborts, cancels, sends CMD_DISCONNECT, moves every target into a zombie drain set with a backstop deadline, clears m_Targets, sets STATE_IDLE, and returns immediately: getState() == idle and getTargetCount() == 0 at once, so the UI never freezes and there is no stale target. The control task's reapZombieTargets() frees a drained target only once m_Stopped and !isConnected() (client freed), and the existing teardownDraining() gate holds STATE_CONNECT until then, preserving the isConnected()-gated completion that prevents the fast-reconnect client-free UAF (PR #62). Stuck teardown is force-freed at the deadline so connect never wedges. The restart path keeps its synchronous force-complete (esp_restart follows). No vendor code touched; isConnected() stays lock-free; no live-client cross-check.

Regression test: tests/host/control_disconnect_test.cpp (ctest control-disconnect) compiles the real FurbleControl + real Camera + MockNimBLE behind minimal host shims. Test A: dead camera -> disconnect() returns < 500 ms, state idle, 0 targets, drain reaps after the link truly drops. Test B: clean present-camera disconnect stays prompt. Mutation-checked: reverting the non-blocking branch makes control-disconnect FAIL at 30.4 s.

Host ctest 15/15, m5stick-s3-debug builds, sim builds. Needs an on-device check: power off camera while connected -> tap Disconnect -> no ~30 s freeze, targets 0, state idle; plus present-camera disconnect-then-immediate-reconnect stays safe.

## Upstream issues
Addresses gkoh/furble#222. Relates to gkoh/furble#71, #221, #252.

author: robinclowers
body:
### Link to Issue or Description of Change

- Closes: #789.


**Problem:**
A function call whose name is absent from toolsDict throws out of getToolAndContext before the try/catch that makes a real tool's failure recoverable. The throw escapes handleFunctionCallList and is caught by LlmAgent.runAndHandleError — the model error handler — so the turn reports UNKNOWN_ERROR and onToolErrorCallback never runs. Worse, the call is left unanswered, and since nothing else in the request changes between iterations the model re-issues it until maxLlmCalls trips: 500 billed calls and 500 error events for one user turn.


**Solution:**
Wrap the lookup. The error runs through the on-tool-error callbacks, and their response — or the resolution error itself when no plugin handles it — is emitted as that call's functionResponse. continue keeps the rest of the batch running, so every functionCall still gets a response and the pairing stays balanced (Gemini rejects a dangling functionCall).

**Why this diverges from adk-python**

adk-python re-raises when no plugin handles it, but the common trigger isn't a hallucinated name, it's a built-in tool.

GoogleSearchTool.processLlmRequest adds itself to config.tools without adding itself to toolsDict (core/src/tools/google_search_tool.ts:30) — as do enterprise_web_search, url_context, google_maps_grounding, vertex_ai_search, and vertex_rag_retrieval, none of which mention toolsDict at all. So tools: [GOOGLE_SEARCH] primes the model with a name that structurally cannot resolve. With GOOGLE_SEARCH genuinely registered, ADK on main says:

Function google_search is not found in the toolsDict. ... Available tools: search_web.

The user registered google_search. Gemini sometimes returns grounding as an explicit functionCall instead of running it server-side, and the user is then billed 500 calls for an inconsistency ADK created.

Re-raising is hard to justify for that, so the message also drops the hallucination claim it can't support. Happy to file the parity question upstream alongside google/adk-python#4775.


### Testing Plan

Three new tests in core/test/agents/functions_test.ts: plugin recovery (callback receives a tool named for the call, with its args), the no-plugin path (response carries the resolution error and the corrected message), and a mixed batch asserting all three calls are answered in order with the real tools' results intact. tool_filter_request_processor_test updated — a filtered tool now returns an error response rather than throwing.

Also fixes an unrelated latent bug the change exposed: SleepyTool in streaming_runner_test.ts had no _getDeclaration(), so sleepy_tool never entered toolsDict and the abort test passed only because the resolution throw ended the run before the tool executed. It now has a declaration and exercises the abort it claims to.

Full core suite passes (226 files / 3342 tests). Verified end-to-end against the issue's repro: per-iteration error events 500 → 0, and a model that reacts to the error resolves in 2 calls.


**Unit Tests:**

- [x] I have added or updated unit tests for my change.
- [x] All unit tests pass locally.

```
 Test Files  241 passed (241)
      Tests  3643 passed (3643)
   Start at  10:57:41
   Duration  20.65s (transform 2.58s, setup 0ms, collect 108.93s, tests 13.30s, environment 19ms, prepare 7.94s)
```

**Manual End-to-End (E2E) Tests:**

See the issue for a self-contained repro.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/google/adk-js/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code.
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas.

- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes.

- [x] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules.

### Additional context

core/test doesn't run on a clean checkout — agent_engine_sandbox_code_executor.ts imports @google-cloud/vertexai, which isn't in node_modules and isn't declared in core/package.json's optional peers. Pre-existing (reproduces on a clean git stash), looks like a gap from a5cdc38. I installed it with --no-save --no-package-lock to run the suite.

author: dmobius3
body:
**Claims no result.** The answer packet has not been opened, no comparison has run, and no verdict exists. This lands before § 8 step 6, and the pre-reveal commit ordering is the evidence the firewall held.

## What this is

Phase B of the Addendum 1 split. Phase A produced the frozen implementation, its method-and-gate manifest, and its raw output inside the clean room. Phase B is the separate qualification pass that proves every pre-reveal gate the manifest registers is real: that it exists, that its declared mutation exists, and that the mutation actually reddens it.

The split exists because five monolithic single-context commissions failed to discharge the § 9 mutation requirement reliably. Splitting qualification out of implementation is what made it discharge.

## What the qualifier establishes

**All nineteen declared mutations executed and went red.** The qualifier parses the nineteen gate identifiers and their declared mutations out of the frozen manifest's § 4 tables at runtime. That parsed registry is the authoritative expected set; no gate list is hard-coded anywhere in the qualifier.

**Exact registry coverage, proven three ways.** Parsed manifest equals implemented handlers before execution; parsed manifest equals executed records after execution; and a parser self-test confirms the linkage is sensitive to manifest changes. That last one is the part worth checking closely: adding a fake gate row, removing a row, duplicating a row, and emptying a mutation cell each drive a failure, and the added or dropped identifier drives a coverage failure rather than a hash failure. The linkage is therefore proven below the integrity layer, which is where it has to hold, since a check that only fires when the file hash changes cannot detect a gate that was never run.

**Phase A is untouched.** All thirteen Phase A artifact hashes match the Addendum 1 table both before and after qualification. Bytecode writing is disabled so no `.pyc` files appear beneath the frozen directory.

**The record is machine-readable and self-incriminating by design.** Each entry in `MUTATION_RESULTS.json` carries both `declared_mutation`, verbatim from the parsed manifest, and `implemented_mutation`, what the harness actually executed. Any divergence between the two is visible in the data rather than resting on prose.

## Two mutation-fidelity defects, found and repaired

Both prior Phase B landings are preserved in history at `f441e0ec` and `a923c554` rather than squashed away, because the defect is part of the record. **Please merge without squashing.** Collapsing the three commits would erase exactly the evidence that the two fidelity defects were caught and repaired before any reveal, which is a weaker record than the one this branch currently carries.

For two gates, the earlier landing executed a mutation *related to* the declared one rather than the declared one itself.

**G-D04** is declared as a Galois swap on the characters of a Galois pair. It was previously substituting one already-computed value for another at the comparison, which tests the equality checker and not the Galois action. It now applies the Galois map to the representation matrices, recomputes through the same consumed path, and the relation fails. An honest stop was available here, since the frozen production path pairs Galois partners from a literal list and computes before that check runs, so it was genuinely open whether the declared mutation could reach the relation at all. It can, and the escape was not needed.

**G-D05** is declared as replacing the torsion formula's input with identity matrices and verifying the output changes. It was previously replacing the representation matrices, which aborted the computation as non-acyclic. An abort is not a changed output. It now substitutes at the formula's own input boundary and the output changes. No record in the set now reports an abort in place of an outcome.

**One sentence the record no longer overstates.** The prior summary claimed no mutation was skipped, substituted, or narrowed. That was false for the two gates above. It now claims only that none was skipped, and points at the paired declared and implemented fields so a future divergence surfaces in the data.

## Process notes for review

The qualifier was produced by a commissioned context, not by this column's code unit, which is permanently ineligible to serve as the M8.8 implementer context under § 4. What is mine here is the commissioning and the verification enumerated in `LANDING_RECORD.md`, including a pair-by-pair read of all nineteen declared against implemented mutations.

Merges clean against current main; the paths are disjoint from the harness work in #452 and #453.

The claim ceiling is unchanged and worth restating so the write-up cannot drift: this is **context isolation, not blindness**. For an AI implementer the training corpus is opaque, so blindness cannot be certified even under perfect task-time isolation, and the word stays banned as a result label. If the later § 8 adjudication yields a successful-run category, the permitted label is context-isolated independent-method reproduction; every other outcome keeps its own § 8 category. The commit ordering is what makes the isolation checkable rather than attested.

## Sequence after this

Ciphertext on the #408 channel once this merges and the pre-reveal harness binding from #451 settles, then § 8 step 6 opens the packet, with you.

author: justmaier
body:
Closes ClickUp `868kv0cmc`.

## What was actually wrong

The ticket says the block list has no remove control. A remove path did exist — an Add/Remove toggle, where flipping to Remove made the chips clickable so they staged into the textarea. That is the trial-and-error behind the ticket.

The real problem is one layer down: **`EmailDomain` is 8295 entries in production, all rendered as chips with no filter.** A one-click delete on a chip you cannot locate fixes nothing, so the filter is the load-bearing half.

## What this does

- Reuses `ListFilterBar` over the entry list — label, Clear button, formatted "N of M" counts.
- Caps rendered chips at 200, with a line saying how many matches are not drawn. The filter runs over the **whole** list before the cap; capping first would search only the first 200 alphabetically and report anything past that as absent.
- Each chip carries its own one-click remove. The Add/Remove toggle stays but now drives only the textarea, so each surface has one mechanism: chip removes one entry, textarea does bulk add or bulk remove.

## What review found that the ticket did not

**The filter matched in the opposite direction to how two of the lists enforce.** `UsernamePartial` enforces `username.includes(entry)` (`user.service.ts:428`) and `MessagePattern` enforces `value.includes(pattern)` (`blocklist.service.ts:215`). So a moderator pasting `xXscammerXx` into the filter got `No entry contains that` while the entry `scammer` that blocks it sat on the list. The match is now bidirectional.

**The remove action reported a count it never verified.** It returned `count: items.length` — the number *submitted*. A removal that matched nothing still rendered "Removed 1 item." above a chip that was still there. Reachable by double-clicking, and by a stale row id (the DTO is Redis-cached for a **month**). `removeBlocklistItems` now returns the real count and the action fails when it is zero.

**Entries are deduped before rendering.** `upsertBlocklist` dedupes only on its update branch, so the first save of a type persists whatever was submitted. Duplicates would collide as `{#each}` keys, and each chip is now identified by its own value.

## 🔴 One finding this PR only warns about

`sync-email-blocklist` (`src/server/jobs/sync-email-blocklist.ts:77`, `0 3 * * 0`) computes `additions = upstream.filter(d => !existingSet.has(d))`. **A domain a moderator removes is by definition absent from `existingSet`, so it is re-added on the next Sunday run.** The job bails when there is more than one `EmailDomain` row; production has exactly one, so nothing protects it there.

Not introduced here — made *reachable* here, on the exact list this change is motivated by. This PR adds a description on the EmailDomain tab saying so. The durable fix is an exclusion set the cron respects, which lives in the main app and belongs in its own ticket.

(Note for anyone testing: **dev has two `EmailDomain` rows, so the cron skips there** and this cannot be reproduced against the dev DB.)

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter ./apps/moderator run typecheck` — 0 errors, 0 warnings. Mutation-proved it can fail.
- `pnpm --filter ./apps/moderator run lint` — clean.
- `pnpm --filter ./apps/moderator exec vitest run` — 56 pass, 0 fail (35 skipped, pre-existing).
- 15 new tests. Every one checked by mutating the source and reading the file back to confirm the mutation landed: cap-before-filter (3 red), case-sensitivity (1 red), dropping the reverse match direction (2 red), and reporting the submitted count again (3 red).

Reviewed with `svelte-review` — correctness, idiom and abstraction lanes, each prompted to refute.

## Open

Whether the chip `×` should remove immediately (as built) or keep a staged flow behind the toggle is Justin's call; the staged variant is a small revert. Not yet demoed on a dev server — that needs a moderator account to log in as.

author: yandv
body:
# Description

Adds two Domain Connect templates for **Araute** (https://araute.com), a Brazilian payments
platform. Both authorise Araute to send transactional e-mail on behalf of a merchant's own domain,
so invoices and receipts reach the merchant's customers from the merchant's address instead of ours.

There are two because the record set is decided by the sending backend, and the two backends
authenticate differently:

| | `araute.com.email-sending-resend` | `araute.com.email-sending-ses` |
|---|---|---|
| DKIM | one TXT at `%dkimSelector%._domainkey` | three CNAMEs, one per token |
| Return path | MX at `send` + SPFM | MX at `send` + SPFM |
| DMARC | TXT at `_dmarc`, `essential: OnApply` | same |

The SES variant follows Amazon's Easy DKIM, where SES holds the signing key and publishes three
CNAME tokens. Its target is not a fixed host: AWS documents that "the hosted zone portion varies by
AWS Region and cell", which is why `%signingZone%` is a variable rather than a literal
`dkim.amazonses.com`.

Merchants commonly send from a subdomain (`mail.example.com`) to keep the root domain's reputation
separate, so both templates are exercised at the apex and with `host` set.

## Type of change

- [x] New template
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue in the template)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality to the template)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing template behavior to be not backward compatible)

# How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Template functionality checked using [Online Editor](https://domainconnect.paulonet.eu/dc/free/templateedit)
- [x] Template file name follows the pattern `<providerId>.<serviceId>.json`
- [x] resource URL provided with `logoUrl` is actually served by a webserver (confirmed 200 `image/svg+xml` at https://www.araute.com/favicon.svg)

Both files also pass the official linter with exit 0:

```
dc-template-linter -loglevel error -tolerate info -logos araute.com.email-sending-resend.json
dc-template-linter -loglevel error -tolerate info -logos araute.com.email-sending-ses.json
```

# Checklist of common problems

- [x] `syncPubKeyDomain` is set (`araute.com`) on both — public key published as TXT at `_dcpubkeyv1.araute.com`
- [x] `warnPhishing` is **not** set alongside `syncPubKeyDomain`
- [x] `syncRedirectDomain` is set (`app.araute.com`) on both — the synchronous flow uses `redirect_uri`
- [x] no TXT record contains SPF content — the SPF line uses `SPFM` in both
- [x] `txtConflictMatchingMode` is set on every TXT record (`All` on DKIM, `Prefix` + `v=DMARC1` on DMARC)
- [x] no variable is used as a bare full record value **except the DKIM key in the non-SES template**, justified below
- [x] no bare variable is used as the full `host` label — DKIM hosts are `%dkimSelector%._domainkey` and `%dkimTokenN%._domainkey`, with the RFC 6376 label fixed
- [x] no variable is used in the `host` field to create a subdomain — the `host` parameter carries the sending subdomain
- [x] `%host%` does not appear explicitly in any `host` attribute
- [x] `essential` is set to `OnApply` on both DMARC records

**Justification for the bare variables.**

In `araute.com.email-sending-resend`, the DKIM record's `data` is `%dkimValue%` with no fixed prefix. A DKIM
TXT value is entirely key material minted by the sending provider, and its exact shape is the
provider's to choose: it may arrive as `p=…` alone or as `v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=…`. Fixing any prefix
would break the moment that shape changes and would produce a record that does not validate. The
record is pinned to a `._domainkey` host, so it can only ever write a DKIM record.

In `araute.com.email-sending-ses`, each CNAME's `pointsTo` is `%dkimTokenN%.%signingZone%`. Neither
half can be fixed: the token is minted per identity, and AWS documents the zone as varying by Region
and cell, retrievable only from the `SigningHostedZone` field of the API response.

## Online Editor test results

author: bohdankhrystov
body:
Twelfth ticket of `STORY-0502`. `duelServer` installs `standingsRoutes` on `components.wallClock`.

This guards a specific embarrassment: a route with eleven passing tests that the real server never
installs, so CI stays green and production answers `404`.

## Falsification — three mutations, all run

1. **Route installation removed.** The test reddens with `404` instead of `200`. It boots the **real**
   `duelServer(serverComponents(config, dataSource))` against a real database rather than
   constructing the route directly the way `StandingsRouteTest` does — which is why this fires at
   all. A wiring test that builds its own route cannot see whether the server installs one.
2. **A different clock** (`Clock.fixed` at the epoch) passed instead of `components.wallClock`. The
   **test does not redden**, and the reason is structural rather than sloppy: the real server boots
   with `systemUTC`, so no test here can fix the clock, and the assertion can only check the season's
   *shape*. A 1970 season satisfies `\d{4}-\d{2}` perfectly well. The gate is instead the `verify:`
   grep, which pins the exact call including `components.wallClock` — recorded plainly rather than
   left to look like test coverage.
3. **Route installed at `/api/ladder`.** Reddens with `404` — the path is pinned.

All reverted.

## Verify

```
./gradlew :poker-server:test --tests '*DuelServerRoutesTest' -PrequireDocker=true
./gradlew :poker-server:test --tests '*ServerComponentsTest' -PrequireDocker=true
./gradlew :poker-server:ktlintCheck
grep -qF 'standingsRoutes(components.reads, components.standings, components.wallClock)' …/Application.kt
```

All exit 0. Per `ADR-0062` the clock is a `java.time.Clock` from the composition root, never
`ServerClock` — that one is `System.nanoTime()` and yields a season in 1970.

author: cybersamada
body:
## Summary

Ahmed, 2026-08-21: **"Never ever set my emails to read. This is very important."**

While diagnosing that, this repo turned out to have a genuine defect of exactly this kind. It is **not** the cause of what happened to his personal mailbox (this script runs under `wcmmail@westdellcorp.com`, and his mailbox has no `+-billing` or `Invoice-Processed` label), but it has been quietly marking billing threads read.

**The defect.** Reading a thread's messages through `GmailApp` marks the thread READ as a side effect of looking. The test path already knew this:

- `testRun()` (Test.gs) captures `wasUnread` and restores it in a `finally`.
- `SETUP.md` promises *"Read/unread status is restored automatically."*

`processInvoices()` — the path that actually runs on a trigger — never did. So the safe-looking test run cleaned up after itself while the real run silently marked every invoice thread it opened as read. That asymmetry is the bug.

**The fix.** `withReadStateRestored_` in `GmailService.gs`, applied at the three helpers that touch messages (`getPdfAttachments_`, `threadHasAnyPdf_`, `describeThreadAttachments_`) rather than at the caller in `Main.gs`. Fixing it at the helpers covers every call path — the real run, the test run, and anything added later — instead of one loop remembering and the next one forgetting.

It only ever restores **towards** unread:

```js
if (wasUnread && !thread.isUnread()) thread.markUnread();
```

so this helper can never itself be the thing that marks something read. That asymmetry is deliberate.

Also imports the `never-set-an-email-to-read` boundary into `canon/procore-facts.json`, stated once at its owner in `Procore_Claude_Intergration#51`, plus a CLAUDE.md section recording the rule and why the defect existed.

## Test plan

- `node --check` on `GmailService.gs` — passes.
- No Apps Script runtime here, so the restore itself is **not** live-verified. It mirrors the exact pattern `testRun()` has used successfully since it was written, which is the strongest evidence available from this side.
- **Whoever runs `processInvoices()` next should confirm a previously-unread billing thread is still unread afterwards.** That is the real check and it has not been done.
- `canon.py check` exits 0.

---

author: aumaidkh
body:
# fix(sync): pull an existing account's data on the first run after sign-in

Closes #312. Based on `fix/auto-otp-detection`.

## What

Signing in on an account that already has cars, service logs and documents sometimes landed on a completely empty app — Home, Garage, Costs and Timeline all showing their first-run empty states, with nothing on screen to say a download had been lost. This fixes the five separate defects that could each swallow that first pull, all of them silent.

## Why

**The one that fits the report.** Six of the nine syncables resolved their scope like this:

```kotlin
carId = { get<ActiveCarProvider>().activeCarId.value?.value }
```

`PrimaryCarProvider.activeCarId` is `observePrimaryCar().stateIn(scope, Eagerly, initialValue = null)`, fed by a SQLDelight query. On the first run after signing in, the engine pulls `CARS` and writes them, then reaches those six tables milliseconds later — before that flow has re-emitted. Each fetch takes its early exit:

```kotlin
val car = carId() ?: return emptyList()
```

An empty list is indistinguishable from a server with nothing new. So the pull reported `Pulled(count = 0)`, the runner returned `true`, the engine returned `Success`, and the worker returned `Result.success()`. Cursor untouched, `lastError` null, job dropped. Nothing pulled those five entities again until the owner wrote something themselves — on a screen showing them nothing to act on.

`ActiveCarProvider` is a lazy Koin `single`, so on a fresh install the sync worker is often the first thing to resolve it: the flow was constructed microseconds earlier with `initialValue = null`. The race is not close.

Two more consequences of the same scoping: a second car's rows never arrived at all, and an account whose server rows carry `is_primary = false` never pulled those six tables on **any** run, because `selectPrimaryCar` is `WHERE is_primary = 1`.

**Four others, each able to lose the pull on its own:**

1. `OdoSyncWorker` mapped every `Skipped` to `Result.success()`, and `SessionSyncGate` returned `false` for any null token — covering both "nobody is signed in" and "a refresh that just timed out". A sign-in sync that asked a moment too early was recorded as done and dropped.
2. The engine stopped at the first failed entity. `PROFILES` is first and `CARS` second, so a profile that would not sync meant cars, service logs, documents, costs and reminders were never reached. That is exactly the "no data at all" shape rather than partial data.
3. `SqlDelightLocalUserDataWipe` catches and swallows its transaction, so a failed sign-out left the cursors behind while the owner believed they had signed out.
4. `OdoSessionManager.refreshLocked` treated any `Left` as terminal, and `SupabaseTokenEndpoint.refresh` mapped *everything* — timeout, dropped connection, 5xx — to `DomainError.SessionExpired`. A renewal attempted on a flaky connection ended the session as decisively as a revoked token, silently.

**Two claims from the issue that do not hold**, recorded so nobody re-derives them: `scheduleStartupSync()` is *not* dead code (it runs at `KoinInit.kt:165`, right after session restore — which makes the race worse, not better, since every launch re-runs it), and the maintenance gate cannot swallow the sign-in sync (`DefaultAppStatusProvider` seeds `availability` with `Allowed` — fail open).

**What the uploaded logs showed.** All three sessions contain zero lines tagged `sync`, though `SyncTelemetry.TAG = "sync"` logs at INFO and DEBUG lines are present. The lifecycle order in each file proves `scheduleStartupSync()` ran. So the job was enqueued and the worker never executed — and all three also carry `RemoteConfig fetchAndActivate failed`, pointing at the `NetworkType.CONNECTED` constraint. Nothing re-requested a sync when connectivity returned. That gap is fixed here too.

## How

**Pull by `owner_id`, not by car.** `fetchSince(carId, …)` becomes `fetchSince(ownerId, …)` on the six ports and their Supabase adapters (`owner_id=eq.$ownerId`); the six sync tables take an `ownerId` lambda wired to `CurrentOwnerProvider`, which reads the in-memory session synchronously. `CarSyncTable` and `ProfileSyncTable` already did exactly this. Every affected table has `owner_id NOT NULL` server-side and RLS already filters on it, so this is the scope the server was always going to enforce — and there is no flow left to lose a race with. Fixes the race, the `is_primary` dependency and the single-car limit together. The push path is untouched; rows still carry their own `car_id`.

**A missing scope is not an empty page.** `SyncTable.fetch` returns `FetchResult.Rows` or `FetchResult.ScopeMissing`. The runner turns the second into the same outcome as a timeout: cursor untouched, entity recorded as failed, run reported `Partial`, which is a retry. Defence in depth, so the next scoped entity someone adds cannot reintroduce this.

**A three-valued gate.** `SyncGate.evaluate()` returns `Allowed` / `NoSession` / `Unavailable`. `SyncResult.Skipped` gained `retryable`, and the worker returns `retry()` for a retryable skip. Only "nobody is signed in" is still recorded as done — signing in is what changes that, and burning wakeups until then helps nobody.

**Push and pull as separate phases.** `Syncable` splits into `pushTo` / `pullFrom`. A refused push still stops the push phase — `SyncEntity` order is FK order and a child sent before its parent is a foreign-key error. A refused pull stops nothing: fetching has no ordering requirement, and cars can be pulled whether or not profiles was. The run still reports `Partial`, so the scheduler retries what failed.

**Only a real refusal ends a session.** New `DomainError.SessionUnavailable`; `refresh` maps 400/401/403 to `SessionExpired` and everything else — 429, any 5xx, a request that got no answer — to the new value. `refreshLocked` clears the session only for the terminal one.

**Cursor hygiene.** The wipe retries `sync_state.deleteAll()` on its own when the big transaction throws, because of the three things it does, a surviving cursor is the one nobody can see. The wipe and adoption both now cover `trips`, which neither did. Adoption evicts rows belonging to a previous account and clears the cursors beside them — finishing a sign-out that did not — and runs *after* the placeholder rows have been adopted, so offline work is never what gets removed. Self-limiting: a clean device keeps its cursors.

**Foreground and reconnect pulls.** `SyncReason.AppForeground` on `ProcessLifecycleOwner.onStart`, and a new `SyncReason.Reconnected` on a `ConnectivityManager` callback. Both were declared and never requested.

**Sync says what it is doing.** `sync_requested` at the scheduler, `sync_work_state` (the platform job's state and attempt count), and `sync_scope_missing`. `sync_entity_moved` gained a `phase` field — the event name and both count fields are unchanged, so existing queries still sum to the same totals. Without these, a worker that never ran and a worker that was never enqueued produce the same log: nothing.

### Server-side

`supabase/migrations/20260822090000_sync_owner_indexes.sql` — `reminders` and `health_scores` only ever indexed `car_id`, so their owner-scoped pull would seq-scan. **This needs applying before merge.**

## Testing

`:androidApp:assembleDebug` plus `testAndroidHostTest` on `:core:sync`, `:core:data`, `:core:platform`, `:core:domain`, `:infrastructure:database`, `:infrastructure:supabase`, `:feature:auth`, and `:feature:{profile,reminders,garage,dashboard,timeline}`. All green.

New tests, each pinning a defect above:

- **`FirstPullTest`** — the regression this got past. Pull into a database with **zero cars** and assert service logs still arrive; assert a second car's entries arrive too; assert a run with no owner is a retry rather than a successful pull of nothing.
- **`SyncRunnerTest`** — a fetch that cannot scope does not move the cursor and is recorded as a failure; a genuinely empty pull i

author: aubincorinaldiecooper-bit
body:
Found by reading the logs from your first upload on the new pipeline. Frontend counterpart is CLIPITFRONTEND#18.

## The problem

The drawer says *"you can ask now, the search will wait for it."* **It did not wait.**

A question asked while the video was still being read fell straight through to the footage path: ten calls carrying MP4 bytes, about two minutes, and roughly fifty times the cost of the same question asked ninety seconds later. Nobody decided that — it is simply what happened when the notes were not ready yet, and the copy described the behaviour we meant to have rather than the one we had.

The window is not small. From the upload you just did:

| | |
|---|---|
| video searchable | `18:19:54` |
| finished being read | `18:22:05` |

That is **two minutes and ten seconds** during which every question silently took the expensive path.

## The change

The search waits for the read to finish, using the same bounded re-enqueue the transcript wait already uses.

**Measured, not assumed:** reading that 20-minute video took 130 seconds, and searching the same video's footage takes about the same. So waiting costs the person nothing in wall clock. It cost **$0.0013 to answer from notes against $0.06 against footage** — the same answer, forty-five times cheaper.

Past `INDEX_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (four minutes) the search reads the footage anyway, because someone waiting on an index that has got stuck must still get an answer.

**A correction skips the wait entirely.** It is going to the footage regardless — that is what a correction means — so the notes finishing changes nothing for it.

## What the same logs say about the rest

Worth recording since it is the first full run of the new pipeline:

- **Reading the video**: 10 chunks, 55 scenes, 0 failed, 1 partially described (2 seconds uncovered in chunk 0), $0.0737 once.
- **Answering from memory**: 3.5s / $0.0013 for one match, 11.5s / $0.0031 for five matches merged to three. Against ~160s / $0.061 before.
- **Three of ten chunks hit the 2,500-token thinking cap** while being read. That is the number to raise if the notes start missing things — and the honest place to look first if `questionsNotesCouldNotAnswer` starts filling up.

## Testing

`npx vitest run` — 230 passed, 15 files.

author: johanx22x
body:
`packages/xwayland-satellite/PKGBUILD` ends its header with **"DELETE THIS
WHOLE DIRECTORY once the fix is in the repos"**, and nothing was ever going to
notice that moment — the patched package works, so there is no symptom left to
prompt anybody. This is that reminder, written as the repo asked for it.

## How it decides

The PKGBUILD already spells out the rule: it is versioned `0.8.2-1.1` so that
it beats the `0.8.2-1` in `extra` and **loses** to any future `0.8.2-2` or
`0.8.3`. `vercmp` is pacman's own implementation of that ordering, so the check
is one comparison between `pacman -Si xwayland-satellite` and
`$pkgver-$pkgrel`.

It does not claim the fix is in there — a rebuild could bump the version for
anything. It says the thing this package was pinned against has moved, and the
issue it opens asks for the check by hand: open Resolve under niri and see
whether the project manager appears.

## Local output

Today, against `extra`:

```
$ tests/xwayland-satellite-watch.sh
xwayland-satellite-watch: repositories have 0.8.2-1, this repo builds 0.8.2-1.1
xwayland-satellite-watch: still pinned, nothing to do
```

And pointed at a copy of the PKGBUILD reading `pkgver=0.8.1`, so that `extra`
overtakes it:

```
xwayland-satellite-watch: repositories have 0.8.2-1, this repo builds 0.8.1-1.1
xwayland-satellite-watch: the repository build now wins -- pacman will replace the local one by itself, so packages/xwayland-satellite/ can be deleted
$GITHUB_OUTPUT:
overtaken=true
repo_version=0.8.2-1
patched_version=0.8.1-1.1
```

The issue step was run with `gh` stubbed out, both branches: with nothing open
it produces the body below, and with one already open it prints `already open,
nothing to say` and exits 0.

```
`pacman -Si xwayland-satellite` reports **0.8.3-1**, which now beats
the **0.8.2-1.1** built from `packages/xwayland-satellite/`.
...
- check that the repository build really carries the fix from PR #480 —
  open DaVinci Resolve under niri and see whether the project manager appears
- delete `packages/xwayland-satellite/`
- drop whatever points at it from the README and `install.sh`
```

## Why a separate workflow

What changes here is not this repository, it is Arch's. A `pull_request` check
would ask the question only when somebody happened to open one — the wrong
trigger for "has the outside world moved yet" — and would then answer it on
every unrelated pull request forever. Weekly, plus `workflow_dispatch` so it
can be tried without waiting.

## What is not verified

Scheduled workflows only run from the default branch, so this does nothing
until it is merged and cannot be exercised from a branch — `workflow_dispatch`
after merge is how to see it run. The YAML parses and both `run:` blocks pass
`shellcheck -S warning`; `actionlint` is not installed here. The job needs
`issues: write`, which it declares, and issues are enabled on this repository.

author: goedelsoup
body:
Closes #148.

`6aaf18e` gave `is_open_question` a third arm — a value in a property the class declared `type: claim` — and left `tools.json` saying two, with a note forbidding a third **by name**. So `yidam open-questions` and a *correctly* conforming MCP server answered differently over the same corpus: the one failure the freeze exists to prevent, with the CLI as the thing that moved. Nothing here could notice — the contract is JSON, the predicate is Rust, and no test read both.

The reporter could not adopt the structural route at all. Reverting their serialized `"[open]"` to a bare `open` would make `open-questions` find their 26 open questions and their two-arm MCP tool return **zero**, so they kept the workaround that `6aaf18e` was supposed to retire.

## Option 1 of the three, and why

**The original prohibition was aimed at a different mechanism.** It was written against matching a blessed key name — `data.get("claim_tag") == "open"` — which a corpus cannot opt out of: `status: open` on a ballot measure becomes an open claim. The ontology route has no such hazard, and one property decides it:

> With no `type: claim` declaration anywhere, `ClaimFields::load` records no class and `count_structural` returns on `fields.is_empty()` — so the arm matches nothing and a two-arm server returns the **identical set**.

It cannot quietly widen an answer. It diverges only on the corpus that named the field, which is the corpus that was being answered wrongly. That inverts the note's own rationale: the arm doesn't make two corpora incomparable, it makes a structured one comparable for the first time.

The alternatives cost more than they look. Dropping the arm returns the reporting consumer to reshaping data for a `contains()` call. A second tool leaves the **core** tool answering 2-of-26 on a structured corpus while every agent has to know to ask twice — the same question, split by serialization.

`contract` 0.1.0 → 0.2.0, `mcp/VERSION` with it. The notes now forbid what is actually dangerous: a fourth arm, and a key name blessed by anything but the ontology.

## The conformance corpus ships, because the cases describe it

The follow-up report measured the **reports** fixture and concluded the case's rationale described a corpus that had been replaced. It named the wrong tree — the MCP cases run on a different fixture, which does still carry one node per arm, so `count: 2` held. **But the mistake was the contract's to make.** `mcp/README.md` said the cases run "over the fixture corpus in `corpus/`" and no such directory existed: the corpus was heredocs inside `tests/mcp_serve.rs`, so `count: {open_questions: 2}` named nodes a consumer had no way to see. One did the reasonable thing and re-expressed every `count` and `equals` against a corpus of its own — which turns a conformance suite into a check that a server agrees with itself.

So `corpus/` exists. `mcp_serve.rs` copies and `git init`s it the way `report_goldens.rs` stages its fixture, and the README documents each node and what it is the only witness for:

| Node | Sole witness for |
|---|---|
| `concept/knowledge-graph` | the only node that is **not** open; the only outgoing edge |
| `concept/traversal` | the **label** arm; also the backwards walk `neighbors` needs |
| `concept/retrieval` | the **`[open]`-in-body** arm |
| `concept/embedding-space` | the **declared-field** arm — no `?`, no bracketed token in the file |

Asserting a case's `count` directly is the obvious way to consume these files, and it is now also the correct one.

## And the two versions are pinned to each other

`mcp/VERSION` is read by nothing; `tools.json`'s `contract` is compiled into the server and returned in the capability block. A version nobody reads is a version nobody notices going stale — the same drift class one layer down, and I just hand-bumped both.

The pin lives in `versioning_layers.rs`, **not** `mcp_serve.rs`: that file is `#![cfg(feature = "index")]` and `cli-full` never runs on a pull request, so a check placed there would first speak up after the merge that broke it. Worth noting for this PR generally — CI will not compile `mcp_serve.rs` at all. It was run locally, along with `mise run ci`, `ci-cli-full`, and `parity-check`; all exit 0.

## Mutation-checked, both ways

- `concept.ont.yml`'s `type: claim` → `type: string`: the case fails at **2** nodes and the failure names `concept/embedding-space` as the one missing.
- The two version files disagreeing: the new pin fails and prints both.

## Left alone deliberately

RFC-0005 still proposes two arms and RFC-0001 still proposes a golden asserting a structural tag is *not* reported. Both were true when written, and this repository keeps RFCs as testimony about a change rather than a changelog of one — `6aaf18e` contradicted RFC-0001 the same way and did not amend it. Happy to add superseding notes if that reading is wrong.

**What:**
Optimized `UnifiedMusicSourceImpl.kt` by extracting an invariant list (`listOf("url", "picUrl", "coverImgUrl", "avatarUrl")`) from the `findUrlRecursive` function into a `companion object` (as `URL_KEYS`). Also refactored `getSongUrl` to avoid repeatedly casting `json as? JsonObject` by introducing a local `jsonObj` variable.

**Why:**
The list was being reallocated on every recursive call in `findUrlRecursive`, causing unnecessary memory allocations and garbage collection overhead. Furthermore, redundant casts in `getSongUrl` wasted CPU cycles. By caching these objects/casts, the code is both cleaner and slightly faster.

**Impact:**
Reduced memory allocations during JSON traversal when extracting URLs. Less CPU overhead due to avoided redundant type casting.

**Measurement:**
Memory allocation and garbage collection are slightly lower per recursive JSON parse tree traversal, providing better runtime stability over long playback sessions.

author: suxrobgm
body:
The dispatch agent can now counter a broker by email when a load-board listing pays below the carrier's rate floor. A dispatcher approves every outbound offer, and broker replies come back through a Resend inbound webhook and wake the agent for the next round.

Implements `docs/roadmap/ai-rate-negotiation.md` (email channel). Voice negotiation stays out of scope.

## What changed

- New `TenantFeature.AIRateNegotiation` (Professional and above) and `Permission.Negotiation.View/Manage`.
- Per-lane rate floors (`LaneRateFloor`) with CRUD and a resolver: exact lane, then origin-state-to-anywhere, then anywhere-to-destination-state, then the tenant default. No floor means the agent refuses to negotiate.
- Agent tools `get_rate_floor`, `get_negotiation_thread`, and the write tool `propose_counter_offer`. `book_loadboard_load` gained an optional `negotiated_total_rate`.
- Outbound mail threads properly (`Reply-To`, `In-Reply-To`, `References`) and is rendered from a Liquid template; the model supplies one sanitized paragraph.
- Replies arrive on `offer-{token}@{sender domain}` and route through a master-DB `InboundEmailRoute` row, so no tenant id appears in an address and a thread can be revoked.
- TMS portal: negotiations list, thread detail, lane rate-floor CRUD, and an approval card that renders the actual email before you approve it.

The website pricing page now also lists load board integrations and broker credit checks under Professional, matching the plan seeder.

## Safety properties

- `propose_counter_offer` is an ordinary write tool, so nothing sends until a dispatcher approves the decision.
- Inbound mail can only append a message and request a turn. It never executes anything.
- A `From` that does not match the thread's broker address is quarantined and never shown to the agent.
- Broker text reaches the model fenced in a labelled UNTRUSTED block, and the prompt says to treat it as data.
- The recipient is read off the listing server-side and is never a model input.
- Webhook signatures are verified (Svix) before the body is parsed, and fail closed.

## Verification

author: danfiedler-msft
body:
## Summary

This PR pins GitHub Actions to full-length commit SHAs for improved security and reproducibility and adds a 7 day cooldown to Dependabot configuration for GitHub Actions. This work is described in more detail at https://aka.ms/action-pinning.

## Why?

Pinning actions to commit SHAs prevents supply-chain attacks where a tag could be moved to point to malicious code. This is a recommended security best practice per the [GitHub Actions security hardening guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions).

This change mitigates the risk of tag retargeting to malicious code as seen in incidents like the [tj-actions/changed-files action compromise](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/harden-runner-detection-tj-actions-changed-files-action-is-compromised) or [codfish/semantic-release-action compromise](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/supply-chain-compromise-codfish-semantic-release-action) and improves the integrity and reproducibility of the CI/CD pipeline.

## What changed?

**Action pinning:** Third-party action references in `.github/workflows/` that used mutable tag-based references (e.g., `actions/checkout@v4`) have been updated to full-length commit SHAs with a version comment (e.g., `actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`) using the [pinact](https://github.com/suzuki-shunsuke/pinact) tool. References that were already pinned to a SHA, or that used immutable release tags, were left unchanged.

**Dependabot configuration:** `.github/dependabot.yml` has been updated to ensure a `github-actions` package-ecosystem section is present with a `cooldown` configuration (`default-days: 7`). If the file did not exist, it was created. If a `github-actions` section already existed, only the `cooldown` block was added or its `default-days` value was increased to 7 if it was lower. The 7-day cooldown provides a window for the community to detect and report compromised releases before they are automatically proposed as updates, reducing exposure to supply-chain attacks via newly published malicious versions.

## Is this safe to merge?

Yes. The pinned SHAs correspond to the same commits that the existing tags pointed to. No behavioral changes in action execution are introduced. You can verify the pinned SHA value using the GitHub REST API (e.g., the commit hash for `actions/checkout@v7` can be found in the `sha` property in the JSON response for `GET https://api.github.com/repos/actions/checkout/commits/v7`).

## Additional Information

For more information, please see https://aka.ms/action-pinning

author: cao825
body:
## Summary

Three defects in the escalation rung let it open `needs-human` issues nothing but a human
could ever close (recon#needs-human-board-classification-2026-08-21, six measured open
issues). Each is fixed independently but the fixes compose into one lifecycle guarantee:
an escalation this system opens must be one this system can close.

1. **`src/lib/sweep.ts` — don't escalate on a check that has merely not started.**
   `DISPOSITION_RULES` gained a new row (inserted immediately before the terminal
   catch-all) that reads `checksState === "none"` a third way: below
   `policy.absentCeilingMinutes` (this repo's own measured time-to-first-check-run,
   already load-bearing for the ABSENT re-push remedy) the disposition is `"wait"` and no
   issue opens; at or above the ceiling the row does not match and the PR falls through to
   the SAME terminal catch-all as before, unchanged. The age computation was factored out
   of `absentChecksRepushDecision` into an exported `absentAgeMinutes(pr, now)` so both the
   re-push question and the disposition question read the identical clock. An unreadable
   `lastActivityAt` fails toward escalate (unchanged today's behavior), never toward wait.

2. **`src/lib/escalate.ts` — every opened escalation carries the queue label.**
   `createEscalationIssue`'s ensureLabel-degrade loop (W1-T99) previously let ANY wanted
   label — including `needs-human`/`fleet-notice`, the one field
   `RETIRABLE_ESCALATION_LABELS` (sweep.ts) filters retirement candidates on — silently
   drop out of the `create()` call when its provisioning failed. The queue label is now
   excluded from the degradable set entirely: it is unconditionally the first entry in the
   `labels` array `create()` receives, regardless of what `ensureLabel` returns for it. Only
   the decorative class/ask-type labels may still degrade (W1-T99's original guarantee,
   preserved byte-for-byte). If the queue label truly cannot be attached, `create()` itself
   now throws — `escalate()`'s already-documented contract, degraded by `tryEscalate` to a
   visible, retriable `escalation.failed` ledger line — instead of silently minting a
   permanently un-retirable issue.

3. **`src/lib/escalate.ts` — refuse an unresolvable referent rather than open one.**
   `escalate()`/`escalateWithJudge()` now run every `Escalation` through
   `refuseUnlessResolvable` before dedup. A `taskId` that is empty or the JS-stringified
   `"undefined"`/`"null"` sentinel (the two measured shapes: rationale's
   `no_task_trailer: 2` and the `Task: undefined` issues) is rewritten to the synthetic
   `PR-<n>` referent when a PR is nameable in the escalation's own `summary`/`detail`
   (reusing the existing `extractPrRef` scan) — the exact shape
   `buildEscalationReconcileCandidates` (run-task.ts) already resolves via a bare
   PR-number lookup, no plan entry required. When no PR is nameable either, the call
   throws rather than opening an issue no lookup could ever retire. Every other taskId
   shape — a real plan task id, GRILL's `TRIAGE-<feedbackId>` id (the only viable grill
   mechanism, LEARNINGS.md) — passes through byte-identical; this cannot misfire on a
   legitimate caller.

Design note (v) is honored: nothing here bulk-closes any of the six currently-open issues —
this changes only what the NEXT escalation looks like.

## Acceptance criteria

- **"a required check with zero runs on a head too young to have been scheduled disposes
  to wait and opens nothing"** — `test/escalation-retirability.test.ts`:
  `"deriveDisposition: checksState 'none' 2 minutes after the push -> wait, never
  blocked-ambiguous"`, `"...right at the ceiling still waits; just past it escalates"`, and
  the `runSweep` integration test `"...opens NO escalation this pass"` (asserts
  `deps.escalated.length === 0`).
- **"a genuinely absent required check on an older head still escalates exactly as it does
  today"** — same file: `"...an hour-old head still escalates exactly as it does today —
  blocked-ambiguous, terminal catch-all wording unchanged"` (asserts the disposition AND
  the exact pre-existing reason string), plus the `runSweep` integration test `"...escalates
  exactly as today"`.
- **"every escalation this system opens carries the queue label the retirement path
  filters on"** — same file: `"escalate: the queue label is attached even when ITS OWN
  provisioning fails"`, `"...the measured six-issue shape — EVERY label's provisioning
  fails at once — still opens with the queue label attached"`, `"...a gateway with no
  ensureLabel at all still attaches the queue label (back-compat)"`, and
  `"escalateWithJudge: a DEMOTED escalation still carries the fleet-notice queue label..."`.
  The pre-existing `test/escalate.test.ts` canonical-2026-07-17 test (class-label
  degrade-don't-lose) still passes unchanged, proving the decorative-label degrade path is
  untouched.
- **"an escalation whose referent no lookup can resolve is refused rather than opened"** —
  same file: `"escalate: refuses an empty Task field..."`,
  `"...refuses a literal 'undefined' Task field..."`,
  `"...a broken Task field is NORMALIZED to the synthetic PR-<n> referent..."`,
  `"...a real plan task id passes through byte-identical..."`, and
  `"...GRILL's own referent shape (TRIAGE-<feedbackId>, never a PR) is UNAFFECTED..."`.
- **The lifecycle guarantee, tested as one property (design iv)** — same file:
  `"lifecycle guarantee: a too-young zero-run head opens nothing; a genuinely absent one
  opens an issue that is labelled AND names a resolvable referent"` — a two-PR `runSweep`
  pass wired to the REAL `escalate()` over a fake `IssueGateway`, asserting all three arms
  in one flow.

`npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` is clean. `node --test` over
`test/escalation-retirability.test.ts` (18/18), `test/sweep*.test.ts` + `test/escalate.test.ts`
+ related escalation-wiring suites (490 + 356 passing), and `test/run-task.test.ts` (302/302,
including the pre-existing `buildEscalationReconcileCandidates`/canonical-label-degrade
tests) all pass with zero regressions.

## Out of scope (follow-ups, not filed here)

- research: confirm current live status of the twelve `needs-human` issues cited in this
  task's rationale via `gh issue list`, since recon's classification predates this PR and no
  GitHub API read was made while implementing — useful before any operator triage pass on
  the existing six.
- task: W1-T298 (queue-starvation escalation) / W1-T186 (naming the observed blocker) own
  the fourth shape named in rationale (7) — `#2063`'s `Task: daemon` starvation notice —
  deliberately not touched here.

author: nixsin
body:
Follows [#135](https://github.com/nixsin/marketplace/pull/135). CLAUDE.md is loaded in full before any work starts; five sections were **topic reference** — things you look up when working on that area — rather than operating instructions needed to work on anything else.

## Moved

Same pattern already established by `docs/ci.md`, `docs/cloudflare.md`, `docs/render.md`, `docs/infrastructure.md`:

| Section | Lines | New home |
|---|---|---|
| AI code review gate | 345 | `docs/ai-review.md` |
| Web e2e testing | 173 | `docs/testing.md` |
| Security headers | 134 | `docs/security-headers.md` |
| Badges / dashboard | 82 | `docs/metrics.md` |
| Design system | 72 | `docs/design-system.md` |

## What stayed is not a bare link

Each pointer keeps the rules needed to act correctly *without* reading further:

- **Never let an AI verdict satisfy the review requirement**, and never route around it with a PAT — a live review already caught and rejected that. Plus the four rules for converging a review, and the override-log format with the update-it-now discipline.
- `test-e2e-web` **is a required check**, is filtered on `api`/`web`/`deps`, and its screenshot baselines are **Linux-generated**.
- The CSP is deliberately **nonce-free**, because nonces force dynamic rendering.
- A badge-publishing job needs its own `permissions: contents: write` — **bitten twice**, and the introducing PR structurally cannot catch it.
- Only `components/ui/**` is shadcn-vendored, so editing anything else is safe.

## Result

```
this PR:      1,981 → 1,268 lines    ~30.8k → ~19k tokens
with #135:    2,283 → 1,268 lines    ~35.8k → ~19k tokens   (47%)
```

## No content deleted

The five docs total **836** lines against **806** moved — the difference is each file's own title and context header. Every paragraph preserved verbatim.

## Note on the merge commit

This branch was cut before #135 merged. Squash-merging created a new commit, so `main`'s history no longer contained its base and `CLAUDE.md` conflicted — the trap CLAUDE.md documents for stacked PRs. Resolved by taking this branch's version, which is the superset, then verifying #135's corrections survived: the "11 required checks" line is present and zero stale "informational, not required" claims remain.

## Verification

Link and anchor checks **9/9** · section count unchanged · each doc opens with a title and a one-line statement of scope, so it reads standalone.

author: jorgeg94
body:
Give the continuum operator its own timing stage

Fallout from rebasing onto the Fock/quadrature timing fix, and worth a commit
of its own rather than being folded silently into the rebase.

The continuum operator was charged to STAGE_FOCK by a lap in the SCF loop. That
lap no longer exists on main: `assemble_fock` closes its own stage, and the
caller's lap was removed because `report_lap` increments a stage's CALL COUNT as
well as its seconds, so lapping the same stage twice per iteration reported two
Fock builds per iteration.

Restoring that lap to carry the continuum would have reintroduced exactly the
bug the fix removed. So the continuum gets its own row instead, which is more
honest anyway: it is a separate physical step, and the row says what it costs.
On the dianion that is a fraction of a percent against the quadrature, which is
worth being able to see rather than infer.

The final Fock rebuild after convergence laps it too. It already applied the
operator -- it must, or the reported energy would be the gas-phase one -- but
did not lap, so the stage counted one fewer than the Fock builds it shadows.

Rebased onto main (12 commits, including the timing fix and a unit-test PR).
Re-verified after: PCM validation 4/4, ctest 104/104, both linters clean, and
the water C-PCM case still reproduces its reference to 3e-12.

Design record for migrating RigelBuild/compass off GitHub Dependabot onto
the same self-hosted Renovate orion runs, adapted to compass's layout and
running in GitHub Actions (compass has no Woodpecker). Fleet converges on one
dependency manager; Dependabot's hidden GitHub-billed features go away.

Ships as its own PR ahead of implementation, per the design workflow: the
record is reviewed as pure design, and its merge freezes the contract the
impl PRs build against.

Key decisions (Matt-ratified after a design-critic red-team):
- Runner: a plain GHA job (checkout -> install-nix -> gate-tools toolchain ->
  vendored-fork devenv shim -> pinned `bunx renovate@44.33.1`), reusing
  compass's existing per-job nix bootstrap.
- Auth: a GitHub App minting a per-run installation token (no long-lived PAT);
  the App needs the Workflows permission or github-actions bump PRs can't push.
- Cadence: daily, including the devenv-nixpkgs channel.
- Managers: port 5 of orion's 7 customManagers; ADD the github-actions manager
  (compass keeps SHA-pinned actions Dependabot maintained); drop the dead nix
  manager and provider lockstep; go tracked via tools/toolchain/versions/go.nix.

(tools/design-ledger-gate/index.ts:45 PRODUCT_DIR=docs/designs/product) and no

author: icontre2
body:
Este es el fallo de verdad detrás de "el login de Google y Facebook no funciona".

## La evidencia

Confirmado contra los registros reales de Supabase de esta cuenta:

- Login con Google completado hace unos minutos (`resultado: 'ok'`, actor `icontre97@gmail.com`).
- Login con Facebook completado ayer.
- Pero la fila de `fantasy_links` **no se ha actualizado desde ayer a las 13:33**, pese a dos accesos sociales completados después. Esa es la huella del fallo.

## La causa

`resolverEnlace`, en la rama que restaura sesión desde el enlace guardado (entras con Google **sin** sesión de LALIGA activa), renovaba el token de LALIGA cuando hacía falta pero **nunca guardaba el resultado**.

Azure B2C rota el refresh token en cada renovación — el que devuelve no es el mismo que se le mandó — así que la fila se quedaba con uno **ya gastado**.

La primera vez funcionaba: el token guardado aún servía. La siguiente, `tokensVigentes` intentaba renovar con ese token ya consumido, LALIGA lo rechazaba, y el mensaje era "tu permiso ha caducado, reconéctala". No había caducado: se había tirado sin querer, en nuestro propio código.

`access.ts` ya hacía esto bien en su propio camino de renovación (`actualizarTokens` tras `refreshTokens`); a esta rama del callback le faltaba el mismo paso.

## El arreglo

Una línea: `await actualizarTokens(...)` antes de crear la sesión.

## De paso

Se saca `resolverEnlace` de `route.ts` a `social-callback.ts`, con imports relativos: es la única forma de poder probarlo con `node --test` sin pasar por el compilador de Next, que es quien resuelve el alias `@/` de la ruta. Al intentarlo salieron a la luz varios imports sin extensión en la cadena `session.ts → auth.ts → config.ts` que nunca se habían ejecutado fuera de Next; corregidos (sin cambio de comportamiento).

## Pruebas nuevas

- Fija que el token renovado **se guarda de verdad** — descifrando lo que llega a la base y comprobando que es el NUEVO, no el viejo repetido.
- Cuando LALIGA rechaza incluso el refresh nuevo, se dice la verdad y no se guarda nada inválido.

## Comprobado

`tsc`, `eslint`, 258 pruebas, `next build`. Todo en verde.

## Después de fusionar

La fila del usuario afectado sigue con el token gastado de ayer. Hace falta reconectar LALIGA **una vez más** (email+contraseña, o el token de la sesión oficial) para que se guarde un par de tokens bueno. A partir de ahí, con el arreglo puesto, debería mantenerse solo indefinidamente.
