author: niolson
body:
## Why

Nothing in production verified that an instance could reach its database. `/up` is liveness-only by design and never touches it, and `/api/health` — which did check the database — was registered only under `local`/`testing`, so the route did not exist in production. Redis was covered only by accident, via the Redis-backed session middleware.

The result: a database outage of any cause — a dropped network path, a crash-looping container, a botched credential rotation, a full disk — left every health check green while users got 500s.

## What changed

`/api/health` is now registered in every environment and does real round-trips to both datastores. 200 when reachable, 503 when not, so a monitor can act on the status code alone with no keyword matching.

| State | Status | Body |
|---|---|---|
| Healthy | 200 | `{"status":"ok","checks":{"database":"ok","redis":"ok"}}` |
| Database only | 503 | `…{"database":"unreachable","redis":"ok"}` |
| Redis only | 503 | `…{"database":"ok","redis":"unreachable"}` |
| Both | 503 | `…{"database":"unreachable","redis":"unreachable"}` |

Three decisions worth calling out:

- **Both dependencies are checked even when the first fails.** Losing both at once points at the network path out of the instance; losing one points at that datastore. Short-circuiting would collapse those into a single indistinguishable alert.
- **Redis reports `skipped`, not `ok`, when nothing is configured to use it** (session/cache/queue/broadcast driver). Reporting a Redis nobody talks to as healthy would claim a result the probe never tested, and would report an install on other drivers as degraded.
- **`/up` is deliberately unchanged** and stays what the container healthcheck polls. A healthcheck that failed on a datastore blip would make Docker restart the container, turning an outage into a restart loop. There is a test pinning `/up` at 200 with the database unreachable.

## Bounding the work

The checks are bounded so an unreachable host fails fast rather than holding a PHP worker for the default socket timeout: a new short-timeout, no-retry `readiness` Redis connection, and a short-timeout clone of the default database connection.

This needed measuring rather than assuming. An earlier version using `DB::select()` took **12s** against a host that drops packets — Laravel retries once at the connector layer and again in `Connection::run`, multiplying the 3s timeout by four. Going straight to the PDO halves that to a measured 6s, plus 3s for Redis. A refused connection returns immediately. Those numbers are recorded in comments.

## Config change

Adds a `readiness` connection under `database.redis` — same server as `default`, with a short timeout and `max_retries => 0`. No new env vars. Verified to survive `config:cache` and `route:cache`, which is what the container entrypoint's `php artisan optimize` runs.

## ⚠️ Deployment note

The body names which dependency is unreachable, because that distinction is the diagnosis. That assumes the path is reachable by your monitoring and not from the internet — **restrict `/api/health` at your reverse proxy.** If it has to stay public, reduce the body to `status` alone; the reasoning is on `HealthController`.

The endpoint is unauthenticated and rate limited to 20/min per IP. It reports only three fixed verdicts per dependency — no exception text, hostnames, driver names, or versions — and a test asserts none of those appear in any state.

## Testing

11 feature tests in `tests/Feature/HealthEndpointsTest.php`: healthy, each datastore unreachable individually, both unreachable, Redis skipped when unused, `/up` unaffected by a database outage, and a parameterized leak check across all three states.

Full suite: 1598 passed. PHPStan and Pint clean. Also verified end-to-end against a real MySQL and Redis, and with each outage injected before boot to confirm the actual status codes and bodies.

author: zackees
body:
Slice of #971 (phase 5/9, `platform::ipc`).

## What moved

The backend connection path carried a raw `interprocess::local_socket::Stream`
end to end: `connect_to_backend` -> `BackendConnection.stream` -> `FrameClient`
-> `FrameClient::into_stream` -> `OwnedBackendIo`, with
`backend_handle::Connection` dialling the same native type on its own. It
migrates as one unit — splitting it would only have relocated
`into_legacy_ipc_stream` bridges from one seam to the next.

New facade primitive: `Stream::into_owned_fd` on the two unix trees. Handing
over the descriptor that backs a negotiated connection is what `OwnedBackendIo`
is for, and owning that transfer is what keeps the `Stream::UdSocket` match out
of `adopt.rs`.

`backend_handle::Connection::connect` now uses `ipc::Endpoint::new` +
`ipc::Stream::connect` instead of `wrap_socket_name`. Same `to_fs_name`/pipe
resolution, so accepted names are unchanged; a rejected name now reports
`InvalidInput` rather than `Other`.

## What deliberately stayed

`client_v2::ClientSession::connect_backend` and the `control_socket` post-Hello
callback keep their raw-stream contracts — `into_legacy_ipc_stream` is
documented as holding those until the next major release. `connect_backend`
gains a `pub(crate)` `connect_backend_ipc` twin so in-repo callers stop
round-tripping through the native type.

## Public surface

`BackendConnection.stream` is public and changes type. The consumer docs
reference only `endpoint` and `route`; the documented ways to use the stream
(`FrameClient`, `into_backend_io`) are unchanged.

Running total in `crates/running-process/src`: **60 -> 45**.

## Verification

- Windows: a `--features daemon --all-targets` check and the default client
  lane are both clean.
- 89 focused broker tests pass (`backend_sdk`, `adopt`, `toy_three_party`,
  `backend_handle`, `handoff_serve`, `doctor`, `client_v2`).
- `./lint` green.
- The unix-only `into_owned_fd` was compiled by cross-checking the lib for
  `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`; only the binaries fail there, at link time, on a
  local cross-toolchain flag unrelated to this change. Linux/macOS CI is the
  authority.

Refs #971.

author: mr3826
body:
Production run 32511063613 aborted its migration step on `ALTER COLUMN token DROP NOT NULL` with `column "token" of relation "password_reset_tokens" does not exist`, while CI stayed green. Rollback passed and the incumbent backend stayed healthy; nothing was partially applied.

## Root cause

Two lineages of `password_reset_tokens` exist:

- **squash** (`20260520_000`, every fresh/CI database): `token TEXT NOT NULL`, `used BOOLEAN NOT NULL`
- **pre-squash** (`archive/20260408_001`, production): `token_hash NOT NULL`, `used_at` — and **no** `token`, **no** `used`

Production's ledger marks the squash executed (see `20260816_001`), so it never ran there. The migration's bare `ALTER COLUMN` statements assumed the squash shape, which only CI has.

## Changes

- `20260814_001` guards every statement on `information_schema` (the pattern already used by `20260611_003`/`20260611_004`) and adds the entity columns `token_hash`/`used_at` where the ledger skipped `20260522_003`. Converges both lineages; re-runnable, since the runner does not wrap migrations in a transaction.
- New integration test drives the migration against **both** shapes on a real Postgres. Against the pre-fix migration it fails with the exact production error; mocked migration unit tests cannot see this class of defect.
- The isolated restore drill (`backup.yml`) now runs pending migrations against the **restored production dump** — nightly after the backup, and on demand with an optional candidate image — then reports the schema-drift audit. The migrator carries no production database coordinates and refuses to start unless `DATABASE_URL` names the drill's isolated container; the drill asserts production's postgres process and migration ledger are unchanged afterwards.

## Verification

- New integration test: 3/3 pass; 3/3 fail against the pre-fix migration with `column "token" ... does not exist`
- Full migration chain on a fresh database: pass
- Full pending chain on a production-shaped database (pre-squash table + 31-row ledger stamped executed): `20260814_001` through `20260820_003` all applied
- `workflow-deploy-guard` suite, `src/database/__tests__` unit suites, and the test-discovery guard: pass
- `backup.yml` parses as YAML; the drill script passes `bash -n`

author: sourcehawk
body:
## Description

Closes #153

The restore code merged across six pull requests written in parallel, and the one sweep that ran before the merge worked from a checklist rather than from a full reading. This is the deliberate second pass: the merged restore code read end to end and made to read as though one person wrote it.

**It changes no observable behaviour** — no condition reason, no message, no event, no phase, and no order of side effects moves.

This pull request is no longer stacked. #155, #156 and #157 have merged, so its diff is the sweep alone: 24 files, and every one of them a file the sweep changed.

## Changes

- **One terminal branch for the three restore kinds.** `restore.Finish` holds it. Each controller carried a byte-identical copy, grown by #155 (collect the Jobs) and #157 (withdraw the suspension) landing separately. The three controllers lose `resumeCluster`, `releaseClaim` and `claimant`.
- **`Finish` answers `(Outcome, error)`,** the shape `Primary` and `CollectJobs` already use, so `pkg/restore` answers the same way everywhere. Collection converges over more than one look — foreground propagation outlives the call, so a Job that still exists means its pods can still hold the broker volumes — and `Finish` stops there. The unsuspend and the claim release stay behind that gate, and each terminal branch requeues on `Outcome.Wait`.
- **`restore.MovedVersion`.** #157 added `movedVersion` to both logical restore controllers, byte-identical down to its reason and its message. It now lives beside `WritesVersion`, whose answer it already asks for, with a test of its own.
- **`versionTarget` asks `WritesVersion` for the version rule** instead of spelling `versionPattern.MatchString(in.Version)` a second time. That expression is the whole body of `WritesVersion`, whose own doc says a phase that holds a cluster to the version of its backup asks it first.
- **`Take` and `Give` take the owner and the cluster name.** `pkg/restore` builds the claimant identity once, in `claimantOf`, so no controller writes the identity of its own resource by hand.
- **`ReadTarget` is unexported.** The first sweep hoisted `ResolveTarget` into `pkg/restore` as the shape a phase reports in, and every caller uses it; the package still published a second exported door to the same read.
- **`failure` and `progressing` moved next to `Outcome`.** Both the preparation step and the primary-storage phase report through them, and both comments still said "the primary-storage phase".
- **Two files reordered to #164's order-within-a-file rule, two godocs sized to #167's length bound.** `claim.go` opened with `claimantOf`, above the two functions that call it; `prepare.go` opened with the two version functions, so its entry point was the third function. `Finish` carried 32 godoc lines over an 18-line body and `MovedVersion` 14 over 13; the ordering rationale moved to the three call sites it constrains, where a tidy-up meets it.
- **Comments the merged code outgrew.** `Target`'s "two entry points a controller reaches" (there are four, and they are `Prepare` and `Primary`); the `pkg/restore` package summary, which never mentioned preparing the cluster; a `pointintimerestore` package doc that a merge broke mid-sentence; and `EventReasonStarted`, documented as per-broker while the relational kind also emits it at admission.
- **One name per concept in the two sibling logical restores.** `backup.SourceCluster` → `backup.Cluster` (the Elasticsearch name for the same fact, and the name its consumer `compatibility.BackupCluster` already uses); the local holding the resolved target renamed `resolved` → `target`; and `notSuspended`'s "may only touch" → "only touches", matching its sibling.

### Why the merges are behaviour-preserving

The three terminal branches were byte-identical apart from the receiver name and the cluster-reference field. `logicalrestoreelasticsearch`, as it stood on `main`:

```go
restore.StageTerminal(&lres, &lres.Status.RestoreProgress)
collected, err := restore.CollectJobs(ctx, r.Client, r.APIReader, &lres, &lres.Status.RestoreProgress)
if err != nil || !collected.Done {
    return ctrl.Result{RequeueAfter: collected.Wait}, err
}
if err := r.resumeCluster(ctx, &lres); err != nil { return ctrl.Result{}, err }
return ctrl.Result{}, r.releaseClaim(ctx, &lres)
```

`pointintimerestore`, with `lres` replaced by `pitr` and `Spec.TargetClusterRef.Name` by `Spec.ClusterRef.Name`, and `logicalrestorerdbms` with `lrr`, were the same lines and the same 25 lines of comment. Both wrappers were single calls with no logic of their own: `resumeCluster` is `restore.Resume(ctx, r.Client, r.APIReader, &x.Status.RestoreProgress, types.NamespacedName{Namespace: x.Namespace, Name: <ref>})`, and `releaseClaim` is `restore.Give(ctx, r.Client, r.APIReader, x.Namespace, <ref>, claimant(x))`. `Finish` makes the same four calls in the same order, returns on the first error, and gates the last two on `collected.Done` exactly as the branches did, so the reason, the message, the event and the requeue a user sees are unchanged.

`movedVersion` was byte-identical in the two admit files — `diff` of the two ranges prints nothing — including the `v1.ReasonIncompatibleTarget` reason and every character of the message a user reads. `claimant` was the same struct literal in all three controllers: `clusterclaim.Claimant{Kind: x.GetKind(), Name: x.Name, UID: x.UID}`. `claimantOf` builds it from `conditions.Owner`, which carries the same three getters, and `Take`/`Give` derive the namespace from the owner, which every call site already passed as `x.Namespace`. `versionTarget`'s `!versionPattern.MatchString(in.Version)` and `!WritesVersion(in.Version)` are the same boolean: the second is the body of the first.

## Near-duplicates left alone, and why

Extending the list in #153. Each of these looks mergeable and is not.

- **`pinnedBackup` in the two logical restore controllers.** Same shape as `movedVersion`, and not the same case: the message names the kind and the artifact it identifies — "LogicalBackupElasticsearch … pair with another record snapshot" against "LogicalBackupRDBMS … its dump lies under another key". That is the `backupBucket` rule of #153, which stays duplicated for the same reason.
- **`claimant` in the two backup controllers.** The same three-line literal exists five times across the repo, two of them in `logicalbackupelasticsearch` and `logicalbackuprdbms`. `clusterclaim` is the right home for a shared constructor, but those two are outside this issue's scope and their suites call `claimant(...)` at fourteen assertion sites. That hoist is a change of its own, with the backup controllers in scope.
- **`restore.Apply`, `BuildJob` and `RecreateClaims` stay exported with no caller outside `pkg/restore`.** Unlike `ReadTarget`, none of them is superseded by an exported sibling that does the same job — they are the package's rendering and applying contract, and their GoDoc is what a reader of `pkg/restore` needs. The same now holds for `Resume` and `Give`, whose only caller is `Finish`. Narrowing that surface is an API decision, not a coherence fix.
- **`isJob` in `pkg/restore/holder.go` against `controllerOf` in `pkg/podstate`.** Both answer "does this controller reference name a batch Job?", and they answer differently: `isJob` requires the exact `batch/v1`, `controllerOf` parses the reference and compares the group alone. Sharing one would newly match a Job of another version.
- **The dead guard in `zoneFailure`.** Its only caller iterates a map that by construction holds `zoneVars` keys alone, so `if !slices.Contains(zoneVars, name)` can never fire in production. `TestZoneFailure` covers it with `CAMUNDA_CLUSTER_SIZE`: the test encodes the contract that the function answers for any variable, so the guard stays.
- **`backupFacts` in the Elasticsearch controller, inlined in the relational one.** The Elasticsearch backup needs a nil check on `status.storage` before it can name the buck

The review round on #714/#716 produced two commits (`d1b65e9b`, `b7dabdcc`) that landed only on `MigrationFromJDk11ToAWSCorretto17` and are now live in prod (image `640…53e1dc94`). `development` never received them, so anyone working off dev is missing guards that prod has.

author: nemanjaglumac
body:
Resolves DEV-2760

## Summary

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Rather than attempting to cherry-pick changes from `master` or `release-x.63.x`, this PR encapsulates the core logic from them. tl;dr We want to unconditionally run tests when a commit is merged to `release-x.58.x` branch.

Every gate in _run-tests.yml_ re-derived its own answer to "is this a branch where everything must run?", and several of them got it wrong. A new `should-run` job answers it once -- `force-run`, `force-skip`, or `defer` -- and every downstream gate reads that verdict.

Three things this fixes on release branches:

  - A release-branch push that touched no backend files skipped every driver job, H2 and Postgres included. `driver-decision` checked the global skip flag ahead of the master/release check, and run-tests.yml passes `skip: backend_all != 'true'`. force-run now sits at Priority 1, ahead of skip. Verified against release-x.58.x: 0 drivers ran before, 20 after.

  - A release-branch push touching only e2e specs ran just those specs. The narrowing expression had no event guard, so it applied to pushes as well as PRs. It is now pull-request-only.

  - The `ci skip` label did not stop the uberjar. It gated only files-changed, whose skipped-job outputs are empty strings, so the uberjar's docs-only guard evaluated true and it built anyway. That label is replaced by `ci:skip`, which every gate honors, alongside a new `ci:run-all`.

The driver decision's `--is-master-or-release` flag becomes `--force-run`, so a `ci:run-all` label can force a full run from a PR. backend.yml, app-db.yml and drivers.yml take a matching `force-run` input.

The old migrations tests are broken, so `mb/old-migrations-test` is now excluded (the logic from #80214).

author: roitsch-code
body:
Hours after the variety work shipped, the chat handed the owner a 450 ml recipe whose **final pour was 225 g — half the water — in the 15 s the clock had left**, after a **two-and-a-half-minute hole** where nothing happens. With a Brew button under it.

Round 1 touched the chat, but only for **variety**. Every defect in the report is a **quality** defect, and the gap was documented in CLAUDE.md for weeks: *"the chat's `start_brew` path runs no fidelity guard at all"*. I read past it and measured the neighbouring surface instead.

`/recommend` runs **ten** deterministic guards. The chat's `start_brew` ran **one**. Verified by grep — `normalizeGrindToGrinder`, `reconcileToReference`, `vesselOverflow`, `stripMinimalAgitationSwirls`, `stripProactiveDripAssist`, `calibrateTargetTimes`, `calibrateDripAssistFinish` each had exactly one call site, all in `recommend.ts`.

## Every defect traced to a sentence /recommend has and the chat didn't

| Reported | Cause |
|---|---|
| 225 g in 15 s, 2:30 dead gap | `/recommend`'s prompt carries the ~4 g/s pourability rule **and** "3–5 pours, never one giant final pour". Neither was anywhere in the chat prompt. |
| Hatakeyama "geduldige Pours" with no gooseneck | The kettle section drew one consequence — put the disc on it — and framed the disc as fully restoring pour control. Nothing said a recipe whose *technique* needs a gooseneck is off the table. |
| Clever after "Nein. Orea." | The prompt **asks for it** ("Immersion … worth one clause"), and the override rule was explicitly *profile*-scoped, so narrowing a set he owns overrode nothing. |
| "Apex oder Classic?" | No rule told the chat to make the brewing call. Three licensed asking — with both bottoms' flow ranking in its own context. |
| Emoji, raw `\| \| \|` | Weakest voice ban of seven AI surfaces; renderer knew only bold+italic while the prompt itself demonstrates a GFM table. |

## What ships

**`src/lib/recipe/validateRecipe.ts`** — the same checks as *questions*. It validates the **rendered timeline**, which is load-bearing: the model never wrote that dead gap, it was *derived* (three pours over a 3:30 clock leaves a hole), so an authored-step check passes the recipe.

**Validate, not repair.** `/recommend` corrects in place and the user only sees the result — unchanged, it's measured and it works. The chat has already said the numbers out loud, so a silent rewrite splits message from timer (#198). A failed recipe goes back as an error `tool_result`, **one** repair round, then no Brew button and the user is told why.

**A real `/recommend` bug fell out:** `parseGrindDegrees` read `"26 clicks"` as 26 degrees, so **every travel recipe** looked ~350° too fine and had its grind silently overwritten. Found only because the validator printed its comparison.

**`april-1-2-3` → `verified: false`.** April's own page (owner-supplied) publishes no 1-2-3 method; not one figure matches and `minimal-agitation` contradicts their "pour aggressively so that you agitate the grounds". It was a fidelity snap target, so this corrupted `/recommend` too. Peer audit: four entries already unverified; `rolf-april-v60` re-checked against its URL and holds up exactly — left alone.

## Verification

`tsc`, 50 src + 372 dataflow tests, corpus clean. The **anchor test is the reported recipe with its real numbers and it must be rejected**. Route-level tests assert the handler *imports and calls* the validator (#530/#535 both shipped on producer-only tests). The renderer is verified by **rendering it**, not by reading source.

**Not measured yet:** how often the model now writes a brewable recipe first time. The validator guarantees a broken one can't reach the timer; whether the prompt rules stop it being written needs a live chat run. That failure mode is a wait, not a bad brew.

---

author: denyspupin
body:
## Intent

Phase 2 / v2.0.0, PR 2 of 3. Makes the middleware context type-safe (finding F-05), addressing the actual criticism from the review: middleware could not participate in the library's core promise of type safety. Stacked on #46.

## Changes

- `RpcMiddlewareContext<Procedures>` is now a discriminated union keyed by procedure name: narrowing on `ctx.procedure` narrows `ctx.payload` to that procedure's request type.
- Validation-style middleware no longer needs `as keyof typeof validators` casts (README Zod example rewritten; compile-guarded in `tests/type-contract.compile.ts`).
- Config accepts `RpcMiddleware[]` only — scalar form removed; `.use()` unchanged.
- `RpcServerConfig` is generic over the procedure schema.
- Bare `RpcMiddleware` keeps an open-schema default (`procedure: string`, `payload: unknown`) for schema-agnostic helpers, but typed servers require `RpcMiddleware<Procedures>` (TS rejects cross-constraint assignment).

D7 escape hatch was considered: the union proved ergonomic in practice, so the full retype ships rather than falling back to array-only cleanup.

## Migration

- Declare middleware against your schema: `const mw: RpcMiddleware<Procedures> = async (ctx) => {...}`.
- Pass config middleware as an array: `middleware: [mw]`, not `middleware: mw`.
- If you annotate config objects directly, `RpcServerConfig` now requires a type argument: `RpcServerConfig<Procedures>`.

## Verification

- Full gate green on the stacked branch: typecheck, lint, 169 tests, coverage 98/92/95/98, build, packed-consumer ESM+CJS smoke
- New compile-time guards: payload narrowing per procedure, void-request field access fails, scalar config form fails
- README §Middleware and §Runtime validation rewritten against the new signature

author: dbwiddis
body:
Completes the follow-up announced in #3652, which fixed `FileSystemMetrics` and deferred the other two binders.

## The problem

`DiskMetrics` and `NetworkMetrics` called `updateAttributes()` **inside each meter's sampling lambda**, so a single scrape queried the same device once per meter — five times for a disk, seven for an interface — and every meter's value came from a *different* reading.

That is wasteful, but the sharper problem is that it makes pairs of metrics incomparable. `system.network.errors` divided by `system.network.packet.count` is a natural rate to compute, and the two numerators were measured at different moments. Same for `system.disk.io` over `system.disk.operations`.

## The change

Both binders now build one memoized supplier per device and hand it to every meter, exactly as `FileSystemMetrics` has since #3652:

```java
Supplier<HWDiskStore> refreshed = Memoizer.memoize(() -> {
    disk.updateAttributes();
    return disk;
}, Memoizer.defaultExpiration());
```

One query per device per expiration window, and one snapshot per scrape.

The deliberate GC-root fields now retain the **suppliers** rather than the device lists, since the supplier is what Micrometer weakly references. The suppliers close over the devices, so those stay reachable through them — retaining the old list would have left the suppliers collectible and silently broken the metrics after a GC. `FunctionCounter.Builder` has no `strongReference()` of its own, as `Gauge.Builder` does, so those fields are still the only thing keeping the measured object alive.

The per-meter registration is now a shared private helper in each class, which is what makes the seven- and six-line builder chains readable once the value function is the only thing that varies.

## Tests

New `DiskMetricsTest` and `NetworkMetricsTest` bind a device whose counters advance on every refresh and count the refreshes, following `FileSystemMetricsTest`'s fixture approach. They assert both halves: that one scrape refreshes the device once, and that every meter agrees with every other.

Negative-tested — dropping the `memoize` fails them at 6 refreshes for the disk and 7 for the interface, so they are load-bearing rather than tautological. `NetworkMetricsTest` backs its fixture with the loopback `NetworkInterface`, since that is all `AbstractNetworkIF` needs, and skips via an assumption if there is none.

## Verification

Full gate green on macOS JDK 25 (`spotless:apply sortpom:sort checkstyle:check install forbiddenapis:check javadoc:javadoc -Paggregate-coverage`), plus `-Perror-prone` for NullAway. `oshi-metrics` is platform-independent, so CI covers the rest.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Disk and network metrics now use one shared reading per device during each scrape.
  * Related meters report consistent values for the same disk or network interface.
  * Reduced system queries improve monitoring efficiency, especially with many registered metrics.
  * Metric binding is more lightweight, with device data read only when metrics are collected.
  * Network connection-count metrics now share cached readings within the refresh window.
* **Documentation**

author: map-boy
body:
## Summary
This PR adds a complete Android implementation of the SmartMotos ride-sharing app, mirroring the existing iOS codebase. The Android app is built with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Firebase, with a shared Firestore schema documented in SCHEMA.md.

## Key Changes

### Android App Structure
- **SmartRepository.kt**: Kotlin port of the iOS SmartRepository.swift, providing centralized Firebase Firestore data management with StateFlow-based reactive streams for users, trips, drivers, topups, and pending driver approvals
- **Models.kt**: Data classes for UserProfile, RideTrip, LocationPoint, TopupRequest, and DriverInfo matching the Firestore schema exactly
- **AuthViewModel.kt**: Phone authentication flow using Firebase Auth with OTP verification and auto-retrieval support
- **MainActivity.kt**: Entry point with Jetpack Compose UI, auth state management, and listener lifecycle integration

### Build Configuration
- **app/build.gradle.kts**: Android app module configuration with Compose, Firebase SDK (auth, Firestore, functions, messaging), and Material3 dependencies
- **build.gradle.kts**: Root-level Gradle configuration with Android and Kotlin plugin versions
- **settings.gradle.kts**: Gradle settings with repository configuration
- **gradle.properties**: JVM memory and Android build options
- **gradlew / gradlew.bat**: Gradle wrapper scripts for cross-platform builds

### Firebase & Cloud Functions
- **functions/src/index.ts**: Cloud Functions for admin user creation with role-based access control
- **functions/package.json & tsconfig.json**: TypeScript configuration for Cloud Functions
- **firestore.rules**: Security rules for users, trips, topupRequests, and roleChangeRequests collections with role-based access
- **firestore.indexes.json**: Composite index for trips collection (riderId + createdAt)
- **firebase.json**: Firebase project configuration for Firestore, functions, and deployment

### Documentation & Configuration
- **SCHEMA.md**: Single source of truth for Firestore schema, field types, and validation rules across all platforms
- **.firebaserc**: Firebase project configuration
- **AndroidManifest.xml**: Android app permissions (internet, location) and activity declaration
- **CI/CD workflows**: Updated build-and-release.yml and new ci.yml with Android build steps

### iOS Updates
- **SmartRepository.swift**: Added centralized error logging via `lastFirestoreError` property to surface Firestore listener failures (previously silent)
- **project.yml**: Fixed source path configuration for XcodeGen

### Git Configuration
- **.gitignore**: Added Android-specific ignores (google-services.json, .gradle, build/, *.apk, *.aab, etc.)

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Schema-First Design**: SCHEMA.md is the authoritative source; all platform implementations (iOS, Android) must match field names and types exactly
- **Reactive Data Flow**: SmartRepository uses Kotlin StateFlow for reactive UI updates, mirroring iOS @Published properties
- **Error Visibility**: Added explicit Firestore listener error logging to prevent silent data failures (e.g., missing composite indexes)
- **Phone Auth**: Supports both manual OTP entry and Android auto-retrieval for seamless authentication
- **Role-Based Access**: Firestore rules enforce passenger-only creation, driver/admin read access, and admin-only deletions
- **Gradle Wrapper**: Included for reproducible builds across environments

author: cgetzen
body:
## What this changes

- Adds an offline repertoire compiler with deterministic 80/90/95 coverage checkpoints.
- Stores dated historical evidence separately from the versioned repertoire/teaching policy.
- Resolves canonical position identity at generation time and commits a static generated artifact; the browser never queries the opening database or runs discovery.
- Applies the process to major Caro-Kann decision points: the top-level reply to 1...c6, the primary Advance ...c5 position, the Exchange position after ...cxd5, and the 2.Nc3 d5 decision.
- Adds four generated 2.Nc3 responses required to reach ~95% internal coverage: 3.d4, 3.Qf3, 3.exd5, and 3.d3.
- Projects the dated evidence into curriculum tiers: 2.Nc3 remains Core; 2.Nf3 and 2.c4 are Important; 2.d3 becomes Sideline.
- Moves terminal repertoire alternatives onto the generated evidence path and accepts Hillbilly Bg4 alongside Bf5 based on the reviewed engine/theory evidence.
- Separates the move actually played in history from canonical decision semantics, so rewind/forward cannot change which primary or accepted repertoire moves are valid.
- Adds stale-generated-artifact CI checks, domain/regression tests, and generator documentation.

## Architecture

Historical data and engine/theory review are compile-time inputs only. Generated responses enter the same canonical `(position, opponent move)` response registry as curated content. No parallel runtime training system is introduced.

History reconstruction may preserve the move the learner actually played, but attempt validation, hints, and decision teaching are projected from the canonical repertoire decision at that displayed ply. The same displayed position therefore has the same primary and accepted moves regardless of navigation path.

## Evidence snapshot

body:
Terminal **30 of 30**, sweep #6. 500 phases, ids **P14501–P15000**. Base `3b2da445`.

**DO NOT MERGE — the owner gated this wave. This PR is open and waiting for his approval.**

Six files, all additions, no product file touched. One commit per numbered item, so a veto can be honoured by reverting exactly one.

---

## The honest headline

**The product came back clean. The scaffolding around it did not.**

42 live navigations across all five panels, both sizes, both skins, on port 4130: zero console errors, zero page errors, zero 5xx. The money agreed with itself across four surfaces — the database function, the manager's floor, the owner's Dashboard and Reports, and the admin's bill ledger. Every cache had a writer that busts it. Every breadcrumb kind reached a screen. Aangan rendered Aangan's branding, not restaurant #1's. The classic this terminal was sent to hunt — the admin access-tree endpoint not busting the guest menu cache — is closed at all three layers.

**One product fault**, found by comparing a pair of files, which is what a cross-panel terminal is for. **Five defects in one test guard.** **Four coverage holes in the sweep's own arithmetic.** **Four territories that never ran at all.**

`348` rows pass · `56` record a real problem in a file this terminal may not write to · `96` are reserved, each with a written reason **and** the command that re-derives its list.

---

## 🟢 Built (items 1, 3, 4, 5)

**Item 1 — `.claude/sweep/LEDGER/INDEX.md`.** Twenty-six ledger files existed with no way to know what they covered, which phase numbers were free, or what nobody had ever checked. The index is now the master record and the ID registry every future sweep reads first: all 30 territories with their permanent blocks and their own pass/problem/reserved counts; a coverage table built by cross-producing every file in the repo against every territory's own bullets; the gap list ordered by what a real restaurant loses; the three ID faults with a reserved repair block; the standing pre-empts, each sourced rather than remembered; the commands that recompute every number; and a plain answer to "will the next run come back clean?" (no).

**Item 2 — the skill now says "re-run before you re-invent", four times over.** `SKILL.md` gained a Stage 0 that runs before planning, and the rule is in its frontmatter `description:` so it is visible before the body loads. `PROMPT-STYLE.md` gained Rule Zero — *a prompt without its ledger rows is a broken prompt* — the prompt skeleton itself carries the re-run instruction, and cleanup in both files is now forbidden from ever deleting or archiving `LEDGER/`. **These two files are NOT in this PR: `.claude/skills/**` is gitignored, so they were edited in place in the shared folder, which is the only place Claude Code loads a skill from.** The same instruction is mirrored into `INDEX.md` and `docs/QA-500-PHASES.md`, both of which *are* in this PR, so the rule survives in the repo either way.

**Item 3 — `docs/QA-500-PHASES.md`.** Two different things were both called "the tests". The doc now opens with a table separating them — the suite is a gate that runs in minutes, the ledger is a memory of everything ever checked — and closes with how a sweep finding becomes a suite phase, and why a ledger row citing a retired guard is worse than no row (the `verify:cache` lesson).

**Item 4 — `LEDGER/T30.md`.** The 500 permanent checks. No row is filler: an earlier draft had 107 identical "reserved" rows, and they were replaced with one row per real file carrying a real computed result.

**Item 5 — the findings, the ideas, and a working guard.** Plus a complete `scripts/verify-ledger-index.mjs`, saved as `.txt` because `scripts/` and `package.json` belong to other terminals.

---

## 🔗 HANDOFFS — the merge terminal collects these

**1 · Three per-restaurant panel doors give the browser tab no name.** `app/r/[restaurant]/{manager,kitchen,tablet}/page.tsx`. Their `/manager`, `/kitchen`, `/tablet` twins each set `export const metadata = { title: "… — Aevidine" }` — and `app/manager/page.tsx` says why inline: three open panels once gave a manager three identical tabs (T15 sweep, 2026-08-05). The per-restaurant twins never got it. **One line per file.** `/login` is not affected — neither side sets a title, so they agree. Owner: nobody names these files.

**2 · `verify:realtime` has five defects, and two of them hide the rest.** `scripts/verify-realtime.mjs`, T28's territory — **whose ledger was never filed.** Its own step-5 comment reads *"A guard that is permanently red is a guard people learn to skip."*
- fails step 1 on **correct** behaviour — the breadcrumb IS written (counted: 8 → 9 for French House); it loses the socket warm-up race
- **crashes at step 4**, so step 5 never runs at all: `sessions.restaurant_id` is `NOT NULL` and the insert omits it, then `s.id` throws on `null`
- its session cleanup deletes that table's session in **every** restaurant — no `restaurant_id` filter
- its category step flips `active` by **slug alone**, hitting all **7** restaurants sharing `drinks`, including Aangan the read-only control — and the script dies two steps later, so a kill in that window leaves a category off
- its dish step picks a row with an unscoped, unordered `.limit(1)`

**3 · `verify:pointers` is red on clean `main`.** `docs/GUARD-MAP.md` has no row for `verify:split-payment` or `verify:t24-money-rules`. Proved before changing anything and re-proved after; this branch touches neither that file nor `package.json`. Owner: T29 — ledger never filed.

**4 · Every count in `CLAUDE.md` and the sweep prompts is wrong.** 55/81/339/48 against **56/84/362/50**. The last matters most: CLAUDE.md's own invariant is "that count must equal the number that grep `tokenIsValid`" — both are 50 today so it holds, but a terminal told "48" greps 48 and stops. **Write the command, not the digit.**

**5 · Three ledger files break "one ID, one check, forever".** T9 overran its block by 18 ids into T10's; T13 repeats 15 inside itself; T6 repeats 3. `INDEX.md` reserves `P15001`–`P15100` and allocates `P15001`–`P15036`.

**6 · 73 rows across 15 ledger files do not render at all** — a cell holding an unescaped `|` from a `grep -c 'a|b'` or a `… | wc -l`. The text survives, the row does not, so nothing can count it.

---

## Coverage holes — the next sweep's first assignment

No file anywhere is claimed by two territories: **the fence held.** Its arithmetic leaked in four places.

1. **`components/PanelFrame.tsx` and `components/RealtimeProvider.tsx`** — every panel route renders through `PanelFrame`, every live update flows through the realtime layer, and neither is named by any of the 30 territories. The thinnest-checked load-bearing code in the product.
2. **The four per-restaurant panel doors** — and three of the four already carry handoff 1. Unowned ground is where drift lives.
3. **The print helper's two halves** — `app/aevinite/printing/page.tsx` and `app/api/print-agent/[...path]/route.ts`.
4. **`app/api/admin/rate-limits/route.ts`** — position 26 of **50**, between T19's `head -25` and T20's `tail -24`. Its sign-in check is present (verified); the gap is that nobody was told to look.

Plus **T26–T29 (`P12501`–`P14500`) never ran** — 2,000 checks never executed once, including every check on the repo's own 130 guards.

---

## Checked carefully and deliberately NOT filed

Recorded as permanent `✅` rows so no future sweep re-files them:

- **The owner's revenue INCLUDES soft-deleted bills.** Measured: French House August-to-date is ₹3,76,788 all-in versus ₹2,08,231.50 excluding binned bills. This is **required** — `docs/COMPLIANCE-GUARDRAILS.md` §4, and migration 309's header states the asymmetry (what is *owed* drops a deleted bill, what was *collected* keeps it). **The single most dangerous thing in the ledger to "fix".**

author: maxi-smidt
body:
## Summary
- `document_service.py`, `extract.py`, `merge.py`, and `member_merge.py` raised `fastapi.HTTPException` directly, coupling reusable business logic to the web framework — the exact problem #896 describes (also complicates background jobs and unit tests).
- Added `backend/app/core/exceptions.py`: a `DomainError` base (carries `status_code` + `detail`) with `NotFoundError` (404), `InvalidInputError` (400), `AccessDeniedError` (403), and `ConflictError` (409) subclasses, plus `install_domain_error_handler(app)` — one function that registers the `DomainError -> JSONResponse` mapping, called from both `app.main` (the real app) and the `client` test fixture in `conftest.py` (so HTTP-level tests exercise the same mapping the real app uses). This satisfies "exception mapping is centralized."
- All four service files now raise the appropriate `DomainError` subclass instead of `HTTPException`, with the exact same status codes and detail strings as before (verified via the existing test suite, updated only to `pytest.raises(DomainError)` where they previously asserted `pytest.raises(HTTPException)`).
- `job_service.py`'s background-job runner previously special-cased `isinstance(exc, HTTPException)` to unwrap a clean error message; it now checks `DomainError` instead and no longer imports `HTTPException` at all. `trees.py`'s `_do_merge`/`_do_extract` background-job wrapper functions (which run off the request/response cycle, inside a threadpool background task) now raise `NotFoundError("User not found")` instead of `HTTPException`, so the whole background-job path is HTTP-free.
- `document_service.save_document` previously caught its own `QuotaExceeded` and converted it to `HTTPException(413, ...)` internally — inconsistent with the ~15 other call sites in this codebase that let `QuotaExceeded` propagate and catch it in the router. Moved that catch to `documents.py`'s `save_document_route`, matching the established convention.
- Added `backend/tests/test_domain_exceptions.py`: isolated tests for the handler itself (each `DomainError` subclass maps to its status code; a custom subclass with no dedicated handler still maps via the base-class registration), satisfying "exception mapping is... tested."

Closes #896

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run ruff check` (backend)
- [x] `uv run python -m compileall app alembic` + `python -c "import app.main"`
- [x] `uv run pytest` (backend, full suite green, including the new `test_domain_exceptions.py` and the updated `test_extract_move.py` / `test_merge.py` / `test_merge_preview.py` / `test_member_merge.py`)
- [x] Confirmed `grep -rn HTTPException app/services/` returns nothing for the four touched services
- [x] HTTP status codes/response bodies unchanged: existing tests assert `resp.status_code` / `exc.value.status_code` against the same values as before this change

💡 What: Implemented a caching mechanism in `_build_project_file_index` to reuse precalculated SHA-1 hashes by verifying that file `mtime` and `size` remain unchanged.
🎯 Why: Previously, saving or loading a storyboard project re-hashed every video and image by reading the full bytes into memory (`hashlib.sha1(path.read_bytes())`), introducing severe latency for large asset folders.
📈 Impact: Index generation time is radically reduced for unmodified files. In tests profiling 70MB of synthetic data, warm times dropped from ~0.127s down to ~0.003s, eliminating unnecessary I/O.
🔬 Measurement: Verify by loading a project with large video files; subsequent saves/loads will be noticeably instantaneous compared to the cold start.

body:
## Summary
Implements the foundational rule `rules/robust-file-ops.md` to prevent common agent failure modes during file manipulations and state synchronization.

### Key Additions
- **Freshness & Stale Buffer Verification**: Enforces inspecting target file ranges and re-anchoring line slices before applying edits.
- **Surgical Edits & Anti-Truncation Heuristics**: Restricts full-file overwrites on existing files (>50 lines) to avoid streaming token limits and whole-file rewrite truncation loops.
- **Strict Target Uniqueness & Context Anchoring**: Mandates 2-3 lines of surrounding context to prevent ambiguous replacement matches.
- **Idempotent Failure Recovery**: Outlines a structured diagnostic sequence (Inspect -> Check if already applied -> Recalibrate) rather than blind retry loops.
- **Post-Edit Integrity**: Validation of syntax and AST integrity after file edits.

author: kodestar
body:
Chapter batch 31 of the wave-2 campaign - the **last full batch**; the 727-row
tail (batch 32) follows it. Enrich-only: it creates nothing, places nothing in a
series, and every existing fact wins.

## The band

| | |
|---|---|
| ASINs attempted | 9,500 |
| chapter lists fetched | 7,297 |
| no chapter list in the mirror | 2,202 (23.2%) |
| transient errors (deferred) | 1 |

23.2% against batch 30's 26.1% and batch 29's 26.4% - a third batch in the
twenties. The per-500 ok windows:

```
493 197 461 485 498 500 500 498 497 483
486 411 258 289 282 293 263 231 172
```

**This batch does not show batch 25's interleaving.** There is no 500 next to a
17: eight windows sit at 483 or better, the smallest is 172, and the back half
declines smoothly from 486 to 172. That is a different shape from b26-b30 and it
is one batch, so it is no more a trend than the alternation was - but it should
be read as it is rather than assimilated to the previous six. The rate was read
off the fetch log rather than assumed - no 403 and no rate-limit cliff (a 403
stops the loop outright). The single transient error arrived between rows 4,500
and 5,000 and none followed.

## What landed

- **5,766 recordings** go from no chapter timeline to one - **206,746 chapter
  rows** (tree total 8,691,705 -> 8,898,451).
- **1,352 rows** named a recording that already carried chapters. That is nearly
  four times batch 30's 359, and b30 was itself well up on b29's 196 and b28's
  122. It is not batch overlap - batch 31's 9,500 ASINs are disjoint from batches
  28, 29 and 30's - so this cohort simply carries many regional SKUs of
  recordings earlier batches already filled under a different ASIN.
- **256 rows** are a second SKU of a recording an earlier row in *this* batch
  filled, landing on **176 distinct recordings**, and **39 of those recordings
  drew more than one** second SKU (up to four). **78 rows are both pre-filled and
  a second SKU.** The two sets overlap as they did in b28/b30; the voided row is
  in neither this time, so the arithmetic is a single subtraction: 1,352 + 256 +
  1 = 1,609 rows, minus 78 counted twice = **1,531** distinct. 5,766 + 1,531 =
  **7,297**.
- **131** of the 1,531 distinct untouched rows state a list of a different length
  than the one recorded - the case the fill-absent rule exists for. Every one of
  the 131 length mismatches the post-run verification found is in that set; none
  outside it.
- **1 list voided whole** for a zero-length section marker - the known class. The
  rule is `length <= 0` on any chapter (`buildChapters`), and the whole list is
  refused rather than a broken timeline stored: `B0DYPBPRV2` (*The North Wind*,
  French edition -> `the-north-wind-alexandria-warwick/nadine-girard-2025`), ch 4
  "PREMIÈRE PARTIE La maison des épines". The following chapter starts at exactly
  the **same** offset (62,878 ms) rather than an earlier one, so the zero length
  is the whole of the defect - the batch-30 `B0FP2ZH874` shape.
- **0 conflicts** - the `--conflicts` worklist is empty.
- **2 new provenance stamps** - the batch 21/27 class, not b30's zero:
  `enders-game/dan-schlosser-2015` (`B01CF3FZAE`) and
  `exeter-season-1/jeanne-tripplehorn-2023` (`B0BZQHJ311`) are
  `audiosilo-books-import` records carrying no `libex-import` source for their
  ASIN. Enrich fills absent facts on any tier and existing values win
  (`applyScope`, as designed). HEAD carried **zero** `2026-08-21` stamps, so the
  absolute count and the b28 diff-against-HEAD both give 2.

### Every ASIN resolved

**All 7,297** resolved to exactly one recording - 0 not in the catalogue, 0 with
an unresolvable region, 0 sitting on more than one recording. Every region was
read from the recorded `asin[]` entry; none guessed.

## Whole-tree equivalence proof

Every one of the **277,628** work entries was hashed before and after with
`chapters` and any `2026-08-21` provenance stamp removed, compared as a sorted
(slug, entry-hash) **set** rather than in file order (pack splits move entries
between files):

- set hash `726520b24e4d28e1...` **identical** before and after
- **0 entries lost, 0 added, 0 changed** outside chapters
- `people`, `series` and `data/redirects.json` byte-identical
- recordings carrying chapters 243,203 -> 248,969: **5,766 went 0 -> n, none lost
  a list, none changed length**
- an independent normalized field-level diff over the 2,377 changed pack files
  reports **0** entries differing outside chapters

**The proof covers a different family set this batch.** `works-community` left
this repository in `ef37ce09b` (the community-layer split), so the tree now holds
works, people, series and the one non-pack `redirects.json`, and the redirect
table is hashed in the sidecar family's place. The set-hash value is new
(`726520b2...` where b29/b30 proved `48343a32...`) because main gained ten works
and a handful of people/series through the intake commits between the two
batches - the tree moved on main, not under this run.

The file-order works hash did **not** move (`62b55c03...` on both sides) even
though 71 packs split - the same luck batch 25 had, since a split only changes
the walk when it reorders the sorted file list. That is not a proof, which is
exactly why the sorted-set comparison is.

## Spot check

5 enriched recordings compared field-by-field against their mirror source
(`the-queens-child`, `jehovah-and-hades-book-2`, `my-wizard-buddy-book-1`,
`renata-ama-la-luna-renata-loves-the-moon`, `kens-ketchup-covered-kittens`):
**0 mismatches** in `title`, `start_ms` or `length_ms`, and **0 key-set
deviations**. The pick deliberately excludes every pre-filled, second-SKU and
voided row, so all five are rows this run actually wrote. 297 source titles
across 87 of the 7,297 lists pad a chapter title with whitespace (~1.2% of
lists, the lowest share of the campaign); the importer trims it, as in batches
21-30.

## Gate

`go build` / `go vet` / `go test -race` / `golangci-lint` (0 issues) /
`metafmt --check` / `metacheck` all green. metacheck: **277,628 works,
123,118 people, 45,172 series**, no problems.

**The advisory baseline moved before this batch touched anything** - the batch-28
lesson, and by far the largest such move yet. Batch 30 finished at 2,884; this
base reads **2,532**. The difference is the community-layer split: the
mis-scaled-sidecar class counted 352 lines and is now **0 on both sides**,
because the sidecars it reads are no longer in this tree. A new class
(`0 sidecar keys riding a redirect`) appears beside it, also zero. So there is
**no #2060 accrual to report this batch**, for the first time since batch 17 -
the accrual continues in the community repository, not here. The remainder of the
gap is the ten works and the people/series the intake commits added.

Advisory delta **2,532 -> 2,534 (+2)**, fully accounted once the pack path is
stripped from the comparison (9 lines new, 7 gone), and **all of it oversized
entries, 16 -> 18**:

- **Two new**, both single-entry exemptions and both the expected consequence of
  filling timelines on a heavily recorded classic: `return-of-sherlock-holmes`
  (342,752 bytes) and `the-adventures-of-sherlock-holmes` (291,657 bytes).
- **Seven restated larger** under the same exemption: `war-and-peace`
  367,906 -> 783,404, `dracula` 407,082 -> 420,891, `les-miserables`
  518,999 -> 520,397, `little-women` 399,209 -> 407,094, `treasure-island`
  328,641 -> 334,071, `the-count-of-monte-cristo` 315,730 -> 318,206,
  `a-tale-of-two-cities` 310,534 -> 312,036.

## Pack layout

2,448 files changed - **2,377 M + 71 A**, +1,923,130 / -877,574. **Nothing
renamed and nothing deleted.**

**No works directory crossed the 512-pack cap**, and none could have - the
largest is `data/works/il-traditore-krosann-saga-vol-6` at 322. All sixteen
directories grew by due median splits and none shrank:

| | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0` 312 -> 316 | `ascendant-king` 293 -> 298 | `chhoti-durga-s1e2` 266 -> 272 | `deep-fried-death` 279 ->

body:
## Inhalt
- erweitert `Reiseziele` ohne doppelte bestehende Ziele um Miami ↔ Bangkok, Chicago ↔ Barcelona, Lissabon ↔ Kopenhagen und Prag ↔ Budapest
- nutzt den bereits vorhandenen Tokyo-Eintrag weiter und ergänzt dafür das Drive-Bild
- verwendet weiterhin denselben bestehenden `traumhaus`-Pack (`Unser Traumhaus`) statt eine zweite Kategorie anzulegen
- verwendet weiterhin denselben `aussen`-Pack (`Traumhaus Außenbereich`) statt zu duplizieren
- erweitert `Aktivitäten` zu `Aktivitäten & Hobbys` um 6 weitere Paare
- verwendet weiterhin den bestehenden `ringe`-Pack (`Verlobungsringe`)
- fügt `Getränke` mit 7 Paaren hinzu
- fügt `Tiere` mit 9 vollständigen Paaren hinzu; das einzelne Pferd-Motiv bleibt Reserve

## Eiscreme
`custom_gourmet_eissorten` und seine 7 bestehenden Eis-Paare wurden bewusst **nicht geändert**.

## Drive-Bilder jetzt wirklich im GitHub-Projekt
- 53 aus Google Drive übernommene und für die App komprimierte WebP-Bilder sind physisch im Repository unter `app/src/main/assets/drive_tot_assets.zip` enthalten
- enthalten sind Getränke, Tiere, die neuen Aktivitäten/Hobbys sowie die neuen Reiseziele inklusive Tokyo
- die Reisebilder wurden vor dem Bundling so aufbereitet, dass die eingebrannte Ortsbeschriftung nicht mehr sichtbar ist; der kurze Ortsname kommt nur aus dem App-Text
- `DriveTotAssetInstaller.kt` entpackt die Bilder beim App-Start in den lokalen App-Speicher
- `HarmonyViewModel` registriert diese lokalen Dateien direkt nach `DeveloperDataManager.init()` und nach jedem Supabase-Refresh erneut
- dadurch haben die Drive-Bilder Vorrang vor den in `TotImageProvider` hinterlegten Web-Fallbacks und funktionieren offline wie die anderen lokal ausgelieferten Bildspiele

## Deduplizierung
- `Unser Traumhaus`, `Traumhaus Außenbereich` und `Verlobungsringe` bleiben dieselben bestehenden Packs; logisch bereits vorhandene Drive-Paare werden nicht doppelt angelegt
- Reiseziele werden nicht doppelt angelegt; Tokyo erhält nur sein fehlendes Bild

## Datenmodell
Die Packs werden in `GeneratedHarmonyContent.kt` mit den bestehenden IDs bereitgestellt, damit sie nach `DeveloperDataManager`-/Supabase-Synchronisierung nicht wieder durch ältere Defaults ersetzt werden.

## Finaler Diff gegen main
Nur 5 produktive Dateien:
- `app/src/main/assets/drive_tot_assets.zip`
- `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/DriveTotAssetInstaller.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/example/data/GeneratedHarmonyContent.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/HarmonyViewModel.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/example/ui/components/TotImageProvider.kt`

## Prüfung
- Branch ist 0 Commits hinter `main`
- Eis-Pack unverändert
- 53 erwartete Bilddateien befinden sich im Bundle
- lokale Bildregistrierung wird auch nach Supabase-Sync wiederhergestellt
- kein erfolgreicher Android-Build behauptet; die Änderung wurde statisch auf Daten-, Pfad- und Mapping-Konsistenz geprüft

author: homunculuslabs
body:
Adds two boundary fixes and a seam test suite closing the #23977 residue of the scheduled-task `edit` REST family (found by execution-based post-merge reviews of #23930; umbrella family #23917/#23832).

## What changed

**1. `POST /:id/edit` with an explicit `{}` body now returns the sibling 400** instead of performing a durable empty write. At base, `{}` is schema-valid (`.partial().strict()`), passes the `body === undefined` guard, and lands in `applyEdit`, which `Object.assign`s an empty patch, re-persists the row, and appends a spurious `edited {keys:[]}` state-log row (HTTP 200). The typed UI client `applyScheduledTask` (`packages/ui/src/api/client-scheduled-tasks.ts`) sends exactly `JSON.stringify(payload ?? {})` for every verb — so `{}` is the literal wire body of a payload-less edit call. The empty-body gate sits before the read-only-key scan and schema parse; the error message mirrors the body-less case's contract (`snooze`'s `.refine` already 400s an empty payload — sibling consistency).

**2. `POST /test-probe` body reads now honor `transfer-encoding`**, mirroring the apply-verb gate #23930 fixed: `(contentLength > 0 || transfer-encoding !== undefined)`. A chunked probe with `{"kind":"checkin"}` no longer silently runs the default reminder kind. Honest tightening note: a chunked request with zero body bytes now 400s (reader parse error) instead of defaulting to reminder — same choice #23930 made for `edit` and two reviewers upheld; no in-repo client sends an empty chunked POST here.

**3. New seam integration suite** (`scheduled-tasks.seam.test.ts`): drives `buildSchedulingRoutes` (the production `routes:` adapter, `plugin-routes.ts`) with real `IncomingMessage` streams, the REAL core `readJsonBody` reader, and the real `ScheduledTaskRunnerService` (host-injected in-memory stores via `registerScheduledTaskRunnerDeps`, the documented injection point). This pins the real-reader contracts the framing gates now depend on — empty-chunked → 400 parse error, malformed → 400, JSON `null` → 400 non-object, >1MiB → 413, chunked-without-content-length reads — which were previously pinned by NO in-repo test (the route suite's `ctx.readJsonBody` is a stream-blind mock, and the adapter seam had zero tests).

## Evidence (all execution, real reader/runner/routes)

- **Package suite at head `6ec57d36705`** (rebased on develop `f8a29be4c24`): 35 files / **561 tests pass** (was 549; +12 new: 2 unit + 10 seam). `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-scheduling test`.
- **Red control A (unit)** — route source reverted to pristine develop, new tests kept: the two #23977 unit tests fail exactly as the issue predicts (`{}` edit: expected 400, got 200). 
- **Red control B (seam)** — entire worktree at pristine develop, only the new seam suite present: exactly the 2 residue tests fail (`{}` edit 200-not-400; chunked probe `reminder`-not-`checkin`) while all 8 real-reader pins pass — proving the suite drives the real reader, not a mock.
- **Independent RP review (opus, converged)**: APPROVE, zero must-fix. The reviewer independently re-ran the 561-test suite in the worktree, re-ran its own red control (exactly 4 #23977-named failures at base), re-ran biome, verified the diff base byte-for-byte against `origin/develop` blobs, verified the snooze sibling contract, confirmed no in-repo caller sends `{}` to edit expecting 200 (the only non-test `applyScheduledTask` caller invokes snooze/acknowledge/complete/dismiss, never edit), verified the void-dispatch path (`TestNoop` → `fired`, no `lastDispatchResult` — now pinned by assertion), and confirmed no bypass to the empty-patch persist path is constructible (JSON cannot express symbol keys; `__proto__` own-key → 409 via the read-only scan, re-checked inside `applyEdit`).
- **Typecheck**: `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — 1 error, `packages/ui/src/bridge/storage-bridge.ts` missing `@elizaos/capacitor-secure-store`. IDENTICAL at pristine develop in the same worktree (symlinked node_modules platform-package artifact); zero errors from this delta's files.
- **Lint**: `npx biome check` on all three changed files — clean (including the reviewer's independent re-run).
- **Build**: `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-scheduling build` passes.
- **Plugin boundary gate**: no new imports; `rg "@elizaos/(app-core|agent|plugin-personal-assistant|plugin-google-workspace)" plugins/plugin-scheduling/src` matches comments/strings only (pre-existing).
- Reviewer nits applied before push: `afterEach` service teardown in the seam suite, endpoint-contract note in the route header, explicit `lastDispatchResult === undefined` pin on the void-dispatch probe.

## Test plan for reviewers

```
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-scheduling test        # 561 pass
# red control: revert only src/routes/scheduled-tasks.ts to develop, re-run —
# exactly the 4 #23977-named tests fail (2 unit + 2 seam), everything else green
```

Closes #23977

author: mitre88
body: ## 🔗 Linked Issue Found by direct code audit. Issues are disabled on this fork, so no fork issue can be linked. The defect also exists on current upstream `Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai` `main` (`mergeObjects` in `internal/components/filemerge/json_merge.go` still replaces arrays wholesale), so this fix is a candidate for upstreaming via the issue-first workflow. ## 🏷️ PR Type - [x] `type:bug` — Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## 📝 Summary The Claude Code permission overlay carries a fixed 8-entry `deny` array, and `MergeJSONObjects` deep-merges maps but replaces every non-map value — including arrays — wholesale. The result: **every install and every sync silently deleted any deny rules the user had added** to `~/.claude/settings.json`, leaving only the stock list. A user who hardened their setup with rules like `Read(secrets/**)` or `Bash(my-custom-danger *)` lost them with no warning, recurring on every run. This is a silent, repeating loss of user *security* configuration. **Fix:** a new `__append_unique__` merge sentinel in `filemerge`, mirroring the existing `__replace__` sentinel. When an overlay value is `{"__append_unique__": [...]}`, the overlay list is **unioned** with the base list: user entries are always preserved, stock entries are appended only when absent (equality via `reflect.DeepEqual`, so non-comparable JSON values are safe). The Claude overlay's `deny` list now uses the sentinel. **Scope note:** `defaultMode` is intentionally still forced to `bypassPermissions` — that is the component's documented purpose (see the overlay's doc comment). This fix is strictly about not deleting user data. ## 📂 Changes | File / Area | What Changed | |-------------|-------------| | `internal/components/filemerge/json_merge.go` | New `__append_unique__` sentinel: `asAppendUniqueSentinel` + `appendUnique` (union with dedup), wired into `mergeObjects` alongside the existing `__replace__` handling | | `internal/components/permissions/inject.go` | Claude Code overlay's `deny` list now uses the sentinel instead of a plain array | | `internal/components/filemerge/json_merge_test.go` | 5 new tests: base-entry preservation, dedup with no base key, corrupt (non-list) base, idempotency across repeated merges, and sentinel-never-leaks (including nested under a missing parent key) | | `internal/components/permissions/inject_test.go` | Regression test: user deny rules survive `Inject`, stock rules present, shared entries not duplicated, second `Inject` reports `Changed=false` | ## 🧪 Test Plan **Unit Tests** ```bash go test ./... ``` **E2E Tests** (Docker required) ```bash cd e2e && ./docker-test.sh ``` - [x] Unit tests pass (`go test ./...`) — full suite green, including 6 new tests - [ ] E2E tests pass (`cd e2e && ./docker-test.sh`) — Docker not available in this environment; change is pure JSON-merge logic covered by unit tests - [x] Manually tested locally — `TestInjectClaudeCodePreservesUserDenyEntries` was run against the previous overlay and fails exactly as described (`user deny rule "Bash(my-custom-danger *)" was deleted by Inject`); it passes with the fix ## ✅ Contributor Checklist - [ ] PR is linked to an issue with `status:approved` (issues are disabled on this fork — see Linked Issue section) - [ ] I have added the appropriate `type:*` label to this PR (labels require maintainer permissions) - [x] Unit tests pass (`go test ./...`) - [ ] E2E tests pass (Docker unavailable in this environment) - [x] I have updated documentation if necessary (sentinel documented in code; no user-facing doc changes needed) - [x] My commits follow Conventional Commits format - [x] My commits do not include `Co-Authored-By` trailers

author: guiferpa
body:
A terceira e última corrente do IR, e a única que mexia em semântica. ## O que havia ``` OpLoad name p OpPushFeed imm 0 ref

; escreve no environ de quem chama OpCall name area ; le' de la' ``` Os dois lados combinavam um lugar que **o IR nunca menciona**. Pelo que estava escrito, `OpCall` não dependia de nada: não referenciava o push, nem o load. Isso funciona num interpretador, onde o lugar combinado existe. Não funciona para um passe que reordena — nada dizia que mover o push para depois da chamada é errado — nem para um backend, que não tem environ nenhum. ## O que passa a haver ``` OpLoad name p OpCall name area ref

``` **Onde os valores ficam durante uma chamada é convenção de chamada, e convenção de chamada é do alvo:** environ aqui, memória ou pilha numa cadeia, `locals` em WASM, registradores numa ABI. O IR diz *o que* é passado; cada um decide *onde* vai. `OpPushFeed` sai do vocabulário — ele existia só para mutar o lugar combinado. ## E some um perigo que estava documentado em vez de consertado `.claude/agents/aurora-internals.md` avisava: > *"`OpPushArg` mutates the current frame's args map, and `OpCall` passes that same map into the new frame (`SetArguments`, not a copy). Nested/recursive calls therefore share and overwrite argument slots — **assume this when debugging wrong argument values**."* Um escopo que recebeu dois valores e chamou outro com um **passava o segundo adiante**, sentado numa posição que o chamado nunca pretendeu ler — e ler aquilo parecia leitura comum. ``` ident inner = defer { feed(1) + 1; }; ident outer = defer { inner(feed(0)); }; ident answer = outer(7, 99); ``` Antes: `inner` lia 99 e respondia **100**. Agora recebe exatamente um valor, lê além do fim, e responde **1** — que é a regra desde a #92. O teste procura pelo 100, que é um número que **não existe em lugar nenhum do fonte**: ele só pode aparecer se o vazamento acontecer. ## Estado das três correntes | construção | antes | agora | |---|---|---| | `shape` | n × `OpJoin` | uma instrução (#101) | | literal de tape | n × `OpPull` | uma instrução (#101) | | chamada | n × `OpPushFeed` + `OpCall` | uma instrução | `make check` verde, 0 issues. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: dbraun
body:
`faustax.diffvox` compiles `dsp/diffvox/*.dsp` to NNX so the chain is differentiable in JAX. That is what a training loop wants and what bulk offline rendering does not: the NNX path pays a per-sample `scan`, while DawDreamer runs libfaust's compiled C++ at native speed.

This adds `DawDreamerChain`, a second renderer of the **same** Faust sources. Same constructor, same `process(x, preset)` shapes, same send topology as `Chain`, and the same physical parameter dicts from `eq_params` / `compressor_params` / `pingpong_params` / `fdn_params` — so swapping backends is a one-line change and the Faust source stays the single definition of the effect.

```python
preset = load_preset_dataset("presets/internal")[7]
wet_jax = Chain().process(dry, preset)                        # differentiable
wet_cpp = DawDreamerChain().process(np.asarray(dry), preset)  # fast
```

## Agreement between the backends

Measured on the curated presets: **correlation 1.000000**, relative error **1.4e-5 to 4e-4**.

That residual is not topology — it is compiler version. DawDreamer bundles libfaust **2.85.9** while the checked-in `_generated` modules came from **2.87.0**, and two Faust releases order the arithmetic of one program differently. `libfaust_version()` reports what is actually in use, and the tests assert on relative error and correlation rather than a sample tolerance that would be wrong the moment either side moves.

Keeping faustax on 2.87.0 is deliberate; the gap is documented rather than engineered away.

## Two details that cost debugging

- **Faust shortnames are not DawDreamer's labels.** The FDN's slider is `b0-0` by label and `b0_0` as the shortname `faustax.diffvox`'s parameter dicts use. The stage indexes both spellings and raises on an unknown key, rather than silently leaving a parameter at its default.
- **A DawDreamer processor does not own the engine it was made from**, and recompiles lazily on the first `set_parameter`. A caller passing a temporary engine had it collected and hit a compile failure that pointed at the faustlibraries path. The stage now holds its engine. (Found by the tests in this PR.)

## Testing

`tests/test_diffvox_dawdreamer.py` — 11 tests: per-stage channel arity, unknown-slider rejection, both label spellings, determinism, a send-tail check that would catch a mis-wired graph, and the cross-backend comparison.

Full suite on this branch: **215 passed, 8 skipped**.

⚠️ The new tests `importorskip("dawdreamer")`, and faustax's own venv does not have it — I ran them from an environment that does. **CI will skip this entire file** unless `dawdreamer` is added to the test extra.

## Note

`libfaust_version()` scans DawDreamer's extension module for a version string, because DawDreamer exposes no version API. It is diagnostic-only and returns `None` on failure, but it is the one piece here that could go stale if DawDreamer changes packaging.

author: msgaihede
body:
Left and right now step one card through the whole deck rather than one
pile, and a pile boundary is not a stop: right off the foot of a pile
lands on the head of the next, left off the head lands on the foot of the
one before. Entering at the near edge is what makes the walk reversible -
one press then the other is the card you started on. Empty piles are
still skipped and both ends still clamp rather than wrap, so the two keys
read the entire deck and nothing else.

Up and down reach no branch at all. This view has no scrollport of its
own, so the press falls to DeckEditor's page scroller, which is what a
reader pressing them on a wall of card art wants - "up does nothing"
would be a claim, and leaving the key alone is the absence of one. It is
AllPrintingsDialog's own stance, and the two surfaces now take the same
step on the same two keys.

CategoryGrip drops the same two: the desk answers left and right
everywhere on it, cards and grips alike, so a reader learns one pair
rather than finding that a heading takes four presses and a card takes
two. The reorder loses nothing - Up did what Left does and Down what
Right does - and its tooltip now says so. CategoriesDialog's own grip
stays on up/down, because its piles are a vertical list in a dialog.

Driven in the shipped window at 1920x1080 on a debug build: thirteen
presses walk a fourteen-card deck exactly once across four pile
boundaries, five more move nothing, and five ArrowDowns scroll the desk
0 -> 200px with the caret unmoved. Recorded in decks-live-findings.md.

author: noshiro-pf
body:
## 概要

`strict-ts-lib-v7.0` が 107 個の lib を 1 パッケージに同梱し npm に公開されたので、root `package.json` の GitHub Release URL 依存を通常のレジストリ依存 `^0.2.0` に置き換える。

前提となる upstream の変更は [strict-typescript-lib#123 / #125 / #127](https://github.com/noshiro-pf/strict-typescript-lib) で、v5.0〜v7.0 の全系統が npm に publish 済み。

## 消えるもの

`pnpm-workspace.yaml` の 2 設定が両方不要になる。

| 設定 | なぜ要ったか | なぜ不要になるか |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `blockExoticSubdeps: false` | メタパッケージの依存 107 件が URL で、pnpm は URL を**推移的**依存として拒否する | 直接依存の URL は元から許可されており、そもそもレジストリ依存になった |
| `publicHoistPattern: ['@typescript/lib-*']` | 推移的依存は `node_modules/.pnpm/` の下にしか入らず、`libReplacement` の探索範囲に並ばない | ホイストすべき推移的依存が無い |

`blockExoticSubdeps` はリポジトリ全体に効く boolean だったので、これが消えることで URL 依存の穴も閉じる。

## 代わりに要るもの

lib が「名前で解決できるパッケージ」ではなく「1 パッケージの中の `libs/` 配下」になるため、`paths` が必要になる。

```jsonc
"@typescript/lib-*": ["../../node_modules/strict-ts-lib-v7.0/libs/*"]
```

共有設定 `tools/configs/tsconfig/tsconfig.type-check.json` に置くだけでは足りない。**`paths` は `extends` 先に対してマージではなく置換**されるので、自前の `paths` を持つ 15 パッケージはこれを再掲する必要がある。

## サイレント失敗への対策

マッピングが欠けても TypeScript は何も言わない。探して、見つからず、自分の宣言を黙って使い続ける — 「opt-in しているように見えて実は素の lib で検査されている」状態になる。これを検出可能にするため 2 つ入れた。

- **`check:root:tsconfig-lib-paths`**（新規 `tools/scripts/cmd/check-tsconfig-lib-paths.mts`）— `paths` を定義していてこのエントリが無い tsconfig で落ちる。まだ `libReplacement` を有効化していないパッケージも対象にしてあるので、有効化した時点で既に正しい。
- **`libs/octokit-safe-types/test/strict-lib-active.mts`**（新規）— `Number.isFinite('1')` への `@ts-expect-error`。strict lib は引数を `number` に絞るので拒否し、素の lib は `unknown` なので受理する。置換が効かなくなった瞬間に `TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive` で落ちる（`paths` を外して実測済み）。

`check:root:lockfile` は例外が消えたぶん単純になり、`tarball:` を 1 件でも見つけたら落ちるようになった。

## 実測

- `pnpm-lock.yaml` の `tarball:` エントリ **0 件**（従来 108 件）
- `node_modules/@typescript/` ディレクトリ **消滅**
- `--traceResolution` の `@typescript/lib-*` 解決 **88/88 成功**
- `check:root:tsconfig-lib-paths` → `15 tsconfig file(s) map @typescript/lib-* onto strict-ts-lib-v7.0.`

## ドキュメント

- `CLAUDE.md` の Dependencies 節 — 「1 件の URL 依存 + 2 設定」から「通常のレジストリ依存 + `paths` + 2 チェック」へ書き換え
- `docs/strict-typescript-lib-integration.md` — 「移行完了（2026-08-21）」節を追加

## 検証

body:
Un-checking "sold" is the wrong tool when a record leaves the collection without a sale (given away, no longer owned): it clears only `sold`/`sold_at`, leaves `sold_price`/buyer behind, and puts the record straight back on the public shop as purchasable.

Each admin listings row now gets a **Delete…** link (next to Discogs / eBay solds / Popsike) that permanently removes the record:

- refuses with a toast if the record is inside a parcel (`shipments.record_ids` has no FK, so orphan ids would break parcel labels — remove it in Fulfillment first)
- confirms before doing anything irreversible
- removes the record's photos from the `record-photos` storage bucket
- deletes the row; `price_history`, `pending_price_changes`, `market_snapshots`, and `record_events` all cascade
- updates local state so the row and its pending price changes disappear without a reload

Backed by a new `"admin deletes records"` RLS policy (already applied in Supabase via migration `admin_deletes_records_policy` — the table previously had no DELETE policy at all).

The record that prompted this (Puscifer — Existential Reckoning: Rewired, id 339, marked sold with no buyer) has already been deleted directly in the database; its phantom $35 is out of the Sold/Net stats and the empty "No buyer set" fulfillment card is gone.

author: crossarc-sugawara
body:
## なぜ

**「ラジオで目覚まし」を「どのプランでもお使いいただけます」と書いていたが、実装ではプレミアム限定だった。** 同じズレが他にもある前提で、コードから全機能のプラン制限を洗い直した。

判定は `plan/Plan.kt` の `PlanCapabilities.of()`（77〜103行）1箇所に集約されていて、列は6つ。プラン状態を読んでいる **29ファイル・43箇所すべて**を追った結果、**サイトとのズレは目覚ましの1件だけ**だった。表の既存6行は実装と一致していた。

## 料金表（B-1）

|  | フリー | スタンダード | プレミアム |
|---|---|---|---|
| 月額 | 0円 | 250円 | 500円 |
| 広告 | あり | なし | なし |
| 録音の保有数 | 5件 | 10件 | 無制限 |
| 再生速度 | 1倍のみ | 6段階 | 6段階 |
| 自動録音 | − | − | ○ |
| チャプター | − | − | ○ |
| **ラジオで目覚まし** | **−** | **−** | **○** |
| **radiko プレミアム連携** | **○** | **○** | **○** |

- **並びを変えた。** 広告・保有数・再生速度（スタンダードで変わる）を上、プレミアムだけの3つを下。前の並びは自動録音とチャプターが間に挟まり、「250円で何が変わるのか」が読み取れなかった
- **再生速度は「6段階」**にし、内訳（0.5 / 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 3 / 5倍）を表の下に注記した。実装は `PlaybackSpeed.OPTIONS` の6つの固定値で、「0.5〜5倍」だと無段階に読める
- **radiko プレミアムが radiko 社との契約である**ことを表のすぐ下に明記した。ここは問い合わせになりやすい

## プラン表記（B-2）

- プレミアム限定 → `（プレミアム）`、スタンダード以上 → `（スタンダード以上）`、全プラン → 何も付けない
- 冒頭に読み方を1行置いた
- **オンエア曲は書き分けた。** 「表示」は全プラン、「頭出しの目印として使う」のがプレミアム
- **お気に入りの登録そのものは全プラン**であることも明記（自動で録るかどうかが変わるだけ）

### 降格したときの挙動

利用者がいちばん不安に思うところなので、それぞれの説明に添えた。

| どこに書いたか | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 録音の保有数 | 上限に達しても、**すでに録音した音声は消えない** |
| 自動録音 | **登録した予約は消えない。** プレミアムに戻すと再開する |
| チャプター | **作成済みのチャプターは消えない。** 戻すとそのまま表示される |
| ラジオで目覚まし | **登録した設定は消えない。** 戻すとそのまま鳴り出す |

いずれも実装どおり（`PlanLimits.canRecord` / `AutoRecordWorker:67` / `ChapterPolicy` / `AlarmPolicy` の各コメントに同じ方針が書かれている）。

## 年間プランが無い理由（B-3）

> 個人で作っているアプリなので、1年ぶんを先にお預かりするのは荷が重い、というのが正直なところです。使ってみて合わなければいつでも止められる形にしておきたい、という気持ちもあります。

## 文体（B-4）

各機能に、使う場面が想像できる一言を添えた（「電車や飛行機の中など、電波の届かないところでも」「寝落ちしても、朝までかかりっぱなしになりません」など）。絵文字・内輪ネタ・誇張・他アプリとの比較は入れていない。プライバシーポリシーには手を入れていない。

## 突き合わせ

表の8行と本文のプラン表記を1行ずつ確認し、食い違いが無いことを確かめた。表に無い全プラン機能13項目も、フェーズAで「コードを見て制限が無い」と確認したものだけを挙げている。

author: andrewbarba
body:
### Summary

eve internals currently have no programmatic registration path into the runtime graph, so every built-in invents its own: static tool arrays with synthetic paths, hand-flattened channel routes plus three bespoke callback-route builders, `connection_search` re-scraping message history every step, and delegation tools injected by scattered predicates. This PR adds the research plan for fixing that at the root: a single internal **framework feature** catalog where each built-in declares its primitives once, using the same shapes the authored pipeline produces, merged through one shared merge function with unified sentinel-disable semantics.

The document covers the feature API, catalog resolution flow, a migration map for every existing hack, connection_search state ownership, externally observable semantics (one intentional change: discovered tools persist across compaction), invariants, scope boundaries, and validation strategy. Implementation will follow in phases after review of this plan.

### Validation

Docs-only research proposal; no runtime checks apply. Pre-commit hooks formatted the document; CI runs the baseline lint/docs checks.
